name: Zac
description:
Zac Woof-ron is a heartthrob movie star looking to settle down with the right person! 

As you know from his movie career, Zac is a 2-year-old, purebred red heeler male, about 37 pounds and high energy. After finishing his press tour for his latest movie, âMission Impossible: ACDâ, Zac came into foster care with ACDRA with the goal of retiring from the fast-paced motion picture industry and finding a forever home. Accordingly, Zacâs publicist agreed to finally let us share his full life story so far. You see, Zac was tied outside for most of his young life, with little to no interaction with people or other dogs. When his owner died, he was taken to a shelter in NC.  Zac has been in foster care on a farm with 2 other ACDs, cows, and horses. 

Although he is a bit slow to warm up to new people, Zac quickly becomes your best friend. He absolutely must be with his person at all times and gives the best body hugs ever! He has great recall and therefore a fence isnât required. He would do best with an energetic person in an active home with a yard that is dedicated to exercising him mentally and physically. Zac would make a great running, biking, or hiking partner or even agility dog. Inside the house, Zac isnât destructive (he has had free run of the house) although he does like to relocate his foster dadâs clothing around the house, and he settles right down to snuggle on your lap. He is already mostly potty trained and has learned to use the doggie door, sit, lie down, and wait. He will be easy to train as he is smart and highly food motivated. Zac loves to ride in the car and walks well on the leash. He has begun to show some interest in toys and fetch. Although Zac typically sleeps on the bed with his foster dad and canine housemates, he has occasionally been crated during the night and does just fine.  

Zac would thrive best in an ACD-experienced home without children or cats. He needs a patient person who will be able to harness his energy (and occasional mouthiness) in order help him achieve his full potential as a good canine citizen through training and exercise. Although he gets along with his foster brother and sister, they are no match for his energy level. Therefore, Zac requests a home with another dog who likes to chase and roughhouse as much as he does! 

Zac is neutered, microchipped, heartworm negative, and up to date on HW and flea/tick prevention.He is located in Adamstown, MD.

For questions, please contact mdrancherld@yahoo.com.

name: TATE
description:
Tate is an adorable 2 year old, 22 pound Cockapoo.  She came to use from a local shelter where her owner had turned her in.  Her owner was older and didn't have the time or energy for Tate.  She came to us with a condition called Microphthalmia.  This is where one eye is very small and often with other abnormalities.  Tate could not see out of the eye and it was uncomfortable for her.  We removed the eye which is completely healed.

Tate is very affectionate. She loves to play with toys and with other dogs.  She loves to cuddle in bed and on the sofa.  Tate is house trained and crate trained.  She loves her walks but needs more leash training.  We're working on it..   She likes to ride in the car.  Tate does sleep in bed.  She is good with respectful children that are 10 or older.  Tate would love another dog to play with but would be fine with an interactive family that has a lot of time for her.  We introduced Tate to cats and she would definitely chase if the cat would run.  It doesn't appear that she would hurt the cat but unless the cat was VERY laid back she would do best without a cat in the home.

Tate is a sweet girl that had little training in her early life.  She is very smart and eager to please.  She and her new owner would have a lot of fun in an obedience class.  Tate quickly learned to ring bells at the door to go outside but then took it a bit too far by ringing them too much.  This shows us that she is eager to have an active family that will do a lot of things where she can be included.  

Tate's adoption requirements are a fenced yard or area large enough for her to run and play that leads directly into the home.  She is not a candidate for an underground fence.  Tate needs someone who is not working a typical 8 hour work day; someone that works very part time, works from home and can their dog in their work space or someone that is retired.  She would love children that are 10 or older in the home and would do super with another playful dog.  If she is an only dog the family must be active with the time and desire to have a dog involved in a major part of their life.  After having very little attention for the first two years of her life, Tate deserves to have a home where she is cherished.  Tate's new home must continue with her natural care program.  We will place Tate within an hour drive from Akron, OH. which includes the Cleveland, Akron/Canton, Youngstown area.

Star-Mar Rescue is a natural care provider and we place our dogs in homes that are already on a natural care program or are eager to learn. We use no chemicals on our dogs, no commercial flea products (oral or topical), do blood titer testing instead of randomly vaccinating. Our yards are without fertilizer and weed killer and our homes are toxin free. We feel that dogs can be protected without being harmed by harsh chemicals and unnecessary vaccinations and do best on a species appropriate, no grain, raw diet. Frozen raw diets, freeze dried or dehydrated no grain. Raw, no grain foods are easily gotten at many pet stores and on line and are no more expensive than a high quality dry food. This simple step will provide your dog the nutrition needed to keep them healthy and happy for many years unlike feeding a lifetime of processed foods. We are happy to help with this transition. For more information go to Star-Mar Rescue Natural Care facebook page and click on \"videos\" in the column to the left and watch the 7 part series called The Truth About Pet Cancer. It will give you an understanding of what we are doing and why. Please do some research on natural care and raw feeding and decide whether or not you are wanting to care for Tate in this manner before requesting an application.

If you feel that your lifestyle and environment meet with Tate's needs, please directly contact Martha at learymjri@aol.com or call 330-466-3667 or 330-262-0515 for an application or more information. PLEASE DO NOT USE THE LINK PROVIDED AS IT IS NOT ALWAYS RELIABLE. Tate's adoption will require an approved application and a home visit, with adoption completed at her foster home in Akron, OH. Tate's adoption fee is $275. We will work to place her within an 1 hour driving distance from his foster home in Akron, OH. so that we can conduct a home visit bringing Tate with us. This includes the Cleveland, Akron/Canton, Youngstown, Elyria, Loraine areas of OH. 

STAR-MAR RESCUE IS REGISTERED WITH THE OHIO DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AS REQUIRED BY LAW

I used to get all the cuddles and attention due to my anxiety and hard early life but these days they are really busy with the toddler and growing another baby. My mom adopted me at 5 years old from Alabama and from then I've lived an amazing life, traveled all over, and really enjoy being by my owners side. I'm now 12 years old and enjoy the calmer things in life, like a nice walk, sleeping all day and sniffing around the yard. Since the addition of my new sister I am not a huge fan of other dogs and little humans in my space. While I may be getting older I still have a lot of spunk for being 12 years old. I am looking for a new owner in a peaceful home that will give me all the love and attention I deserve. Here is a few things about me:

-I love belly rubs.

-I enjoy a nice car ride even though sometimes I get anxiety and would rather sit in the floor boards.

-I do leashes but prefer being free to roam and wander. Don't worry I won't go too far away from you.

-I'm a rescue so I can be skittish and have snapped if I feel threatened or scared.

-I like to protect my home and humans so I will bark when people come to the door or I first meet them, then I usually warm up.

-I'm potty trained.

-I'm neutered.

-I will sleep on the dog bed or cuddled up with you and I am good about staying off the furniture... most the time. ;)

-I shake, sit and really enjoy food, especially the good stuff you eat.

My ideal home would be no other dogs or young kids and a yard to explore, I'm not a big fan of peeing on pavement and loud noises of the city. The sooner we can find someone the better. Please reach out if you think Jakey is a good fit for you and your home. Seth

name: Meredith
description: Meredith was rescued from a high-kill shelter in Alabama. Being a black dog, she had very little chance of being adopted down south. She was another dog that was in trouble and was in danger of being euthanized the next day. So, of course, I couldn't let that happen. She was fully vetted, spayed, and spent about 2 weeks in a foster home in AL with a shepherd X, who became her good friend. When she came to NY, she went to a friend who fostered her, who has an older hound X and 4 cats. When the foster mom brought her young nieces home for a weekend, Merri, as her foster mom likes to call her, was wonderful with them! There have been no problems with Merri with either the cats, the dog or with anyone new that she meets. Merri is 2 yrs. old, weighs 59 lbs, is fully housebroken, sits, and walks well on leash. She is a special girl, looking for that special home. If you feel that Merri is the dog for you. please call Sindee. 914-299-3700.

name: Kypsie
description:
Kypsie and her litter mates arrived to our rescue on August 10th from Opelika, Alabama.  This litter was surrendered to a very high kill shelter and were literally saved within hours of euthanization.  The shelter was already overflowing and owner surrenders are the first to be put down.  We are most grateful that we could save them!

We believe this litter of puppies are a mix of labrador retriever, hound, spaniel and a couple look a little pittie.  Keep in mind, there can be different fathers in a litter which is probably why there is such a variety in this group!   They are around 3 months old and will probably grow to be medium to large dogs....depending on the puppy.

Kypsie is a very sweet, friendly pup!  She is a player and can always be found rough housing with her littermates.  She is a pretty sociable dog and enjoys both her furry companions and her humans.  

Kypsie has received all of her distemper/parvo vaccines, dewormed multiple times and current on flea/tick preventative.  Her adoption fee is $350.  

If you are interested in adopting Kypsie, please submit an application on our website at https://worthytails.rescuegroups.org.  For any questions you have, please send an email to her foster mom, Jessie at jessie.wilson@comcast.net.

Thank you for your interest in a rescue puppy!

name: Carter
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Fill out an Adoption Application
Brief description: Carter is an absolute goofball with a huge heart! He is housetrained and crate trained. He even sleeps through the night. He can be destructive when left alone in the house so the crate is important. He came to us from Alabama with an awful case of mange and skin infection but he is mange free and the skin infection is getting better everyday.
Likes: Carter likes everybody but loves to play and run and wrestle. Snuggles are a daily necessity.
Dislikes: Peanut butter and being scolded.
Personality: Carter has the best personality! He can be serious but he is most likely to be an absolute goofball. He will get quite offended or embarrassed if you need to scold him and will sulk for a bit but he will eventually forgive you, LOL.
Temperament: Carter does not like to be forced to do anything, such as taking meds, but will gladly do it if offered with a food he likes. He is a mouthy boy so trimming his nails is interesting but I'm sure in time he will learn to accept it. He loves car rides and so far he thinks a vet appointment is just an organized social hour. Carter wants to please his people and is highly food motivated. Just give him a minute to think about what you are asking and he will do his best to please!
Energy level: Carter is a typical young dog. He can get pretty excited and do zoomies for a few minutes and he loves to rough house with other dogs but he has learned to relax and enjoy a good nap too.
Favorite activities: He is quite social and loves to meet people. He also loves to play with any toy that is strong enough to withstand his serious attention.
Good with cats, dogs, and kids over 6?: Carter has not been cat tested but has a very strong prey drive so I would not recommend small pets. So far he has liked every dog he has met and he thinks little people are pretty special! He does not know his own strength so he needs to be closely monitored around little ones.
Not good with: Personal Space! He is a bit of a bully and does not understand why he can't lay on your head or another dogs head...
Housetrained: Carter seems to be 100% house trained! He has access to a fenced yard through a doggy door and has never had an accident in his crate.
Crate trained: Yes, Carter does well in his crate.
Challenges: Being a young boy Carter thinks EVERYTHING should go in his mouth. He will chew anything that doesn't chew him first. When he gets bored, he will find a nice shoe or box to chew on for fun. He is not even sorry afterwards, LOL...
Any Medical issues? Carter came to us with a horrible case of bacterial and fungal skin infection, most likely caused by untreated demodex mange. He has been on antibiotics and antifungal meds since coming into foster care and his skin is improving slowly but surely.
What would be the best kind of home? The best home for Carter would be an active home. A home with older kids or active adults. He would like to have a K9 of equal size and energy to wrestle with too but I believe he would be ok being an only dog if need be. With his strong prey drive I would not recommend cats or small dogs.

Fostered in West Lafayette, OH.
Application Fees, Adoption Donations and Rescue Policy: Please know that 100% of our funds are used for rescuing the dogs.
Our rescue policy requires the following:

Adopters must have their primary residence in one of the following states: Pennsylvania, Ohio, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, West Virginia, Virginia, and parts of North Carolina.
Applications for giant breed dogs must be submitted by the property owner.
Homes with children under 6 years of age will not be approved for adoption.
Homes with children should have a fenced yard.
Pets currently in the applicant's home must have a history of appropriate veterinary care. Veterinary records will be checked.
All references must be checked before any visitation of the dog is permitted at the foster home.
All family members must be present during the home visit to the applicant's home.
Any dog(s) in the applicant's home must have an introductory meeting with the rescue dog being considered, before any adoption can be completed.

For additional information please review our FAQs or contact: mastiffstomutts@gmail.com

description:

There are 2 chihuahuas that live in her foster home, she has not tried to hurt them. She will chase the cat in the house and anything small she sees outside. So we are reccomending no small animals or cats at this time.
This girl has a very sweet personality and just wants to please and be told she is a good girl. She loves people. If you tell her it is ok, she will gently rise up on her two hind legs and put her two front paws on you and give you kisses.
Mya is also a snuggler who is good at her job!
Mya is heartworm negative, on preventative, house broken, crate trained, up to date on all vaccines, micro chipped and spayed.

name: Shannon (NY)
description:
Hello, I am Shannon! I am a super sweet, loveable and CALM liver and white pointer. Iâm between 1-2 years old. Originally from Alabama, now in northern NY, I arrived in pretty rough shape, but thankfully my foster folks and the doggie doctors have helped to transform me.

Iâm really easy to live with because I love everyone â people especially, but also dogs and probably even cats. My foster folks tell me that Iâm the easiest foster theyâve ever had the pleasure of fostering. Iâm a happy girl, with a constantly wagging tail and a sweet, gentle and loyal disposition. All I need is a warm, comfortable dog bed, but I would much prefer to share your couch or your bed, if you will let me! I weigh just under 50 pounds, which is just the right size for snuggling. I definitely love cuddles and belly rubs. Being close to my beloved humans is my favorite thing. I could see myself being an excellent companion to a retiree or someone who works from home.

I am doing my best to be a polite houseguest and my folks report that I am exceptionally well behaved. The resident dogs have become fast friends. I know that the bathroom is outside and I have very tidy bathroom habits. I can be left alone in the house uncrated, although I will tolerate being crated if you insist. I walk wonderfully on leash at a heel. No pulling! I havenât made a peep since I arrived. I ride perfectly in the car. I give gentle kisses and take treats nicely. I donât go through the trash, counter surf, bark, or chew things that I should not. I am a Velcro dog and like to stick close to home, so I could adjust to apartment life or an unfenced yard easily.

You should know that I was found as a stray with a fractured pelvis and front leg, probably the result of getting hit by a car. These fractures are healed now and I get around just fine, including going up and down stairs, but overly boisterous little humans and dogs wonât be a great fit for me. I prefer a laid-back lifestyle that includes soft couches and cuddles instead of long runs or rigorous play sessions.

I am fully vaccinated, dewormed and heartworm negative. I have been spayed, microchipped, and put on monthly flea/tick and heartworm preventative.

name: Beau
description:
Update on Beau. After consulting with a trainer, it does appear that Beau is mostly if not all Anatolian Shepherd. He is going to need a home that has experience with livestock guarding breeds and room for him to run. He does get along well with other dogs and cats too. He will not do well with small children as he does not like when small children are loud and jumpy. He can also be protective of his home when his family is not home. He does get very attached to his family and will do best in a home without a lot of traffic and is willing to put him away when they have visitors. While he is very friendly with everyone outside the home, he is an Anatolian and bred to guard his home. Knowledge of this breed is best for this boy. Beau is pretty much a big teddy bear with his family and is very well behaved in the house. His lumps are just fatty lipomas according to the cytology and our vet says they do not need any further treatment.

Beau came to us from a shelter in Alabama. He was found as a stray and no one came to claim him. He is a very big and sweet boy. He is 103 pounds and appears to be a lab, hound with maybe something else in him too. Beau has definitely lived in a home before. He is housebroken and even gets along very well with cats. He really does seem to like being with cats and he does also seem to get along very well with other dogs. We think he is about 5-7 years old and he is very much a gentle giant. He does have some weird lumps that we have the vet checking out and all his bloodwork has come back normal. So we think this maybe normal for him. He is neutered, up to date with vaccines, microchipped and heartworm and Lyme negtive. His adoption fee is $200.00. If you are interested in adopting Beau, please visit our website www.LHARinc.org go to Adopt and complete the dog adoption application.

name: Bella
description: Bella came to us from an Alabama shelter very pregnant. She was originally from a hoarding household before she came to the shelter. Bella is at least a couple of years old and weighs about 60 pounds. She had her puppies and they have been adopted so now we need to find her a forever home. We think that Bella will do best in a home with another friendly, social dog her size and a securely fenced in yard. Bella did also test positive for heartworm, so she has been treated for her heartworm and now spayed. Please check with your vet about adopting a dog that was previously heartworm positive. Bella is still scared and insecure, but she does not have a mean bone in her body. She is very low energy and still needs to learn how to be a dog. She is a very sweet girl, but does seem to have had some abuse in the past, so a calm quiet home would be best for her. name: Sassy
description:
We are actively looking for a foster home or an adoptive home for Sassy.
Sassy is presumed to be about 3 years old. She is an Australian Cattle dog, she was rescued from an Alabama shelter just in time for her to give birth to 5 beautiful puppies on July 19, 2019. Since that time Sassy has been an incredible mother providing for her pups and keeping them safe. As the little ones find homes of their own it is now time for Sassy to find her next family which will allow her to find her confidence and independence. Sassy is timid and would do great with another dog showing her that humans are trustworthy. She has learned how to walk on hardwood floors (which was very scary the first few times) and is housebroken and crate trained. She is not destructive and may not be the biggest fan of the leash but loves exploring the backyard. Spending time with Sassy it is clear that she craves affection, she is looking for the right home to help her break down those walls.
We are a foster-based rescue organization with foster homes throughout the state of Florida. name: Tom
description: Tom is available for foster or adoption. He is a Basenji mix of about 18 pounds and is currently fostered in Brandenton,FL (Manatee County). He came to us from a shelter in Alabama. He has been very quiet in his foster home, and has not barked at all. He occasionally plays with the other dogs, but he is really his own person with that Basenji aloofness. He does like to snuggle loves to be on the bed with you. Plays some with toys, but spends most of his time hunting lizards. He has gone in the pond but we have not seen any swimming yet. He is rather submissive to people, loves his belly rubs. He seems to be a bit head shy. Not afraid of noises, rain or thunder. Crate trained, extremely clean, fur is just so soft, and housebroken. He does not use the doggie door yet. Rides okay in the car. Will be a great dog for a moderately active family or an older couple. I think he would like his people around all the time. He is an adventurous soul and should ideally have a fenced yard, he feels the grass is greener on the other side. He does not at this time have a good recall either. Leash walk is okay but could use some fine tuning. Cats are probably a no, and he can be a bit leash aggressive to other dogs. Off lead he is just fine with dogs. He currently lives with 12 others, no issues, big and little, male and female. Overall, this little dude would be a great rv companion, fishing buddy, or just a snuggle buddy. Currently fostered in Bradenton area. Please research Basenjis as they are not dogs for everyone and he has Basenji qualities. name: Bean
description:
And here's Bean! Bean is a very shy dog but once he warms up to you, he is your shadow. He is a 9.5 pound, 2 year old chihuahua mix who made the journey all the way from Alabama to find his forever home.

Bean is adapting to life here in Michigan. You can usually find him in his \"spot\" - either his crate or a spot near his foster mom. But when given the chance, he loves to run outside to burn off energy! 

Bean has been around children, dogs and cats and has done well. He is crate trained and house trained. He does well on a leash, knows his name, and loves treats! He doesn't love bath time and has shown no desire to play with toys either. He would rather just cuddle up.

Bean is up to date on vaccines, is fixed, and microchipped. Bean would love you to meet him and let him prove that he can be a good dog for you! Go to www.pettalesrescue.com and fill out an application. Once approved, one of our volunteers will contact you to set up a time to meet him. Thank you for adopting, not shopping!

name: Roland
description:
Roland is a 4-year-old Schnauzer who loves to run, play, and sit on laps! He does well with other dogs and would do best with an active family.

Roland was transferred to our shelter from Alabama after a tornado destroyed the shelter he was living in. As one of the few surviving dogs from the storm, he has been through a lot and is more than ready to find his forever home!

If you are looking for a sweet boy that will always be grateful for the love you give him, look no further than Roland!

name: Shilo
description:
Shilo is a 2-year-old Boxer mix that loves belly rubs and cuddling on the couch. She is very sweet and does fine with other dogs, although she gets a little bit jealous when the attention is not on her. 

She was transferred to our shelter from Alabama after her shelter was destroyed by a tornado. As one of the few surviving dogs, she has been through a lot and is more than ready to find her loving forever home! 

If you are looking for an affectionate dog who will always be grateful for the love you give her, look no further than Shilo!

name: Rose
description:
Meet Rose! She is a 2 1/2 year old Boxer mix. Rose came to our rescue from Alabama after her owner surrendered her pregnant and heartworm positive. Roseâs puppies have all found their forever homes and now that Rose has gone through her heartworm treatment it is her turn to find her forever home and get the love she deserves! 

Rose is house trained, crate trained, working on leash training. She loves to sleep next to you and cuddle. She loves to play and plays well with other dogs. She is not a fan of cats and would do well with kids. She is spayed, microchipped, and UTD on age appropriate vaccines.

Rose is available for adoption through Pet Tales Rescue in Grand Rapids, MI. Please go to www.pettalesrescue.com and fill out an application. Her adoption fee is $235 plus $15 for the microchip for a total of $250 payable by cash or card through the rescue's website.

* Pet Tales Rescue does not have a physical shelter location as all of our pets are in foster homes. To meet Rose or one of our other fosters, you will need to fill out an application. After your application is reviewed, one of our volunteers will contact you to set up a time to meet her. Thank you for adopting, not shopping!

name: Walker
description:
Meet Walker!  Walker is a one year old Shepherd Mix who weighs about 70 lbs. He came all the way from an Alabama shelter on a rescue transport to find his forever home here in Michigan! He is very friendly once he gets to know you. He is looking for someone who just wants a buddy by their side, but will take the time to gain his trust. Also...loves to play in water, especially sprinklers - video available upon request!  He is great with his foster family's other dogs, mildly interested in their chickens, goats and horses. Not sure about cats.

Walker will need a fenced in yard and an adult family or one with older children. His new owner must be patient with him, as Walker has a very strong \"flight\" response when scared but does OK when you slowly introduce him to new things. Walker does well on a leash, but is very scared of getting into cars. He is housetrained, does well in his crate. Up to date on all vaccinations, microchipped and neutered. 

Walker is available for adoption through Pet Tales Rescue in Grand Rapids, MI. Please go to www.pettalesrescue.com and fill out an application. His adoption fee is $235 plus $15 for the microchip for a total of $250 payable by cash or card through the rescue's website.

* Pet Tales Rescue does not have a physical shelter location as all of our pets are in foster homes. To meet Walker or one of our other fosters, you will need to fill out an application. After your application is reviewed, one of our volunteers will contact you to set up a time to meet him. Thank you for adopting, not shopping!

name: Baxter
description: You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Baxter is a very sweet boy that came from Alabama. Once he arrived we found out he was heartworm positive. He has been undergoing treatment and will receive at least 1 more injection prior to being available for adoption. He is house trained, crate trained, and he is a little bit of a puller on the leash. His excitement for other dogs can come off as aggression, however, once the proper introductions, he loves them. Baxter should not be around cats... as they are looked at as food! If you are interested in Baxter, please fill out an application on our website mattysheartandsoulanimalrescue.rescuegroups.org. Please also be mindful that we will not let him be adopted until at least one month after his last injection.

description:
IN NEED OF LOCAL FOSTER OR ADOPTER/ AVAILABLE FOR FOSTER TO ADOPT FOR LOCAL ADOPTERS

https://youtu.be/lXq1JFX5JbU

Chevy is approx. 5 years old (approx. DOB 1-12-14), male, 38 lbs., vetted, is or will be neutered, and micro-chipped. Chevy is a very
sweet southern boy from Alabama! He gets along with all dogs he has come across, loves to play, talks to you (if you make a siren noise he will sing), LOVES to cuddle on your lap, loves to sleep with you, and is just generally happy all the way around! He is potty trained, and exhibits a very high prey drive (so no cats, bunnies, chickens, etc. and kids please). Stay tuned for more information as Chevy is a new rescue!

If you are interested in fostering or adopting Chevy please fill out an Application at www.Passion-4-Paws.org (please make sure you have the Vermont site) thanks!

Check out his Facebook page (please \"Like\" us while you are there): https://tinyurl.com/y3hvcb25

Please note Fosters have 1st option of Adoption.

Disclosure:

Breed labels are often incorrect: we rarely know the genetic lineage of the dogs we rescue. Many shelters and rescues specify breeds based on appearance; however, research has shown that less than 2% of a dog's DNA determines appearance!

Passion 4 Paws does not practice the use of labels pertaining to compatibility with others or dog breed. Labels such as \"dog friendly\" and \"child friendly\" should be used with caution as they often over-simplify the personalities and behavior of dogs.

name: Tyson
description:
Tyson the Boxer might seem ruff and tuff but he is as sweet as can be!  
Weighing in at 60 lbs. this 2-3 year old boy from Alabama is a lover not a fighter and is excellent with other dogs.

name: BEAUTIFUL BROWNIE
description:
This beauty is called Beautiful Brownie affectionately by her rescue foster. She is beautiful inside and out. At the age of 9-10 years old she weighs 38 pounds and is a Catahoula mix girl who exudes a calm spirit of love and desire to be your everything in life. She has beautiful bi-colored eyes with a little white spot on her right eye and she is ready to give you a smile at the drop of a hat when you speak to affectionately to her. Brownie is easy on a leash, housebroken, gentle and kind. She would make a great companion for a someone like a retired couple or single person who wants to be a beloved person in a dog's life. Brownie was saved from a place in Alabama where they were going to shoot her for killing a few chickens that were roaming free; a common thing in the dog world to chase those feathery little things. She is getting a dental and full vetting and heartworm treatment. This girl would have died for sure had she stayed with this family who did nothing for her except food and water. Please consider making Brownie's senior years her best ones yet.

ADOPTION FEE REQUIRED. Contact ccrtennessee@gmail.com.

name: Aria
description:
Aria is available for foster or adoption, and we are actively seeking a foster or adopter home in Florida so she can go on transport, she is currently located in Alabama. We are a foster-based rescue and always looking for foster families. Aria is 3-4 years, 67 lbs and good with other dogs. She is not over-the-top in energy and will make someone a nice companion. She is a happy girl who loves children. She came into the rescue with her puppies who have all been adopted, now it's her turn! One of her puppies was DNA tested, and it would appear that Aria is a German Shepherd mix.
She loves car rides and loves attention. She loves to give you kisses. She's been around a cat at a vet and didn't seem to pay much attention to it at all so there's a good chance she'll be okay with kitty friends. Aria would make someone a loving companion as she isn't a barker or trouble maker!
Aria is spayed, up-to-date on vaccines and preventives, microchipped and heartworm-free.
We are a foster-based rescue organization with foster homes throughout the state of Florida. We predominantly save dogs from municipal shelters throughout the Southeastern U.S. Our rescue dogs live in foster homes - there is no central facility. description:

name: Faith
description:
Hello, My name is Faith. I am an energetic, talkative, funny Siberian Husky girl looking for my forever home.  I am looking for a home that has experience in huskies, that is very energetic and that will keep up with my training.

My story:

I was brought here from Animal control down by Detroit MI. I was adopted once from there but brought back due to some pretty sever issues that landed me on what is called the Euthanization list. I am not sure what that means, all I know is that I have heard that it  isn't a good thing. The person at animal control along with another individual did not feel I should be euthanized. They found this lady at the rescue I am at now, and the rest is history.
       When I arrived here, I had absolutely NO training.  I also had the \"MINE\" complex, meaning what is mine is mine, what is yours is mine and I owned everything. I certainly felt I did not need to do anything that was asked of me.  I knew a few basic commands but I wouldnt do them unless there was something in it for me. Yes, some of this is husky behavior, however, mine was to the extreme. Should anyone have tried to take something from me that I felt was mine ( and everything was mine) I would behave badly and sometimes bite them. HOWEVER,
       After a year of rehabilitation, leadership, training and desensitization with things I am a very well rounded girl. I know my basic commands such as, sit, wait, leave it, down, off, stay, bring it and shake. My foster mommy said I never had any direction in my life or leadership causing me to  act out badly and develop the \"mine\" complex to the extreme. 
        My foster mommy can now place her hand into my food dish with food and I will eat around her hand ( I also had issues with being possessive over my food while in the dish). She can safely take things out of my mouth like toys, bones and anything else I decide to put into it that she needs to fish out (yup, now that  is my NORMAL husky behavior showing up). She has desensitized, me from everything she can think of, given me direction, training and leadership. 
        I am playful, I love to play fetch although, there are times when the bring the toy back consists of me bringing the toy to my foster mom , me waiting for her to get close and taking off with the toy. Its a fun game!
        I like to play with other dogs but I can be overbearing and dominant with some dogs. I do best with other male dogs but I can do well  with other females with proper introductions. NO CATS or small animals (chickens etc)  however,  DO have a very high prey drive! 
        I like to go for car rides, and I ride very well in a vehicle . I walk well on the leash now with minimal corrections unless I see something that gets me really excited. I know my basic commands such as sit, stay, down, off, leave it, shake and bring it (still working on that!). I also am a talker and most of the time I never shut up! 
        If you would like to learn even more about me please contact my foster mommy through this site! Im sure she will talk forever about me!  

You can also apply to meet me at www.fewstepsfromhome.com and follow the link to the meet and greet/pre-adoption application.

Hope to meet you soon! oh, bring treats! Im VERY treat motivated!! 

PS. no young kids please

name: Sophia Loren
description: Sophia Loren is a wonderfully sweet, calm and gentle senior lady. She enjoys the company of people and loves going for strolls around the Sanctuary. She has excellent leash manners, though she doesn't like to hurry. Although she was born in 2008, Sophia has a playful side, which her caregivers discovered when she met a young puppy who became her roommate. Sophia followed her around the yard and wanted to play, which was very sweet to see. She has been considerate to all the other dogs she's met at the Sanctuary and has passed a cat test here. Sophia came to Best Friends from a shelter in Arizona. She would do well in a quiet, low-key home. She'll be the perfect companion to keep you company while watching TV, reading a book or simply snuggling on the couch.

name: Pixie
description: Pixie is a very vivacious shepherd mix who is just as beautiful on the outside as she is on the inside. She loves taking long walks, getting belly rubs and playing in the water. Although she can be picky about her doggie friends and bossy with other dogs at times, she loves playing with them once she's been introduced properly and she gets to know them. Pixie tends to guard food, so precautions must be taken when feeding her or giving her treats. She can be a bit nervous when new people try to handle her too much, but she loves playing with people she knows. Pixie was born in 2014 and came to Best Friends from a rescue organization in Arizona. She would be a great addition to an active home.

name: Pebbles
description: Pebbles may be a little shy and fearful with strangers, but given time to warm up to new people she will let her big personality loose. She loves to chase and herd her doggie roommates around, she always has something to talk about and she has fun doing her own thing. She's also striking to look at with her white coat and extra-large ears. Born in 2014, Pebbles came to Best Friends from a humane society in Arizona. Her caregivers in Dogtown are hand feeding her to help her build trust with people. She would do best with a person or family who can be patient and help her blossom into a dog who will enjoy fun activities like car rides and long walks. Pebbles has a generous sponsor who will pay her adoption fee.

name: Wyatt
description: When Wyatt arrived at the Sanctuary from a rescue organization in Arizona, he was feral. He didn't know how to walk on leash, and he was terrified of everyone and everything. Now, Wyatt is still shy and fearful, and is still considered a flight risk. But with the right doggie friend by his side and a patient person to guide him, he really comes out of his shell. He walks on leash nicely now and loves going for walks with his doggie roommate. He just recently learned that the car is not such a scary thing. He will get in the car and go for short rides, but Dogtown caregivers and trainers are still working on getting him to be more comfortable in the car. When he gets comfortable enough around people, he will show his huge and goofy personality. Wyatt was born in 2014. He needs a home with a person or family who will give him a chance, someone who will show him patience and allow him time to get used to a new environment. Wyatt would also do best in a home with a confident dog who can show him that the world is not so scary. He does seem to prefer female dogs over other males. Because Wyatt can jump fences, he needs a home with a secure yard so he does not try to flee out of fear. Wyatt is already crate trained and is still working on his car skills. He has even been learning to do agility with his roommate. Sailing over agility obstacles he was once afraid of has really helped to boost his confidence. Wyatt has lots of potential. Will you be the one who helps him unleash it?

name: CB
description: CB loves everyone, but she tends to be a bit exuberant with both people and dogs. She has a great heart and the best intentions, but her manners could use some work. Whether you're an old friend or it's your first introduction, CB tends to resort to jumping and grabbing when she gets excited. Though her trainers are working with her on this, she will need a home where her training is kept consistent. CB can be a very sweet girl when she's calm and collected. She loves belly rubs and playing with toys. She can also be great with other dogs as long as they can tolerate her rough play style. Born in 2010, she's perfectly healthy. She came to Best Friends from a rescue in Arizona who just couldn't find the right match. Could you be the right match for her?

name: Fred
description: Fred's a guy who likes to take it slow. It takes time for him to form relationships with people and to give his trust. He used to struggle with meeting and bonding with people but has made remarkable progress since coming to the Sanctuary. Once you've earned Fred's trust, the rewards are great. Deep down, he's a very gentle, loving and affectionate dog. He's also extremely smart and responds well to training that requires him to think. Fred was born in 2011 and came from a rescue in Arizona that was closing. He was diagnosed with a spinal condition and takes some medication to help him feel comfortable. Because he's still a bit insecure and anxious, he'll need to find a home with someone who can continue to help him build his confidence, keep up his training and guide him through successful introductions with both people and other dogs. But Fred promises he's worth it. Fred has a generous sponsor who has offered to pay for his adoption fee.

name: Tucker
description:
Tucker is in a foster home with his sister Leia. There are also cats in their foster home for any adopters that do have a kitty, they are already introduced!

Tucker came with the litter of 3mo olds that were pulled by us from a more remote shelter in Arizona. He came with 18 other huskies that were all saved from the same neglectful home. Our rescue was able to pull 12 of them. All of the dogs in this litter do great with other dogs, but some are a little more skittish with people at first. They seem to warm up and become very snuggly and loving for the most part, but definitely would benefit from longterm socialization work.

According to his foster, Tucker is completely potty trained in their home (new changes like a home move can sometimes back this process up a little, so as with all puppies, some patience may be required). The fosters are working on crate-training still, as well as taking treats more gently â Tucker has been showing some good progress with this. Tucker is the more snuggly, loving dog of the two puppies in the foster home. He also loves to play with other dogs!

Fill out an application (note our response time may be 1-2week as we consider applicants and the puppies still need a couple weeks to be ready for their forever homes): http://azhuskyrescue.com/adoption-application/

name: Gunner
description:
Gunner came with the litter of 3mo olds that were pulled by us from a more remote shelter in Arizona. He came with 18 other huskies that were all saved from the same neglectful home. Our rescue was able to pull 12 of them. All of the dogs in this litter do great with other dogs, but some are a little more skittish with people at first. They seem to warm up and become very snuggly and loving for the most part, but definitely would benefit from longterm socialization work.

Gunner is a very playful active little guy. He is always ready to go anywhere and just loves being around people and other dogs. So far gunner has enjoyed camping, hiking, 4wheeling and nightly walks with his foster brothers. Gunner has been great in the crate while we are at work. Gunner will get into anything so you will need to keep your eyes on him. He seems to have a stubborn personality so not getting him to chew on things or potty training has been rough but he seems to be getting better. This little guy needs someone who loves being active and loves being on the go. He seems to love kids and especially other dogs.

Fill out an application (note our response time may be 1-2week as we consider applicants and the puppies still need a couple weeks to be ready for their forever homes): http://azhuskyrescue.com/adoption-application/

name: Roman
description: âRomanâ is a 3-4y old MN Rottweiler Mix that is still looking for his forever home. He is a giant goofball and enjoys destroying squeaky toys and playing with blankets. He likes to go on walks or going to the park but is also okay with laying around the house. Roman can be very pushy with other dogs so weâre recommending he goes as the only dog in the home. He takes a little longer to warm up to men than women but is a total love bug once he gets to know you. Roman came from a pretty rough situation, where he was kept in a kennel much too small for him, outside in the Arizona heat for almost two years. He came to me underweight and with scars around his eyes, ears and nose from all the fly bites. Because of this we are looking for a home that has Rottweiler experience. Roman is kennel trained, house trained and formally trained in obedience. He knows how to walk nicely on a leash, sit and stay, lay down and stay, how to find the heel position and come when called. He comes with three free handling sessions to the new owners to help his transition to his new home go as smoothly as possible. Please donât hesitate to ask any questions. You can fill out an application at http://www.rottenrottie.com under the forms tab.

name: Floyd
description:
Floyd is back and looking for his forever home again!
He needs a home with another dog and someone who will be dedicated to teaching him the ways of life. He really looks for the direction of other dogs. In his previous home he was the only dog and was around 2 small children. He felt he needed to be the boss in the situation and just couldn't learn how to \"dog\".

Now that he is back with us and being fostered with other dogs he has a new outlook on life and is quickly learning what his role in life is. He is a fantastic dog who adores people and other dogs. He thinks kitties would be tasty though. He is a terrier mix that originally came from Arizona with his siblings. Another local shelter here brought them up and then they fell I'll with Parvo and that shelter was going to euthanize. We stepped up to take them when they were 10 weeks old. name: Abe
description:
Big and handsome, friendly and well behaved -- Abe has it all! Heâs about 3.5 years old and a bit hefty at his current food-loving 86 pounds. Abe comes to us from a rescue partner in Arkansas who scooped him up as a shelter stray in the nick of time. 

Abe has been soaking up a lot of loving and giving loads in return in his foster homes both in Arkansas and now here with us.  Heâs house trained, crate trained, knows some basic commands and is pretty good on leash walks.  Abe gets along well with other dogs, but itâs people he loves the most.  By your side is his favorite place.  His attitude towards cats?  âMeh, kinda boring,â he wags.

Abe made his home with his rescuer in Arkansas while he was being treated for heartworms, an issue seen with many dogs in that part of the country.  âOnce I got the ok from the vet that Iâd recovered from my treatment, I was first in line to hop on the transport van to Colorado . . . and here I am!â woofs our boy.  To keep him healthy, Abeâs family needs to commit to having him on heartworm preventative year round.  Helping him lose a few pounds would be welcome, too!

A pleasantly active big handsome love who loves being loved on, Abe woofs: âCome on over real soon, bring cookies, and letâs get acquainted. I know weâre gonna be BFFâs in no time and then weâll head home together forever!â

name: Emma PUPPY
description:
Miss Emma is absolutely too cute for words, but weâll do our best!  Petite and a â10â on the Adorable Scale, sheâs about six months old and oh so easy to scoop up and cuddle at her current 25 pounds.  We think this little Lab mix puppy with some hints of brown brindle on her legs will be a smaller girl when sheâs all grown up.  This baby girl comes to us as a stray from Arkansas.

Miss Emma is super friendly, curious about life around her, very playful and loves toys.  Always ready to give you puppy kisses, she likes to cuddle and curl up into a tiny ball next to you on the sofa.  Our little girl knows sit, takes treats nicely and is very eager to please.  As you would expect, house training and crate training are works in process.  She plays well with other dogs but remember, sheâs full of good-natured puppy exuberance some oldsters may not appreciate!
 
 Puppies, while adorable, are not for everyone.  Think carefully if your lifestyle has room for the extraordinary responsibility of raising a puppy.  Do you truly have time for the daily nurturing and constant supervision required?  Do you mind piddles on your floor, chewing on your things and, before you know it, a âteenage puppyâ with ideas of her own?  The proper handling and socialization of a puppy are critical to their development into a well-adjusted adult.  As Emma grows she will require your steady, kind leadership, commitment to his training and rely on you for her extensive daily exercise needs.
  
If you would like Emma, a little âdog to beâ, to consider your application, please tell us why your home would be suitable for a puppy in the comments section of your application
. 
Emma will only be placed in a home with:  (1) adults or older children who can treat a dog with kindness and respect and (2) one that clearly has the dedication and substantial time throughout the day to devote to raising a puppy to responsible adulthood.

In addition to the adoption fee, there is a required $200 spay deposit refundable upon proof of spay.

Interested in a specific dog, please fill out an application if you are interested in a dog. The number of individual inquiries is overwhelming and we are finding it difficult to respond to each one. We cannot guarantee you will receive a timely response.
 
Paws New England is a rescue, not a shelter, and as such we do not have our dogs housed in one location - they are in foster homes both in New England and in our southern foster homes. If you're interested in a specific dog, please complete a short online application and you will receive a reply within 48 hours so you can ask questions.

Donations for our young, healthy puppies and dogs support their fellow canines of advanced age or suffering from injuries and abuse whose donations are reduced but whose veterinary costs are typically much higher. We appreciate your understanding that your dog will help others in need.

All known information about the animal is listed above. We do our best to give accurate information, but most of our dogs are rescues and do not come with a known history.

Paws New England abides by the dog importation regulations set forth in the states of MA, CT, NH and RI.

name: Goose (VA)
description:
SILLY GOOSE! 
Goose is a handsome and cuddly 1 year old pointer mix (we think with Labrador Retriever), originally from Arkansas. He, along with his mother and his siblings were living outside an abandoned home, and needed rescue quickly to keep them safe. We are not certain who his dad was, but because of his looks, his dad sure was a handsome gent!
Goose is very sweet, and loves to give full body hugs. Goose is good with dog and cats, and is a total lovebug. He is working on his leash manners, as he is a little uncertain with loud city noises. Goosey is goofy and sweet, snuggly and handsome.
Some notes from his foster home:
Goose is a typical young dog who needs exercise and stimulation.  He is also a big boy (around 75 lbs) and he would do best with another dog (or 2!) who is willing to run and play with him in the yard to burn off some energy.  He is willing to entertain himself (see the video here: Goose Entertains Himself with Gymnastics! ).  He is fascinated with birds and butterflies, and squirrels are possibly the most exciting thing ever!
Perhaps due to his time abandoned, he does show some resource guarding.  He eats in his crate at his foster home, and high-value treats like knucklebones need to be closely monitored with other dogs around.  He freely exchanges anything he has for a cookie with his foster parents.  He is very food motivated and knows sit and down, but his recall is still a work in progress.  His leash walking is improving, but if he sees a squirrel, all bets are off!

If you are interested in fostering for us, please complete a PRO Volunteer Form: http://www.pointerrescue.org/volunteer.html

name: Gracie
description:
Hi there, they call me Grace. Or Gracie Lee. Or Pretty Girl. Or Big Head. Or Smooch! I have lots of nicknames because my foster mom really, really loves me. I'm a 60# Black Mouth Cur. I originally came from Arkansas and I'm 2 years old.
    I love to run! When I get the zoomies in the yard, I run figure eights around the trees and it makes my mom laugh every time. I also love other dogs and would really like to have a brother or sister.
    Mom says I'm very good at entertaining myself. Bones are my favorite, but I like chew toys, ropes and large outside fetch toys. Inside, I love to unstuff all the little toys, then watch mom stuff it back in, so I can rip it up again. Great fun! Ha ha!
    When mom has to be away, I run right in my kennel and wait for her to come back. When she does, I do my happy dance! I can kennel at night also, but mom lets me sleep in her bed, where I snuggle under the covers and don't move until she gets up. I like to be toasty warm! I'm also an experienced couch potato, mom gives me 5 stars.
    I had a very difficult start to life. I was not treated kindly and not socialized at all with people or animals. I have since learned a lot about dogs but have not met cats. I am still working on people skills. Because of the way I was treated in the past, I'm scared of people I don't know and I bark at them. I can look scary, but I'm really just unsure. Once I get to know someone, I practically drown them in kisses. I'm just slow to trust, and I get a little nervous in new situations, but I have come so, so far already and I really want to like everybody. I'm smart too. I know around 25 commands and words.
    If you are the kind of person who has the love and patience to continue helping me with my social skills, I'll walk, run, play as often as you like, chill when you want to chill, and I'll love you forever.
 No cats, no young kids.
\"Courtesy posting\

name: Honor
description:
This lovely little girl is 3-4 years old and 38lbs. She came to us from Arkansas where she was found nearly starved and very sick with heartworm. She has since gained weight and recovered, and recently made the journey to Rochester to find her forever home! She is full of love, kisses, and snuggles, and would love a nice family to call her own.

Honor likes to play, but she likes to snuggle even more. She would prefer to be a lap dog and potato on the couch most of the day. She is not super active but she loves sunbathing and relaxing outside. She gets along well with other dogs and wouldn't mind a playmate, so long as they don't play too rough and respect her space when she's tired. No cats for this girl!

Honor is crate-trained and potty trained. She has not had any accidents at her foster home and has been fine being left for a regular workday, but her medication makes her need to go potty a bit more frequently than most dogs, so a family who works shorter shifts or is available to let her out for a potty break mid-day would be ideal for her.

She can be nervous around her food, so she prefers to eat alone in her crate. She is fine taking treats, even with other dogs, as long as she understands clearly who each piece is meant for. As soon as she sees dinner coming she runs to her crate and dances while she waits.

Honor is a gem of a dog and will make someone very happy. Her foster parents would be keeping her if she didn't chase their cats! They say she is wonderful, affectionate, just an all-around good girl. If you would like to meet her, please submit the adoption application at K9Orphans.org !!

name: Maisy
description:
Maisy is not technically a Circle of Hope dog.  She is what we refer to as a \"courtesy post.\"  Volunteers with our group are sometimes contacted by friends or family who need help re-homing a dog.   That is what is going on with Maisy.  She is currently living with a family in upstate NY who is friends with a long time volunteer of Circle of Hope.  

This family adopted Maisy from a rescue group in Arkansas just over ago  when she was 10 weeks old.  This family has young children and the bottom line is that she is not a good fit with them and we will not place her in a home with them. The energy level and unpredictable activities of little kids can get Maisy nervous and we aren't sure we can trust her with that.  We won't describe her as aggressive, and the best trainer in our area agrees and has said several times that she is not an aggressive dog.   She is great with teenagers and adults and loves to meet them all the time.  She also seems to love to play with other dogs. The doggie day camp she goes to says she never has had any issues.  She is energetic and brings that energy to doggie games, so maybe a home with an older dog would not be a good fit.  She also would not be good in a home with cats.

Maisy is very smart, active and playful.  She would love a home with lots of activity and maybe even where she could be taught how to do a job on a farm.  She is looking for frequent engagement.  She isn't a dog who likes to hang out alone.  When left alone for a long period of time she gets nervous and bored. She really likes a routine and adult companionship that is task oriented.   She loves to play in the snow, shallow water (although not really a swimmer), tug of war and chase balls.  She is great in the car and always up for walks, jogs and hikes.  She is good on a leash, is crate trained, house broken and up to date with all of her vet care.  She is truly loved by this family she has been with, but they know their home is not the best match for her due to their young children.  If you think you have what Masiy needs and could give her that perfect home please let us know.  All interested adopters please email Cari at carilifluke@gmail.com.  I will send you an application to fill out once I hear from you.

name: Griffin
description: Hi my name is Griffin. I am a 9 month old shepherd mix. I am from Arkansas, on my journey to Wisconsin to meet my foster parents I did not know what to expect. When I got here I was extremely scared and did not know what was going to happen to me but when I got here, I knew that my life was going to change forever. My fosters have been super amazing for me and gave me all the time I needed to adjust to life outside the kennel. I am learning my name, learning how to sit, lay down and come when I'm called. I'm kennel trained and I am mostly potty trained. I love to cuddle and to be close to the people that I depend on. I enjoy playing with dogs of all kinds and being around children. Before coming to my foster family I did not know what a bed was and it scared me and now I can't wait for my fosters to get home so I can cuddle with them. I get a little bit nervous around men and and get a little bit nervous when somebody goes into pet me too quickly or turns around too quickly when I am near, but it is just from the abuse that I experienced before coming to Wisconsin. I am learning every day that I am able to trust humans and the people that surround me and that not everybody is out to hurt me. I would love to have a home preferably with a family or a couple with another dog in the home. I am a super lovable, happy and eager to learn puppy. I even like horses and cows. I have a great recall once I am bonded to you. Did I mention I love other dogs and want a home with another dog? Although I can be nervous please know I don't have a mean bone in my body and just need time to learn that you wont hurt me like the one person did.

Britt is a 1 year old, black and tan, natural eared female Doberman with a docked tail. She is spayed, up to date on vaccinations, microchipped, and negative for heartworms and intestinal parasites.

Poor Britt came to GDR from a shelter south of Atlanta where she had been taken in along with 2 other Dobermans as a neglect case. Luckily she has an amazing and patient foster who slowly eased her into being an inside dog little by little. Now Britt, while still shy, is getting used to indoor luxuries. She loves to play with her foster brother and sister, exploring the yard and chasing each other. She has enjoyed several toys that they've given her and has figured out how to really play but alsoappreciates her quiet time indoors. She is potty trained, but due to her skittish nature has not been introduced to a crate as she has not needed one. She has done well with the other dogs in the home, but will not be adopted to a home with kids or small animals. She has done well with the infant in the home, but because her background is unknown and interactions have been limited, we are not comfotable adopting her to a home with small kids. The best home for Britt would be a quiet home that wants a companion that is playful, but also happy to chill in the house.

If you are interested in adopting Britt, you csn complete an adoption application here on our website.

name: Jazzy
description:
Meet Jazzy!! Jazzy's shelter name was Jazz, and the handlers liked the name, so they decided to keep it, but make it just a little â¦ well â¦ jazzier!! So Jazzy it is! Jazzy had been a shelter dog more than once - that's just so sad. She was owned by someone who developed health problems and couldn't care for her, so she was relinquished to the shelter. She was adopted again, and ... not long after that, came back in much worse condition than she left. She was tethered in the second owner's front yard, she had significant hair loss, and was underweight - the note was made that it appeared as though she had not eaten in several days. She was treated for her skin condition, and she gained some weight. She developed an upper respiratory infection and was treated, and she gained some weight. She was spayed and recovered, and gained some weight. All in all, this not-so-little girl gained 23 pounds at the shelter, and is more than slightly rubenesque!! We think she was eating her food, and as much of everyone else's food as she could - poor thing probably just couldn't get past feeling so very hungry!  

  We were drawn to her sunny disposition, so we temperament tested her, and we were thrilled when she passed!! After 185 days in the shelter, she was finally going to get to leave!! This chubby girl (we will work on her weight!!) is a sharpei / pit mix, with a golden brown coat, and smiling face. She does love so very much to give kisses - and we have the pictures to prove it!! She is extremely playful, and loves to engage in toy games with her people.

 Want to help us make sure that the rest of Jazzy's days are full of fun, without any chains or missed meals? Put your application in today - www.caninecellmates.org!

  Jazzy is located in Atlanta, GA and is available for adoption immediately. She will be able to go to her forever home after graduation from the Canine CellMates program. Jazzy is spayed, microchipped and up to date on all her shots. Canine CellMates dogs are trained in items similar to the Canine Good Citizen (CGC) test. They learn basic obedience and commands such as sit, down, stay, go to place, and leave it. They are also crate trained. If you are interested in adopting Jazzy, please fill out an adoption application at www.caninecellmates.org. or email adopt@caninecellmates.org for more information.

name: Cola
description:
Are you looking for the perfect new addition to your family? Well, then look no further than Cola herself. Cola is a 1.5-year-old Black Labrador Retriever mix, fully grown at about 47 pounds. She was rescued from Lyons, Georgia. She is known in her foster home as the \"ready-made-perfect-angel\". Cola is put simply - as wonderful as they come. She follows her foster mom like a shadow and is super obedient and smart. She would love a family with children to play with her. When Cola gets excited her whole body swings as she wiggles with joy - it is quite the site! She has a very happy tail as well. Cola walks very well on a leash, is crate trained, and also primarily housebroken. She gets along very well with other dogs and cats too. Cola is a happy, social, loving dog who simply cannot wait to find her people!

Cola is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

Home for Good Dog Rescue (HFGDR) is a 100 percent foster-based rescue located in Summit with offices in Berkeley Heights, NJ. All of our dogs live in loving local foster homes until they find forever families of their own. Our fosters begin basic training, housebreaking, and leash walking skills to help pair you with the perfect pup for life!

We update Petfinder and our website multiple times daily, so if a dog is available on Petfinder and our website they are still available for adoption. We process all our applications in the order we receive them, and for that reason sometimes the dog or dogs in whom you are interested in may be adopted before your own processing concludes.

In order to apply for adoption and set up an individual meet and greet with one of our dogs, please visit us at www.HomeforGoodDogs.org.

Find us on Facebook at www.facebook.com/HomeForGoodDogRescue.

name: Daisy
description:
Meet sweet, sweet, Daisy. This poor girl was rescued from Lyons, Georgia. It was clear to see that Daisy had suffered through some tough times prior to being rescued by Home for Good. At first, she was wary of new humans, taking her time to warm up. It is evident that she had never felt the gentle hand of a human in her lifetime. However, day by day, Daisy has been coming out of her shell. She thrives in the company of other dogs and would truly love a sibling in her forever home. Daisy has the sweetest, most gentle temperament and loves to receive affection. She is 1 years old and fully grown at about 46 pounds. She is a Cattle Dog/Lab mix. She is crate trained and learning the ropes of leash training. She simply needs a patient forever home to shower her with all the love and affection she so truly deserves!

Daisy is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

name: Hudson
description:

His foster mom says he is a special boy who deserves only the best home.

name: Quest
description:

He was given to animal control.  They say no one wants you when your old and gray and this was the case with Quest.  They said he would never be adopted and that he was too old to even try.  Well, Home For Good saw more than life in this soul.  His Quest to find a forever family begins.  If you are seeking a gentle soul, who is loyal, lovable and craves attention then Quest is your man.  He is calm and walks great on a leash.

Quest is up to date with all vaccinations, neutered and microchipped.

She still has a lot of life in her and a lot of love to give.  Luna LOVES water, she is a great swimmer and would be a great passenger on a boat.  If you love the water, Luna is your girl. Luna is a smart girl who is very treat motivated and easy to train.  She will lay down in her pool...then come to you for a treat before she goes inside.

name: Ella
description:
This is the story of the E Litter. Their mother, Coco, was found alone, abandoned in Barnwell, South Carolina. It was clear that she had been nursing quite recently however, at the time, none of her puppies had been claimed nor found. A week after rescuing Coco, Home for Good Dog Rescue got a call stating that Coco's puppies, now known as the E Litter, had been found. They were found by a good samaritan in the insulation of a trailer, all malnourished and dehydrated. They are all very very lucky to be alive. Once this litter arrived at Home for Good's Aiken, SC property, they receive all the attention, love, and care, they so truly needed. Within no time, these pups were all nursed back to a clean bill of health and are now ready to find the forever homes they so truly deserve!

They are now about 2 months old, 10 pounds each and the cutest Labrador Retriever/Hound mixes. They are a very playful and outgoing bunch despite their rough start to life - it is clear that they are all so happy to be given a second chance! These pups love other dogs, cats, and children. They would make perfect family companions. In their foster homes, they have begun to work on their crate, leash, and house training. Now, all they need are forever families to call their own.

Ella is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

name: Dale
description:
Name: Dale
Breed: Shepherd/Hound/Lab Mix
Age: 6 years old (As of August 2019)
Good With Dogs: Yes. Dale enjoys playing with and socializing with female dogs and happy, submissive dogs. He is a lady's man.
Good With Cats: Yes
Good With Children: Yes
Heartworm Status: Negative

Dale is a very sweet boy who came from an animal neglect case out of Bibb County. Even though he had a rough start at life, he has a lot of love to give and hasn't let his past define him. He does well with some dogs, and we would say he's selective, but we always require other companions to meet dogs prior to adoption to ensure it is a great match for everyone. He especially loves likes female dogs and submissive dogs that appreciate his status as being his own man.

 He does well with everyone, including small children. He's a very intelligent boy. He thinks he is macho when he is in an environment where he knows what to expect, but with new situations - like the first time he met nail clippers, he turned into a squeaky little mouse in about ten seconds. He gains confidence quickly in new places, and likes to go for walks in his harness. He's stubborn and good natured. Dale is a proud, dapper guy that likes to patrol his grounds, go for walks, and get his back scratched. He is soft like a teddy bear. He is the perfect model who doesn't mind being dressed at all!

name: Ralph
description: Ralph is a very handsome Dogo Argentino/Pit bull terrier mix who would love to be your new best friend.Shy and fearful at first, and excited once he knows you, Ralph is learning how to greet people appropriately. In fact, he came to Best Friends from a rescue group in Boise, Idaho because he needed to work on his training. He's a big boy, so learning manners, like not jumping up on people, is especially important.Ralph loves fluffy toys (though he tends to de-fluff them in a hurry). He also loves getting affection from people he knows, and running in the park. Ralph is not good with cats. He also does not do well with other dogs, so he would be best in a home without them.Ralph may be a very large and powerful boy, but he is also very sweet. He needs someone who can handle him and give him the attention and love he deserves. All he's looking for is one special person or family who will give him a chance.Ralph is part of our Single Pets* program! That means that he is eligible for a free flight home and waived adoption fee!*Single pets do best as the only dog or cat in the home.

description:

description: Brew is in need of a medical foster, she is currently located in Bradenton, FL (Manatee County). Brew is an English Bulldog we saved from a high kill shelter in Tampa. She is 8 years old and in a neglected state. She has a medical history of arthritis spondylosis, she is heartworm positive and required a removal of a blueberry sized mammary node during spay. She is underweight at 35 pounds and will require 3 meals a day. She is quiet,sleeps a lot and the only issue we have seen is some guarding of her xpen area when other dogs nose around. She's fine with other dogs but offers no interactions and turns her head away. Once we have her tuned up she will be available for adoption or long term fostering through heartworm treatment. If you are interested in Brew and have experience with English Bulldogs please contact us. PUPDATE. Brew has been with us for almost a week. She has seen our vet. Her liver values were abnormal and we have had her on supplements and will retest the 2nd week of Sept. She has gotten more energetic,is eating well, and actually is playing with some of the other dogs. She loves people and absolutely loves being pet. She is actually chasing flies! She is becoming a dog again!! Once we do our vet re-check, she will be available for foster to adopt or medical foster. We are a foster-based rescue organization with foster homes throughout the state of Florida. We predominantly save dogs from municipal shelters throughout the Southeastern U.S. Our rescue dogs live in foster homes - there is no central facility. If interested in meeting one of our wonderful adoptable dogs, please fill out an application at ewenityfarmsbch.com. Information on adoption donation amounts and our process can also be found at this site.

name: Coyotl
description:
Please go to www.peanutsplacerescue.org to fill out the online adoption application and to read the Important information page for fees.   Please like us on Facebook to see current dogs as soon as they arrive.   

#9 on the list is Coyotl. Coyotl is a rare coated xoloitzcuintli. Donât worry if you donât know what that is, most people donât!   Theyâre a very ancient Aztec breed known as xolos (pronounced show low). Usually they are hairless but having hair is not a desirable trait in the breeding world and we rescued six of them from a Breeder in Florida when her building was destroyed in a hurricane.  They were extremely feral when rescued as they only were ever handled by one person if at all.  We had them for many months now working on handling and walking on a leash.  Coyotl is about 6 yrs old and 18lbs and is the tallest of the ones we have.  He is also the shyest with handling.  All are sweet once you get them to relax in your lap.  Coyotl needs a secure fenced yard and a dedicated loving patient owner to bring out his best personality.  Heâs absolutely gorgeous and is good with dogs and cats but doesnât really play with them.  Heâs more of the loner in the bunch. He is very quiet and crate trained.  He is stunning looking and that face just melts your heart.  Please go to www.peanutsplacerescue.org to foster or adopt and read the important information page for fees and text 7046509653 with questions or to say youâve applied.

Please like and follow us on Facebook for updates on their rescue and recovery.

name: Sox
description: This is a courtesy post. If you are interested in rescuing or adopting this dog, please contact Rand by email theellardplace@aol.com. This dog is located in Brent, AL.

name: Riley
description:
Riley is 14 years old, 12 lbs. and is currently located in Cocoa, Brevard County.

Riley was surrendered to rescue by a family member after their grandmother passed away.  Unfortunately we don't have much history on Riley as that was not available.  The family was unable to keep Riley due to an upcoming move and knew financially he needed serious dental care.

Riley did have a dental once he came into rescue and had a whopping 20 teeth pulled and he is a much happier dog now!  Before coming into rescue he ate canned food due to his painful mouth.  He now eats kibble but softened with hot water.  

Riley is a sweet gentleman who meshed well with the foster homes Dachshunds, Great Dane and cats.  He LOVES squeaky toys and snoozing in his bed.  Riley does like to take his toys with him when he goes outside to potty.   Riley does have a playful side and will play with the 1 year old Dachshund in his foster home.  

He can be a little protective over his squeaky toys.  

Riley would likely do okay with other dogs or by himself.  He seems to prefer people over the dogs and is a very low key guy.  He loves to sit on your lap and be petted.

Riley has had some accidents in the house, mostly just overnight - some nights he does not have accidents and some he does.  He is crate trained so crating is an option.

Riley is neutered, up to date on vaccines, heartworm tested negative, on a monthly preventative, microchipped and ready for his new forever family!

If you are interested in adopting Riley, please fill out an adoption application on our website at: http://fldr.org/adopt/adoption-application/. The adoption fee is $150

name: Yancey
description:
Meet Yancey!  She is about 2 years old and we believe her to be sweet lab/ hound and possibly a beagle mix.  We rescued her from a high kill shelter in TN and is now in our adoption center in Brewster waiting for her forever home.  

Yancey is such a smart girl and loves all people, and is an active girl.   She would love to run by your side, go hiking, play fetch in the yard or cuddle up next to you and be perfectly happy.   She loves her treats and toys but is still learning how to share her things so an experienced adopter is preferred.  She would do amazing in a home who can give her exercise and enjoy spending time with her.

If they are listed on Petfinder, they are still available. We do not go on a first come first serve basis, but on best fit for the family and most importantly, the puppy.  We are taking our best guess on breed and size when fully grown, based on the puppy's physical appearance.    

Yancey is up to date on her vaccinations, micro-chipped and spayed.

To apply to foster or adopt Yancey please visit snarrnortheast.org

name: Dutch

Junior is doing great and is the cutest little guy in town! Please consider giving him a loving home so he can forget the miserable basement he was living in. Apply at www.nybullycrew.org to submit an adopt or foster application today
