name: Warren
description: Warren the Chi wants a person to love and a lap to warm. He loves to cuddle and every day you'll see your best self reflected in his eyes. This dog breaks our heart. He wants so desperately to be with \"his\" person. Chi experience preferred. Not sure what he would be like with small children but ideal for singles, seniors, and middle-aged professionals. 11 lbs. Came to 1 Love from an overcrowded city animal control facility. With hours to live, 1 Love saved Warren from the \"Big Sleep\" and now hopes to awaken the urge to adopt in some Chihuahua-loving family.

name: Scarlet
description: Scarlet is about 10 months old. She's a pointer mix or lab/cattle dog mix- we don't know for sure. She was surrendered to a vet office by her family because she was in need of surgery for her eyes - she had entropian which means the eyelids/lashes turn in and irritate the eyes and cause infection. She also was covered in ticks - obviously not well cared for. She had the surgery before she came to us and her eyes got infected - we have treated her for that and will update pictures soon! Scarlet weighs 36 pounds and is super sweet and submissive. Scarlet is ready to find her new family!  If you are interested in adopting from Recycled Doggies, please complete an adoption application through our website:  www.recycleddoggies.org. THAT IS THE FIRST STEP IN OUR PROCESS. Please do not just show up at an adoption event and expect to adopt a dog that day - we need time to review your application ahead of time, which is why we ask that you submit your application ahead of time so you don't miss out on the dog you are hoping to adopt while you wait for your application to be reviewed. Our adoption fee is $195.  All of our dogs are spayed/neutered, up to date on age-appropriate vaccines, dewormed, heartworm tested (if over 9 months of age), and microchipped. We do not adopt outside our area, which we define as two hours drive time from downtown Cincinnati (zip code 45202 - use Google Maps to determine if you are within our area) NO EXCEPTIONS. This is for the safety of our dogs, so that in case an adoption does not work out, we can be sure that we can quickly get our dog back. We do not have a shelter or facility - all of our dogs live in volunteer foster homes. In order to not infringe on any more of the time of our foster families, we introduce our dogs to potential adopters at our weekend adoption events posted on our website - please do not request to meet the dog outside of an adoption event as we are unable to grant the request.  If you have additional questions, please email recycleddoggies@gmail.com.

name: Flo Jo
description: Flo Jo is a Chiweenie (chihuahua/dachshund) mix. Sheâs estimated to be 7-8 years old. She was found as a stray out in the country dragging her hind legs behind her due to some injury or impairment. She has some apparent muscle wasting in her hind end and sores on her legs from dragging herself around. We had it checked out and the xrays showed no significant findings as far as arthritis or fractures (but she does have a bullet in her lumbar area but not believed to be causing any issues at this point) but she had some pain in her back so she was started on gabapentin to try to help. description:

Bailey does not like to meet other dogs when heâs on a leash so walks are not much fun.  Bailey does not particularly like to share special space (like his favorite personâs bed) but he does OK once you let him know the rules. He might snap if another dog steps on him or gets in his space but he usually can figure it out. He had an issue when the grown daughter in his foster family tried to get on the mom's bed where Bailey was and nipped at her so that's another thing to consider.  Bailey really needs a privacy fenced backyard (or no neighbors) so heâs not distracted by neighbors (big/little humans or dogs) who will get him all riled up. And heâs very sensitive to sights and sounds around him that make him nervous and he will bark, so no apartment or condo type situation for him. He had an incident where some noise or movement triggered him and he nipped the leg of a person who was doing nothing other than having a conversation with his foster mom - they couldn't figure out what might have triggered him and Bailey has worked with a trainer who also couldn't identify a trigger or replicate that kind of reaction,. but as a result we know that Bailey doesn't do well in many normal social situations. name: Callie
description:
Callie is a 14 year old Chihuahua whose owner died and whose family couldn't keep her permanently. So she made the trip from Cincinnati to Youngstown where she slid into foster home easily.

This girl weighs about 7 1/2 pounds and is fully vetted. She just had a dental so she's much more pleasant to be around. :)  We're really just learning about her.

She's learning to be her foster mom's \"chair Chi\" and is finding her place in the pack. She's a bit nervous and reserved at first, but once she's used to her situation she is a very friendly, sweet girl. She's good with other small dogs and so-so with cats. She would probably prefer a home without a cat, but once properly introduced to one, she should be OK. 

She is crate trained, but during feeding times is very vocal. During that time, she sounds like a wild animal or bird from a jungle. Right before and after feeding you wouldn't think she was a Chihuahua. Other than that, she's pretty good in a crate.

We're working on house training. She will potty outside, but her potty breaks need to be consistent. She loves her basket and blanket, and loves sleeping (like all seniors do!)

Callie would like a quieter household with her own personal human to love and bond with. She's a good little guard Chi who wants a home that she can protect when called upon. She wants regular feeding (and peanut butter snacks!!!) and chair time so she can feel close to her person.

**Callie is being fostered in Youngstown, OH**

Callie's adoption fee is $250. If she sounds like the dog of your dreams please contact Chihuahua Rescue & Transport and she will pack her toys and love and be there in a wag of her tail.

If you would like more information about adopting this dog, please go to our website(www.chihuahua-rescue.org). All dogs listed are adoptable in the 10 Midwestern states(OH/IN/KY/IL/MN/MI/WI/PA/IA/MO). We do transport! All of our dogs are spread out throughout the Midwest in foster homes.

Please fill out an adoption application at: www.tinyurl.com/CRTMidwestApp

name: TILLIE
description:
PLEASE DO NOT USE THE PETFINDER LINK TO CONTACT US AS THIS LINK IS NOT ALWAYS RELIABLE! 

Tillie is a tiny little (6 pound) Yorkie, Broken Coated Jack Russell, Maltese mix. She came to use from a hoarding situation where she was confined in a basement without much human contact. She has blossomed in rescue.

Tillie is house trained, crate trained, does well on a leash and enjoys riding in a car, sleeping in bed. Our little Ragamuffin is very sweet and attached to her foster providers but still timid with people she does not know.  She does warm up but will need a quiet, calm home full of TLC and an understanding of her past. She will continue to heal as she settles into her forever life and experiences more fun doggie things to do.

Tillie's adoption will require a securely fenced yard or fenced area that leads directly into the home.  She will need someone that is not working away from home a typical 8 hour work day; someone that works from home and can have their dog in their work space, someone who works VERY part time of is retired.  Tillie will need another very socialized dog, non alpha dog, in the home that she can emulate which will help her to adjust.  Tillie will blossom with an owner who is calm and kind, that will take her out and about and continue to offer her positive experiences. Adopters must live within a 1.5 hour drive from Wooster OH which includes The Cleveland and Columbus areas.

Star-Mar Rescue is a natural care provider and we place our dogs in homes that are already on a natural care program or are eager to learn. We use no chemicals on our dogs, no commercial flea products (oral or topical), do blood titers instead of randomly vaccinating. Our yards are without fertilizer and weed killer and our homes are toxin free. We feel that dogs can be protected without being harmed by harsh chemicals and unnecessary vaccinations and do best on a species appropriate, no grain, raw diet. Frozen raw diets, freeze dried or dehydrated no grain. Raw, no grain foods are easily gotten at many pet stores and on line and are no more expensive than a high quality dry food. This simple step will provide your dog the nutrition needed to keep them healthy and happy for many years unlike feeding a lifetime of processed foods. We are happy to help with this transition. For more information go to Star-Mar Rescue Natural Care facebook page and click on \"videos\" in the column to the left and watch the 7 part series called The Truth About Pet Cancer. It will give you an understanding of what we are doing and why. Please do some research on natural care and raw feeding and decide whether or not you can care for Tillie in this manner before requesting an application.

If you feel that your lifestyle and environment meet with Tillie's needs, please directly contact Martha at learymjri@aol.com or call 330-466-3667 or 330-262-0515 for an application or more information. PLEASE DO NOT USE THE LINK PROVIDED BY PETFINDER AS IT IS NOT ALWAYS RELIABLE.  Tillie's adoption will require an approved application and a home visit, with adoption completed at her foster home in Wooster, OH. Tillie's adoption fee is $300. We will work to place her within a 1.5 hour driving distance from her foster home in Wooster, OH. so that we can conduct a home visit bringing Tillie with us. This area includes the Columbus, Cleveland area of OH.

name: 1908-1683 Mac
description:
MAC - 11 years old, 80 pounds, house trained, very friendly, loves people, good with kids, cats & dogs, loves pizza, good on leash, severe allergies, lipoma (fatty tumor)

MAC had been with his previous family his whole 11 years. He had even traveled from Cleveland, Ohio to stay with them. It's almost tragic to think this boy had everything he knew torn away from him when he was surrendered to us at the Virginia Beach Animal Care and Adoption Center. You'd think a family who traveled so far with their boy would not give him up but whatever the reason, I cannot imagine it was an easy one to make. Moving on...I found Mac to be friendly and easy to handle although when I took too long to get him harnessed or give him a treat, he let me know by barking. Rude! But super cute! lol Mac's family supported my finding by telling us how wonderful he was with everyone from young children to adults to cats and even other dogs. He's an amiable boy who wants to just be at your side, outside walking and enjoying the fresh air or lying next to you at night. Mac is awesome. He is a bit older and we're told (and you can see) a decent size lipoma on his side/chest. A lipoma is basically a fatty tumor which doesn't have to be removed unless it seems to be hurting the dog. With Mac, his lipoma doesn't seem to get in the way at all. He is a good walker and had a blast in the yard! He still has lots of energy to expend but we need to be aware he may not walk as far or run as fast as some of his younger counterparts. Mac does have severe allergies so please be aware that this may mean there is an extra financial obligation to keep his allergies in check. Mac is a great boy who seems like he would be an easy fit into most homes. Please bring your resident dog in to meet him if you have one. Please bring your kids in to meet him! Let's find this senior a home so he doesn't have to live in a shelter cage. Mac is waiting in our large dog adoption kennel and his id number is 1908-1683. WE are located at 341 S Birdneck Road in Virginia Beach and are open daily except for Tuesdays. Thanks for considering adoption!

name: STEELE
description:
Steele (aka The Miracle Dog) arrived to NY in April 2019 from Cobb County Georgia. 
He had been hit by a car and surrendered by his former owner to a local shelter where he languished in pain and requiring extensive veterinarian care ( he received the utmost of care while he was at the shelter) 
He has a huge fan club of Guardian Angels and sponsors who got him shipped up to New York where he went into emergency surgery several times to save his life. 
He is now FULLY recovered and through out all his medicals and specialty care he remained ever so sweet and gentle. 
Basically it was touch and go for a while and we did not know if he was going to survive....so yes he is the Miracle Dog!!!
So tens of thousand dollars in veterinary bills later he is now up for adoption!

name: Riley
description:
Riley is 14 years old, 12 lbs. and is currently located in Cocoa, Brevard County.

Riley was surrendered to rescue by a family member after their grandmother passed away.  Unfortunately we don't have much history on Riley as that was not available.  The family was unable to keep Riley due to an upcoming move and knew financially he needed serious dental care.

Riley did have a dental once he came into rescue and had a whopping 20 teeth pulled and he is a much happier dog now!  Before coming into rescue he ate canned food due to his painful mouth.  He now eats kibble but softened with hot water.  

Riley is a sweet gentleman who meshed well with the foster homes Dachshunds, Great Dane and cats.  He LOVES squeaky toys and snoozing in his bed.  Riley does like to take his toys with him when he goes outside to potty.   Riley does have a playful side and will play with the 1 year old Dachshund in his foster home.  

He can be a little protective over his squeaky toys.  

Riley would likely do okay with other dogs or by himself.  He seems to prefer people over the dogs and is a very low key guy.  He loves to sit on your lap and be petted.

Riley has had some accidents in the house, mostly just overnight - some nights he does not have accidents and some he does.  He is crate trained so crating is an option.

Riley is neutered, up to date on vaccines, heartworm tested negative, on a monthly preventative, microchipped and ready for his new forever family!

If you are interested in adopting Riley, please fill out an adoption application on our website at: http://fldr.org/adopt/adoption-application/. The adoption fee is $150

name: Tippi
description: Tipi is a terrier mix that came to us from the city of Coleman. He is a lovable pet that thrives on attention. He has had all his shots and is fixed and will make a great family pet.

name: Josie
description: Josie is very excited about life and wants nothing more than to be with people. This friendly girl is always happy to make new friends and learn new things. Josie is like the Energizer bunny, so she'll need a very active home with a person or family who is up for lots of training and enrichment. She does calm down nicely in quiet environments and is very easygoing on car rides. Born in 2015, Josie came to Best Friends from a humane society in Colorado after she was seized from a dog fighting situation. She has a tick-borne illness that causes her to have very low blood platelets. Because of this condition, Josie must be extra careful to avoid any potentially harmful situations. She also lives alone at the Sanctuary and will need to be the only dog in a home, since her condition can be transmitted to other dogs. Although Josie has a heart murmur that needs to be checked regularly, it does not require medication at this time. At Dogtown, Josie is working on impulse control and staying calm when her caregivers enter her room or put on her harness.

name: Jacko
description: Rescued from a property during a dog fight bust in Colorado, Jacko came to Best Friends from a humane society. At Dogtown he is affectionately called 'Jack Jack.' He adores his toys and treats them like his babies, carrying them around and sleeping with them on his bed. Jacko is playful with new dogs once he has gotten to know them, but he also enjoys sunbathing outside with his roommate at Dogtown. Because of his past, Jacko can be nervous meeting new people, especially if he is meeting them for the first time in a small space. He is more confident meeting people outside in an open space and during a walk. Since walks, treats and toys are some of his favorite things, he will trust new people more quickly if they offer him one of these things. He does take treats nicely, and he is eager to learn new things when treats are the reward. Once he is friends with you, Jacko will run right up to you and stop directly in front of your feet to ask for pets and scratches. He can be a very quiet dog and does not 'talk' very much, unless other dogs are 'talking,' too. He is usually a slow walker, but he loves to run when he feels up to it. Recently, Jacko learned to use a ramp to get into a car. He loves lying down and relaxing in the car and is an excellent passenger. Jacko needs a person or family who will show him that it's OK to trust new people. He'll need extra time to meet new people, especially visitors to a home. When he is comfortable, Jacko is truly a clown. He will play bow at people and flash his adorable smile.

name: Ryder
description: Ryder is your guy! He is approximately 2 years old and a Golden Retriever/Border Collie/Heeler mix-best guess. He is a beautiful strawberry blond and has a long lean body with a docked tail. He loves being part of a pack and gets along well with other dogs. He was found as a stray from the Ute reservation in Cortez, NM, and is so glad he caught his freedom ride to Colorado. This smart goofy guy rides well in the car and hopes to become your favorite adventure buddy. He can be a little reserved at first, but once he becomes comfortable, he is affectionate and enjoys shadowing your every move. Ryder is housebroken and does well in his crate, although he prefers to be outside or free roam in the house. He is learning how to live in a house and once he masters his leash skills, he will make an awesome running buddy. Ryder is UTD on shots, neutered, and microchipped. He will do best with an active home, and someone that will be willing to continue his training. He would love a home with a companion dog, and older kids would suit him fine.Ryder is being fostered in Littleton. Want to meet Ryder and fall in love? Apply to adopt at rezdawgrescue.org

name: Abe
description:
Big and handsome, friendly and well behaved -- Abe has it all! Heâs about 3.5 years old and a bit hefty at his current food-loving 86 pounds. Abe comes to us from a rescue partner in Arkansas who scooped him up as a shelter stray in the nick of time. 

Abe has been soaking up a lot of loving and giving loads in return in his foster homes both in Arkansas and now here with us.  Heâs house trained, crate trained, knows some basic commands and is pretty good on leash walks.  Abe gets along well with other dogs, but itâs people he loves the most.  By your side is his favorite place.  His attitude towards cats?  âMeh, kinda boring,â he wags.

Abe made his home with his rescuer in Arkansas while he was being treated for heartworms, an issue seen with many dogs in that part of the country.  âOnce I got the ok from the vet that Iâd recovered from my treatment, I was first in line to hop on the transport van to Colorado . . . and here I am!â woofs our boy.  To keep him healthy, Abeâs family needs to commit to having him on heartworm preventative year round.  Helping him lose a few pounds would be welcome, too!

A pleasantly active big handsome love who loves being loved on, Abe woofs: âCome on over real soon, bring cookies, and letâs get acquainted. I know weâre gonna be BFFâs in no time and then weâll head home together forever!â

name: Coco
description:
Coco Is a charming 10 year old liver colored Mini. She spent her first six years in a puppy mill. When the mill was closed down by the state, she went to an out of state shelter. They had so many Minis, that they asked for help from some breed rescue groups, and Coco came to Colorado. She was adopted to a wonderful couple, but after three years, and two babies, Coco was no longer comfortable and they asked us to take her back. She is still timid, but comfortable enough to sleep with her foster mom, and she is getting along well with the dogs in her foster home. She loves attention and she would make a great lap companion while you are reading or watching TV.  Coco would do best in an experienced \"mill dog\" home, and she would, of course, love a home with a retired owner or someone who works from home.

Coco is spayed, she is up to date on her vaccinations (rabies, distemper and kennel cough), vet checked, heartworm tested negative and on preventative while in rescue, and microchipped.  Coco had surgery to repair a luxating patella while she has been back with us.  She is nearly fully recovered from that but should not be doing a lot of up and down motion. If you would like to meet Coco, go to www.cominischnauzerrescue.com and complete the on-line adoption application.  We suggest that you print a copy of the application before you hit the \"submit\" button, just in case!  We will give you a call to set up a time to bring Coco for a visit.

name: Minnie
description:
Minnie came all the way from Texas to find a great home in Colorado. She is a tiny owner surrendered terrier mix weighing in at about 8 pounds. We think that she is about 10 years old, but she's quite frisky and nimble. When she came into rescue her skin was in terrible shape. We don't know whether it was the result of a bad diet, a serious flea allergy, or a bacterial infection. She lost a lot of the hair on her body. While her skin is clear now, we donât know if her fur will grow back or if she will stay nekked!  She really doesn't seem to care, and she is not scratchy. She enjoys being with her foster siblings in their fenced-in backyard, and would probably prefer a home with a canine companion.

Minnie is spayed, she is up to date on her vaccinations (rabies, distemper and kennel cough), vet checked, heartworm tested negative and on preventative while in rescue, and microchipped. She also had a dental while in rescue. If you would like to meet Minnie, go to www.cominischnauzerrescue.com and complete the on-line adoption application. We suggest that you print a copy of the application before you hit the \"submit\" button, just in case! We will give you a call to set up a time to bring little Minnie for a visit.

name: Boots

This Boots is made for adopting

One of these days this Boots

Is gonna walk on home with you

name: Daisy  - adventure girl! Zoomie enthusiast!
description:
Hi! I'm Daisy! I'm a gorgeous Blue Heeler who is loving life in the Colorado mountains.

I'm 3 years old and weigh about 45 pounds. I'm house-trained, crate-trained and spayed. These days I'm all big smiles!

I'm always ready for adventure when out and about, but also love snuggling up on the couch with my people and relaxing. 

I love tossing around my fluffy duck toy, chewing on big bones and Kongs, and snoozing in the patches of sun around the house. I walk nicely on a leash (unless there are bunnies - but hey, who can resist bunnies!) and get good zoomies when I'm running around the yard. 

My foster mom says I'm the total package: able to keep up on adventures, trustworthy, snuggly, and adjusting very well. She says I'm super smart, eager to work, and really athletic. She thinks I'd love agility, treibball and freestyle! I've tried barn hunt, which is really fun, too! My ideal home would be one that's committed to giving me plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and positive training. 

I am trustworthy alone at home for reasonable amounts of time while my foster mom works, and sometimes she even takes me to the office with her, where I love getting attention from all her coworkers. Did I mention how much I love my people? It's not necessary for you to have another dog in your home, as I can go either way - both with other dogs and just on my own with you! Like many heelers, I can be dog-selective, though. Look, you don't like everyone you meet, do you? So introductions to other dogs must be done with knowledgeable supervision. I do go to daycare twice a week and everyone there LOVES me, but in big playgroups, I get a little worked up. Oh, and because of that bunny prey-drive thing, I probably wouldn't be the best fit for a home with small dogs unless you're willing to do very careful introductions.

Unfortunately, I didn't get the best start in life. I was found running around in rural Texas with a bullet wound in my hip! Can you believe someone would do that to such a pretty girl? My foster people think I was probably just doing what my breed is meant to do: chase cows! Isn't it fun to see them run and hear them go \"mooooooo!\" when you nip at them?? I was just trying to live my best life... 

So speaking of herding, I am really good at it. Like, amazing. I was born this way! So when we're out walking and a runner or bike or car passes us, I want to herd them... really badly... like really, really badly... My foster mom doesn't like this; she says I send her to the chiropractor every week because when I try to herd these moving things, I lunge to the end of my leash and bark and don't let up until they go away! (Don't worry, though, I watch carefully to see if they're coming back!) It's super fun, I don't know why she doesn't like it. Anyway, my people are teaching me to \"leave it,\" which is boring, but sometimes it's worth it for my paycheck - chicken!!! In the meantime, I don't go for walks in busy places with lots of bikes, like Marshall Mesa or Boulder Creek Path. My foster mom says I might be able to some day, with lots and lots of training and some maturity. Gosh, what do I need, a Ph-freaking-D??? (Yes, says mom.) She also says that giving me enough exercise is a delicate balance of just enough, but not too much so that I'm completely overstimulated, and things that tire out my brain, not just my body.

I'm also terrible on car rides. Usually, getting in the car means we're going somewhere awesome (a new place to hike, or maybe doggie daycare!!!), and I get so excited that I bark my head off and squeal (I have the most beautiful voice, if I do say so myself, and sometimes it's nice just to hear it!)... And sometimes I get frustrated and bark when we pass those pesky bikes. Come on, Mom! Just let me at 'em... I'm better if I can't see out of the car, though, so if you can crate me in the back of your SUV, I'm okay.

So you might be catching on to the fact that my first couple of years were a little rough. No one really taught me self control or how to channel my energy and instincts, so I just let my freak flag fly, and they sent me to the pound! Luckily, SDR took me in, fixed me up, treated my heartworm (whatever that is; all I know is that I feel MUCH better these days) and sent me on my way to my forever home. My ideal home would be in a quieter neighborhood (preferably rural - I'm a country girl from Texas at heart, after all) with people who are committed to lovingly helping me learn how to function better in the busy Colorado lifestyle. It would also be great to have a big yard with a tall wooden fence, too. If I can't see those bikes going by, then I won't try to chase them, and maybe I'll finally relax a little! (If you live in an apartment/condo or a busy area, please don't apply for Daisy unless you have plenty of heeler and/or dog training experience.)

Did I mention I like to snuggle? If snuggling was a Nobel Prize category, I would probably win it every year (and spend the money on bones). As for the other stuff, it makes my people really happy when I work hard at it, and I live to please my people, so I guess I'll keep at it.

Check out my very own video above made by Summit Dog's extraordinary videographers/editors, Molly Steele and Maddie Steele!

For more info and/or to apply to adopt me, go to https://www.summitdogrescue.org/meet-daisy.html

name: Kirie
description:
My name is Kirie. I am available for adoption through Colorado Canine Rescue (CCR), a nonprofit dog rescue located in the Denver area. I came to CCR from Canon City Colorado. There is very little history on me. CCR has been told I am a pit bull breed mix, but that is just a guess made by shelter staff, rescue volunteers, and our veterinarians.

It is said when life gives you lemons, make lemonade. Well Kirie has had quite a few lemons handed to her in her 4 year life span, but definitely making the best lemonade that she can. Kirie was adopted out from CCR as a young dog but two years later wound up in the Aurora Shelter, having been abandoned. They called us so we could take her back into our rescue. Kirie has had TPLO surgery since being returned to us, going through training with a behaviorist, and a foster has worked diligently to get her past her pulling on the leash, and help her master her needs to attack water spouts and sprinkler heads.
Kirie still has separation issues, but does well in the foster home left with other dogs and free reign within the home. She is on a generic Prozac to help her manage with anxiety. Kirie loves to snuggle with her people on the couch and in bed and absolutely loves to give kisses. She is looking for a family that will give her plenty of attention, be home more than not, play fetch, take her on walks in the neighborhood. She adores children and is very gentle with them. Kirie so looks forward to rides in the car. She would enjoy being an only dog, but would do fine with a furry companion that has a laissez-faire attitude. She does best if the door is open or a doggie door for her to go out as needed. She needs a more experienced dog owner because she has been through so much in life.

If you are interested in adopting Kirie, please submit an adoption application located on our website, www.coloradocaninerescue.org. We are asking for a $200 adoption donation for Kirie. Kirie being a bully breed, will only be placed in communities that do not have a ban on bullies. Please note, CCR cannot guarantee the breed composition or ages of our dogs as we usually have no history prior to them entering the shelter. 9/15/19 5:01 PM

description:

Tillie is a tiny little (6 pound) Yorkie, Broken Coated Jack Russell, Maltese mix. She came to use from a hoarding situation where she was confined in a basement without much human contact. She has blossomed in rescue.

Tillie is house trained, crate trained, does well on a leash and enjoys riding in a car, sleeping in bed. Our little Ragamuffin is very sweet and attached to her foster providers but still timid with people she does not know.  She does warm up but will need a quiet, calm home full of TLC and an understanding of her past. She will continue to heal as she settles into her forever life and experiences more fun doggie things to do.

Tillie's adoption will require a securely fenced yard or fenced area that leads directly into the home.  She will need someone that is not working away from home a typical 8 hour work day; someone that works from home and can have their dog in their work space, someone who works VERY part time of is retired.  Tillie will need another very socialized dog, non alpha dog, in the home that she can emulate which will help her to adjust.  Tillie will blossom with an owner who is calm and kind, that will take her out and about and continue to offer her positive experiences. Adopters must live within a 1.5 hour drive from Wooster OH which includes The Cleveland and Columbus areas.

Star-Mar Rescue is a natural care provider and we place our dogs in homes that are already on a natural care program or are eager to learn. We use no chemicals on our dogs, no commercial flea products (oral or topical), do blood titers instead of randomly vaccinating. Our yards are without fertilizer and weed killer and our homes are toxin free. We feel that dogs can be protected without being harmed by harsh chemicals and unnecessary vaccinations and do best on a species appropriate, no grain, raw diet. Frozen raw diets, freeze dried or dehydrated no grain. Raw, no grain foods are easily gotten at many pet stores and on line and are no more expensive than a high quality dry food. This simple step will provide your dog the nutrition needed to keep them healthy and happy for many years unlike feeding a lifetime of processed foods. We are happy to help with this transition. For more information go to Star-Mar Rescue Natural Care facebook page and click on \"videos\" in the column to the left and watch the 7 part series called The Truth About Pet Cancer. It will give you an understanding of what we are doing and why. Please do some research on natural care and raw feeding and decide whether or not you can care for Tillie in this manner before requesting an application.

If you feel that your lifestyle and environment meet with Tillie's needs, please directly contact Martha at learymjri@aol.com or call 330-466-3667 or 330-262-0515 for an application or more information. PLEASE DO NOT USE THE LINK PROVIDED BY PETFINDER AS IT IS NOT ALWAYS RELIABLE.  Tillie's adoption will require an approved application and a home visit, with adoption completed at her foster home in Wooster, OH. Tillie's adoption fee is $300. We will work to place her within a 1.5 hour driving distance from her foster home in Wooster, OH. so that we can conduct a home visit bringing Tillie with us. This area includes the Columbus, Cleveland area of OH.

All of our sweet fur babies are being socialized daily with other dogs, adults, & most importantly, children. They are ALL in homes being cared for by people who LOVE them! BREED IDENTIFICATION:
Please understand that many rescue dogs are mixes of multiple breeds. Petfinder allows us to choose up to two breeds per dog. While the shelters and our rescue do our best in accurately identifying breeds, breed identification is not guaranteed. If there is a certain breed that you do not want, it is very important that you share this with our rescue when applying. When adopting a puppy, breed uncertainty plays a big part in the size/look of the dog as an adult. Please know that any puppy can be a wonderful dog, regardless of preconceived notions of certain breeds, but it is very important that the adopter has the dedication and patience to raise the puppy with boundaries, consistency, structure, & love. The more effort you give towards training & time you allow for exercise, your puppy will grow to be a HUGE source of UNCONDITIONAL LOVE, TOTAL LOYALTY, HAPPINESS, COMFORT & COMPANIONSHIP!

We are a small rescue run by volunteers & focused on finding the right match for both our dogs & for you. If you are interested in adopting through our rescue, you first will need to complete an adoption application & be approved as a potential adopter before meeting any of our pups. No need to be intimidated by our application as it allows us to get to know you & your lifestyle. Of course, the more you can share the better! Please also note, while a fenced yard is fantastic, it is not required by our rescue, however, it may be required for a certain dog. Once adoption applicants are approved to become potential adopters, we offer private appointments where you can meet one or several dogs at the discretion of the rescue. We offer a unique & pleasant experience focused on finding the perfect match. It is extremely important to us that everyone is treated with respect & that NO ONE IS LEFT HANGING. WE WILL GET BACK TO YOU WITHIN 4 TO 5 DAYS of application submission. If there is a dog you are eager to meet, please email us before the 4-5 days! IF YOU DO NOT HEAR FROM US AT THAT POINT, PLEASE CALL US DIRECTLY at 203-241-2351 so that we can check the status of your application and move it forward immediately. We look forward to hearing from you and helping you find your new best friend!

description:
Two year old, 100 lb. Stormy, is in need of a home! He is a great guy that will be a wonderful companion and friend! 

Stormy is WONDERFUL! He is generally peaceful and quiet. He is social, loves people, and is good with other dogs.

This guy is not only beautiful to look at, but he's funny too! Just watching him, will bring a smile to your face!

So good on the leash, his foster families' 11 year old daughter can walk him out in public, with no problem whatsoever!

Stormy ADORES hanging out outside, and watching the world go by. So, in order to safely have him relax outside for the amount of time that he would love, we are requiring his adopters to have a fully enclosed yard, with a physical fence, or at the very least, go to an adopter that like to spend A LOT of time outside!

She is a special soul who deserves a peaceful place to relax and provide companionship. Sheba is located in CT.

LBDR focuses on the rescue, care and placement of black dogs who are in danger of euthanasia due to their color, as well as other dogs who are in immediate need. LBDR is funded by donations which are used solely for the 
care of our dogs.

name: Theon
description:
Name: Theon
Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 5 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

name: Wednesday
description:
Our stunning Wednesday enters the room like an arctic blast of cold on a hot summer night and grabs your attention! This magnificent one and a half year old, black Labrador Retriever mix came to us from a big city Animal Control facility, where she spent some time after a lackluster owners abandoned her. She was rail thin and gaunt when she entered the city shelter system, and took some time to adjust to her harsh surroundings. 

When Wednesday came to our Rescue, she was a wild child, a Black Beauty in need of some firm, loving leadership. It was painfully obvious that her owners had missed all of her social development cues, and woefully neglected her manners and leadership training. Wednesday was as precocious as her Addams Family namesake, and seemed to feel that her opinion was warranted on just about every subject.

In no time, Wednesday has developed into a canine thoroughbred, brimming with potential. An energy and personality match is key to Wednesday's happiness. She is a high energy, athletic dog who needs alot of outdoor exercise. She would gleefully keep rigorous pace with an avid runner, hiker or powerwalker, and seems to thrive in the brisk country air. No doubt about it, Wednesday needs an active adopter, but, also one who is extremely proficient in leadership and obedience training. She is not a dog for the casual or inexperienced adopter.

Wednesday largely appears to be Labrador Retriever, but we also suspect some Border Collie in her DNA. She is a lean, tall dog weighing 47 pounds, and is extremely graceful and athletic. She runs with great speed, and could be an agility champion. Wednesday has the energy and intelligence that we see in this high strung Herding breed, as well as the mischievious and impertinent tendency that sometimes occurs when Border Collies are under exercised and bored! 

As a double dose of working dog, Wednesday definitely needs a job, and she is a natural at obedience work. She knows all her basic commands, and has passed many of the Canine Good Citizenship tests. She handles beautifully on lead, and heels nicely. Wednesday still needs some polish on her stranger manners, since she may, on occasion, greet someone rudely, but motivated adopters should be able to work her through any issues by employing her well honed commands. In the right hands, Wednesday will become a fantastic, well behaved companion.

Wednesday would fare best in an adult home, with adopters experienced in handling large, active breeds. She would overwhelm toddlers and seniors. She could easily join a multi-dog home, with another active, well trained dog, but sometimes, unruly and ill mannered dogs press her buttons. We have not had her around cats, but she would most likely chase them beyond their tolerance level.

Wednesday has respectable house manners and is mostly housetrained. She will need some finetuning on her potty routine as she transitions to a new environment. Wednesday is in good health, and has been spayed. She has been vaccinated for rabies, bordatella, and DHLPPC (distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvo, parainfluenza and coronavirus). She has had the 4dx test, and is negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. She has been microchipped and dewormed, and is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm treatment.

If you are interested in Wednesday, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738.

name: Hero
description:
Our magnificent Hero needs a hero of his own. This beautiful, robust boy is a victim of circumstances. His doting owner lost her home, and desperately tried to find housing to accommodate her beloved companion, whom she had raised from a pup. Hero's Mom took up temporary residence in a local motel, until she could get her bearings, but Hero was booted out by the motel manager. After a tearful goodbye, sad Hero was left in the care of a well-respected town shelter, who pled his case to us.

Hero appears to be a handsome mix of black Labrador Retriever and Border Collie. He has the physique and color of a black Lab, and the white tuxedo markings and black speckled white socks that suggest Border Collie. At 50 pounds, Hero has a solid, muscular build, and yet is easy to handle on lead. As a combination herder and retriever, Hero loves the outdoors, and has a hardwired work ethic that needs to be channeled through exercise and obedience work. 

Hero sometimes seems unsure of his place in the world, and needs to join a home with a strong pack leader, willing to provide the structure that he needs to to thrive. Hero gives the impression of caution at first, as he sizes up strangers, but warms quickly to a gentle touch. Adopters will need to be comfortable putting boundaries between Hero and strangers: he can become overzealous in guarding his person. He would be the ideal watchdog.

Hero seems subdued and intimidated at times, in the midst of our busy foster home, and we sense that a quiet, adult home would suit him best. He is not a big fan of change, and a steady, quiet routine will serve him beautifully.  Hero would be the ideal walking or running companion for an active single or couple. He loves the outdoors, can keep a brisk pace on a hike, and longs to make a one-to-one connection with a strong human personality. Hero could easily join a multi-dog home with another well-trained, calm dog, but cats are a definite no-go.

Hero has progressed nicely in his basic obedience training. The obedience work serves him as a job he can take pride in, and he performs the commands beautifully, either for praise or treats. Obedience training is key to providing the working breeds with the purpose and focus that they need to live happily in a domestic lifestyle.

Hero has good house manners and is house trained and crate trained. Adopters should have appropriate patience, and expect to troubleshoot the occasional accident that will inevitably occur during Hero's transition to a new home. He is in excellent health, and is at an ideal lean body weight. He has been neutered, and has been vaccinated for Rabies, DA2PP (distemper, adrenovirus, parvo and parainfluenza), and Canine Flu. He has been boostered as needed, and has had the 4dx test: negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. He has been dewormed, and microchipped. If you are interested in Hero, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738 for more info.

name: Shiloh
description:
On a cold, snowy night in December of 2012, a PFPO foster family was walking their dogs when they found a sweet black pitbull with an old rope tied to her collar. It was apparent this dog had been tied out and had broken loose. The family took the dog to the shelter to give the owners a chance to claim her. No one came for her.

The family called the shelter everyday to check on her. When it became clear that no one was coming to claim the dog, they asked PFPO to accept her into the foster program. The family called the dog Shiloh.

From the moment Shiloh came to live with her foster family, they knew that she was a sweet and special girl. Shiloh was only about 8 months old and full of energy! Shiloh loved to go on walks, play in the snow, and take catnaps in the sun. Shiloh loved people, but she didnât understand other dogs. So, Shilohâs foster family worked very hard to find her the perfect home and perfect family to love her and her quirks.

Just 6 weeks after she entered her foster familyâs home, Shiloh had an adoption application from a nice retired man who lived in Delaware. After several visits and overnight stays (including an âaccidentâ on the carpet during her first meeting and eating a loaf of bread off the kitchen counter), Shilohâs foster family knew that this was Shilohâs perfect forever family. But, sometimes in life, sad things happen to good dogs.

Shiloh lived with this nice old man for 5 years until he got sick and passed away. Suddenly, Shiloh was without her perfect family. Staying true to the rescueâs promise of always taking back its own, Shiloh is now back with PFPO. She is still sweet. She is still loves adult people (and kids over 10). And, she still doesnât understand other dogs. She needs a new perfect family to love her. 

Could that be you?

Shiloh's adoption fee is $100. She is spayed UTD on vaccines, micro-chipped, heartworm negative and on heartworm/flea/tick prevention.

***WE DO NOT DO OUT OF STATE ADOPTIONS***

If you would like to learn more information about me, or to even adopt me please contact Peace for Paws Ohio at: adopt@peaceforpawsohio.org.

Because we will not do on-the-spot adoptions, we ask that you fill out an adoption application prior to inquiring about meeting any of our pets. Please give us at least 48 hours excluding weekends and holidays to get in touch with you once your application has been submitted.

name: Truman
description:
My name is Truman. I am available for adoption through Colorado Canine Rescue (CCR), a nonprofit dog rescue located in the Denver area. I came to CCR from a owner relinquishment in Denver. CCR believes that I might be a Boxer/German Wirehair breed mix (just a guess by shelter and vet personnel) and I am approximately 7-8 years old. My foster parents tell me I have a kooky personality, maybe it has something to do with my mohawk and big underbite. I am a sweet boy with people, although I have not been around a lot of kids. Since I am starting to enjoy my senior years, I prefer not to share my humans and would need to be the only dog in the house. I do well with cats, I don't even notice they're around until there rubbing against me. I am crate trained and walk well on a leash. I am also trained to use the dog door in my foster's house and will need to go to a home with a yard. I love to go for car rides and hang out with my people. I like to go into the hardware stores because the workers give me treats! I do like to chase the squirrels on the fence (but I think that they are there for my enjoyment because they tease me). In the house I love to stare out the door or windows at the wildlife (squirrels, birds, bunnies, deer), but I don't like those pesky raccoons, don't worry I will keep the yard safe from them. I have been known to be a barker and know what a bark collar is. I sleep on a big comfy dog bed next to yours at night and will only get on the bed if you tell me it is ok. I take treats extra gentle and love fruits and vegetables. I love to chew on dog bones, and play with some toys. I like to go for walks and hikes, I like to play in the water and have been fishing in the mountains. I have been on a boat and love to have the wind just blow through my hair.
Truman will do best with an experienced dog owner/handler. If you are interested in adopting Truman, please submit an adoption application located on our website, coloradocaninerescue.org. We are asking for a $200 adoption donation. He is neutered, housebroken, up to date on vaccinations, and microchipped. Please note, CCR cannot guarantee the breed composition or ages of our dogs as we usually have no history prior to them entering the shelter. In addition, most dogs listed as potty trained will experience an adjustment period as they learn the routines in their new home.

description:

I will be available to adopt/go home after July 5th. I am currently completing a board and train program through High Drive Dog Company in Longmont, Colorado. Part of my adoption requirements include follow up training with High Drive (sponsored by CCR for 3 months), no other animals in the home, no children under 12, and no cities with BSL (breed specific legislation). It is preferred I am adopted to a home with a 6 foot wooden fence. These requirements are non-negotiable. Lemon would do best living with someone who has bully breed experience. Kirie was adopted out from CCR as a young dog but two years later wound up in the Aurora Shelter, having been abandoned. They called us so we could take her back into our rescue. Kirie has had TPLO surgery since being returned to us, going through training with a behaviorist, and a foster has worked diligently to get her past her pulling on the leash, and help her master her needs to attack water spouts and sprinkler heads.
Kirie still has separation issues, but does well in the foster home left with other dogs and free reign within the home. She is on a generic Prozac to help her manage with anxiety. Kirie loves to snuggle with her people on the couch and in bed and absolutely loves to give kisses. She is looking for a family that will give her plenty of attention, be home more than not, play fetch, take her on walks in the neighborhood. She adores children and is very gentle with them. Kirie so looks forward to rides in the car. She would enjoy being an only dog, but would do fine with a furry companion that has a laissez-faire attitude. She does best if the door is open or a doggie door for her to go out as needed. She needs a more experienced dog owner because she has been through so much in life.

name: Glory
description:
Glory came to us from the Edmond, OK animal shelter in horrible condition (as you can see from one of the photos). She had very little coat and her skin was deeply infected. She did not have mange, just horrible flea dermatitis and a yeast infection. So after taking many rounds of mediation and having many medicated baths (that she did not enjoy, but was such a good girl!), we are happy to report that Glory has recovered and has grown a thick, healthy coat now.  

This sweet girl has likely never know a comfy life, but she is thriving in her foster home. She is house trained, will crate just fine (though we think she could be trusted loose in the house), gets along well with other dogs, loves to snuggle, and is so sweet and grateful.

We want to find Glory the loving home she's never had before. She is calm and would be great for retirees or for anyone who just wants a chill dog. Leisurely walks would be great...a back patio where she could relax with you would be fine and dandy too. She is low-maintenance and content. 

Glory does not require any further medication. Her skin is recovering well and she's now happy and healthy. It's a bit hard to tell how old she is because she was neglected so severely for so long, but we guess she's in the middle somewhere--maybe 7ish? A lovely age with a lot of great years ahead.

Will you be Glory's person? Will you give her life the happily-ever-after she deserves? Please complete the online application in the \"more about us\" section. Placements considered within 300 miles of Tulsa, OK.

name: Leroy
description:
LEROY, above all the other animals in our care, embodies the spirit of CompAnimals Pet Rescue and the level of commitment we give to our animals for their entire lives. Here is his story:

About 10 years ago I got a call from a senior citizen who was trying to catch a stray pit bull in her neighborhood in Elkton. The dog would follow children around but eluded adults. She was worried the SPCA would pick him up and euthanize him. The Cecil Co SPCA had a \"no pit bulls\" policy at the time. So for 3 weeks I tried to catch him, make friends with him, bribe him and for 3 weeks the SPCA was bent on catching him as well. Luckily, with the help of a butcher (who lived in the same neighborhood and had been giving him fresh beef) I was able to capture him. He was super friendly and hopped right in my car. We had him vetted and aside from a hairless patch on the top of his head he recovered from his ordeal pretty quickly.

I fostered him myself. He had a distinct hate of cats and for that reason I wasn't able to keep him permanently. He did get along with other dogs and was a well mannered guest. It was probably a year or so before he found his \"forever\" home. Leroy seemed to have lucked out - he had a boy of his own and a big grassy yard. We didn't hear much from him after the initial settling in. There were other dogs to rescue and Leroy was starting his new life.

Fast forward about 4 years - tragedy struck and Leroy's family fell apart. His mom was sick, the house was in foreclosure, Leroy was living in an empty house. We got a call that the family could no longer care for him. Leroy came back.

Due to the family's lack of finances and the stress of it all, Leroy was in horrible shape. His skin condition which, looking back through vet records, had never been fully addressed. He was bald, scabby, bloody and thin. His head was sunken in. His hair loss was so great that you couldn't even distinguish what color he was. He wagged his tail.

Antibiotics and prednisone kicked back the skin a notch but again it never fully recovered. He developed demodex, a type of mange, due to the pred suppressing his immune system. We sent him to a foster home hoping to boost his spirits and give him more 1-on-1 care. Another vet was added to his repertoire. More antibiotics, supplements, shampoos but still his skin was slow to recover. Some prickly hair poked through but not as much as we had hoped for. He developed a sore on his ear and one on his toe which was so painful he didn't want to walk. A culture was done and revealed not one, but 3, drug resistant bacteria. One was resistant to ALL antibiotics. The drugs that we had been giving him were slowly killing him.

Fast forward to a year ago, stopped all Western medicine and enlisted the help of Always Helpful Veterinary Services & Dr Judith Shoemaker. The first visit was hours long as she worked up a plan and refining of supplements, powders and remedies. I noticed her lack of concern at the \"flesh eating bacteria\" - a condition so bad that one vet wanted to amputate part of his ear and toe and another felt it was hopeless and he should be euthanized. She was most concerned with his painful eyes. He has a condition called entropean where the eyelids roll in and the lashes rub against the eye.

Leroy responded quickly under the watchful eye of Dr. Shoemaker. His coat came in glossy and now covers about 2/3 of his body. His skin still has flare ups but not more drug resistant bacteria. He was tested for food allergies and put on an appropriate diet. To someone meeting Leroy today, for the first time, he looks like a wreck - like he was just rescued. But to those of us who have seen him in the road to recovery, he looks beautiful.

Leroy has a pan pal who has him out every week for his medicated bath and some R&R. This same wonderful pen pal is covering most of his medical expenses (thankfully Always Helpful has a monthly payment plan!). She has offered to continue with his support even after he is adopted.

Leroy is now pushing 10 years of age. We would love for him to find his special home but if not, he is welcome to live his life out with us. Somewhere along the line he decided he didn't want to get along with other dogs - his Dr thinks it is because he felt so crappy. He has never lost his love of people - especially children. Leroy adores kids! He is currently getting a break from shelter life and is in a \"vacation\" foster home for a few weeks. Check out the video his foster mom made for him.

If you can be Leroy's guardian angel please fill out an application at www.companimals.org

name: Ellis #2
description:
Ellis #2 is about 1 year old and 41 lbs. He has had a prolapsed anus so he had surgery to tack his colon to his body internally. It has worked well and he is doing fine. Ellis is a sweet and goofy boy. He cannot climb a fence, but has climbed the gate when he sees a dog on the other side he wants to play with or he sees me. He normally does not try to get out, but would need to be supervised. He has a great personality and gets along really well with other dogs. He loves humans too. If you are interested in Ellis please fill out an application at labs4rescue.com.

September 15, 2019 Update from Ellis's Foster Mom in Connecticut: As soon as the Vet in Norwalk does his final exam, I think we will be taking Ellis to play with a neighbor chocolate lab. He wants to play so much when he meets other dogs. We have started dog obedience classes yesterday through our Park & Rec Dept. After all the initial craziness (6 dogs in class), he ended up doing pretty good. He is so friendly with people and children. Loves to be petted and loves to give kisses too. Rides well in the car. Is relatively calm and quiet in the house - until the doorbell rings. There is not an aggressive bone in his body. Likes to keep tabs on his people. Likes to lie at or under your feet.

Ellis's day is up at 6:30, Todd takes him out to potty. Back in for breakfast. Then a long walk around the property. Todd and I take him on walks around the yard. He seems to like laying outdoors. Does not bark at cars or bike riders. Late afternoon is a walk at the beach or the state park for an hour. Loves his dinner! And loves to chew his rawhide chew bone while in the living room with us. We go down to the barn to put the horses in and he loves gobbling up any grain they miss. Also he likes carrots. Around 9:30 he is tired and goes to sleep on his dog bed but will go into his crate at night when we go to bed. Boy oh boy, can that boy snore!

For additional information about Ellis #2 please email Marla Cox at mclabs4rescue@gmail.com. 

Ellis #2 is being fostered in Connecticut.

To expedite the process, please follow the step-by-step instructions outlined and submit an adoption application listing 3-5 dogs of interest. Please hurry as your new best friend is waiting for you!

name: Foster Homes Needed
description:
Every minute matters when it comes to rescuing a Shih Tzu. We may get a short notice that someone needs to surrender their dog or a puppy mill dog needs a temporary home. We can't help if we don't have families willing to foster, and we are always in need of more foster homes!

If you live in the Minneapolis/Saint Paul, Rockford or Chicago, IL areas and want to help save lives, please complete either our online Foster Sign-Up or download a word version here:

http://www.northstarshihtzurescue.org/foster/

(please note: neither dog pictured are available to foster or adopt, both are in their forever homes)

NorthStar Shih Tzu Rescue exists to benefit both Shih Tzu and Shih Tzu blend dogs and the people of our community. We operate as a no-kill rescue that provides rescue and adoption services, and meaningful outreach programs in order to advance the welfare of these companion animals, to serve and educate our community, and to make a positive, loving impact on the lives of both.

NorthStar, located in Excelsior, MN, actively works to rescue Shih Tzu and Shih Tzu blend dogs from dangerous environments and shelters with the ultimate goal of placing them in loving, permanent, adoptive homes. We rescue unwanted, abandoned, and abused dogs. We have them vaccinated, micro-chipped, spayed or neutered, provide other medical care, and rehabilitate them in carefully selected foster homes.

We also serve as a resource to our community and all pet owners by providing education and information on the benefits of adopting an animal in need as well as responsible pet ownership, including the importance of spay/neuter, good nutrition, and positive behavior training. We strive to increase public awareness about companion animal overpopulation, commercial breeders, and to offer solutions to end the killing of adoptable animals.

We work in alliance with local animal shelters, pounds, other rescue groups, and humane society organizations to ensure these animals are not forgotten.

description:
Please contact Pet (information@pethelpersinc.org) for more information about this pet.

My name is Daenerys (Daeny for short) and I am a Beagle/Pit mix about 5 years old weighing 45 pounds. I came to Pet Helpers with my 6 surviving pups and 2 other adult dogs that were my pack. I am an alpha female and it was my responsibility to bring them back food if I could find it and protect them. Some really nice folks followed me home one night and made it possible for ALL of us to be rescued. My puppies have all been adopted into wonderful homes and now it's my turn to find my Forever Family. I've been spayed, microchipped, updated on vaccines and tested negative for heartworm and Lyme. I'm house trained and crate trained, but I really don't need a crate...I'm a pretty laid back kind of gal. When I meet a new dog I have to be introduced properly and spend some time with them to feel comfortable. Because of this I do not do well in a dog park or out walking with other dogs I do not know. I don't like cats, I'll be perfectly honest with you. I love kids and adults though and love to give kisses. I'm easy to leash walk and I really like car rides. If you could please open your heart and home to me, I promise to be loyal and loving. I am fostered in Fairmont, WV, and my adoption fee is $150.00.

If you would like more information please email adoptionisforever@pethelpersinc.org.

name: Lady Bunny
description:
Lady Bunny is a female double merle Australian Shepherd located in Fayetteville, NC.
She is around 6 months of age and is expected to be somewhere between 30-40 lbs when full grown.
As a result of being a double merle Lady Bunny is completely deaf, blind in the left eye but does have some vision on the right.
It's very important to remember that she was born this way so she doesn't realize she's any different and it certainly doesn't slow her down at all.
She is a rather strong willed girl, very smart and high energy!
She is very treat motivated which has made training a lot easier!
So far she is doing fantastic with the hand signals for sit, down, stand, come, stay and spin.
She walks well on leash too.
She is fully crate trained and is doing great with house training.
Lady Bunny would do best with someone that is willing/able to continue her training. 
Aussies are a very smart breed and love to learn.
Lacking some vision from one eye and hearing doesn't change that.
Training is also a great bonding tool!
She absolutely loves playing with other dog's and would do great with another doggie companion.
It would be best for any potential doggie friends to have a more playful/high energy personality because we feel Lady Bunny would be rather overwhelming for an older more laid back dog.
She loves her people and is very attentive, meaning she checks in frequently without being reminded.
She stays too busy to be a cuddler though.
We are recommending she go to a home without small children due to the fact that when she gets overly excited, she can bite down a little too hard.
Not aggressively at all but it does pinch.
Being an energetic young puppy at times she still finds it difficult to keep all 4 paws on the floor when greeting people.
Lady Bunny isn't a fan of sharing her food or high value treats with doggie friends.
We have been working on this and she has made great progress so it very manageable.
Foster mom can fill you in on what we have been doing to work on the issue.
Lady Bunny is spayed, up to date on all vaccinations, current on heart worm/flea tick prevention and she is also microchipped.
We are requiring a meet and greet prior to adoption.
This is just to help ensure we get the best match possible for Lady Bunny as well as the potential adopter.
With her high energy level and love for playing with other dog's, we feel any existing dog's will need to meet her as well to make sure they don't feel overwhelmed by her high energy playful self.
If you think you would be interested in meeting this adorable girl please follow this link to submit an application-

https://www.australianshepherdsfurever.org/adoption-applicaâ¦

name: Genie
description:
Meet the Adorable Genie!!!

This little brindle Pekingnese girl is just a puppy and such a sweet, silly precious girl! She joined us as an \"owner surrender\" and we immediately recognized some trauma in her behaviors. She clearly wasn't treated very well in her precious life- which broke our hearts. We had a shy, scared little puppy that didn't understand how to really be a puppy. 2 months in foster care and tons of love later, and we have a confident, happy, silly playful girl and what could be better! Genie has been with children, cats, and other dogs. She does great with other dogs, is great with cats and also good with older children. Because of her uncertain past we recommend homes with children over 8 years old. (Ie- no tail pullers lol) 
Genie is under 20 pounds and around a year old.

She is mostly potty trained and we say mostly because she still is very young and will adjust to a new schedule fairly well. She is an \"excited pee-er\" when greeted! description:
This little guy is looking for a sidekick to call his very own. Your name doesn't even have to be Mario! If you're willing to be his best pal for all future adventures, Yoshi would love to receive your application!

In typical lab fashion, Yoshi is all heart and soul. Loving, comical, smart and all about relationships. He is happy to follow his people around, and is great with other dogs. Add some water, and any boring task becomes the most fun ever! A Chocolate Lab mix, Yoshi sports a gorgeous mocha coat and stunning hazel eyes. At 16 weeks old, he is working hard on house-manners 101, and promises to be an excellent student as you help him learn all a puppy needs to know to become an amazing adult.

description:

Biscuit in color, shape size, etc screams Yellow Lab. However, those ears are classic Shepherd ears that go through that awkward stage while they are deciding to stand on their own. We'll call her a Shepador! As sweet as she is cute, Biscuit is great with other dogs and adores people. Currently about 15 weeks old, we suspect she will grow into those ears! She is sure to make an amazing lifelong companion. All she needs is you!

description:
How we love this little girl, and she is so deserving of the perfect happily ever after! Perhaps her new beginning is waiting on a sofa cushion next to you?

Nikki came to us with a single puppy and she was the best mom to him. Having raised him up right, she is ready for a home of her own. One that will cherish her and spend time with her in a favorite chair or section of the couch. Nikki is going to adore her forever person. Estimated at approximately 2 years old, she weighs only about 10 pounds. We suspect she is a mix of Min-Pin and either Dachshund or one of the tiny terrier breeds. She may be a bit shy at first, but is very loving, house-trained and excellent with other dogs. She will show her comical side with a daily case of the play zoomies, then it's back to your lap or at your side she most wants to be!

description:
Say what you will, this litter of three adorable puppies might have been named Larry, Moe & Curly, but they are no stooges...no way! They found their way to our rescue where they knew we would help them. That's pretty darn smart!

Moe, with the adorable white face blaze and nose snippet is positively adorable! A Black Lab, maybe a touch of hound mix, he is an excellent blend of puppy play and puppy cuddles. He loves to play with other dogs and is excellent with people of all ages. At 15 weeks old, he is already working hard on house-manners and puppy manners 101. Moe will be so appreciative of the forever person who takes the time to teach him all the things a puppy needs to know to grow into an amazing adult. We suspect in adulthood, he will be medium to upper medium in size. He will make a wonderful addition to his new home, and we can't wait to tell him he will have a permanent address of his very own!

Moe is available in NY through the Go North Program of The Lucky Puppy Rescue centered in Bonifay and Panama City, FL (NY Lic #1054), The $395 adoption fee includes transportation from FL to NY, neuter surgery, vaccinations, de-worm, flea prevention and heartworm prevention. He will be so appreciative of the forever person who takes the time to teach him all the things a puppy needs to know to grow into an amazing adult. However, his affection and love for his new home will be immense! Perhaps it's you who has been looking for an amazing addition like Larry.

description:

Approximately 15 weeks old, Curly keeps right up with her brothers, and they don't get anything over on her! She holds her own! Just the perfect blend of spirited, sweet and spunky backed up with puppy eyes and cuddles. Curly does not disappoint If you have been looking for a puppy who will grow into a life-long companion, you have found your girl! With her shiny black coat, warm brown eyes, she is already working hard on her house-manners, leash training and basic sills. With your continued guidance, she is going to be an excellent student, and master puppy skills 101 in no time! We suspect she will will be medium to upper medium in adulthood, but the love she'll bring, no measure!

name: Braxton
description:
This guy! Braxton's foster mom bets you'll gush over him just like she does! It's impossible not to! He has such an endearing way about him. From his furrowed little brow with just the right amount of wrinkles, to his almost bobbed tail, it's love!

Braxton is a compact, low rider, his head a little too big for his small legs, a waggle when he walks and a personality sure to keep you laughing. At 6 months old, he has impeccable house manners, is crate-trained, good on the leash, great with other dogs (actually, a little submissive) and loves people! He must visit everyone he sees! In terms of breed, to put it simply, he is the definition of mixed! If we had to guess, given his proportions and coloring, we suspect he is a mix of English Bulldog and Rottweiler...maybe some Retriever could be in those genes as well. Currently about 40 pounds, he will likely be about 55 in adulthood, but will remain low and compact. Braxton is going to fill a home and the hearts who live there with love. He has the best soul!

description:

At approximately 6 months old, we suspect Solomon is a mix of Dane and Black Labrador Retriever. As such, he is going to be a large boy (best estimate is near 90-100 pounds), so his ideal home will have room for him to grow! He sports a stunning, shiny black coat and the warmest brown eyes to melt your heart. Approximately 6 months old, he is excellent with other dogs, adores people and is already doing a great job on his house-training. As handsome as they come, he has an incredible personality to match! Comical, lovable and smart! Whoever is lucky enough to adopt this guy will know the love and loyalty of a life-long companion. 

Solomon is available in NY through the Go North Program of The Lucky Puppy Rescue centered in Bonifay and Panama City, FL (NY Lic #1054). name: Raelyn
description:
Raelyn - beautiful name for a beautiful girl, inside and out. Stunning markings and incredible good looks, but this girl doesn't let it go to her head. Instead, she is humble and kind.

Our dear Raelyn is a little shy at first, but quickly warms and her is how her foster family describes her... gentle, kind, smart, playful and the kids adore her! Approximately 6 months old, Raelyn appears to be an Anatolian Shepherd mix, with perhaps a dash of Retriever in her genes. She sports a fawn coat with black points and her gorgeous facial markings make her so expressive! Raelyn loves to play with the other dogs, is excellent with people and would make a terrific companion for walks or swimming...she loves water, and we suspect will love playing in the winter snow (let's hope we have a little while before that happens)! She is house-trained and also walks well on her leash. So deserving of a home to call her own, Raelyn hopes you might be searching for a girl just like her!

Raelyn is available in NY through the Go North Program of The Lucky Puppy Rescue centered in Bonifay and Panama City, FL (NY Lic #1054). description:
