name: XP Scooby - Flanders, NJ
description:
This is our dog Scooby. He is a Beagle and he is 9 years old. He is a sweet and loving couch potato. He's very quiet, you might even forget that he's home with you. He loves to be rubbed especially around his butt area, that's his favorite spot. He's very playful especially with our other dog and friends at the park.

Scooby likes to be comfortable and warm so he loves the bed, the couch and/or he will find a pile of clothes or blanket and lay on it. He is a great dog, you will love him as much as I do. Please help us to try and find a loving home for him.

Scooby is NOT with 11th Hour Rescue but we are helping with the rehoming process. If you are interested in making this boy a part of your family, please contact Abigail directly at either abigailbennett15@icloud.com or 202-468-1244. Scooby is currently located in Flanders, NJ.

name: Pablo -- Courtesy Post
description:
This handsome gentledog impresses everyone he meets: affectionate, polite, playful, and so clearly grateful to have even a minute of your attention. How was this guy an unclaimed stray at an animal shelter?? 

Pablo especially loves being rubbed on his head and behind his ears. So far he seems friendly with the other dogs here, but he draws the line at cats so should go to a home without kitties. 

Outside, he has a good bit of energy -- you'd never guess he is about 10 years old. Pablo can be a bit mouthy when excited, so, though he loves people of all ages, he is not recommended for a home with small children. 

Pablo is a courtesey post. For more information please call his rescue, Safe Shelter, at 814-485-1579 or 301-478-3206, or email them: safeshelterinc@yahoo.com. Safe Shelter is located in Flintstone, MD, but his fans in Frederick will help arrange a meeting in or near Frederick if that's more convenient. :-)

name: Dingo
description: Dingo loves toys and can be playful, yet he also has a very gentle and calm nature. With people, he is affectionate and easy-going. He also walks very nicely on a leash. Dingo was born in 2013 and came to Best Friends from a rescue organization in Florida. At the Sanctuary, he is working on crate training and basic training cues. Due to an old injury, he currently takes prescription medication for pain. Because Dingo has shown aggression toward other dogs in the past, he cannot live with them and must be the only dog in a home. If you're looking for a calm, quiet dog to be your one and only, Dingo would love to meet you.

name: Hercules
description: Hercules is a super playful dog who loves meeting new people at the Sanctuary. At Dogtown, he loves meeting and playing with new dogs and has demonstrated amazing dog skills. He will adapt to other dogs' play styles, but he does love to roughhouse, run and jump around. He spends some of his time in our Headquarters offices, and snuggling on the couch is his favorite past time. Hercules was born in 2016 and came to the Sanctuary from a Best Friends Network partner shelter in Florida. Because he has bitten in the past, he will need a dog-savvy, adult-only household. An active home would also be best for Hercules, though he does know when it's time to chill out and relax.

name: Scooby
description: Scooby is a fun-loving dog. He is energetic and playful and has done well with all the dogs he's met at the Sanctuary. Born in 2016, Scooby was rescued from Hurricane Irma in Florida. He loves attention and excitement, but he can get nippy if his boundaries aren't respected, so he'll do best in an adult-only household. Because Scooby can get a raspy cough when he gets too excited or overdoes it while playing, he is practicing calm behavior at the Sanctuary. However, he'll still enjoy a home where he can be his fun and active self.

name: Axel
description: Axel is a 2 year old neutered male Wire-haired terrier mix. He is Rascal's brother. He's a little more higher energy than his sister, but is a very fun and sweet dog. He was saved from Florida just before the hurricane. Axel is a good boy who craves attention. He loves being all over you and giving kisses. He loves playing with the other fosters. Scoobie and Axel were fostered together and can play together in the play/exercise yard. He is available after 9/17/19. Apply at http://www.saveadog.org/applytoadopt.asp

name: Scooby

Scoobie is a neutered male 1 year old super laid back, easy going, fun, wonderful fawn colored Lab/Dane, possibly Mastiff mix pup saved from Florida just before the hurricane. description: Huntress Wizard is on her way! She's a sweet & sassy medium pup that comes from Florida. Named after the badass Huntress Wizard from Adventure Time, she'll be sure to swing into your hearts and you won't be able to resister her. To adopt or foster: bit.ly/BadassApp

name: Meadow
description:
Meadow is a 38 pound, 8 month old, female, Lab Mix. She arrived this week from Florida where her shelter had to evacuate due to Hurricane Dorian threats. Meadow has handled her move like a total pro! She loves to meet new people while out and about on walks around NYC. As soon as you meet Meadow you'll see her signature move... a hug and a kiss! She has plenty of confidence outside on her leash, not phased by all the commotion going on around us in NYC. She also knows how to do her business outside! Meadow is friendly with other dogs and is always looking for a playmate. This sweet girl has a lot of love to give and will be sure to brighten your day. 

Meadow has been spayed and is up to date on vaccinations. For more information about her, please fill out an application at www.ALRcares.com and email Julie@ALRcares.com.

name: Dragonfly
description:
Meet the sweetest girl around! Dragonfly is a 48 pound, 5 year old, female, Lab Mix. Dragonfly has had quite the week. She just arrived from Florida where her shelter had to evacuate due to Hurricane Dorian threats. So far she is a natural in NYC. She loves to go on walks around the city and has enjoyed taking in all the sights and smells of central park, never hesitating to say hello to all the tourists.  From the moment we met her, we knew Dragonfly was a special girl. Just as friendly and social as can be, she gets along with every dog she meets and is very polite to the little ones as to not scare them with her size. She has taken to NYC like a natural, she knows to do her business outside and is not phased one bit by all the loud sounds and chaos of the city. Dragonfly is a ball of love and such a trooper after her big journey. This cute pup will make a great addition to your family!

Dragonfly has been spayed and is up to date on vaccinations. For more information about her, please fill out an application at www.ALRcares.com and email Julie@ALRcares.com.

name: Chalupa
description:
please see the note from his rescuer... A man tossed him out at the garbage collection site near the shelter. The site attendant flagged u down and he ran right to us and jumped in the animal control truck. He is coming in from Florida.

Incoming! Please meet Chalupa! He is wonderful with everyone and everything. He is HW pos.. which we'll treat. More info to come as we get to know him... including an age estimate.

description:
Meet Chop! Chop is a great boy that has stolen all of our hearts here! This ray of sunshine is always happy, he loves people, and wants nothing more than a home that will love, snuggle, and play with him! He has had quite the journey to get to Sarl so he can find his furever home. If you would like to read about Chop's heartwarming journey from Florida to New Hampshire please check out the link below to read his story. You will need to copy and paste the link as a new web address. 

https://www.eagletribune.com/news/new_hampshire/saved-from-death/article_d869edbc-522b-5b80-a539-94e2433ed8a7.html

Chop loves to play and is a very energetic and enthusiastic player, so he should go with children aged 10 and up who are not easily knocked down. Chop could potentially go with children as young as 8 years old as long as the family is dog savvy and understands he may jump up and become mouthy. 
Additionally, the adopter of Chop should recognize that Chop is partially blind due to retinal atrophy and can become spooked if he can't see someone walking towards him. Usually calling his name and talking to him does the trick. Once he hears his name and your voice he will look for you. Once he finds you, watch out! He will bombard you will lots of slobbery kisses and will try to sit in your lap! :) He just has so much love to give and really needs a family to share it with.
This boy will make an amazing addition to his new family! If you would like to meet this sweet boy, come down to Salem Animal Rescue League during adoption hours! www.salemanimalrescueleague.org or contact laurelsilvia@comcast.net. Chop is currently in Salem NH.

name: Lily
description:
Gorgeous Lily simply leaves us breathless! This gorgeous, Alpha Diva Husky mix will make Northern breed lovers weak in the knees, but she needs seasoned Husky folks willing to focus on her ongoing training, and rein in her chutzpah. 

Lily came to us last year from a Florida rescue, who asked for our help in solving some behavior quirks that they thought stemmed from some physical abuse in her former home. Lily was slow to trust stangers and very hand shy. She recoiled to human touch and seemed skittish.

Often we find that a Husky's beauty is his or her downfall. These stunning dogs attract a wide array of adopters ranging from extremely savvy, to those novices bewitched with his or her \"wolf-like\" appearance. We believe wholeheartedly that a Husky, regardless of individual temperment, requires dog handling ability that is well above average. Time and time again, we have known Huskies who have foiled the best laid intentions of their novice adopters.

At the age of four, Lily is a formidable presence. She is a Husky mix (possibly part German Shepherd), and weighs in at a very solid 60 pounds. She is tall and leggy, and extremely athletic. While Lily has a generally friendly demeanor and seems to enjoy the attentions of strangers, she also has a very well entrenched Alpha Diva vibe, and requires some serious handling chops and command presence in an adopter. 

Lily would be the ideal companion for very serious Husky folks, who are comfortable establishing rules and boundaries with Huskies, or other large breeds, so that Lily knows exactly where she stands. A loosey-goosey home structure will allow her to assert herself in ways that are not optimal for a human-canine living arrangement! 

The key to success with Lily is a sufficient amount of exercise, and ongoing obedience training to maintain leadership. She is a high-energy dog who needs a couple brisk leash walks each day and, preferably, an active outdoor lifestyle, with a Husky savvy single or couple. She would be the ideal running or walking companion, and would love to accompany her adopters on hiking or camping adventures. She loves the outdoors, and needs to be in a active home, in which she can be integrated into a lifestyle, not relegated to a backyard.

Lily would be best-suited to an only dog environment, or perhaps with one other compatible male. While Lily can be bossy and demanding in the Dog Pack, we certainly wouldn't rule out the right dog chemistry, but we would have to test this carefully at adoption. She seems to have some buddies in her canine playgroup, but then also seems to bully some dogs of lesser stature. We don't think that she would be suitable for a home with cats or small children. 

Lily has decent house manners, that will continue to improve under her adopter's patient, knowledgeable leadership. She is house trained and crate trained, although adopters should expect an accident or two during her transition to a new home. Lily is in excellent health, and has been spayed, and is up to date on routine shots and has tested negative for heartworm and tick borne disease. If you are interested in Lily, please call or text Denise at 860-908-9738, or email Denise@eskiesonline.com for an adoption application.

About us: We are an active multi-breed dog rescue local to New England, situated in Canterbury, Connecticut. Our 21 year history is reflected in our website EskiesOnline.com, and on our Facebook page: Eskies Online.

name: Merlin
description:
****IF YOU ARE INTERESTED**** Visit our website to complete an adoption application: www.nakedkissesdogrescue.org/adoption.


Intake 7/5; Available for adoption on 8/2. 


- 17lbs

- Good with dogs and cats

- Good with men, women, children over 12

- Sweet but takes time to open up

Merlin came to us from a shelter in Florida. They estimated him to be 8 years old, and our vet thinks maybe 10-11 years old. He looks to have not been well cared for during at least part of his life, but he will never know what that is like again. The tops of his ears are missing, possibly from either trauma or frostbite. He wasn't neutered. His ears were horribly infected with pseudomonas, maybe even MRSA. Our vet thinks he had some past trauma to part of his cervical spine, and either that or the ear infection causes a head tilt - which looks pretty cute. It doesn't seem to bother him.

We began working on the ear infection with antibiotics and drops, and his ears are doing much better. There is irreversible damage inside that was done, and he has some hearing loss. Since treating the ear infection, he seems to have recouped some hearing and is responding to us when we call him loudly or if he hears a loud noise. Bonus: thunderstorms don't bother him!

Merlin is a sweet dog but took a few days to start showing personality. Now he is goofy, even playful sometimes! He is a Velcro dog with his foster mom and follows her everywhere she goes. He LOVES car rides. He sleeps with his foster parents at night and doesn't move all night. He has learned to walk on a leash and does so very nicely. He loves getting petted on his face, and he lovvvesss getting his back rubbed above his tail. He dances his rear so hard that sometimes both legs come off the ground at the same time.

Merlin is definitely a Crested because he despises grass. He has gotten really good about using the potty outside, but he has to be set outside most of the time. He won't go out far in that treacherous grass, so sometimes we carry him to the far corner once or twice to make sure he has finished up his business. Housetraining is coming along nicely.

Also a classic Crested trait, is separation anxiety! Merlin says he wants a home where someone is almost always home. He is not a candidate for anyone who works away from home or who is routinely gone for more than a few hours. He will howl and howl and howl if he is separated from his people! Because of that, he also cannot live in attached living because the neighbors may not appreciate his singing.

Perhaps not a Crested trait, but maybe just a trait for anyone who really loves their sleep... Merlin doesn't like being woken up when it's time to leave the couch and go to bed at night. There is no picking him up and waltzing off to the bedroom. Merlin will not just growl, he will warning snap and be annoyed that his beauty sleep was interrupted. We think this is partly because he doesn't want to be bothered, but we also think a big part of it was his ear infection hurting him. He has gotten so much better with every night. We have found it's easiest to just tug on his blanket until he gets up, and that is working well. He's also very food motivated, so if a treat is dangled in his face, he gets right up. We believe in time, this reaction would go away. His ears are feeling better, and he has started to feel settled and at home.

He has allowed people to pet him when on walks, but he has demonstrated body posture that says he does not want them to pet him, so we ask people not to pet him. We feel that will get better with more practice and socialization too, but we like to err on the side of caution and keeping him feeling comfortable.

Merlin loves car rides! He would be great company for anyone who takes long road trips. His foster family takes him along on errands all the time because he really loves it.

Overall, Merlin is a really great dog and is going to make someone the best companion. He is super sweet, adores his foster mom (even our vet commented on that), and the rest of his family are pretty cool too when she's busy. He cannot be placed in a home with children under 12 years old. 

Merlin is up to date on vaccines, heartworm negative, and is microchipped. His senior blood panel was great. He had a dental on 7/10.  He will be ready for adoption on August 2.

name: Bobby
description:
Bobby is available for foster or foster-to-adopt. He's currently being fostered in Bradenton, FL (Manatee County). Bobby is a sweet sweet Jack Russell mix who would love to have a forever home! Other dogs?? That's okay!! By himself?? That's okay too. What Bobby does is roll with the punches. He came to us from a very high-kill shelter in Florida. He has had surgery twice for removal of benign growths. We have not had to do anymore surgeries. He came through with flying colors, considering he is heartworm positive. He will be treated in August, and we are looking for a foster, that can carry him through heartworm treatment, ideally fall in love with him and adopt him. Best. Jack. Ever. He is not noisy, but barks when you come home, not a crazy busy Jack. Loves to go out and explore. He even swims. He loves to be loved on. Follows you around. Expert lizard and fly chaser. Loves toys, balls and squeakies.. Walks great on lead, and loves to ride in the car. He is the perfect companion. He will sleep when you do, be active when you are. He would like someone that is home a lot, or another dog to keep him company. Fenced yard is preferred, but not sure he needs one. He seems to want to stay with you. Crates easily, housebroken, just an all around good guy. Heartworm treatment will be done in St. Petersburg, so the ability to take him to treatment is a must. Bobby is the perfect companion dog.

name: Toby
description:
Toby is an adorable 18 pound, red and white Basenji mix with very distinctive ears. His estimated date of birth is October 2016. He came to ARF from a shelter in Fort Smith after being rescued as an unclaimed stray. This sweet guy had a tough time coping with anxiety, and spent time in the medical unit because he was so scared. He is doing extremely well in a foster home after being given a chance to adjust at his own pace. He is housetrained, with a few accidents here and there. He is crate trained at night, and rests quietly when his crate is covered. 

Toby loves being around other dogs. He is energetic and playful, but also submissive. The two dogs in his foster home have helped his adjustment immensely. He does okay with older kids, but may not be a good fit around younger ones. He chases the cat living in his foster home, but hasn't tried to hurt her. As he has been adjusting to his foster home, he has growled and barked at the members of his foster family. However, he responds well to verbal correction, and this behavior is declining in frequency as he becomes more comfortable.

Toby is very companionable and likes being around people. He follows his foster mom around the house keeping her company in various rooms. His only really bad habit is that he likes to chew, with a particular affinity for shoes and cords. This can be easily managed by providing bones and toys, and keeping human things picked up. Toby shows his Basenji heritage with unusual vocalizations in addition to little barks and growls.

Toby's ideal forever home would be with a family who is patient enough to allow him to acclimate at his own pace. The perfect home for Toby will have at least one other dog, and no young kids. They will also have the ability to tolerate toileting accidents, and to remember to pick up things he's likely to chew. Toby is a smart, resilient little guy, who will be a wonderful addition to his forever family.Toby has a $150.00 adoption fee plus the cost of 6 months of heartworm prevention. 

Note: ARF reserves the right to deny any application that is deemed unsuitable for the animal. Please be aware that our animal adoptions are NOT on a first come- first serve basis. Our sole purpose is to find the best possible home for the animals that fall under our care. We do not ship our animals. All adopters are expected to come to Tulsa if approved.

For details on how to adopt please visit http://www.arftulsa.org/adopt

description:
So, let's talk about Hershey. This pretty girl is wondering why noone has snapped her up yet. Honestly, so are WE!

Hershey is a spunky, adorable spark plug of a dog. She'll fake you out on first meeting by displaying a shy countenance but then look out! We knew she'd shine in a home and we're so glad we snatched her from Franklin County's dreaded euthanasia list. I mean come on, look at this girl!

Does she sound like a match for you? Let's find out! Apply at www.stormsangelsrescue.org

description:

While at the shelter they treated me for ear infections and found I don't hear very well (not sure if this is permanent or not), but I am a guy afterall (#selectivehearing).

Adoption donations are $250 for an adult, $350 for puppies (a dog under one year of age), and $125 for a senior dog (based on the age of the dog). All dogs are spay/neutered, have rabies, distemper vaccine, microchip, heartworm test if age appropriate, and are current on heartworm preventative. Adoption donations are accepted via cash or debit/credit card. There is a $5 fee to run a card.

Please remember to bring a collar and leash with you the day of the adoption.

description:
Hello, my name is Cardi, although my foster mom usually calls me \"Sweet Girl\" or \"Pretty girl.\" I came to ODHS from a hoarding situation, and when I got to my foster house, I wouldn't even come out of the back of my crate for the first 2 days. Since they had me come out of my crate, they've been working with me a little more every day and they tell me how proud of me they are for making progress every day. I've been with my foster family for about a month now and I've gotten much more comfortable with them. I love to follow my foster mom around the house everywhere she goes. I wag my tail and do my happy dance when I see my foster family now. I went from being scared of them, to loving getting pets and treats from them. I love treats! I hardly ever run into my crate when they are home now, because I enjoy being out in the house with my foster fam. I do great with going potty outside in my little puppy pen. I stay in a crate when my humans leave the house and at bedtime. I have 3 human siblings (ages 7-11) in my foster family and 2 canine siblings that are both close to my size. I have done well with my human siblings because they are very calm and patient with me. I don't think I would like to be with young kids that don't know how to be patient and calm with me and give me my space to build up trust with them. I now love playing with dog toys and chasing balls. I love running around and playing with my 2 year old canine brother.  I'm not a big fan of my older canine foster brother though. I have come a long way during my time in my foster home, so although I'll have a transition period to go through in my new home, I know I would blossom with having a fur-ever family. I would love a family that understands that I will need time and patience to build up trust and know that they are good and love me and help me to understand that the world isn't so scary. I am potty trained but on occasion will have an accident inside if left alone for too long. I get along fine with other dogs as long as they aren't annoying me by constantly getting in my personal space, so another older guy or gal like me would be ideal. I'd also prefer older kids as I don't care to be climbed on or have my fluffy tail pulled. I like to be in the presence of my humans & sleeping in their room. I like to roam the house during the day & to snooze on the couch. If you're not looking, I'll be sure to steal any food that I'm able to reach (trash included). I'm a great alert dog, making sure my humans know when unauthorized people or animals come near the house. I'm a good boy. I also love being groomed (brushed, bathed, hairdryer, etc.) although I may need to be muzzled when trimming my nails. If you scratch my butt, I'll never leave you alone.

name: Roco
description:
Hello! I'm Roco. I traveled all the way from Puerto Rico to find my furever family! I'm what you call a street dog, the product of little to no spay/neuter in my area. I was born in March and I am doing so well with crate training.  I sleep in my crate overnight and don't have any accidents (a whole 8 hours).  As far as potty training in my foster home, that is a work in progress, but I am doing very well. I'm a little slow to trust, but I warm up pretty quick.  I prefer females and am afraid of tall men (they are so big).  I am a super jumper if you want to teach me agility.  I'd also love to be trained so I can get those yummy treats (which are the key to my heart).

description:
Mika is starting to get more comfortable in her foster home, but is still hesitant of people, so no cuddling for this girl. name: Wes
description:
Hi guys, I am Wes. I am pretty old and tired, my eyes and ears are not working so well these days. My brother and I ended up with the fine people at the Old Dominion Humane Society after our elderly owner passed way. My brother was a little younger and lucky enough to get adopted, I miss him but I am happy for him. Like most older gentlemen I have some hair loss but with grooming I am looking much better. I spend most of my day sleeping and resting, I sleep quietly in my kennel at night and I have been doing really well about doing my business outside. I do fine with other dogs as long as they do not keep me from napping. I walk on a leash well outside but really struggle with stairs. I think this is because of my poor eyesight. Good news is I only weigh about 10 pounds so I am not heavy to carry. I get along with everyone and enjoy getting pets, oh and kids are great too! I know I might be as cute as some of the young pups and yes I am in the later chapters of my life but I am willing to give you every ounce of love I have left. If you are looking for a sweet quiet older gentlemen to warm your lap in the coming months then I am your guy. Please stop by to see me even if it is just for a short visit.  
 
Thanks,

Wes

name: Rose Talbot-Bassador
description:
09/10/19

I have had the pleasure of Rose Talbot being a houseguest in our home for the past 3 months; I guess I should say she is like one of my own.  She is a sweet and gentle girl who needs to trust and understand love.  She truly hangs on her bed for 95% of her day.  Her exercise consists of running from the backdoor to her bed.  She ventures out to let us know when she wants to go outside or we are late with her meal.  She loves her soft food and treats.  She still goes submissive when you reach down to pet her, but she has improved.  She provides her fur foster siblings with kisses as they come over to check on her.  I will share she would do best in a home that will give her time to adjust, earn her trust and provide a soft bed to lay in.  She really is a low maintenance dog that has captured the heart of her foster mom.  I keep telling her that the perfect family has not come yet, but one day although it will be sad they will come and finally give her her forever home, the one that will provide her with the love and attention she truly deserves.



7/1/19

So are you looking for a new best friend that is so appreciative of the little things?  Are you looking for a gentle soul that just wants a soft bed and love that she deserves?  Are you looking for a new companion that will melt your heart every time you look into her eyes?  Look no further!!!!

Meet Rose, a very gentle girl that finally is getting the love and attention that she deserves.  She has a tough life, but things are looking up for this sweet girl.  She recently made her trip north from Georgia to begin her journey to find a home she can call her own.  

Although she wears her past, she has been doing well with housetraining, gets along with her fur foster siblings, and loves belly rubs.  Unfortunately Rose needed 23 teeth removed, I believe she is feeling so much better; she loves her canned food. name: Jake ( courtesy post)
description:
Hello my name is Jake, 
My family adopted me almost 4 years ago in Cumberland RI. My paperwork said I was a lab/husky mix from Georgia, I wasnât quite a year old yet (according to my paperwork).
When they showed up to get me I was very shy and I smelled pretty terrible, I am surprised they brought me home. After we arrived home I was given a wonderful tubbie with warm water and oatmeal shampoo. I was nice and clean and ready to play. They took me to a soccer game ? 
I had an older brother named Joshua that was 9 years old, he loved to hug me and play with me. 
I had one accident when I was brought home, and I loved my crate. There were two cats at my new home, and they really did not interest me very much, they lived downstairs and I was the king of the upstairs living area. I could go outside whenever I wanted on my run that was in the back yard. 
I had two husky friends next door that I would talk to through the fence. 
My family brought me to two different training classes, but I was told that I needed individual training. 
Mom bought me a prong collar because I would pull her when we would go for a walk, it doesnât hurt, but it reminds me that I cannot pull my Mom when we walk. 
In April 2017 my family started taking care of a 4-month-old infant every weekend to help my momâs best friend. To this day Hunter is still my best friend, and I do not like it when he must leave on Sundayâs. He feeds me my food and gives me my favorite milk bone cookies all the time. Yum! 
My mom and dad love taking me on trips with them because I am not a big fan of the kennel. 
I have been to Dover Foxcroft Maine several times, I love it up there because I can run free. I love all the snow that they get up there and I love chasing my Mom and my brother on their bikes when they are riding down the road. I get a lot of exercise when I am in Maine. 
I have also been to the Outer Banks of North Carolina, I love the sunshine and the beach! I had my own bunk bed in the house we rented for a weekâ¦..I did very well in the truck on the way down and the stop at the hotel over night so we could rest. 
Last week I was in Old Orchard beach laying under my umbrella watching the waves.  I love to go walking and for rides in the truck, my crate and my blanket is my safe place and I have my own room.
 At night we play with my toys, my humans throw them and I run to fetch my squeekies. 
While growing up I started to display some behaviors that my family was not very happy with. I became extremely protective of my humans and I do not like it when people come to visit or strangers come up to me and try to pet me. When my older brother has friends over I have to go in my room in my crate to make sure everyone is safe. I have not bitten anybody but when my family left me over night to go to the water park our neighbor (my momâs close friend) was letting me out to pee and I refused to let her in the house to take me out.  Recently we found out that I was not a lab husky mix, I am actually a lab/chow mix, so that explains why my tongue is black and my behaviors. 
I know that my family loves me very much, they work very hard and do not always have the time to give me the exercise that I need. My older brother is slacking, and he does not let me out to pee when my Mom and Dad are not home, I hear my Mom say itâs a teen thing. They have me training with an E-collar now and Iâm doing very well with. 
My humans want me to be happy and safe and feel that I belong with a single person that has time to exercise with me. I love the kids in my family, but I donât know about other children. 
I am an excellent guard dog and I am totally house broken; my humans never have to lock the doors in the house because nobody is getting passed me. 
I am hoping to find a good home and promise to love you unconditionally like I do my Mom, but before I get into trouble she thinks it is best to see if there is a better living situation for me. I know this is breaking my Momâs heart, but she is trying to protect me. 

If interested in me please email Kimberly Larson at krlarson13@gmail.com

name: Jack
description:
Jack is an approximately 6 year old lab mix from Georgia where he was found as a stray.  Although microchipped, his previous owners never responded to phone calls placed to them regarding finding Jack and therefore he was taken off of stray hold 7 days later and saved by our partners Animal SOS in Georgia. 

We agreed to take Jack and are committed to finding him a forever home.  

Jack is an extremely laid back kind of dog.  He is eager to please and is well trained in all of the standard commands.  He truly just wants a family to be around so he can relax knowing he is loved and cared for.

He is fully housetrained and does well with dogs and cats.

Heâs been on the road for we donât know how long but he certainly never forgot his manners or tricks or how to please and be a companion animal.

He has some lumps and bumps which have been biopsied and have been diagnosed as lipomas and therefore not removed as the vet felt it wasnât necessary.

He has some significant hair loss from a flea infestation which has been managed with some medicated flea baths and nextguard.  He also has bacteria on his skin that he has been given medicated baths for but nothing contagious.

Heâs had a rough time
With pneumonia and has been treated at the emergency vet with antibiotics and nebulizers.  We have repeated xrays multiple times to ensure it continues to improve and have extended courses of antibiotics to ensure he gets back to full health.

He is heartworm negative.

We have been giving him
Liquid collagen to help his skin and hair as well.

He continues to gain weight as needed and is currently at 86 lbs.

Jack does still love to play and learn.  Fetch with a ball is his favorite.

Jack would be an amazing family dog if you are looking for the total package.  He absolutely adores kids and watches over them
Wherever they go.

He comes with a reduced adoption fee as well given his age as we would like that money to go toward helping him continue to get better.

name: DG
description:
Meet DG! This little porker is just too cute. Sheâs a min pin, but missed the memo on the min part :-) We think it makes her only that more adorable and lovable! DG was an owner surrender from a very rural area of Georgia. She was neglected, living outside and being fed chocolate as a regular diet and was even more obese than she is now. We knew we had to get her out of there before she was dead. DG has been in rescue now and has gotten healthy. She has lost some weight (still has more to go!) and gotten spayed. She is a very sweet and quiet girl from what we have seen. DG seems to be good with other dogs; even excitable big dogs trying to play with her. We think she is about 10 years old. DG would love a retirement home and is anxiously awaiting her family while in her foster home in Baltimore County, MD. She is available immediately and foster or adoption applications can be found at www.snarrnortheast.org 
Her adoption fee is $250.

name: Linus
description: Born around May 2016 and arrived at TVR April 23, 2019 Linus is a very special boy who will need a patient, calm, and loving home to help him come out of his shell. He was likely not exposed too much as a young puppy; perhaps he was a stray in the early part of his life. We don't really know the root cause but for Linus the world can be a scary place. In the month that he has been in our care, he has become more confident and secure in his surroundings. He is still easily startled but is able to recover more than when he first arrived to us from Georgia. He has gone from staying in one corner, rarely moving throughout the day, to walking around, wagging his tail when he sees staff, and barking when he sees other dogs. He likes to play with the other dogs and is slowly gaining more confidence interacting with humans. In spite of his fears, he does know how to walk on leash and seems to be relatively house-trained, though accidents are likely during any new, stressful transitions. Linus would probably do best in a home with another dog who is friendly and able to show him the ropes. Because he startles so easily and could bolt out an open door in a panic, he would probably be better in a home without young children. We see so much potential in this sweet guy and with a little time and compassion, we think he could turn into a happy, loving companion. (A note about housetraining: Linus, like many rescue dogs, does seem to be housetrained but Their Voice Rescue does not guarantee that he won't have accidents or behavioral marking incidents in a new home.)

name: Lollie
description:
LOLLIE is a big, mushy, sweet 2-year-old, 55-pound, Black Labrador Retriever mix with a passel of adorable little pups.

Lollie came to us from Georgia, where she had to fend for herself as a lonely stray.  One fine day she wandered onto the property of a family who's male dog lived outside on a chain.  Lollie and the handsome stranger struck up a friendship and soon became romantically involved.  She soon gave birth to a litter, but for reasons unknown to us, the puppies did not survive.

The family, doing what they must have thought to be the right thing, allowed Lollie to stay on at their house, sharing outdoor accommodations with their dog. Before very long... well, there's no need to finish that sentence.  This time the family realized that something had to be done and had the presence of mind to get her into rescue.  So she left Georgia on a midnight train, (a rescue transport), and 12 or so hours later, arrived at the shelter of Animal Alliance.  Two days after her arrival she gave birth to her litter, the beautiful little pups are safe and sound in our care.  As of this writing, 7/18 the little ones are 4 weeks old.  In a few more weeks, the whole little family, including Momma, will be spayed/neutered, vaccinated, et cetera, and ready to take their rightful places in their new adoptive families.

If you would like to meet, foster or adopt Lollie, all you have to do is fill out our online FOSTER/ADOPTION APPLICATION, which can be found in the main menu of our website or at the bottom of this page - just copy and paste the link into your browser. 

Once we've reviewed your application, you can come and meet Lollie!  We think the two of you will hit it off!

Thank you for your interest in helping homeless animals!

***

This pet is spayed or neutered in accordance with our strict policy wherein all animals are altered prior to adoption.  This pet is dewormed, current on vaccines, and started on monthly flea/tick and preventatives.

Animal Alliance's policy is that we will adopt dogs younger than 1 year old to families with children under 9 years old. We do not adopt dogs 1 year or older to families with children under 9 years old due to the unknown history of adult dogs. 

Prior to submitting an application, please see the Animal Alliance Adoption Process for adoption details.

Animal Alliance is not a shelter where all the animals are housed in one location. Animal Alliance is a foster care network and animals are housed in many different locations. If you are interested in adopting a pet, please apply using the online application; applicants who call our phone line will hear a recorded voicemail with this identical message. We adopt many animals each week and meet prospective adopters at various locations so they can meet the animals they are interested in.

To fill out an adoption application, go to:
https://www.animalalliancenj.org/fosteradoption-application/

    Iâm about a big, handsome, 3 year old lemon boy, and FULL of life! I was found as a stray and saved from the Georgia shelter before coming to my foster family in North Carolina. They got me some good food and a doctor of my own, and Iâm almost ready to start the next (and best) chapter of my life! My doctor is taking care of my heart worms and I will finish treatment and be ready to go to my new family in mid-September. 

    My favorite things are food, playing with my ball in the yard, playing with my foster brothers, snacks, running in the yard, and eating. Did I mention playing and eating?!

    My ideal family would spend time running and playing with me, and maybe has a human or dog friend, too! Initially, I was evaluated as not being good with cats, but I donât pay my foster-cat-brother any attention at all. I really hate thunder storms, but my parents have some medicine that helps me not be as scared. I donât really love taking baths, but Iâm told they have to be done.

    If you think I may be the one for you, just let PRO know! My foster parents would love to get to know you!

name: Rose Talbot-Bassador
description:
09/10/19

I have had the pleasure of Rose Talbot being a houseguest in our home for the past 3 months; I guess I should say she is like one of my own.  She is a sweet and gentle girl who needs to trust and understand love.  She truly hangs on her bed for 95% of her day.  Her exercise consists of running from the backdoor to her bed.  She ventures out to let us know when she wants to go outside or we are late with her meal.  She loves her soft food and treats.  She still goes submissive when you reach down to pet her, but she has improved.  She provides her fur foster siblings with kisses as they come over to check on her.  I will share she would do best in a home that will give her time to adjust, earn her trust and provide a soft bed to lay in.  She really is a low maintenance dog that has captured the heart of her foster mom.  I keep telling her that the perfect family has not come yet, but one day although it will be sad they will come and finally give her her forever home, the one that will provide her with the love and attention she truly deserves.

name: SCHROEDER CROSS-POST PORTLAND, MAINE
description:
This handsome fella is Schroeder - a small JRT/Hound, maybe some bully breed in the mix, roughly 5 year old dog brought up from Georgia to Maine by another Maine rescue several years ago when he was a puppy, and is now finding himself in need of a new home. Although his original adoptive family has gone above and beyond with training and working with Schroederâs behaviors over the years, the living environment is just proving to be too much for him despite everyoneâs best and continued efforts to ensure he is not constantly stressed.

Schroeder is a sweet, energetic dog who really loves his people. Although he has been living with young kids for some time and does very well with âhis ownâ, he gets very stressed with the busy neighborhood kids and spooks easily, causing his behavior to worsen while on walks or trying to enjoy any outdoor time and he becomes reactive to other dogs and sometimes people. Ideally he needs a quiet, adult home with older/no children. A condo environment would not work well for him. It is possible he could coexist with another calm, confident dog, but Schroeder will need time to decompress and adjust through this transition so he should be treated as an only dog and be kept calmly separated from any other dogs in the home at least during this initial period. Cats are probably a no-go as his hound instincts send him on a chase.

We are helping to network Schroeder for a new home as we feel he deserves this second chance to find his ideal forever family, and sadly his original rescue is not willing or able to take him back and place him due to liability concerns. We realize that Schroeder is not an easy to place dog, and readily available fosters for a dog like him simply do not exist, but we feel he is a trainable, adoptable dog and he deserves the chance to find that special someone willing to put in the extra effort to provide him with a happy, calm lifestyle. With proper training, invested time and commitment, he has SO much potential and will be a great dog in the right home.

Schroederâs owners are not asking for a re-homing fee, but that his new people continue working with a positive trainer to ensure he has the resources and skills needed to manage his stressors and ensure a successful placement.

If you are interested in helping about this pocket-sized guy, please fill out an application on our website: 
www.buddyupanimalsociety.org/dog-adoption-application

Please help us share Schroeder and find him that perfect forever home he needs and deserves!

? If you have any questions please feel free to email us at info@buddyupanimalsociety.org ?

Thank you for reading about and sharing Schroeder, let's help find this boy his true forever!

description:

Hogan is a black lab/retriever mix around 3 years old that weighs about 45 lbs. He came to us from one of the worst animal shelters in the rural mountains of Georgia. A rescue person saw his picture, went to meet him there, and decided this boy needed to be saved.

Hogan's very favorite thing to do is PLAY! Perhaps that's because he came from a place where he sat alone in a run with nothing to do all day. :( But whether it be Fetch or tug of war, Hogan loves his toys! He's also been going to Agility with a volunteer friend and he does great on the course! He'll even swim when given the chance! Hogan is a smart boy and knows some basic commands like sit, stay, drop and down. He is housebroken, crate trained, and good with most dogs.

Unfortunately, Hogan was recently returned after being adopted for about 8 months because he became very protective of his home. Hogan needs a strong owner who has experience with protective/territorial dogs. Although he was very loving with his family, we feel that Hogan would do best in a home with no children because of his protectiveness. name: Margo
description:
.Margo is a total cutie pie who is sweet as can be and the kind of dog you can't help but feel happy around because her personality is so joyful.  She is about 3 years old and weighs 50 pounds.  She has been here for a more than a year and would love a home of her own with people that would love her for the rest of her life. She was found as a lost doggie.  She is a hound with beautiful markings.  Margo is spayed, housebroken, up to date with her vaccinations, micro-chipped, and heartworm negative.  She knows the commands of sit, stay, and lay down and walks nicely on a leash.

Margo came from a high kill shelter in Georgia where.her time was almost up.  She is a high energy dog who loves to play and run around in the yard with the other dogs.  She is wonderful with people or dogs.  We don't know how she is with cats.  She has shown no aggression since coming here and only seems to have a loving, sweet nature for anyone who comes her way.  

We think she would be fine with older children but because of her energy level may accidentally knock young children down.  Margo loves to play with her toys, including balls, tugs and hard bones; which she loves to bite on.  

Because Margo is a high energy dog a fenced yard would be a must so she would be able to run around and be safe and secure.  

If u think Margo might fit in your family, please call Judi at (908) 510-8721 or send me an application for her. Just click on the Application Button and return it to Save Us Dog Rescue at fries3@aol.com

name: Layla
description:
Layla is one of the most beautiful dogs we have ever had in our rescue.  She is a female Labrador Retriever mix and is 3 1/2 years old.  She is approx 48 pounds.  Layla is spayed, housebroken, heartworm negative, up to date on her vaccinations, and micro-chipped.  She walks well on a leash and would make a good running partner. Layla knows the commands of sit and stay. she also knows how to give her paw and to down when asked. Her favorite thing to do is sit on your lap and go to sleep. Layla also loves to give kisses and cuddle. She has been here for more than two years and no one has shown much interest in her. 

Layla has come into rescue from a kill shelter in Georgia where her time was almost up.  She is doing well since coming into rescue and loves to give kisses and would love nothing more than to sit on your lap and snuggle. Her eyes are the most gorgeous color and seem to penetrate through you as she looks at you. 
She takes her treats very gently from your hand.  We believe Layla would do well with children but care should be taken with very young children who could be knocked over by accident through play.

If u think she might be a match for your family, please email Save Us Dog Rescue at fries3@aol.com or call Judi at (908) 510-8721.

name: Matilda
description:
Meet Matilda! (I've been calling her \"Mattie some too.)

This girl was a stray that we rescued from a shelter in Georgia. She was so sweet, we just had to get her out of that loud and scary place.

She is around a year old and weighs just under 11 pounds. The vet checked her over and said she was a healthy girl, other than fleas and we took care of that! Her best breed guess was Papillon/Terrier mix but whatever the breed is, she is a cutie!

Matilda is spayed current on all vaccines, dewormed, microchipped, heartworm negative, and on heartworm prevention. She must be kept on heartworm prevention all of her life, as all dogs should be.

She is great with most dogs and cats as long as she is slowly introduced (like with most dogs). She can think she is the boss, so some dogs may not appreciate that. Older kids I think would be fine with her, but she's not been \"kid tested\". She seems to be crate trained and we are working on housetraining. She is doing well with that.

The adoption fee is $225 to an approved home. All vet records and her collar will be given to her adopter and the time of adoption.

Here is the link to our adoption application: https://forms.gle/LtT3oVicgYDfrLpL7

The application is to be completed prior to meeting the pet(s) you are interested in adopting. Thank you for looking at our rescues in need of amazing homes!

name: Roxie
description:
Roxie
Pit bull terrier/Cocker Spaniel mix
Spayed female, two years old, 40 lbs. 
Fully vaccinated, dewormed and heartworm negative
If you love pitties and all the love they have to offer then, this is your girl! Roxie is a smart, happy girl who loves to cuddle on the sofa in the home and is also always up for a fun game of fetch in the back yard. She is quick to learn her commands and she will benefit from a dog savvy owner to keep her mentally and physically fit! Like any dog, Roxie needs structure and discipline on a daily basis and she will reward you with love and respect. Housebroken and crate trained, Roxie is a perfect lady in the home. When she was rescued from a high kill shelter in Georgia, she enjoyed playing with a number of dogs at her boarding facility and was sweet and friendly with all her cohorts. 
She still loves to play but is now more selective with her canine playmates. We believe she will flourish in a home as an only dog-yet we are open to the possibility that she may find a perfect forever home with a companionable brother to play the days away with. Roxie is an awesome companion and has a lot of love to give! If you are interested in adopting Roxie, please email littlepups2017@gmail.com or call 757-630-6181.

name: Skyy
description:
Name: Skyy

Approximate Age: Approx. 2yrs old

Breed: Pit mix

Sex: Female

Special Needs: Allergies

Adoption fee: $300.00

Up to date on vaccinations/preventatives, spayed, house/crate trained, microchipped

I came to the rescue back in 2016 from a high kill shelter in Texas. The conditions werent the best to say the least and oh yeah, I was SUPER pregnant. Not a good place for a expecting mom. Thankfully, I was taken from there just in time and was able to have my puppies in a foster home. I was even thrown a huge baby shower by a ton of people who follow SNARR! I was so happy to finally have had my babies and be out of the shelter but my excitement quickly became tragedy. Not long after giving birth, almost half of my babies passed away- only 4 survived. 
Now that my remaining pups have gone to live their own liveshere I sit and wait. While I adore my foster mom, I want a home to call my own. 
Im confused on why I dont have my own home yet Im incredibly adorable and Im hands down the most wiggly tushed pocket pittie youll ever meet! I have never met a person I didnt like, however dogs.not too fond of dogs or any other furry little creatures. I blame that on my high prey drive and Im very smart when it comes down to it- I can be a pro stalker and Im lightning fast so its best that the temptation isnt there in forever home. Give me any kind of human though and its nothing but hugs (literally, I give hugs) and kisses! 
Due to having allergies, I take Benedryl and cannot eat chicken.

Transport to any approved home within the US can be provided at no additional fee
Currently Skyy is located in Lawrenceville, Georgia.


Please visit SNARRANIMALRESCUE.org to fill out an adoption application and our adoption requirements/process can also be found there!

name: Selima
description:
Name: Selima

Approximate Age: 3.5yrs

Breed: Baladi

Sex: Female

Special Needs: Paralyzed

Adoption Fee: $200

Up to date on vaccinations/preventatives. Spayed. Microchipped.

Where I come from people are very unkind to my breed and I was very close to not making it out alive. I was born in Egypt where baladis are considered trash & many people there go out of their way to hurt us. I was born with a hem vertebra and as a very young puppy; a very traumatic injury took away my ability to walk. Some awful individual shot me, rendering me paralyzed. As if that wasnt cruel enough, I was then tossed into a cemetery where I was left to die. Thankfully, not everyone in Egypt is cruel. I was noticed by a person visiting a loved one at the cemetery & was brought to a local rescue for medical care. 
I however was one of the lucky ones. After seeing pictures of how hurt I was, SNARR took me and flew me to the USA to get medical treatment. That was in June 2015. The bullet was removed from my spine and because of the extent of my injuries, my back legs needed to be removed. 
Today, I am a new dog. Even though I dont have any legs, I can cruise around the house just as fast as my four legged siblings. My foster mom has tried to keep diapers on me, but I dont like them so Im not wearing them. I finally trained her, so she just expresses me now & lets me be a naked baby. 
I love playtime with my other siblings, playing dress up for the holidays, snuggling with my foster mom and racing around the house like a maniac. 
There are some things though that make me nervous. Children can be too rambunctious and fast, men can be too big and their voice scares me. My wheelchair? I hate it and would rather be on the ground moving myself. Ive never been around a cat before so Im not sure how I would do with them; I guess they do have the luxury of being able to jump if they want to get away from me though. My ideal home would be with a woman or if there happens to be a man with a soft manner and a ton of patience.

He adores people of all ages, including children, and and absolutely craves attention. He may be a little too enthusiastic for small children, so care will need to be taken in that regard. Diego hasn't gotten the memo that he's larger than your average lap dog, as he loves to get as close as possible to snuggle and offer pittie kisses.

This very smart pup will sit, shake, down and rollover on command; we're still working on 'stay' and 'come.' His leash manners could use some polishing, although a proper harness and additional training will be beneficial. Diego has excellent car manners and will often nod off in the passenger seat. Toys rock his world and this silly guy is always ready to romp and play. He'll chase a ball all day long but hasn't gotten the hang of returning it to you just yet. While Diego shares nicely with humans, he's not inclined to share toys, treats or food with other dogs and may act out in an aggressive manner. He's housebroken and crate trained in foster care and may just need a refresher course in his new home, as he gets the hang of a new routine.

Diego does not do well with dogs who make him feel challenged or threatened. He needs to be your one and only. He's also not a fan of kitties and there can be no cats in his home. If you can offer Diego the exercise, playtime and loving care he craves, he's ready to make your acquaintance. A fenced yard is would be ideal. He's had some hard knocks in life, but Diego has shaken off the dust and is ready for his happily-ever-after to begin.

description:
***Kaydo is currently located in Glenwood, GA but is scheduled to attend our Sept 13-15 adoption event at Rosedale Mills (Pennington, NJ.***

Kaydo came to our rescue as an owner surrender, being among the 19 dogs and puppies that SoCo was asked to find new homes for after their owner was served with an eviction notice. Kaydo was one of his former owner's \"favorites\" and once you spend a little time with him, you'll see why the owner felt that way!

Despite obviously having a hard life, Kaydo remains a very people friendly dog. He also is friendly to most other dogs, especially the females, despite having been attacked by a pack of dogs sometime prior to coming to our rescue. In that attack, Kaydo not only suffered having his left ear ripped in two, his right ear was bitten completely off. His hearing seems fine but his ears will require regular cleanings.

The scars that show on Kaydo's body do not define who he is, you won't find too many dogs as affectionate and loyal as Kaydo. He can be very calm at times, others he just wants to play!

Kaydo has lived and enjoys being both indoors and outdoors. We're not sure how well house trained he is so any potential adopters must be willing to provide additional training, if needed. Kaydo has been fully vetted, kept on his monthly preventatives and recently completed his heartworm treatments.

To apply for the adoption of Kaydo, please submit an application at socorescue.com

He has fun playing fetch with his favorite toy and going on daily walks. Baxter would do well as an only pet or with a friend â he loves everyone!  He is housebroken.

Unfortunately, Baxter was heartworm positive, but he started his treatment and is on his way to a healthy new life. Baxter will be available for adoption after completing his heartworm treatment (early Oct). We are currently taking applications so he can go straight to his new home when ready. Baxter is a foster-to-adopt candidate if you are located in the Greensboro, NC area.

If you are interested in adopting this dog, contact h2hadoptions@gmail.com. An all adult home with a fenced yard (fence must be attached to the home) is required to adopt from Hart-2-Heart Rescue.

Please inquire only if you are willing to come to Greensboro, North Carolina to meet the dog after we schedule your home visit. We do not ship dogs or put them on transports. Adoption fee is $350.

Veterinary Care: All Hart-2-Heart Rescue foster dogs are spayed/neutered, current on heartworm prevention, parvo/distemper, bordetella, and rabies vaccines and are professionally groomed. As needed, our foster dogs have teeth cleanings, extractions, bloodwork and other diagnostic testing.

description:

She was rescued from Halo a few years back. The vet advised her to put her down if she can't find a way to make it work in the home, but sheâs a healthy dog around 5 years old that just needs to be in a home with someone who can love her and show her thatâs the world isnât so bad, and with someone who can help her overcome her trust issues. We definitely do not believe she deserves to lose her life over her lack of trust. 

Jasmine has been nothing but a total sweetheart with humans; we know that with the right home and a good amount of patience, she can be the best dog and make someone really happy!

name: Louise
description:
Here is our sweet girl, Lady Louise!

Buddy Up pulled Louise from Harris County shelter in Houston, Tx with a severe injury to her right eye, nearly 100% proptosis (popping out), which was suspected to be the result of blunt force trauma or injury from another dog. It also appeared to be an injury that she had been suffering with for some time. We don't know the exact details of the trauma Louise experienced, but we do know that she can be a bit overly excited around other dogs, so we need a foster/adoptive home for her either as the only pet, or possibly with another dog similar to her size and energy level that will tolerate her excited energy well as she continues her training. 

Although she is a very sweet girl with all people, she will not be placed in a home with young children due to her her size and energy - she can be a bit clumsy too! Louise is a very excited, bouncy girl and enjoys meeting new people. She is an incredibly sweet, velvety soft pup and everyone that spends times with her cannot help but fall in love. Ideally a mellow adult home able to provide moderate activity to keep her busy and continue training would be perfect for her! No cats for this girl. She is already spayed and up to date on all of her vaccines. 

Louise is an absolute love with everyone she meets and is highly trainable. She is a very smart girl willing and wanting to please, she loves spending time learning new tricks and cuddling up on the couch with company.

Louise is here in Maine and awaiting her forever home. Please email us and send in an application if you can provide a home for this lovely lady! 

Adoption Application: www.buddyupanimalsociety.org/dog-adoption-application

Please email us for additional information: info@buddyupanimalsociety.org

name: Lilly (PA)
description:
Hi, my name is Lil, or as my foster parents call me Lilly Lou. I grew up living in a home in North Carolina but after one of my people passed away the other got really sick and could no longer care for me. I was dropped off at a crowded shelter in the mountains of North Carolina. I wasnât really a big fan of being in the shelter and that is when Pointer Rescue Org showed up and I left with my foster parents. I had a long road trip from North Carolina to Harrisburg, Pennsylvania where Iâm now learning about lots of new things and am excited to find my new forever home. I am a very happy girl that LOVES to be around people and snuggle them on the couch. Every person I have seen I have wanted to meet. The same goes for dogs of all sizes. I enjoy soft, comfortable dog beds where I can get some sun but donât really like laying outside in the hot sun. Iâm not too sure about a lot of dog toys but I really like the soft, fuzzy ones that I can chew on. I get along with the other dog in the house but Iâm not a big fan of playing rough. Just laying around and being close to each other is ok with me. My foster parents tell me I walk well on a leash and donât pull and if I do I know to slow down to let them catch up. I know how to sit, especially if you have some yummy treats for me and will come when called. I LOVE Food and Treats and love to be in the kitchen anytime there is food being cooked. I was told Iâm not the best sous chef but Iâm probably the cutest one. I do like to check out whatâs on the kitchen counter but if you tell me Off I will sadly get off the counter. I enjoy going for walks and hiking but so far I donât like going into any water but I do enjoy a good mud bath. In my dream home I would be the only dog or have a brother or sister that is just as relaxed as me. Iâm a good sleeper and will gladly sleep all night in my kennel unless there is a thunder storm. Iâm not sure about those and if we have one I like to be under the covers in bed with my foster family. If you are looking for a relaxed, sweet southern girl, look no further!

Lil is a white English Pointer with some tan spots. She is around 6-7 years old, up to date on all of her shots (none due until July of 2020), spayed, microchipped, and tested negative for heartworms. She is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm preventative and has been strategically dewormed. She does well with ear cleanings and brushing but needs some coaxing to get a bath and would do best with a groomer or vet trimming her nails.

name: Shiloh
description:
Shiloh is a handsome young boy who is estimated around 3 years of age. Shiloh was completely feral when he arrived with Tier Haven from Hazard, Kentucky. He clearly had never been handled prior to this time and we are unaware of the circumstances surrounding his first few months.

Shiloh still has a very long way to go in trusting people. He has zero confidence in himself or the world around him resulting in a very timid and shy dog. Shiloh has no fear aggression and has never lashed out but is going to require a home with the patience to work with him to overcome his past. Shiloh does really well with people from a distance of about 5-7 feet and will linger on the outskirts of interactions but doesn't know what to do when the attention is turned to him. Shiloh will come up and nudge from behind seeking attention but does best when there isn't a big fuss made about it. He has a desire to be around people but is still so unsure of him.

Shiloh does great with other dogs and really relies on them for social cues. He was running with another dog - Bentley - who we suspect is his brother. Shiloh was definitely the follower and has stayed true to that role. He does great with other dogs and has learned how to navigate play groups really well. He would really benefit from having another dog or group of dogs in a home to show him the ropes and help him overcome his fears.

A volunteer reached out to us about Shiloh within minutes of when he was scheduled to be euthanized - there was certainly a large hand guiding him to safety and we hope to see him fulfill his potential with a loving home. 

If you have a place in your heart and home for this sweet young boy please email tierhavenrescue@gmail.com for an adoption application.

name: Liutenant Dan
description:
Hey everyone! My name is Lt. Dan and I am a year old mixed breed dog. We think I might be an Australian Cattle Dog mix or something, but one thing is for sure: I'm 100% handsome! I'm even more handsome with three legs! Your eyes do not deceive you: I am tripawed and a lucky boy. I am awesome with other dogs but my foster mom says I'm not that great with cats because oh boy do I like to chase them. I'm pretty food motivated and will take all of the snacks you'll give me... but I need a new family to help me watch my figure because of my disability.

Truth be told, I did not have the best start in life. I was dumped on the side of a road where I searched for my family and had to fend for myself. While looking for my family I was hit by a car. I was scared and lonely and was hurt really bad. I was so scared of people and it took three big scary men to catch me. They brought me to a hospital where I met my foster mom. She gave me pain medication and advocated for me. This is where the amazing Mel said foster mom could bring me into the rescue and make me better. They amputated my leg and my foster mom slowly gained my trust as I healed. As you can imagine I am still very scared around new people and strangers. I need my new family to come meet me a few times before I can go home with them. It would also be great if my new family has worked with a fearful dog before. I am getting better with trusting my foster mom about strangers and ignoring them. I love playing with my foster brothers and sisters and can play all day. I have foster kitties in the house that I will chase if they run. I am going to go play with my foster siblings now and my foster mom will tell you more.

Lt. Dan is up to date on vaccines, heartworm negative, and on flea, tick and heartworm prevention monthly. He LOVES playing with other dogs and gets along with dogs of all sizes. He can live with dog savvy cats. Lt. Dan is fearful of new people and his adopter with be required to come to New Jersey a few times to meet him and spend some time with him before he can go to his new home. His adopters will also need to have experience with fearful dogs and will need to work with a positive reinforcement trainer. Once he learns to trust you, Lt. Dan will cuddle with you all day if you let him. He is a medium energy dog who just wants to be with his person. He will gladly occupy you on a long walk or cuddle on the couch all day with you. Because he had his leg amputated his adopters will need to be vigilant about his diet, weight and keep him exercised. Lt. Dan has had a rough beginning but with love and dedication he can overcome his past and be a loving member of a family. Could that be you?

SOHO is a 501c3 public charity focusing on rescuing herding dogs in crisis on the East Coast. Your pets will need to be up to date on vaccinations and heartworm preventative in order to be considered for adoption. Lt. Dan does have some additional adoption requirements: his foster mom would like a potential adopter to come and visit Lt. Dan a few times before taking him home in order to help him bond to his new family. Please note that Lt. Dan is located in HIGHLAND LAKES, NEW JERSEY.

I am not contagious and believe it or not I have greatly improved.  I just need someone who has time for me. I share a kennel with my friend Mikey, a black lab mix.  I am a little shy at first but warm up to new people pretty quick.  Itâs all about the treats!  I really like running and playing in the pastures of green grass at the rescue but I really donât want to spend my whole life here.  Please consider adopting me and I promise you would never regret it.  

I am currently located in Houston, Texas and will travel to the Pacific Northwest with an approved adopter.  My adoption fee is $500US and includes up to date vaccines, neuter, microchip, fecal test, health certificate/check up to travel and airfare on a major airline to Seattle.  You guessed itâ¦no ground transport for this guy because I want to be in my new home in hours versus days.

name: Nigel
description: Nigel is a friendly, fun guy. He is a male black lab. Nigel is a young adult, and we estimate his age to be about one year old. He still has a lot of puppy in him and is lovable and energetic. He weighs 64 lbs and tested negative for heartworms. He will be scheduled to be neutered soon. He came from the Panhandle area of Florida and was a stray before coming to Houndhaven. Nigel is waiting for someone to open their heart and give him the chance to become a loyal, faithful companion for life. To adopt Nigel, please review our policies and submit an application.

name: Gary
description:
In June, a hoarding case was discovered in Hunterdon County. Close to 200 dogs were pulled. We have 5 of 'the 188' here at Jersey Shore Animal Center. Dogs like this will need extra special homes. Lack of socialization will require homes with lots of patience. They are very nervous with new people and situations. Potential adopters may have to come multiple times to visit before these dogs can go home. We will be very particular where these little ones go. All newly adopted dogs are flight risks, but these even more so. A watchful eye is necessary. They are all between 4-8 years old. We have had them all spayed and neutered and brought them up to date on vaccines. They have also had badly needed dentals.

Gary (approx 5 years old and 13 lbs) is one of 'the 188' rescued from Hunterdon County and he's ready to find a home! He would do best with a quiet family who will give him time to settle in and get used to his new surroundings. He'd also thrive in a home with another mellow dog to show him the ropes and provide canine companionship. Gary likes the baby pool!

When dogs come from situations like this rescue in Hunterdon County, they've often never experienced the simple joys in life. Walking on the grass, sunshine on their faces, playing with toys and indulging on treats are all new to them. Our staff and volunteers have slowly started introducing the dogs to a variety of tastes and scents including ham, turkey, and carrots. Each day they make progress and we are so happy to see their personalities shining through.

Please click on the article below to read about the case:
https://www.nj.com/news/2019/07/dogs-rescued-from-hoarding-house-horror-need-you-to-adopt-them.html

*Per JSAC policy, puppies and kittens under 6 months will not be adopted to families with children under the age of 6 years.
