name: Arielle
description:
Arielle is a beautiful, sweet and adorable shepherd /collie mix of 2.5 year .

Arielle was all this time extreme afraid and shy and dared not to look at potential adopters . They all passed her and she was brought back to the kennel.

Luckily for her , her foster mother Brianna who works at our vet felt pity for her and took her home whenever she could and did not had to study in school .

Arielle bloomed open and is finally ready to be adopted .

We would like to give her a forever home with people who are calm with her and let her be herself . She will bloom open to the right person and will win your heart , just the way how she did with the staff .

She is cat and dog friendly and located in Huntington NY .

To become this sweetheart her new family please apply today by filling in the adoption application to find on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com or email us and we send you one

name: Akiro
description:
Akiro is a 1.5 year old chow mix who was saved from high kill shelter Mission in Texas .

Since the summer months dogs and cats are getting dropped. It is only a small shelter and every day it is CODE RED . Local volunteers crying and begging rescues to save . Unfortunately every rescue is completely full house . 
Luckily volunteer Nathalie begged hard enough and we could manage to find a little spot for this sweetheart .

Akiro his leg was hurt . Amputation was the first word in Texas . We stopped the amputation because our surgeons in NY saved already many dogs their legs but also in NY the verdict was amputation .

We all think it is so sad for the dog but the truth is that they adopt very fast to their situation . Akiro can do everything what a 4 legged dog can .

He is good with other dogs and  cats

We don't have to tell you that he is favorite of the staff . He won each of them their hearts on the first day .

He is a happy little fellow who just needs a committed family who will love and spoil him for the rest of his life .

Akiro is located in Huntington NY .

Please only very SERIOUS adopters !

To become his new family, apply today by filling in the adoption application to find on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com or email us and we send you one

name: Argamo
description:
Argamo is a very sweet dog of 4 years old who we saved as all the others from the same kill shelter .

Messenger went open and 40 German Shepherds were on the kill list . We could only take 8 . Argamo was one of the lucky ones and came alive out of the shelter .

His nightmare is over ...

As usual we promise our dogs a family and HOME and we are here to keep that promise to our dogs .

We are looking for a sweet family who will give Argamo and the love he deserves, a bed to snuggle , a few toys to play and lots of quality time .

Argamo is located in Huntington NY . He is a little bit unsure about other dogs , a meet and greet is required . He is not a fan of cats .

To become his new family please apply today by filling in the  adoption link to find on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com or email us and we send you one

name: Assana
description:
Our sweet little baby Assana .

Yes she looks adorable ...but fear is in her eyes .

Her owner passed away and clearly he did not care for his dogs . No vetting, no decent food and they don't know what love is .

9 dogs were on the property . We took 5 in and ALL of them are shaking over their body .

Assana bites the first leash over so we put stronger ones and to keep her safe we put 2 on .

She is cornered and surrenders . She lays on her back and I give her slowly some belly rubs... she is confused ...because she likes this .

This poor baby needs a good person who understands what abuse and neglect can do to a dog . She needs somebody with patience and time to give .

We have seen so many blooming open and it's wonderful how adopters and their dogs come together .

It would be nice if somebody can give her her golden basket where she feels safe and loved .

Assana is 3 years old , is ok with other dogs but also a little bit afraid sometimes and is not a fan of cats .

This little beauty is located in Huntington NY .

To become her new family please apply today by filling in the adoption application to find on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com or email us and we send you one

name: Aster
description:
Meet Aster! Aster is a mixed breed pup who we believe will most likely be a medium sized pup around 50lbs. Whatever he is mixed with I can tell you itâs cute!! This sweet boy loves his people. He also loves playing with the other dogs in his foster home. He is working on potty and crate training and will need a family to continue to work with him. If you would be interested in adding Aster to your family please fill out an application out at 
forrescue.net
His adoption fee is $250 and he will have age appropriate vaccines, neutered, on flea/hw prevention and microchipped. He is located in Huntsville AL.

name: Mary
description:
Mary is a sweet-natured senior girl seeking a retirement home.  Eight-year-old Mary is a former stray from Huron County.  We don't know of her history, but we do know that she's a relaxed, affectionate lady. Mary still has plenty of smiles and love to give.  Consider opening your home to her today!

If you have kids and/or another dog in your family and are interested in adopting a Friendship dog please bring them with you for a meet and greet.  No appointment is necessary.  Stop by anytime during regular business hours. 

All dogs receive one or more vaccinations, a basic veterinary examination, are wormed, heartworm tested, and spayed or neutered.  Dogs 3 months and older are micro-chipped.

name: Dede aka Diamond
description: Hi I'm DEDE aka Diamond. I am a true survivor!!  I survived a very bad Hurricane named Superstorm Sandy that destroyed the shelter I was at! I was so very scared, especially when I first came to New York Bully Crew. It was a horrible storm. Today I am a lot better but I do need a strong experienced pack leader owner to help guide me and make me feel secure. I still tend to get nervous around some people-the stress and trauma I went through from that Hurricane and all the scary things afterwards that went along with it made me a bit insecure. Can you help me by being my leader?? Help me regain my confidence again? I am 8 years old and do ok with  other calm balanced dogs. They make me not so scared when they are near me. I would love a family to help me and my rescue family says I deserve to be treated like a Princess after all I've been through. Please go to www.nybullycrew.org and fill out the application for me. I'm waiting all this time for you!! I do hope you come for me soon!! Thank you!

name: Smokey
description: Smokey is shy with people, but he loves walks and food so that is the key to his heart. He needs time to get comfortable in new places and with new people, but he will accept treats and warm up quickly. He is not yet comfortable being petted or handled by people, but he loves doing activities with other dogs and learning from them. Smokey absolutely adores other dogs here at the Sanctuary. He is very active and playful when he's around them, and they help him build his confidence. Smokey was born in 2014 and came to Best Friends from a humane society in Idaho. He can jump fences, so he is considered a flight risk. In a former foster home, he was a bit of an escape artist, so he will need a home with a secure enclosure and someone with a watchful eye. At the Sanctuary, he is working on crate training, getting into and riding in a car and getting more comfortable with new places. He already walks well on a leash. Smokey will need some time to adjust to a new home, but with time and patience he will make a wonderful companion.

name: Ralph
description: Ralph is a very handsome Dogo Argentino/Pit bull terrier mix who would love to be your new best friend.Shy and fearful at first, and excited once he knows you, Ralph is learning how to greet people appropriately. In fact, he came to Best Friends from a rescue group in Boise, Idaho because he needed to work on his training. He's a big boy, so learning manners, like not jumping up on people, is especially important.Ralph loves fluffy toys (though he tends to de-fluff them in a hurry). He also loves getting affection from people he knows, and running in the park. Ralph is not good with cats. He also does not do well with other dogs, so he would be best in a home without them.Ralph may be a very large and powerful boy, but he is also very sweet. He needs someone who can handle him and give him the attention and love he deserves. All he's looking for is one special person or family who will give him a chance.Ralph is part of our Single Pets* program! That means that he is eligible for a free flight home and waived adoption fee!*Single pets do best as the only dog or cat in the home.

name: Dapper
description:
THIS IS A COURTESY LISTING. HUNAH IS NOT PLACING THIS DOG. PLEASE CONTACT THE OWNER DIRECTLY.

Rescue: Mikeyâs Chance Canine Rescue
Location: Kennewick, WA

Description:
Dapper is a handsome boy whoâs looking for an active family to call his own! He is a very sweet, large (75 lbs), 2 year old male border collie/German shepherd mix.  Dapper was pulled by Mikeyâs Chance Rescue from a high kill shelter in Idaho. Dapper has never met a dog or person he doesnât like! Good with children of all ages, but due to his prey drive heâs not recommended to a home with cats or other small animals. He knows basic commands (sit, lay down, stay). If you have questions, please contact Mikeyâs Chance! (Can be found on FB or at www.mikeyschance.com)

name: Sosa
description: Sosa is a sensitive sweetheart. He's also a fun, active dog who loves toys, water, walks and car rides. Born in 2014, Sosa was picked up as a stray and came to Best Friends from a shelter in Indiana. Sosa appreciates having a predictable routine. He loves to lounge in the shade after playing in his kiddie pool. He also enjoys breaks in his crate where he can work on one of his favorite things: a frozen treat. Sosa loves doing agility and catches on quickly to new training cues. He's also learning to play with a flirt pole, which encourages him to chase and play with a toy on a long rope while helping him with impulse control. Sosa really likes hanging out with his friends at Dogtown. He's a good role model for other dogs, and he has plenty of play dates here. Sosa is working on getting more and more comfortable when he's out exploring new places. He's looking for a patient person or family who can help him learn about life in a home, since we believe he never had one of his own. Although he may need a slight adjustment period in a home, Sosa is a wonderful dog who bonds well with people and would probably do best with a dog friend to show him the ropes.

name: Sundance
description: Sundance's name fits him perfectly. He has a unique personality that will make you fall in love with him. He also dances with excitement when he's happy to see you. He is shy and fearful with strangers, but once he knows you, he will always greet you with a smile and gaze at you in a loving way. He can be a little quirky, and his caregivers say he is like a wiggly cat in a dog's body, but that's what makes him so endearing. Born in 2013, Sundance came to the Sanctuary from a Best Friends Network Partner in Indiana. He guards food and is not comfortable with strangers entering his room or yard. He does better meeting them outside of his area first. At Dogtown, Sundance is doing great with going to his 'place' to wait for his food and with trading his bowls to reduce food guarding. He does not enjoy a lot of handling, especially by new people. He will accept occasional pets but prefers to just do a happy dance around you. He is also difficult for medical handling. He has become comfortable enough with day-to-day handling that he can be harnessed for walks, and he is working on muzzle training for upcoming vet appointments. When it comes to other dogs, Sundance can be picky and seems to prefer females. If you're looking for a dog who dances to his own beat, Sundance would love to meet you.

name: Jax
description:
PLEASE READ THE COMPLETE BIO ON JAX BEFORE APPLYING

Jax is almost ready for adoption!

Jax is a Shih Tzu that came from a true Puppy Mill in Indiana then sold here through a Mall Petstore.  It was recently discovered that he had a liver-shunt and required surgery to repair it.  Jax will need to stay on a low-protein diet or special prescription diet food specific for the liver (please do your homework, the food is not cheap, fortunately heâs a little dog and therefore only eats about a cup a day) he will need to stay on this food for the remainder of his life which should be at least 15 more years.  

Information on liver Shunts:  Congenital portosystemic shunts (AKA liver shunts) are relatively common birth defects in pets where the blood vessels in the abdomen develop abnormally and instead of funneling blood from the intestines through the liver, the blood is able to bypass the liver and enters the systemic circulation. This abnormal blood flow prevents the liver from doing its job of processing the blood â eliminating medications, waste products, and toxins, breaking down nutrients from food, and regulating the bodyâs energy balance.  

You will also need to pay attention to the treats you also give Jax:  some better treat options for dogs with shunts include meat-free dog biscuits, human snacks such as animal crackers and breakfast cereal, or non-toxic fruits and vegetables.
Jax is making up for lost time from being a sick puppy for the last few months before his surgery, but now he is acting like a normal puppy again.  Given he came from a puppy mill, he was clearly not handled/loved on so if you are looking for a companion to sit in your lap..Jax is not the dog for you!  Jax will only go to a home that currently has another small dog of similar size and still on the younger side to play with him and help him learn what is it to be a love pet to us humans. Jax is looking for a home that has the time to invest is proper training and social skills. He is working currently working on leash training and to go potty outdoors.  Jax is crate trained and will use a pad indoors.  Please note:  Jax is not 100% housebroken.  Jax is heartworm negative, neutered and is up to date on vaccinations. Jax has a microchip that will be transferred to the adopter upon completion of the adoption process.  
Jax will only be adopted out locally at this time!!  
Please feel free to email me, his foster mom at lexie30093@gmail.com  
The adoption fee Jax is $ 300.00. 


To find out more information about Jax,  please contact the foster parent at: lexie30093@gmail.com

name: June
description:
Meet Ms. June! She was picked up by animal control after wandering around for several weeks. She has a microchip that revealed that she came from a breeder in Indiana and from the looks of her, she is a purebred English lab. Another group rescued her but they asked us to take her so we can find an appropriate \"lab-loving\" home.

She is about 82 pounds but could stand to lose a few pounds. She's great with people and dogs. We are unsure how she is with cats.She is crate trained, has good house manners,and LOVES the water! Her coat is a little worse for the wear after being on the road for a while but we are tending to that and she will look like a new dog very soon.

If you would like to adoptJune, please go to www.atlantalabrescue.com and submit an application to start the process.

name: Noah
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Please contact stephodellfcr@hotmail.com for more information about this pet.Noah is an active 5 year old smooth coat male BC. He and his brothers came from Central Indiana and are being fostered in Plymouth, Indiana. If you would like additional information on Noah, contact Stephany at stephodellfcr@hotmail.com. For additional information on adopting Noah or any of the other CBBCR foster dogs, go to the CBBCR website at www.comebyebcrescue.org. Update January 18, 2016
Ty and Noah

These two handsome boys are brothers and are now about 4 1/2 years of age. It isn't required that they be adopted together but they would sure love that possibility. These boys are very sweet and affectionate boys. Ty and Noah need to be placed in a home without children.

They are initially a bit suspicious of people they don't know, Ty more so than Noah, but given a little bit of time to become familiar they are both loves. They are both good with other dogs and regularly interact with other dogs. They both love to chase along after my Border Collie when we are playing fetch.

Noah likes to stalk kitties and Ty could care less about them. They both enjoy riding in the vehicle but both are nervous when they are in an unfamiliar environment. They are both good in the house but are still crated when I am not home. Their crate behavior is much better now compared to when they were youngsters but still need the opportunity to go out for potty breaks often and shouldn't be left for more than about 4 hours at a time.

Their idea of a perfect home setting would be a quiet, country setting with a large fenced yard for them to play and have fun with their people and to have at least one stay at home parent. They would be best as home bodies and to go along places for ride alongs but are not the type of dogs that will enjoy going EVERYWHERE and being around lot of \"strangers\" on a regular basis. If they are not adopted together they would do best in a home with another dog because they do seem to feel safer when they are in the presence of other dogs.

Noah has been introduced to some agility obstacles and even though he is hesitant at first, when he is given a little time to get the obstacle figured out he seems to have fun learning how to maneuver the obstacle. These boys are looking for a patient person to provide them with a forever home. Someone who will love them for the soft, sensitive boys that they are and allow them to live in a quiet and predictable home.
*******************************************
Noah - This guy is a sweet boy that is typically very comfortable meeting new people when they come here for meet and greets. He likes toys but will shred soft, squeaky toys. He is foodie and enjoys learning. He did get to go to an agility open class once and very quickly found out how much fun it is to put his paws up on things ;) He is a very cuddly and affectionate guy. He does tend to have times in his crate where he salivates and has anxiety - but it is not all the time and seems to happen randomlynot because of one thing or another. He is good in the car, reasonable on leash. Good for bathing and nail trimming. I really like Noah and think he has the potential to be a nice companion level pooch for the right person. He gets a bit worried in new environments and is a soft, sensitive young guythat also will need a patient and understanding human. (9/24/14) *******************************************************
Oh, baby Noah.....he is sooooooooooooooooo cute and also a tennis ball junky! He loves, loves, loves tennis balls!!! He takes a bit longer than Spense and Jude to warm up to new people and a new evironment....he and his brother Ty are the most 'soft' of this litter born on September 16, 2013. He is a foodie puppy, and lots of ball drive, and once comfortable in his environment is such a fun boy. He very much enjoys playing with other dogs....was a barker at my kitties at first but now they are old news....he is very good in his crate...it is a rare day that he would have an accident in his crate....which again is awesome compared to how we started. I believe Noah will blossom into a wonderful companion level dog in the right home, that is patient and gentle and knows how to keep him safe and satisfied in his day to day adventures!! (3/28/14)

name: Willy
description:
Willy is a beagle and was born in April of 2013. He came to us from another shelter (Franklin County in Indiana) on April 24, 2019. Willy was a stray and became friends with another beagle, Katie, while at Franklin. She also came to AAF, but has since been adopted. Willy may still be missing her. He is very shy with people he does not know.

If you are interested in meeting Willy, please come in during adoption hours (below) and ask to meet him. Please be patient during the process as he takes some time to warm up. It might even take more than one visit. Thank you for considering adopting a pet from the Animal Adoption Foundation.

All AAF cats and dogs are vaccinated, spayed or neutered and micro-chipped. All cats receive a FelV/FIV combination test while dogs over the age of 8 months are tested for heartworms. All pets are also treated for both intestinal parasites and fleas. The AAF is proud of the medical attention that is given to each and every pet as their health and well-being is of the utmost importance to our organization. 

The adoption fees for our pets are as follows:
Kittens: $85
Cats 5 Months and older: $60
Puppies: $150
Dogs 5 Months and older: $135

You can visit all of our pets available for adoption:

name: Bear
description:
Bear was surrendered by his owner to an animal control officer because his owner would not bring him inside because the temperatures were over 90 degrees outside. Thankfully there is a local ordinance that requires owners to bring them inside when the temperature is extremely cold or hot here. He is between 5 and 6 years old and has lived his entire life on a chain. Since the shelter was full, we had to agree to pull him right away, as they have no choice but to euthanize for space when they get owner surrenders. He is in need of a foster or forever home in the Indianapolis area, where we can provide the needed medical care for him. ear is very easy going, and gentle, and gets along well with other dogs. He is untested with cats.  He is very easy going, and seems to like all people.  He rides fine in a vehicle too. He does not pull on a leash.  He is very sweet and a little timid. He has been groomed, had a biopsy done on some bumps on his back that were the result of flea dermatitis we found out, and is undergoing heartworm treatment.  His fly strikes have healed nicely. If you would like to help Bear, please complete a foster or adoption application on our website, www.igpr.org. Bear is located in Indianapolis, Indiana.

We recommend obedience training for all newly adopted pyrs, to help you create a special bond with you and your new friend, and so you have a well behaved canine. Great Pyrenees are willing to learn, but are not as eager to comply with commands as much as other breeds. They are bred to be independent thinkers. Applicants must be over 25, own their own home and all children in household must be over 6 years old. Your resident pets must be up to date on vaccines, sterilized, you must have a good history of vet care for them, and you must have used heartworm preventative year round for your dogs. 


Bear will be placed as an inside pet with outside privileges. You MUST have a securely fenced yard accessible from your home. Invisible fencing does not work with this breed and they will take the shock for the freedom.  Great Pyrenees are bred to roam and will create their own territory if not secured, which can led to them being lost, hit by vehicles or shot by people who see them as a threat. The breed is not a good off leash dog, and cannot be trusted to not run away.  A Great Pyrenees off leash is a \" DisAPyr.\" 

If you are interested in adopting or fostering, please complete the appropriate application on our website, www.igpr.org under the Adopt tab. 

All of our dogs marked as needing foster homes are also available for adoption.  If a dog is listed on this site, it is available.  No need to contact us to see if it is,  We do require you  complete the adoption application prior to meeting a dog.

We also offer a foster to adopt program. You foster the dog, and have first right of refusal on them if an approved application is submitted for them. 

In fostering a dog, the dog comes to you fully vetted. and groomed. You provide good quality food, grooming, and we provide the heartworm preventative and medical care, if needed* .(*Based on approval from IGPR.)

description: Rescued from a property during a dog fight bust in Colorado, Jacko came to Best Friends from a humane society. At Dogtown he is affectionately called 'Jack Jack.' name: Bizzie
description:
Age: 4-5 Years (as of 9/6/18)
Weight: 62.7 (as of 9/6/18)

This dog has been spayed/neutered, is up to date on shots, on heartworm preventative and is microchipped.

Bizzie is loving and very sweet!
She's one of those dogs who epitomizes canine forgiveness - you'll see this when you read her backstory. Fortunately for Bizzie, her future's looking ever so bright! We're thinking she's a blend of Chow Chow and Shepherd probably born sometime in 2014 or 2015. She has been fine with adult dogs and puppies; she has not been introduced to cats. She's been great with all adults, and though she has not lived with children, we think she would be okay with older, dog-respectful kids. House training and crate training are in the works, and she seems to do fine on leash. A dog who has lived on a chain for years, like Bizzie did, can have a tendency towards guard dog behaviors and though she has not shown any of these tendencies, her adopters will likely need to work with a professional trainer to help her accept strangers and work through any fears she might exhibit.

Bizzie loves to run and play with other dogs, people and toys! She rides well in the car while crated, she's very calm. Though a fenced yard would be great to get in some running and playing, daily leash walks for business, exercise and fun will work just as well to keep her happy and healthy. And to keep that canine mind sharp, think puzzle toys and games. Bizzie really just wants to find a forever home where she'll be loved and cared for. Could that be your home? Fill out an application today and her people will get right back to you!

Bizzie's Backstory: Bizzie truly deserves a wonderful life. Her first 3-4 years were very hard. She was from the south side of Jackson, Mississippi, and was tied out on a 6-foot chain to be used as a guard dog. Her shelter was limited to a carport, no matter what the temperature or weather was like. She often did not have food nor water, except when a neighbor was contacted for dog food. After that, the neighbor often checked on her and would feed her and give her water. We know that Bizzie had at least one litter of puppies that a rescue took, but Bizzie was left behind. However the rescue did provide a spay for her. Bizzie's friend finally convinced her owner to relinquish her. When the vet checked Bizzie, she did have heartworm, which has been treated and she is now clear. At first, this pretty girl was scared when anyone approached her with a leash - maybe she was afraid she would be tied out again. Of course, we know that this will never again be the case!

Medical Note: This dog has been treated for heartworm disease with melarsomine injections. Once treatment is completed and the dog tests negative for microfilaria, the dog will be cleared to resume normal activity and able to be adopted. Untreated heartworm disease can cause lasting damage to the heart, lungs and arteries, and can affect the dog's health and quality of life even after the parasites are gone, possibly presenting as medical complications and/or new conditions in the future. This dog showed no symptoms of heartworm disease before or during treatment. A good resource for more information on heartworm disease is: https://www.heartwormsociety.org/pet-owner-resources/ heartworm-basics. Please check with your vet if you should have any questions or concerns about this condition, and discuss any concerns you may have with your SOS Adoption Counselor.

name: Sparky
description:
It's been over 10 years since the water rose up in Waveland, MS. Over 3,500 days since the hurricane cracked the skies open and drove the sea right into town. If you have to ask which hurricane, well, then you probably aren't from around here. Katrina made landfall at Waveland, MS, a small town of 7,000 just an hour east of New Orleans, on August 29, 2005, and you'd be hard-pressed to find any of God's good creatures in Waveland that don't remember. Destin and Sparky remember.



Chaos is too simple of a word to convey what that time was like, but it's the closest thing we've got. Fortunately, there were a few clear minds that day, including Doll Stanley and In Defense of Animals. The organization recognized the doom bearing down on animals in the region, petitioning courts to release captured animals in the pound. Destin was one such animal, languishing in the pound as the storm bore down on the Gulf Coast. At the 11th hour, a judge granted the request, forcing animal control to release the animals to safety. When they reached Destin, the water was already up to her neck. Destin and 34 other animals were rescued that night, but, sadly, thousands more souls lost their lives all along the coast. Destin and Sparky, who was discovered after the storm, were some of the lucky ones.



A number of animal rescue facilities went to work in the aftermath of Katrina, and ARF was one of the organizations born from the rubble. The 35 dogs from Waveland made the trip north to Jackson, and a few more groups soon followed. Destin and Sparky were placed together in their new home, and quickly became inseparable, sharing a bond that few of us can scarcely imagine. Yet over 3,500 days after the storm arrived, these two remain with ARF. Every one of the other 35 dogs has moved on, either adopted to a wonderful home or crossing the rainbow bridge. We've twice attempted to adopt Sparky individually, but both dogs immediately grew depressed and stopped eating. Their bond is unique and irreplaceable, and so even though we know how challenging it is to adopt two older dogs, we know that they need to be together. They are sweet and spunky, despite their advanced age. But the wisdom in their eyes is surely enough reward for providing a forever home.



Katrina had an impact that still reverberates throughout the region. As we think of it, we still mourn for those that have been lost. Yet we also recognize the events that catalyzed the creation of ARF, and are reminded of our mission. If you can't adopt Destin and Sparky today, then please continue joining us in this mission. Stop by sometime to walk these wonderful dogs. The lifeblood of this organization is our supporters, and we're grateful every day that you've helped us make it this far.

Sparky, Hound Mix has been shared from Shelter Exchange - http://www.shelterexchange.org.

name: Sprocket
description:
Sprocket is my name and I am the best boy in the world. I have been patiently waiting for a chance to prove it to my forever family. I have had some pretty rough experiences. These are the parts of my life that I have chosen to forget, but people see them all over my body. Good fortune came my way when Eleventh Hour Rescue saved me from the streets of Jersey City. They cleaned me up and made sure I was fully recovered.

  

 I am easy to take care of with a very short coat that needs occasional brushing mostly because I love it. I don't like to walk very far, but exercise is as important for my mind as it is for my body. I like to walk for about 15 minutes. I am built for comfort not for speed. I like to play with a jolly ball and to spend time outside sniffing around. I love to sit on a bench with a kissable human. I am a little shy with new people and I don't like loud noises. I will let you know I am unhappy about it by heading back indoors.

  

 A greeting from me means hoisting my \"low to the ground\" little body up as close as I can get and giving lots of kisses. When it is time for you to go I will head for my comfy bed and settle in with a toy and a Nylabone to chew. I learned to sleep in my crate, too. I may need a little time to get used to sleeping in a crate again after having a kennel run for a while, but I am a smart boy!

  

 Here are some obedience things I know: sit, down, stay, walking nicely on a leash with very little pulling.

  

 If you think we could be friends, even if you want to foster rather than adopt me, please fill out an application at www.ehrdogs.org & ask for me by name - SPROCKET!

name: Hank
description:
WE ARE NOT A SHELTER. WE ARE A NO-KILL 501-C-3 NON-PROFIT RESCUE: To see an animal, you must fill out an application first and then once approved, we can set up for you to meet the animal you are interested in.

Here is the Dog Application that you can copy and paste into a browser: https://fs17.formsite.com/waverlypetrescue/form028182466/index.html

Hank was a stray and his time was up in a kill shelter in Kansas. A WPR volunteer was adopting a dog from this shelter in Kansas, and decided to take Hank too so that he would not be put down the next day. They knew Hank could be a WPR dog. They just couldn't leave him knowing he would be put down. So Hank is now a Waverly Pet Rescue dog. He is living in a foster home. He is up to date on shots, tested heartworm negative, and neutered.

Hank is about 3 years old as of May 2019. We have had him for a couple of weeks now and he is doing well! He has not been around cats or children yet.

5/17/19: So we picked up Hank last night.  He is such a sweet boy, but very timid.  Unsure of everything.  But, he has already made great improvements in the 24 hours we have had him.  It will just take some time to make him understand that he is in a safe place and everything is okay.  I think he will be a great dog.  He is very loving.  No aggression at all.  He is eating good too.  And getting along great with our dog.  In fact, I think it helped having our dog.  She kind of shows him the ropes sometimes.  He has done great with the kennel as well, and so far seems as though he is housebroke.

5/26/19: My daughter is interning at a vet clinic this summer so she showed some pictures of Hank to another employee and they think that he is a boxer/pit bull mix.  When I googled brindle boxer pit mix I got some pictures that do look a lot like Hank.  He unofficially weighs 52 lbs.  We weighed him here at home.  Here are a few words of how I would describe Hank.  Hank is a sweet boy and loves everyone.  He's shy with new experiences but with patience he comes around.  Gets along great with other dogs.  Likes to go for walks.  Housebroke.  He goes in his kennel great at night, but not so much in the morning for the day.  He has been destructive with cushions and blankets in his kennel during the day, but outside of his kennel he's pretty good.  He really likes being around people and seems to be so happy.  He's a pretty cool dog overall.  

6/18/19 UPDATE: I had him briefly around a 3 yr old child and he did fine. Was a little startled by the childâs quick movements but I think children a little older would understand better. I can play with his feet and tail and he doesnât care. I lay on him when we snuggle and play and he loves it.  He has never shown any aggression at all. I think he would probably do just fine with the kids.  He loves attention. 

8/2/19 UPDATE: Hank is doing great!  He just recently learned how to shake.  He is so eager to please.  I no longer have any problems getting him to go into his kennel in the morning.  I get a small treat out and most of the time he heads to his kennel without me even telling him to.  Otherwise, I just tell him to go \"kennel up\" and away he goes.  He then sits in his kennel waiting while I gather toys and bones to put in his kennel with him.  He loves going on walks on a leash, and enjoys playing in our little dog baby pool.  He is not a barker.  About the only time he barks is sometimes when he is playing with our dog.  He prefers back scratches over belly rubs.  Hank is a happy sweet fun dog who just wants to be loved. Will someone please adopt Hank and give him a forever home? $175.00 adoption fee.

To see an animal, you must fill out an application first and then once approved, we can set up for you to meet the animal you are interested in. We do background checks on all applicants. name: Jaco
description:
Meet Jaco!  He's a 10 month old purebred German Shorthaired Pointer puppy.  He's a lovely all liver male with a docked tail.  This boy joined our rescue from an overflowing shelter in Kansas.  He is bouncy, full of energy, and will do well with breed experienced owners ready for a high energy GSP.  

From his foster:  \"He is doing awesome so far.  He is SUPER sweet with us, and is even more velcro'd to me than Huck (figure that might lessen as he gets more settled in?) He shows absolutely NO sign of food or toy aggression. He has \"Sit\" for treats down about 80% already, has had zero bathroom accidents.  Being outside during the fireworks caused him no more that a turned head and perked ears too!  \"Down\" is a big struggle though - he's very gentle when he rears up and falls into you so that's not a big deal, but refraining from checking out cabinets may take some dog whisperer type training... haha  He's a super sweet dog, and while at almost a year old he's definitely still a puppy, he heeds verbal correction quickly. He shows a lot of intelligence and is learning commands really well. Plus, when he is carrying on with our other dogs and starts 'getting mouthy', he sounds like Chewbacca.
We are trying to get good video of the Chewbacca thing - it's really funny to hear him doing it.  His coat is super silky and he has a very expressive face - there's no doubt when he's happy, unhappy, tired, inquisitive, excited, or just generally in a goofy-guy mood.  There's more I forgot... He sits and will also shake for treats.  At feeding time when we put his bowl on the counter to fill it he automatically goes to the other end of the room and sits and waits for us to tell him to come eat.  We about have him good to go on fetch with a tennis ball too, meaning sitting and waiting for you to throw it and then dropping the ball right to you when he brings it back.\

name: Lilly "LuLu" Lonestar
description:
HI! I'm Lilly, I just made a very long trip from a shelter in San Antonio with my sisters Karolina, and Venus (who already found her forever home). Now I live with my foster family and I am learning my way as a family dog. I would do best in a home with another dog who can show me the ropes. When I'm not playing with my doggie friends I enjoy rolling around in the grass, getting the zoomies, playing with stuffed animals and laying on a nice warm bed/couch. I have lived with little people too, though it can take me awhile to adjust. I've never had a home of my own so I can be shy, but once I get to know you, I'm a sweet girl who will be your best friend.

Is my new home your home?

Apply to adopt LILLY DAVIS LONESTAR at www.EHRDOGS.org!

name: Bull
description: Foster update: Bull is a total sweetheart. He is calm, gentle and affectionate. He doesn't have an angry bone in his body. He is low maintenance and is happiest resting at home and getting cuddles. He loves to pick a comfy spot and fall asleep. Every so often, he wakes up, chews on his toys, then goes back to his spot with the toy still in his mouth. He loves belly rubs and asks for them as much as he can. Often by flopping his body onto yours. Bull is fully house-trained and hasn't had any accidents. Bull is a goofball. In addition to his goofy expressions, he also has some very special moves. Amongst his favorites, he loves to lay on the sofa with his head hanging off the side, so much so that he ends up sliding onto the floor, with his hind legs still stretched out on the edge of the sofa. Another signature move is what we call the Bull-dozer. Bull nuzzles his smushy head into your lap, succumbing to the heavenly pets, his butt still high up in the air, until he can no longer keep himself up and flops his 55-pound body onto you, dozing off into doggy dreamland. At home, Bull is the perfect chilled out pup. Outdoors, he is still getting used to the scary NYC noises. He gets frightened by the loud sounds and by all of the commotion, but to be fair, so do I! He doesn't pull on the leash but we are still working on walking straight - he likes to run into you from time to time, mostly because he's busy observing his surroundings. He is great with other dogs and other people, and is friendly to everyone he meets. Bull is so gentle, he needs a bit of love and encouragement to have his doggy side come out more. He's slowly learning how to play fetch and tug of war, and play with other dogs. I'm sure he'll be a pro in no time. Bull is a total smush and would do well in a calm and loving household, where he can relax and get lots of cuddles. He is such a gentleman and can't wait to make his forever family very happy! name: Pike - ADOPTED
description:
This is Pike from the \"mountain\" litter.  He was born on May 11, 2019 at his foster's home.  His mother Shasta was saved from a high-kill Kentucky shelter so Pike and his siblings would have had an uncertain fate had we not gotten her out in the nick of time!  

Pike is a mixed breed and and is the \"big\" brother of the litter he currently weighs around 25# and will likely be 50-65# when he grows up.  He is a typical puppy full of energy and liveliness.  He enjoys playing with other dogs as well as cats and kittens.  He recalls to his name and he likes to play with toys.  He enjoys playing in water and chasing frogs.  

Pike's  is a busy boy and will need a family that can keep up with him!

When thinking about adopting a puppy please consider how it will change your life. You must have a home environment in which the puppy will not be home alone more than 4 hours a day total. You must be committed to learning how to and training your puppy. Puppies need to be socialized with other dogs so that they know how to behave when they encounter other dogs.  

Puppies need a lot of love and attention and cannot be crated as a convenience for you. Puppies should never be crated more than a total of 7 hours within a 24 hour period. You may have to take them out in the middle of the night. Puppies must be taken out on a regular schedule..sun, rain, Sleet or snow.  They require lots of play time and exercise.  

You may have to clean up messes. Puppies like to chew..it is how they explore their world so your family will need to be diligent about keeping things that you don't want chewed up put away. Having a puppy is a wonderful experience if you are prepared. If you are ready to experience the joys of adding a puppy to your family visit our website goldenhuggs.org for more information about adoption.

GHR ONLY ADOPTS TO ADULTS OVER THE AGE OF 25 AND PUPPIES TO  PEOPLE WHO HAVE TIME FOR THEM. WE DO NOT ADOPT TO FAMILIES WITH CHILDREN UNDER THE AGE OF 5.

It doesn't matter where the pups are from; it only matters where they live the rest of their lives. If you are interested in adopting, please complete an application at www.goldenhuggs.org, this is the first step in the process. The adoption fee  includes spay or neuter, shots  age appropriate and transportation to the New England drop off points. For more information, please contact  info@goldenhuggs.org.

Hi my name is Duke.  I'm about 2 years old and under 15 pounds.  I'm originally from Kentucky where I lived with two other dogs until our owner couldn't afford to care for us any more.  I've been in my foster home since Jan. 2019.   As you can see from my pictures, I love to be on a lap, it  doesn't matter whose, as long as I can be close to someone.  I am really a people dog.   I have quite the personality.  I'm a lover, a snuggler, a kisser, a hoarder of toys/bones, a thief of toys/bones from the other dogs and a bit of a napoleon.  I'm not a fan of big dogs....there's that napoleon complex, or submissive dogs because I like to be the big cheese.  If another dog puts me in my place when I try to be bossy, I will typically be their friend unless toys are involved and then I'm going to steal them.  My foster mom noticed my back legs would sometimes kick out, like they slipped out of the socket.  The doctor examined me and noticed I didn't have knee sockets in my back legs.  I had a successful surgery.  I hated being confined and not being able to run and play with my foster friends, but I survived the healing period and have been released by the doctor.  Since I never had the stability in my legs I was not able to jump.  Now that my legs are fixed, I can jump, but my brain doesn't know that.  If you have a cat, it must like to play and be chased.  I know there is someone out there looking for a little lovable goofball like me...I just wish they would hurry up and meet me on Sunday from 11:00 - 1:45 pm at PetsMart.

---FAQ---

Is This Dog Currently Available?... This dog is available at the Small Miracles rescue facility in Ellicott City.  To submit an application, please come meet this dog in person.  You can bring your application with you, or you can fill one out when you come in.  Dogs will be removed from PetFinder only when they have an approved application or more than three (3) interested applicants.

Where did this dog come from?...  We rescue dogs from 100% kill shelters in West Virginia and on occasion from Kentucky.  On rare occasions we accept owner surrenders.  Due to the nature of the shelters they were rescued from, we often do not know the dogs' history.

How Old is this dog?...  We look at a dogs' teeth to estimate its age, and then the age is reevaluated by our veterinary staff when the dog is spayed/neutered.  If an age is not posted online, please feel free to inquire.

Is this dog Good With Kids?...  We occasionally know for sure if a dog is good with kids because it came from a home with kids.  This is rare.  We always suggest you bring your children in to meet the dog if you are seriously interested in adopting.  Dogs may like some kids and may dislike others.  Dogs are individuals, just like kids are.

Is this dog Housebroken?...  Advice from a veterinarian:  Even if a dog is housebroken at my house, it does not mean that it understands not to pee at someone else's house.  It ONLY understands not to pee at my house.  Some dogs make the connection that they should only pee outside.  Some must be retrained when they come home.  All we can tell you for sure is whether/or not a dog's crate is clean when we come to walk them in the AM.  All this means is that they are crate trained and waited to pee until we took them outside.

What is this dog's Temperament?...  We do not have a clear picture of a dog's temperament until we have allowed them to settle in for a few days.  Even then they are living in a shelter environment with many other dogs and a lot of daily activity.  It can be difficult to say a dog is \"calm\" or \"nervous\" when the shelter environment is playing a big role in that behavior.  We only rescue FRIENDLY dogs who have no known bite history.  If a dog is at Small Miracles, it likes people and has a good temperament.  We always suggest you meet the dog to see if it is the right fit for your lifestyle. 

What are your Fees?...  Base adoption fee is $325 for adult dogs and puppies.  To this, we add a $30 microchip fee, which we register for you, and a 6 month supply of heartworm preventative.  Heartworm preventative costs $40-60 depending on the weight of the dog.  This means that a large dog will total $405.00 and an extra large dog will total $415.00.

Why can't I adopt a FREE dog?...  Our adoption fee covers many procedures which cost much more for us then the amount we ask for from you. We spay/neuter all pets, and we give them their first round of vaccines (canine distemper, bordatella, Rabies if age appropriate).  At a typical vet clinic this would cost you $500 at minimum for the surgery, and each vaccine is roughly $35 each.  Even if your adopted dog does not have all of its shots due to the mandatory waiting period between booster shots, we offer vaccinations at the low cost of $20/shot.  We test all dogs for heartworm disease and tickborn illnesses such as Lymes.  We never euthanize a heartworm positive dog, and treatment routinely costs us $3000/dog.  We collect a fecal sample from every rescued dog and run a microscopic parasite test.  Any parasites found will be treated with two rounds of the appropriate dewormer.  We treat all dogs for fleas and ticks with Advantage.  If a dog has significant dental disease or \"very dirty teeth\

name: Freddie
description:
FREDDIE:

Howdy friends, Iâm Freddie. I was just awarded my freedom pass from the state of Kentucky.  Iâm a whimsical, fun-loving 2-year-old Black Labâ¦ ~ 80 lbs. of love!  Iâve been told from a private source that I could be a star on the Dog Bowl because of my muscular, athletic build and my gregarious attitude. When I see you coming to visit me, I get so excited. Iâm working on my manners for overexcitement, but once Iâm with you, I am a great walker, right by your side. Iâm such a friendly, sweet, welcoming, happy, goofy ball of enthusiasm. Having people in my life really lights up my world, and itâs obvious my magical existence lights up the world of anyone spending time with me too.  Iâm a big fellow, but donât let my size fool you, I am a big lovebug and a big lap dog too!  I may be ~80 lbs, but the love in my heart crushes the scales! My goal in life is to make you happy. Iâm an intelligent boy with a 3.0 GPA in dog obedience, and I would love to further my education with you by my side. My goal is to be on the Deanâs list with a 4.0 GPA, and most importantly, for you to be proud of me. My gorgeous black glistening coat is so beautiful, it could glow in the dark. I am such a handsome fellow but my friends always tell me they have a crush on my mind, they fell in love with my personality, and my handsome looks are just a big bonus! 

Rose are red, violets are blue . . .  please take me home with YOU! Email:  rescue@lamanchaanimalrescue.org.

- 2 years old
- Black Lab mix

 

UTD vaccinations, chipped, spayed/neutered, wormed.

name: Dexter
description:
DEXTER:

Hello all, my nameâs DEXTER. I am a mid-size ~45 lbs Hound mixed with lots and lots of love!  I came to LaMancha from Kentucky after living outside all my life (9 whole years!) on a chain tied to box!  Life-on-the-chain was very lonely and sad, and it was so hard living outside 24/7 in all weather elements. It feels so good to be set free of chains. Please donât let the number deter you--donât be fooled by my age! It may be nice to be eligible for those senior discounts, but by no means do I want to be called a senior. Just remember, nowadays, just like humans, we can take a decade off our age . . . and I feel great! I have the perfect energy, and Iâm not ready to settle down, unless of course, you are!  Iâll adapt to your lifestyle pretty quickly. Iâm happily living my life at LaMancha temporarily till my perfect people comes along and adds me to their family. I am an easy guy to fall in love with because of my high-spirited personality, cheerful, positive attitude, and striking, adorable looks. I already have a big fan base at LaMancha. It has been an easy transition for me from living outside tied up all my life to having freedom. Love is like the wind; you canât see it but you can feel it, and the LaMancha volunteers have done wonders for my soul.  

The feeling of freedom never felt so good! My soul and happiness are free from chains now but my freedom is up to you! Letâs live that amazing life we both dream about. What makes you happy will make me happy.  Please come meet me: rescue@lamanchaanimalrescue.org.

- 9 years young
- Hound mix

Dogs will be removed from PetFinder only when they have an approved application or more than three (3) interested applicants.

Where did this dog come from?...  We rescue dogs from 100% kill shelters in West Virginia and on occasion from Kentucky.  On rare occasions we accept owner surrenders.  Due to the nature of the shelters they were rescued from, we often do not know the dogs' history.

How Old is this dog?...  We look at a dogs' teeth to estimate its age, and then the age is reevaluated by our veterinary staff when the dog is spayed/neutered.  If an age is not posted online, please feel free to inquire.

Is this dog Good With Kids?...  We occasionally know for sure if a dog is good with kids because it came from a home with kids.  This is rare.  We always suggest you bring your children in to meet the dog if you are seriously interested in adopting.  Dogs may like some kids and may dislike others.  Dogs are individuals, just like kids are.

Is this dog Housebroken?...  Advice from a veterinarian:  Even if a dog is housebroken at my house, it does not mean that it understands not to pee at someone else's house.  It ONLY understands not to pee at my house.  Some dogs make the connection that they should only pee outside.  Some must be retrained when they come home.  All we can tell you for sure is whether/or not a dog's crate is clean when we come to walk them in the AM.  All this means is that they are crate trained and waited to pee until we took them outside.

What is this dog's Temperament?...  We do not have a clear picture of a dog's temperament until we have allowed them to settle in for a few days.  Even then they are living in a shelter environment with many other dogs and a lot of daily activity.  It can be difficult to say a dog is \"calm\" or \"nervous\" when the shelter environment is playing a big role in that behavior.  We only rescue FRIENDLY dogs who have no known bite history.  If a dog is at Small Miracles, it likes people and has a good temperament.  We always suggest you meet the dog to see if it is the right fit for your lifestyle. 

What are your Fees?...  Base adoption fee is $325 for adult dogs and puppies.  To this, we add a $30 microchip fee, which we register for you, and a 6 month supply of heartworm preventative.  Heartworm preventative costs $40-60 depending on the weight of the dog.  This means that a large dog will total $405.00 and an extra large dog will total $415.00.

Why can't I adopt a FREE dog?...  Our adoption fee covers many procedures which cost much more for us then the amount we ask for from you. We spay/neuter all pets, and we give them their first round of vaccines (canine distemper, bordatella, Rabies if age appropriate).  At a typical vet clinic this would cost you $500 at minimum for the surgery, and each vaccine is roughly $35 each.  Even if your adopted dog does not have all of its shots due to the mandatory waiting period between booster shots, we offer vaccinations at the low cost of $20/shot.  We test all dogs for heartworm disease and tickborn illnesses such as Lymes.  We never euthanize a heartworm positive dog, and treatment routinely costs us $3000/dog.  We collect a fecal sample from every rescued dog and run a microscopic parasite test.  Any parasites found will be treated with two rounds of the appropriate dewormer.  We treat all dogs for fleas and ticks with Advantage.  If a dog has significant dental disease or \"very dirty teeth\

Kassie is part of a litter of 13 puppies that came to us from Kentucky. They were turned in by their owners to Dumas Rescue. The puppies have had multiple dewormings, received their first distemper/parvo combo shot, microchipped, flea/tick/HW preventative applied, and received a clean bill of health from our veterinarian, Timberview Veterinary Hospital. These puppies are staying in a foster home in New Cumberland PA 17070. We do adopt out of state, but you need to appear in person to complete the adoption. You should mapquest New Cumberland to see if you are willing to travel that far before completing an adoption application. You must have an approved adoption application on file before you can schedule a visit with the puppies. You can complete one online at https://homewardbound2u.rescuegroups.org. If you have questions about their personality, you can email their foster mom, Tiffany, at twhite@weavermoving.com. Teena Nigro will be processing your adoption applications.

name: Vito
description:
weight: 10 pounds
estimated age: 2 years

From Vito's Foster Mom
Vito is currently in a foster home where he is learning how to be a 'normal' dog. We have no idea what his story is, but he is a smart boy who is eager to please. Vito would do best in a home with a person who has experience with reactive/anxious dogs. He would also love a small laid-back dog sibling who he can play with and snuggle up to. He loves to go for walks and does very well on a leash, but gets overly excited when he sees other dogs or strangers. He's working on that and will need continued training to greet dogs and strangers. For this reason, he needs to be in a home with no small children. Vito is house trained except for a rare 'oops', and he will sleep in a crate, in a dog bed, or in your bed. He loves belly rubs, cuddling up with you for a nap, and running free in a fenced yard. If you have the patience and are willing to put in some work, you will be rewarded with a wonderful little dog!

name: Millie *Foster*
description:

If you are interested in more information about me including my most up-to-date status and/or would like to set up a meeting with me, please send a completed adoption application (found here - http://www.providenceac.org/adopt-a-pet/how-to-adopt/) to foster@providenceac.org today! I hope to hear from you soon! XOXO Millie\

name: Toni
description:
This Cute little man is Antonio! Antonio came from a hoarding situation down in Kentucky so has not had the best living environment for most of his life. He is coming along well at his foster's house he currently lives with other dogs, cats and 2 kids and does good. Antonio can be shy when first meeting but once he comes around he loves cuddling in your lap and following you around the house, he even has cute little spaz moments where he jumps around! He would love a home that understands at first he will be shy but comes around and will love you unconditionally! They are working on his potty training and are coming along great! Antonio is looking for his special home...Could that be you!!???

description:
Brianna is a 2 year old Mountain Cur mix that came to us from Kentucky with 6 puppies.  Her pups have all been adopted and now it is mom's turn!  She was bone thin when she came to us, giving everything she could to her babies.  She was a wonderful mom, and once we got her fattened up, she was able to raise her pups just fine.  Brianna is very sweet and is a perfect size to be a part of your family.  She is good with kids, other dogs, and doesn't mind the cats.   

This dog's adoption fee is $175. That fee includes spaying/ neutering, microchipping, deworming and vaccinations. If you would like an adoption application, please send an email message to adoptprebleco@yahoo.com

name: Farro
description:
Hi, my name is Farro! I'm originally from Lexington Ky, my two sisters, brother and I were born the weekend of the Kentucky derby. Everyone just thinks I'm super cute because of my unique coat...AND they're right! Momma is a Rat or Fox Terrier and I never met my daddy but I think I take after momma's side of the family because everything about me from my gorgeous fur and my long supermodel legs to my \"working dog\" personality just screams terrier. (Wirehair Fox Terrier I think if I could trace my ancestry) I am a calm personality most of the time but I can hold my own with my bossy sisters. I'm bigger than my sisters at 10 pounds, but I have an athlete's build. I love, treats and laying in your lap to get petted but I love the outdoors too. I have so much to do and see every day that I don't have much time for lying around napping! I love to explore! I love TOYS, other dogs, kids and getting attention from EVERYONE! My diva sisters are usually hogging all the attention but I shoulder them out of the way when I've had enough of waiting for my turn. I live with a Mastiff, Boxer/Pit, Shih-Poo and my two sisters and I can take them all on! I am only 17 weeks old but I'm mature for my age. I'm good in my crate and keep it pretty clean. Since I'm not a baby anymore I'm in school learning some basic obedience (sit, down and here) and walking on a harness and leash. Cheese is my favorite food mostly because I only get it when I'm in school. I am looking for a place of my own where I can explore with friends, get a job and see some of the worlds. I'm all recovered from my surgery and ready to move out to my own place. Do you think a fun-loving, hard-working, studious and an adventurous roommate is your pace? If so apply to meet me!

DOB 5/4/2019

name: Duke
description:
Duke is a beautiful black and tan German Shepherd with a classic coloring and confirmation that speaks to american bloodlines. Duke is estimated around 15 months of age. Duke came to us from a rural area of Kentucky where he had been living on a farm but was surrendered to the shelter for chasing livestock. Duke doesn't have much herding sense and is certainly not the best farm dog but he has lots of love to give. 

Duke is the definition of a big baby - he enjoys cuddles, butt scratches, and always being nearby for lovings. Duke is an enthusiastic boy who doesn't have a good concept of personal space therefore he is thrilled to be the over-sized lap dog you didn't know you needed. Duke does well when introduced to new people in public and introduced properly to visitors. He has been around children 7 and up without any issues but given his size and energy level we would not recommend him for a home with children under 6 or children that are not accustomed to large dogs.  

Duke does well with the other dogs in his foster home and navigates play groups well. He is a sensitive soul and gets his feelings hurt pretty easily which is in contrast of his lack of manners when meeting new dogs. He can be a typical pushy young dog when meeting new dogs and gets his feelings hurt when the other dog tells him to knock it off. He is learning with every interaction though and getting a good handle on social behavior. Duke has not been around any dogs under 40 lbs nor has he been tested with cats. 

Duke is searching for an active and loving home that will feed his sense of adventure while also providing guidance and training to ensure he keeps his best paw forward. If you're the home for Duke please email Tierhavenrescue@gmail.com for an adoption application or visit adoptapet.com/tierhaven for FAQs

name: Macy
description:
Macy is an adorable young girl around 9 months of age who is believed to be a Shepherd Cattle dog mix. Macy came from a rural part of Kentucky where she was live-trapped after being born to a pack of Shepherds that were free-roaming on a farm. Macy had zero human contact prior to being trapped and has been very slow to warm up. She is considered semi-feral at this point and is still overcoming her fears. 

Macy prefers to avoid all human contact but has begrudgingly learned how to walk on a leash and tolerate being handled for daily living. Macy is a fear biter and if cornered - such as when she is in her crate and needs to come out - she will lash out in fear. If you move slowly with Macy she settles down and will allow you to handle her but she gets overwhelmed easily when rushed. Macy is going to require extensive ongoing handling, training, and socialization coupled with lots of patience as she continues to grow and bond. 

Macy connects with other dogs much better than she does people as a result of her early life in a pack. She does well meeting new dogs and is quick to follow their lead. She isn't at a place of comfort that she plays often but every now and then she will forget the people are around and start to play with one of the other young dogs. Macy has not been around cats or small dogs although she is relatively small herself. We do not know how she would do as there is not true way to test her given her discomfort on leash. 

Macy has a sweet soul and is trying her best to overcome her fears and bond with the people around her. Macy is searching for a home that can provide her a stable environment and ongoing work as she continues to grow beyond her past. 

If you have a place in your heart and home for Macy please email Tierhavenrescue@gmail.com for an adoption application or visit adoptapet.com/tierhaven for FAQ

name: Crissy & Molly
description: Crissy is an 8 year old Cattledog/Hound mix while Molly is a 10 year old lab mix. These girls have been through a lot together and we would like them to live their lives out together in the perfect home. Crissy and Molly lived with one owner most of their adult lives. He passed away roughly 8 months ago and a family friend agreed to take the two girls to avoid them being sent to the shelter. Their previous owner lived in Florida so the girls were transported from Florida to Kentucky to settle in with the family friend. Unfortunately, just as these girls were settling and really starting to get comfortable again the new owner accepted a new position  with her job and was transferred to Texas and did not plan to take the two senior girls with her so they were surrendered to our facility. These girls are very easy going, Molly is very sweet and happy to see everyone, Crissy can be a bit shy at first but will quickly approach for attention, Crissy just isn't as excitable as Molly. Both are very mild mannered and are fine with other animals. As far as we know they are housebroke, Molly had a lipoma (fatty growth) removed from her leg when she was spayed but there is no need for any additional treatment. Crissy had a large wart taken off her ear when she was spayed but again, there is no need for additional treatment. These girls have been given a clean bill of health and are just looking for the perfect family to love them and give them the stability they are desperate for.

name: Aretha
description:
Beautiful Aretha has the stunning markings of a Catahoula Leopard Dog, gorgeous amber eyes, and undeniable charisma. Sheâs just 2 years old (est. birthdate 4/17) and weighs a healthy 60 pounds. 

Aretha has travelled a long, rough road. She came to STAF from an overcrowded, high-kill county shelter in Kentucky. Upon arrival, we discovered that she had a microchip registered in Tennessee. We reached out to her family of record, who told us that theyâd given her away and did not want her back. To add insult to injury (literally!) a paw injury required Aretha to spend five weeks on restricted exercise and in an e-collar. 

Aretha likes rubs and pets as much as the next dog, but she is happiest with vigorous exercise and hard workouts. The Catahoula in her needs a purpose in life â¦ retrieving tennis balls, brisk walks and running are her favorites.  She also shows great potential on agility courses. If there is a doggy-version of a triathlon, weâve no doubt Aretha would rock that, too. Sufficiently exercised, she is a undemanding, affectionate girl. 

Thanks to a weekly training class and special attention from The Pet Spot trainers (thank you, Eric & Lee!), Aretha has a great obedience-foundation and is happy to work for treats and praise. And speaking of praise, hereâs some from Arethaâs favorite volunteer and standing Thursday-night training date: âAretha is one of the smartest dogs I have been around. She is very trainable, and would be a great Frisbee dog. Properly presented, Aretha will accept new tasks and training very well. I keep treats in my pocket, and Aretha will paw at my pocket asking for a treat. Her vision is incredible, and she can spot people, dogs, birds at amazing distances. Aretha will bond quickly with her new family. I think in a day or two, with some play and treats and pets, she will be a great dog for an active lifestyle family.â

name: Shiloh
description:
Shiloh is a handsome young boy who is estimated around 3 years of age. Shiloh was completely feral when he arrived with Tier Haven from Hazard, Kentucky. He clearly had never been handled prior to this time and we are unaware of the circumstances surrounding his first few months.

Shiloh still has a very long way to go in trusting people. He has zero confidence in himself or the world around him resulting in a very timid and shy dog. Shiloh has no fear aggression and has never lashed out but is going to require a home with the patience to work with him to overcome his past. Shiloh does really well with people from a distance of about 5-7 feet and will linger on the outskirts of interactions but doesn't know what to do when the attention is turned to him. Shiloh will come up and nudge from behind seeking attention but does best when there isn't a big fuss made about it. He has a desire to be around people but is still so unsure of him.

Shiloh does great with other dogs and really relies on them for social cues. He was running with another dog - Bentley - who we suspect is his brother. Shiloh was definitely the follower and has stayed true to that role. He does great with other dogs and has learned how to navigate play groups really well. He would really benefit from having another dog or group of dogs in a home to show him the ropes and help him overcome his fears.

A volunteer reached out to us about Shiloh within minutes of when he was scheduled to be euthanized - there was certainly a large hand guiding him to safety and we hope to see him fulfill his potential with a loving home. 

If you have a place in your heart and home for this sweet young boy please email tierhavenrescue@gmail.com for an adoption application.

description:

He is an easy keeper.  He is completely vetted including a microchip.  He likes rides in the car, will play with some toys or sit quietly near his human when you watch tv or chill out on the patio.

He has a beautiful sable soft coat that glistens in the sun.  His adoption fee is $100.00,  If you are intersted in adopting this senior, please go to the website on the home page under services and complete an application. www.faerielandrescue.org.

name: Rebecca
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.
SBF (single brindle female) seeking long term commitment. No fakers. I like long walks or snuggling by the

TV

. I'm very laid back. I have 4 grown offspring that are all out of the house. I came here from Kentucky in April 2019. I have had some obstacles to overcome and conquered every one like a true Southern belle.

If you'd like to be interviewed for possible acceptance, please fill out an application.

Note from foster family;

This girl has been a dream foster. Rebekah ( we call her Lexi, short for Lexington, Kentucky) is potty trained, she is an amazing walker, she's a talker. I mean like a 16 year old girl who's really going to try to get her way. She's not much of a player. Meaning that playing fetch or toys with people just not her thing. But, if you say \"walk\" or even make her think there's going to be a walk in her near feature she loses it. Never seen a dog so excited to go on walks. Walks are very important for Lexi. Please consider if you already have a life style that includes or the ability to walk at least 2 times a day. We do about .5 -2 miles each walk 2-3 times a day. She has become accustomed to hanging out at our cabin. Lexi is my only foster I have EVER let off leash. I know I might get in trouble with NDLB because I'm sure this is not allowed but we did this with extreme caution and only after we had her for about 3 months. She pretty much just lays in the sun, eats grass and moves to a shady spot when she gets warm. She loves chasing bugs and the occasional critter so we still keep a close eye on her. Someone really loved this dog once; I sure wish I had her whole story.

Her only behavior that concerns me is I'm pretty sure she's an escape artist. Might be how she ended up in this situation. I think she would do best in a laid back household as she take time to warm up to new people.

Lexi kennels without a problem, even when we first got her. She has been with us for a long time now, we don't kennel her anymore.

She does really well with other dogs but too much peopleing can be stressful for her. She lets you know when she needs a break from a crowd of people.

Adoption fee includes: Full veterinary exam, prepaid microchip, dewormed, Distemper combo vaccines appropriate to age, Bordetella vaccine, rabies vaccination, alter, 4dx, heartworm and flea/tick preventative while in rescue. Adoption fee: $425.00

name: Mousey
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.
Name: Mousey
DOB: 6/17/17
Weight: 43.8 Pounds
Adoption Fee: $350

Hi there my name is Mousey but my foster family calls me Libby! My foster parents say I'm the sweetest but they really hope I will learn to trust others too so others can see just how sweet I am. They say if you take one look at my piercing eyes you can see into my soul. I came to Minnesota from Kentucky and was in a shelter for some time and I was so scared I would spend my days hiding under a pile of blankets. I didn't find comfort in any humans until my foster parents, I have learned to trust them but I am still working on my trust in strangers. My foster parents say that a dog savvy owner will be very beneficial to help instill confidence in me and continue to work on my training. When I see new people I bark and growl and I can look really mean but I'm doing it because I'm scared. It would be best for me to be in a home that doesn't have a lot of visitors and to have a bit of space outside because I have a hard time having fun outside when I'm making sure the neighbors are staying put. I stay in the crate during the day and I keep my crate clean and I'm going potty on a schedule!

I love going on walks and my interaction with all dogs has been great. I really look to other dogs to know that everything is okay. My new home should have confident dog already in the home so I can continue my socialization training through them. Once we get over our initial meeting, I will love you more than you can imagine. I am a great cuddle buddy; I do great in car rides and just really can't get enough love! Please fill out an application if you would like to meet me or learn more about me!
