name: Blake
description:
Blake is a 5-year-old neutered yellow male lab. He weighs 62 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Blake is a sweet, happy boy. He is good with other dogs and used to live with two others in his previous home. We don't know how Blake is with cats. He is very curious and is quite interested in all the daily activity of the suburbs. He loves to look out the window at home and in the car. He has been fascinated by joggers and was completely mesmerized by a sprinkler. He has been very interested in everything the family is doing. He likes to lay in the kitchen while we are cooking and eating dinner, but never begs or gets into the garbage. Blake does not bark and does not jump on strangers. He has not had the opportunity to learn basic commands but has demonstrated he can learn quickly and responds when you correct him. He went from crazy dog on a leash to a calmer and responsive walker on the harness. Blake will make a great addition to a family and will quickly bond. He has loads of personality and has perfect house manners.

UPDATE from Blakeâs foster family:  Blake is a sweet, sweet boy and is doing great in his foster townhome. He is housebroken and has free reign over the house when his foster needs to be gone. He has not been crated; he did scratch at the door when left alone initially, but calmed after a couple of days. His foster works-from-home, so he does get a potty break every four hours. Blake is great with the fosterâs teenager. He knows sit, and he quickly learned paw! He is a great eater, is not protective of his food, and sleeps through the night. He gets excited when you first get home and tends to jump, but that is something that can be trained. Blake is a love bug and loves snuggling in your bed or the sofa - he would a family that will let him on the furniture:) 

Blake is a playful guy and walks ~4 miles each day to expend his energy. He is very strong, and his handler needs to be prepared for him to pull hard if he senses something he wants to investigate. He is learning to walk on a leash and doing MUCH better, but ongoing training is needed. He wants to meet people and dogs on his walks and does well; he has not spent time alone with other pups while with his fosters. Blake is a cuddly, fun-loving boy and is the perfect match for a family willing to give him the exercise and ongoing training he needs.

description:
Lakota is a 2-year-old boy born July 2017 who came to us from a shelter where his previous owners dumped him. He was purchased as a puppy and lived most of his life outside. He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

Lakota would do best in a home with no young children. He did well when seeing other dogs on walks and we will continue to work with him and see how he does with a female companion. He is super smart and knows how to sit. name: Apollo the White Knight
description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature. 

If you are interested in adopting Apollo, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

name: Pokie
description:
Pokie is a 9-year-old neutered male chocolate lab. Pokie weighs 61 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Pokie is an exceptionally loving, sweet boy that adores all people and his toys. This silly boy has a toy on him at all times - so much so that we've had to teach him to check his toy at the door before he goes outside. Pokie has exceptional house manners. He is fully house trained and has full run of the house while we're out. He also loves going for rides in the car. Pokie is quiet and only lets out an occasional bark when there's someone at the door. Pokie is partially blind due to complications from diabetes, but he does see shadows and gets around just fine. He loves running around the yard and playing ball (he listens for the bounce and is quite good at locating it). His diabetes is well controlled with two injections a day that are quite easy to do. Pokie's other passion is food and he equates getting his insulin with a biscuit, so he eagerly sits in anticipation of getting his injection and treat. He would do well as an only dog or have a laid back doggy companion. No kitties. Pokie has so much love to give his forever family. He is such a sweet gentleman, LOVES people, toys and catching some rays. Pokie is mostly blind due to diabetes, but runs full speed around the house. He has excellent house manners and is a complete sweetheart. Pokie would do great as an only dog or with another super laid back companion. 

Foster family reports: Pokie is a wonderful companion. He loves to play with people and is getting along with the pack. Pokie adores everyone he meets and is very affectionate. Pokie loves to play ball (he tracks very well with his hearing). He is perfect in the house - he has never had an accident or gotten into anything he shouldnât. His thyroid and diabetes management have remained very stable. He would probably do best with a quiet doggy sibling or on his own.

description:
Maddie is our little Miss Cutie Patootie! She is a short and stocky malamute girl with so much personality. She is guaranteed to make you smile every day with her paw up for high fives and zoomies. Maddie was born October 2011. She is easy and independent. She is called a little miss spit fire, because she is a tough little cookie! She is sassy and all malamute. She enjoys being in her crate and doesn't make a peep. Or hanging outside watching everyone and everything. She also enjoys hiking and just loves the outdoors! She is also happy just laying around on her doggy bed and just being in the same room as you. Don't let that adorable teddy bear look fool you, she isn't a cuddler and prefers her space, EXCEPT when salmon treats are involved. She will come right up to you, give you high fives and show so much excitement for treat time! Just give her space and time to get to know you. She had a very rough life and is hesitant to trust people. Despite this, she sits nicely to put her collar on before going on a walk. She also rides well in car but generally speaking, Maddie doesn't just do things willingly, which is why positive training works well for her. KronchUSA salmon treats really help us encourage Maddie to make good choices. She likes to protest a little bit just enough so she feels like she had a choice.  

She will roll over for belly rubs and come up to you for some love but when shes had enough she will leave and go about her business. She was potty trained at one time but will need a refresher. She does not like other dogs but can be around them. If given the chance she will let other dogs know she is boss and that's why we recommend her as being the only dog in the home. When you are out on a walk she won't get upset seeing another dog as long as they are behaving. She isn't dog aggressive but won't back down from a challenge either. 

In May 2017, Maddie had ACL surgery on her right knee and is doing well. Of note, she was debarked as a pup so she doesn't have her 'woowoo' but don't let that stop you from giving this girl her second chance. She needs a home with Northern Breed experience. She has a strict limited ingredient diet --- salmon only protein and fat. Typical malamute she cannot be around small dogs or pets including cats.

description:
Born in August 2014, Bucky has a great sense of humor and is full of personality.  He would love to be your hiking companion followed by a picnic with a chicken sandwich. He LOVES car rides and visiting the nearby pet stores where all the goodies are. Bucky is a very social Malamute/Husky mix and would love a family of his own. He is a free spirit who responds beautifully to pawsitive communication. He enjoys chasing and burying balls (especially squeaky balls) and really enjoys going out on hikes exploring. He has separation anxiety and would do best in a home with a stay at home human. He is an amazing boy with high predatory behavior that can spot any critter or find deer. With cheerful redirection, he will give up the chase to stay with his human.

Bucky is always ready for an adventure but we believe he is trying to find his furever home. Bucky will behave so well, then out of the blue it's like he has to celebrate being good and will surprise you with the fastest zoomies!  However, this is far and few these days. He enjoys just being where you are & hanging out. He has been receiving positive training and has learned to redirect his excitement by sitting for a treat and sitting so the car door opens for an adventure. Most recently he is learning to relax, which he enjoys with chicken sandwich bite size rewards. Bucky looks like a very tall Siberian Husky. Bucky would benefit from pawsitive reinforcement training classes and someone with a good sense of humor. Bucky just wants to have fun, so learning how to communicate being consistent & calm works great for Bucky, especially with a soft yummy treat. 

With so much to give, he definitely will make someone happy once he settles in and knows he's loved. He prefers to be the only pet in the home...who doesn't like to be the star of the show?!?!  We recommend reading, Positive Perspectives 2 - Know your Dog Train your Dog by Pat Miller.  This book will open your eyes from a dogs perspective & help you communicate & train in a pawsitive manner.  To know Bucky is to love Bucky. He is such a sweet boy who is searching for his furever home & hooman. Those who meet Bucky can't believe that he hasn't been adopted.

description:

Both are up to date on shots. These dogs are approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Fergus & Jamie are in pretty rough shape but we can fix that. What we don't need to fix is their wonderful spirit and love they have to give. They like to be with you and get like attention.  Jamie will put his head in your lap while Fergus prefers to put a paw in your lap. They are happy to meet everyone with their tails wagging and like getting their bellies and head rubbed. They are inside dogs that like to go outside. They are bonded and will be adopted together. Fergus & Jamie would like a home with a family that will give them lots of love and has a yard where they can play. name: Dagwood
description:
Dagwood is a 1-year-old neutered yellow male lab. He weighs 70 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Dagwood is a super sweet boy! When he first came to us he was very scared and timid. He has really come out of his shell and he loves people! He is still leery of other dogs, mostly those that are \"in your face\" type dogs. He does well with dogs that just coexist with him and do not try to initiate too much. He gets a little intimated if shown too much attention by another dog. Dagwood has lots of good points. He is good on leash and loves to go on group walks. He is affectionate and well behaved. He is housebroken. He also presents his challenges. He is terrified of a crate and will try to break out. He is an escape artist with containment, possibly from his formative years of having to live in a pen with MANY other dogs. He would be best placed with someone who is home most of the time or where he could go with them a lot. We do not have any cat history on him and he is approved for kids 10 and up.

We're not sure how she got to be so large but she's the most food-unmotivated lab! She may or may not eat her breakfast and she's really not into fruits or veggies. She'd also like a couple walks a day to help her build up her stamina and lose some of those pesky pounds. She recently visited with a friend for a weekend sleepover and met two very dog-savvy cats. She initially appeared to want to play with them but that was more effort than she wanted to expend and she laid back down. Marley/Penny found the toy basket, and although she is not a huge player or retriever, she periodically picks up a tennis ball and brings it to you or gnaws on one of the many bones all over the house. She LOVES her walks she doesn't go far and not too fast but she loves all the smells and all the people and dogs met so far. Marley/Penny is a very easy dog that requires little more than a place to sleep, a few pats on her head, some belly scratches and some food. Do you have room in your heart and home for Penny?

name: Doodle Dandy
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8551

2-3 year old Male beagle about 15lbs. Was found in a southern Virginia shelter by a volunteer. 

This dog tested positive for Ehrlichia before arriving to the rescue. Ehrlichia is a very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Ehrlichia is not contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get this disease is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

name: Theon
description:
Name: Theon
Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 5 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 5 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift.

description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8549

 Diane von Furstenberg is a beagle mix girls who is about 5 years old and 27 lbs. Just look at those melting chocolate eyes and smooth long ears - talk about easy on the eyes. 

Diane, who is is fondly called Jolene by her foster family, is a pretty low-key dog. She is timid around new people and will need an adopter who understands that she's going to take some time to warm up. This is all so new to her, and we don't know her background, so perhaps she hasn't had a loving home before. She is very playful with the other dog in her foster home, and this is when we see her fun, quirky side come out. Her foster family is working on slowly socializing her, and helping her to build confidence so her true personality can shine. She is working on her house-training, and does well in a crate - no accidents there, and she is a quiet sleeper. And she walks well on a leash. She is just the sweetest little thing, and we will update her profile as she comes out of her shell more.

This dog tested positive for Ehrlichia and Anaplasmosis before arriving to the rescue. These are very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Neither is contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get either is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

description:
Name: Rosie (fka Jenny)
Suspected Breed: Pit Bull Terrier Mix
Approximate Age: 3 years old
Approximate Weight: 43 lbs
Personality: calm, affectionate, very sweet	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: DC area foster home

Meet Rosie! She's the most chill pup you will meet! She is calm, affectionate, and loves to snuggle. This girl is the sweetest and she is so grateful to be in a rescue searching for her forever home. 

Rosie is one of the few \"bully\" mixes in the Prince George's County Shelter to leave alive. This is due to a ban on bully breeds in the county that prevents adoption of these dogs to the general public. The only bully dogs that leave the shelter alive are released to approved rescues.

The shelter has a group of dedicated staff and volunteers who evaluate and work with these dogs to identify the most highly adoptable ones and pitch them to DC rescues, pleading for their help in saving them. This group lobbied hard for Rosie to be rescued, and DC PAWS is fortunate to have had a willing foster who allowed us to rescue this very deserving gal.

Upon meeting Rosie, it was very clear why she was a staff favorite. She is so gentle and lovely. She gets along well with other dogs and even cats! She is a total couch potato and would make a great fit for an adopter who loves to binge watch Netflix. She would love a calm home where she can be spoiled!

Like most shelter dogs, Rosie may need a refresher on housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Rosie, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

name: Zekke
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8390

Look into my eyes....you will be hypnotized by my charm!

Hello, my name is Zekke! I am six months old and estimated to be a husky mix. I arrived at my foster familys house after a super fun flight all the way from NC. Have you been on a plane ride? It was sure fun.

I've been hanging out with my foster family for a few weeks now and while its fun here, I would sure like to find my forever family as well. Below are some fun things my family wants you to know about me.

- I am crate trained. Im quiet in my crate and sleep the night away and know to keep it nice and tidy with my toys. Can't ask for more than that can you?
- I have kept my crate clean and dry. (If I bark in my crate its because I have to go out)
- I appear to be housebroken but foster Mom says accidents can happen in a new environment. Don't worry, we will both be learning when I come home with you but we will both quickly know how to talk to each other. 
- Ive just about mastered this whole leash walking thing. It was brand new to me when I arrived but I like to take walks so I'm learning how to walk like a good boy mom says. I still get excited sometimes and get tangled in foster mom's legs but we are working through it.
- Im learning other fun things too. I LOVE treats so teaching me things is pretty easy. Ive mastered sit & lay down and am trying REALLY HARD on stay (that one is tough, I like to be with mom when we are outside (she hides cookies in her pockets for me, how can I resist that)) 
 - I appear to be a roll with the punches type of pup. Ive liked everyone, 2 and 4 legged that Ive met so far. 
- Foster Mom says I am one of the easiest fosters they have had. I am quiet, keep the place clean and follow the rules. I think she likes me. :)
- I would do best in a home with older kids (over 12) until I settle down a bit more. Im pretty mouthy still, just like most teenagers. I am working on keeping this under control and am getting better each day. These foster family people don't take any back talk from me about this, they are tough. Mom says my forever people will have to continue to be tough and remind me about this until I fully outgrow it.
- I would be a great hiking or running partner with a little training. Mom & I are doing a bit of running and I LOVE IT! The foster kids started school so we have been super busy and unable to hike but we have talked about it and I'm pretty sure I would like that as well. I love to be busy.
- TOYS! I have discovered TOYS and love them. I am getting pretty good with fetch (I will bring the ball back most of the time, sometimes I get distracted) and love soft toys that make noise. Foster mom told me not to destroy them and I'm doing really good with it. I really am enjoying the toy box here. I like to take one outside each time we go. Silly foster mom picks them all up and brings back inside at bedtime every night for me to start again in the morning.
- I met cats, chickens, turkeys and pigs and am happy to report that I did not bother any of them or care about them.
- two new things we have discovered this week. I like to swim and I liked being in arlington for an event. 

Do you like my new pictures? I went to an event and there was a nice guy named Drew there who took them. I think I look pretty handsome (even if it was 100 degrees that day...whew!)

Anyway, Ill be hanging out in Nokesville, VA. I am able to go home with you as soon as you are approved to adopt. My foster family says someone is going to be very lucky to have me.

name: Zekke
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8390

Look into my eyes....you will be hypnotized by my charm!

Hello, my name is Zekke! I am seven months old and estimated to be a husky/white shepherd mix. I arrived at my foster familys house after a super fun flight all the way from NC. Have you been on a plane ride? It was sure fun.

I've been hanging out with my foster family for a few weeks now and while its fun here, I would sure like to find my forever family as well. Below are some fun things my family wants you to know about me.

- I am crate trained. Im quiet in my crate and sleep the night away and know to keep it nice and tidy with my toys. Can't ask for more than that can you?
- I have kept my crate clean and dry. (If I bark in my crate its because I have to go out)
- I appear to be housebroken but foster Mom says accidents can happen in a new environment. Don't worry, we will both be learning when I come home with you but we will both quickly know how to talk to each other. 
- Ive just about mastered this whole leash walking thing. It was brand new to me when I arrived but I like to take walks so I'm learning how to walk like a good boy mom says. I still get excited sometimes and get tangled in foster mom's legs but we are working through it. *** UPDATE *** Zekke has this down. Has recently been out on a busy street and was perfect on the leash with his foster family and with others.
- Im learning other fun things too. I LOVE treats so teaching me things is pretty easy. Ive mastered sit & lay down and am trying REALLY HARD on stay (that one is tough, I like to be with mom when we are outside (she hides cookies in her pockets for me, how can I resist that)) 
 - I appear to be a roll with the punches type of pup. Ive liked everyone, 2 and 4 legged that Ive met so far. 
- Foster Mom says I am one of the easiest fosters they have had. I am quiet, keep the place clean and follow the rules. I think she likes me. :)
- I would do best in a home with older kids (over 12) until I settle down a bit more. Im pretty mouthy still, just like most teenagers. I am working on keeping this under control and am getting better each day. These foster family people don't take any back talk from me about this, they are tough. Mom says my forever people will have to continue to be tough and remind me about this until I fully outgrow it. *** UPDATE ***: Zekke has really gotten this under control. He has recently met children as young as 1 and did really well with them. He seems to understand they are small and to be gentle with them.
- I would be a great hiking or running partner with a little training. Mom & I are doing a bit of running and I LOVE IT! The foster kids started school so we have been super busy and unable to hike but we have talked about it and I'm pretty sure I would like that as well. I love to be busy.
- TOYS! I have discovered TOYS and love them. I am getting pretty good with fetch (I will bring the ball back most of the time, sometimes I get distracted) and love soft toys that make noise. Foster mom told me not to destroy them and I'm doing really good with it. I really am enjoying the toy box here. I like to take one outside each time we go. Silly foster mom picks them all up and brings back inside at bedtime every night for me to start again in the morning.
- I met cats, chickens, turkeys and pigs and am happy to report that I did not bother any of them or care about them.
- two new things we have discovered this week. I like to swim and I liked being in Arlington for an event. 
- I am super dog friendly. Honestly, I have not met another dog that I have not gotten along with.

Do you like my new pictures? I went to an event and there was a nice guy named Drew there who took them. I think I look pretty handsome (even if it was 100 degrees that day...whew!)

Anyway, Ill be hanging out in Nokesville, VA. I am able to go home with you as soon as you are approved to adopt. My foster family says someone is going to be very lucky to have me.

Are you looking for the perfect, smartest little puppy? STOP right here, you found her! Ribeye is the last of the Steak Pups to find her forever home. Her life started out a bit rough, she was surrendered with her siblings who all were undernourished and scared. She made her way to OPH and has grown so much both physically and mentally. She is amazingly smart, already mastering the \"sit\" command, does well in a crate and housebreaking has been a breeze. She wants to love and please her fosters ALL of the time. She is up-to-date on age appropriate vaccines and will need to be altered at the appropriate age per the spay/neuter agreement you will be signing at the time of adoption.

Please note that because she is so young, she has only received 2 sets of the required 3 sets puppy vaccinations. This is very IMPORTANT because it means that her immune system will not be fully functioning until about 16 weeks of age. She MUST stay out of public places where she could be exposed to the germs of many other dogs for another 6-8 weeks after she goes home. These no puppy zones include all pet stores, dog parks, and for apartment dwellers, areas used by other dogs. These requirements are strictly for the puppys medical safety and longevity.

name: Fritos
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs7865

\"Under your scars I pray you're like a shooting star in the rain. You're everything that feels like home to me.\" From the song \"Scars\" by Godsmack

* Will love you unconditionally until the very end? 
* Loves to be outside playing ball, going for walks, car rides, maybe runs or possibly a frisbee partner? 
* Will keep your yard critter free? 
* Comes pre-loaded with a billion kisses? 
* Is pre-trained for belly rubs? 
* Enjoys learning new tricks? 
* Can be self-entertained with toys and bones?

I recently had Medical Patellar Luxation (MPL) Surgery! The wonderful vet who did my surgery said I am finally ready to find my forever home! I can do everything a dog can do: take walks, go for power walks and even play fetch now! 
So if you are looking for a great dog, Come with me, the time is right, there will be no better team!

name: Flannery O'Connor
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs7491

Flannery is 2 years old and weighs about 30 lbs with a look and a personality like a min-pin. She is an energetic, busy girl who LOVES to go for lots of walks and would likely even be a nice running buddy. She is smart and curious and will thrive on challenges. She just completed an Intro to Agility class and was a SUPERSTAR! With more training, she could be a serious competitor. She has mastered the tunnel, A-frame, hoop, and can jump anything you put in front of her. She has also been introduced to the teeter and the dog walk. Flannery will fetch anything - balls, frisbees, toys, even rocks!

Her funny personality, keeps us all chuckling. She loves to play with toys and when no one is available to play with, she will just toss toys to herself! Flannery is also a first-class snuggler and a Phillies fan.

Like her namesake, Flannery is a spunky southern girl. She will need an adopter who has some dog experience. That steller brain of hers could easily take over the show. She will do best in a home without children, while she adores children, she has a tendency to nip grabby hands. She gets along fine with other dogs, does fine with cats, has great recall off-leash, and is housebroken and crate-trained. She is smart, willing, intense, athletic, and speedy. While Flannery can be a quirky dog, she is also a sweetheart who will keep you entertained and adored for years to come. Looking for a best, best, best friend? Look no further.

name: Betty (fka Chili/Totoro)
description:
Name: Betty (fka Chili/Totoro)
Breed: Lab mix
Approximate Age: 1.5 years old
Approximate Weight: 20 lbs
Personality: People friendly, but sensitive around men
Observations with Dogs: slightly reactive - will need training 
Observations with Cats: unknown
Observations with Kids: cannot be placed in home with kids under 18
Currently Living at: DC area foster home

Meet Betty! Betty is a sweetheart in need of a loving home. Betty has a lot of great attributes - she loves to play, seeks out affection and attention, and is a quick learner. Betty is also very sensitive and has shown a hesitancy towards men. She is also slightly reactive towards dogs while on a leash. Betty will need a very patient, experienced dog owner to help her come out of her shell and become the best dog she can be. She will do best in a low traffic, calm home. She would also benefit from working with a behavioral consultant to help manage her fear of men and to feel more comfortable on a leash. Betty is the kind of dog that needs love and compassion and is the reason why rescues exist. If you feel you can give her a chance, please apply to adopt her!

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Betty, please submit an adoption application at http://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogsDC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

She would do best with a patient adopter in a calm home, where she can have the space to come out of her shell. She is worth it, trust us! Because she is so shy with humans, she would be happiest in a home with another dog to help build her confidence. She needs a bit of stable living to learn that not all humans mean to bring her harm or neglect. She is good with other dogs and cats.

Foster reports Del is very friendly and great with other dogs and people, and also very affectionate! Just watch some clips of her and her!

When the shelter asked us to save this sweet senior, how could we say no? Just look at her adorable frosted face? How does a dog like this end up in the shelter, we wonder? Currently Living at: DC area foster home

Meet majestic Gulliver! Surrendered at a SC shelter for not getting along with the resident dogs, Gulliver quickly proved that he is indeed good with most dogs... sometimes dogs just need a proper introduction. Although Gulliver passed his cat test, he is VERY interested in cats & may want to play with them. Obviously most cats wouldn't enjoy this so he may do better in a house with no cats. He does well with other dogs but he MUST have a PROPER introduction. He can only be adopted by an experienced (large breed) adopter who is willing to hire a trainer. Gulliver was not given any training in his first home so he needs a lot of work on his manners. If he were to go to a home with another dog, there should be 2 adults in the home. It is just too much for one person to handle Gulliver + another dog.

In addition to the above, we're looking for an adopter who doesn't have young children (under 12) & has a fenced (6') in yard. Please make sure you fit all of the above criteria before applying.

Gulliver is still somewhat of a puppy, but he is very treat motivated and smart, so training him should be a breeze. He already knows numerous commands after just a few days in a foster home.

Gulliver is a tad bit underweight if you can believe it, and we need to note that he is a bit of a resource guarder with food. Given his size, he needs an experienced adopter who will agree to work with a DC PAWS approved positive reinforcement trainer to address that issue and to generally teach him how to be a gentleman.

This pup is a rare rescue find (well, perhaps not THAT rare), and his previous guardian's loss can be your gain.

Please note that we anticipate A LOT of interest in this guy and we may not be able to respond to each application right away; we are an all-volunteer rescue of individuals with full time jobs and do our best to be responsive, but sometimes it can be overwhelming with popular breeds like this one. Our goal is to find a home and family that are the best fit for Gulliver, and vice versa. As such, applications will not necessarily be considered on a first come, first served basis. That being said, we anticipate a good match will be found quickly, but we always encourage applications since you never know when applications may fall through.

description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8478

Hi! My name is Steel Magnolia and my foster family calls me Maggie. I am being fostered in Frederick, MD.

Im guessed to be a Hound mix and estimated to be about 2 years old. Im a sweet and gentle girl and I currently weigh about 34 lbs. My foster family is trying to get me to gain some pounds.

Click here to see me in action in my foster home! 

I am...
* A friendly girl and like people of all ages I have met at adoption events.
* Learning about the crate. I am quiet inside and listen to classical music.
* I only had a few potty accidents when I first arrived.I now tell my foster parents when I need to go outside!
* Calm girl inside and get my wiggles out in the yard or on walks.
* I have been friendly with dogs I have met including my foster dog brother and sister. We take walks together and lounge together in the living room.
* My foster family thinks a home without a cat would be a good home for me.

Check back for more updates about me and apply today to set up a meet and greet! 
To adopt this dog, or any OPH dog, fill out the simple online application at https://ophrescue.org 
Operation Paws for Homes, Inc. (OPH) rescues dogs of all breeds and ages from high-kill shelters in NC, VA, MD, and SC, reducing the numbers being euthanized. With limited resources, the shelters are forced to put down 50-90% of the animals that come in the front door. OPH provides pet adoption services to families located in VA, DC, MD, PA and neighboring states. OPH is a 501(c)(3) organization and is 100% donor funded. OPH does not operate a shelter or have a physical location. We rely on foster families who open their homes to give love and attention to each dog before finding a forever home.

name: The Hobbit
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8481

 Meet The Hobbit - known fondly to her foster family as Lady Arwen or Lady for short. She is a 45-50 pound, one year old, beagle/spaniel/lab mix is our best guess. She has gorgeous creamy coloring and luxurious fur - hard to keep your hand out of it. And she doesn't mind the gentle petting and attention at all. She has her nose to the ground all the time - perhaps a nod to her beagle heritage? And she has long silky fur that one might associate with a spaniel. She is so gentle and sweet, and has done beautifully with children, other dogs and car rides. Each day we see more of her exquisite personality shining through. She's very loving and sweet. She's also smart and loves to cuddle. She's been really great with our 2 year old and our 12 year old twins, but our 7 year old is a little too rambunctious for her.

More about this darling girl:
- She is house trained in her foster home, and has visited homes of family members and remembered her house manners there as well.
- She is crate trained, and knows that her crate is her personal den and uses it at time to get some downtime, to relax and unwind. She is a smart girl understanding her personal space.
- She is working on improving her leash skills. She likely never walked on a leash before coming to her foster home, and she likes to pull. With training she is improving and to become really adept and walk on a loose leash, her adoptive family will need to continue the training process.
- She may be shy when meeting new people, but she has impeccable manners - not a jumper
- She is learning her house manners - she likes being on the couch which is fine in her foster home, but she may have to be trained otherwise in her adoptive home. She is very agile and has jumped up to get food from the table. She is learning quickly that is is not acceptable in her foster home. 
- She is generally quiet. She will alert at random times but it's few and far between.
- She is learning to trust humans more thoroughly and quickly, and her fosters are consciously socializing her to help her build confidence. She would rather people kneel down to pet her instead of looming over her. She gets nervous if someone comes up behind her too quickly and can startle if she is bumped into by accident. I think she needs more work on trusting humans in general. She shows no reactivity or aggression, but retreats to her crate if she feels overwhelmed. 
- She loves to run around in the backyard. She loves to play with other dogs. She seems to be a moderate energy dog and she is still trying to figure out how it all works inside a home.
- She loves to play with other dogs.
- She has not been exposed to cats, but her foster thinks she could do well with a confident cat. She's tried to go after squirrels on walks and birds get her attention.

name: Belle (& Taco)
description:
This sweet bonded pair, Taco & Belle, have had unfortunate luck in their very short lives. They lost their original owner suddenly to a stroke and were passed around to different family members for a few months. They ended up with the 80-year-old grandmother who was legally blind and taking care of her disabled son, so she didn't have the time or bandwidth to take on two young dogs. A family member reached out to Worthy Dog for help, and we gladly took them in.

The duo came to N. VA and were adopted in February by a very sweet couple, and we thought they had found their forever home. Sadly, their current mom, Lynn, who is only in her 30's, is going through a significant and unexpected health challenge, and suffering from kidney failure. She had a kidney transplant 18 years ago and was in great health when she adopted the pups. The couple was so very excited to have these dogs, and even started an Instagram account for Taco & Bell to share updates

About two months ago, Lynn's kidney started failing, and she ended up in the hospital for weeks. She is now on the transplant list waiting for a donor and has to do dialysis 3 to 4 days a week. She travels from VA to MD to a military facility for treatment, and the dialysis wipes out her energy when she gets home. Lynn has been the primary caregiver for the pups and had the flexibility to work from home. Her husband is active duty, and travels frequently, so he's not home during the day to help. Her mom and friends have been helping out, and kept Taco & Bell when she was hospitalized, but it's not a long-term solution.

In the interest of the dogs, Lynn has made the difficult decision to rehome them. She feels they aren't getting the time and attention they deserve, and with another transplant surgery in her future, she may be out of commission for an extended period. She wants to find a home for them before transplant surgery, and have peace of mind that they will be well taken care of. She is fostering them until a great family can be found.

TACO & BELLE

Taco & Belle have been together their whole lives and are a bonded pair. Taco is more timid, but loves his buddy Belle, and looks to her for reassurance. Taco needs a little more time to settle in and trust, but once he connects, he's very trusting and affectionate. Both dogs fancy themselves lap dogs once they get to know you.

This adorable duo loves to play and will keep each other entertained during the day. They are crate trained, enjoy their daily walks, and are potty trained, but do need regular potty breaks. Belle lets you know she needs to go out, and Taco will follow her lead once he settles in. Initially, Taco was prone to marking or excited peeing when he was unexpectedly picked up, but that was more about nerves. They used a belly band to settle him in, and both dogs have been trained on pee pads. Lynn will leave them gated in the kitchen when she goes in for treatment, and has a dog walker or her mom come in when she's out of the home for more than 5 or 6 hours.

These two pups are very connected, so we will only adopt them out as a pair. They are buddies who love to play and nap together and keep each other entertained. They are both afraid of loud noises and strangers and need time to acclimate to visitors, but once they know the person, like grandma, they are all excitement and kisses.

We feel a quiet, calm home is the best fit for them - an adult or senior couple, or empty nesters would be ideal. If you are looking for two little pups who will add joy and much entertainment to your life, please apply today. They are long overdue for their forever home.

name: Bella
description:
Meet sweet, playful Bella who is a petite 32lbs and 1 year old!  She is currently being fostered in Tennessee and available for adoption and transport to most northern states upon a confirmed adoption. Her adoption fee is $275 and is inclusive of ALL transportation and vetting costs.  Bella is spayed, microchipped, current on vaccines, heartworm negative and has recently been given the 6 month Proheart heartworm preventative.  Read on for more info on this loving and special girl!

Bella is a very loving dog.  She will curl up next to you, enjoys sleeping next to foster mom, she is SMART and has responded well to training which is still a work in progress. She was brought into our rescue mid August when her family had some tragic circumstances and due to no fault of their own had to surrender her.  She had been adopted by them just a couple of months before, from a city animal shelter after living as a stray on the streets of Memphis.  She is clearly a survivor! While the shelter had put her at 2-3 years old, our vet said she is actually in the region of 11-12 months.   Putting the pieces together, we believe she was likely born as a stray and survived on the streets for the first part of her life, as so many dogs in Memphis do, before finding herself in the shelter.   Obviously, she had no \"training\" or experience of living in a home.  She came a long way with her first family but didn't have a lot of socialization with other pets because she was an only dog and didn't go out much.  She's now in a foster home where she is exposed to other dogs and cats (she is NOT a fan of cats) and is actually doing well with the dogs in the foster home.  She LOVES going to doggy daycare.  That being said, she has been somewhat selective at daycare. She passed all their tests and is doing really well, however she does better with dogs bigger than herself.  She's not aggressive, but does try to be alpha with smaller dogs, and can be barky and reactive if another dog shows alpha behavior toward her.  For that reason, we think Bella will do best if she is an only dog or if there are other dogs in the home, it must be with someone who feels confident they can work with introductions and integrations.  We have tested Bella with kids 10 and above, and she has been absolutely great with them.

Bella would love a forever home where she can show you how loyal and smart she is! Please donât hesitate to reach out with any questions.

description: Hi, my name is Miami Max and I came to Animal Haven from Miami. My story is pretty intense, but I don't let it get me down! Some amazing rescuers saved my life after I was dragged behind a car, severely injuring my legs and side. It's taken lots of medical treatment to get me on the mend, but I am healing really well! And despite such severe cruelty, I could not be sweeter. I would do best in an adults-only home as the only dog, because I want to be the star. My favorite pastime is giving out kisses and wagging my whole body to tell you I love you. Meet me at Animal Haven!

name: Raven
description:
In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Shakespeare writes of Hermia: \"And though she be but little, she is fierce\". We could not think of a more apt quote to describe our quite small but mighty friend Raven! Raven may be short in stature but she has an infectious personality and spirit that endears her to everyone at our shelter. She has many quirks, such as she gets a little \"foamy\" around the mouth when playing with a favorite toy, but it's all of her quirks that make Raven into such a fascinating dog. 

Raven came to us from our rescue partner that helps transport dogs from Miami to the Northeast and from day one we knew we had a special dog on our hands. It was not just Raven's looks, but also physically how she walked and moved. Raven does have arthritis, and has been having regular acupuncture appointments to help with her condition. She is an incredibly special soul that lights up whenever she is around her friends (both human and stuffed toys) and is waiting for her very own family to come along and see just how incredible she really is!

Contact the Adoptions team at (914) 273-1674 or adoptions@adoptadog,org for more information!

The first step to adopting one of our dogs is to fill out our online adoptions questionnaire located here: http://bit.ly/2WpQHiY

name: Johnny
description: Johnny from the Miami 22 fighting ring rescue has made great strides since being with us at New York Bully Crew. He truly is a sweetheart. He loves his walks and we are happy to report that this once broken and battered boy is now playful and learning how to just be a dog. You really need to meet this handsome bunny-eared boy to truly appreciate his personality. He would love a family of his own. Go to www.nybullycrew.com and fill out the app for our Johnny-boy.

name: Cheetah
description: Hello everyone, my name is Cheetah and I have been in the shelter system for almost 2yrs.  I came to Angelâs Retreat after being pulled from a kill shelter in Miami where I was about to be PTS as I had kennel-cough.  I won the lottery and a donor flew me to NYC in her private plane!  Now I spend my days relaxing by my favorite window and taking walks outside.  Iâm a little on the slow side due to my age, but I still have lots of love to give.  I love being pet and bully sticks are my favorite!  I would make a great companion for someone looking for an easy-going gal.

name: Ramsey
description:
Courtesy Post: Meet Ramsey, He came all the way from a Miami , Florida kill shelter when his foster mom saw he was out of options. Ramsey is your typical mutt which is the best breed ! He appears to have a little of everything- Shepherd, Lab, Bulldog, Terrier ? ...but who knows ! All we are sure of is he is the best boy if you are looking for a loyal companion. Ramsey is 4 to 5 years and 68lbs. He is a healthy and happy boy. He is great with dogs of all sizes, but likes to chase cats. Ramsey is great with kids too! Ramsey is very smart and intuitive, listens to direction, and can free roam without getting into trouble! . Ramsey loves companionship and would do best in a home where he is not left alone for more than a few hours a day. He is good in the car and loves his daily walks. Ramsey is living in South Bend

name: Walker
description:
Meet Walker!  Walker is a one year old Shepherd Mix who weighs about 70 lbs. He came all the way from an Alabama shelter on a rescue transport to find his forever home here in Michigan! He is very friendly once he gets to know you. He is looking for someone who just wants a buddy by their side, but will take the time to gain his trust. Also...loves to play in water, especially sprinklers - video available upon request!  He is great with his foster family's other dogs, mildly interested in their chickens, goats and horses. Not sure about cats.

Walker will need a fenced in yard and an adult family or one with older children. His new owner must be patient with him, as Walker has a very strong \"flight\" response when scared but does OK when you slowly introduce him to new things. Walker does well on a leash, but is very scared of getting into cars. He is housetrained, does well in his crate. Up to date on all vaccinations, microchipped and neutered. 

Walker is available for adoption through Pet Tales Rescue in Grand Rapids, MI. Please go to www.pettalesrescue.com and fill out an application. His adoption fee is $235 plus $15 for the microchip for a total of $250 payable by cash or card through the rescue's website.

* Pet Tales Rescue does not have a physical shelter location as all of our pets are in foster homes. To meet Walker or one of our other fosters, you will need to fill out an application. After your application is reviewed, one of our volunteers will contact you to set up a time to meet him. Thank you for adopting, not shopping!

name: Buffy
description: Buffy came to us from Van Buren county, Michigan. She is not yet available for adoption, awaiting a Rabies vaccination and spaying. She is a high energy and very playful girl. She would be best in a home without small children, but probably a great companion for teens and pre-teens. She is super loving and craves a good belly rub. Ask us about her timeline regarding adoption availabilty

name: Roxie
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Roxie came in stray from Mifflin County. She had face full of porcupine quills. The owner was found and the she was surrendered. Roxie was adopted and went missing... only to be found 3 days later in the woods, porcupined again and very ill. She came back to ODAAT and has been in foster since. We were unsure what her future would hold. She had a bad leg injury that thankfully healed.
Roxie tolerates kids very well. She is extremely chill. A very relaxed, laid back girl
, she would probably do best in a home where she was able to be the Queen. She will attach herself to you immediately. She lays her head against your leg when standing and wants petted. She is most happy just to lay beside you. She loves to ride in the car and honestly... just be with you. We would not suggest cats for Roxie, but she LOVES stuffed animals. She acts like they are her babies.
The Perfect home we are looking for:
Family who wants a companion. A dog that will be dedicated thru and thru.
Family who has possibly one other dog that is laid back and does not care if they play.
Family who will give her all the affection and attention she so deserves.
Family that wants Roxie to be a part of their family. Her favorite place to be is on the sofa beside you... so if sofas are off limits... this girl is not for you.
If your home sounds like the perfect place for our girl, applications are available on our website www.onedogatatime.us.

name: Jake
description:

Jake and Elle are sweet and submissive dogs. They love to meet new friends - dogs and cats alike! Jake is a little less reserved than his sister, Elle. In their foster homes, they are working super hard on their leash training skills and getting better every day. At night, these two sleep in their crates without a problem. Hi, my name is Rocko and I just joined my foster family (I am sitting in my foster mom's lap as she writes this!) I am a super sweet, constant shadow of a lap dog. I love giving kisses! I start off a little shy at first, but it takes me just a few minutes to warm up to my person; treats help! I pick a person but if they aren't home, I pick my second person, and so on. I would love to find a family of my own soon!

My foster home has dogs and cats, and I get along with everyone. I am very persistent to be on my person's lap so I should be the only lap dog in your home. I really like the bigger dog best. The dog my size is bossy and I don't like drama.

I love all people but the very young little people make me nervous if they go too quickly at me. I am very gentle with children but I will need adult supervision around the little people to make sure they go slow and are gentle with me. I am just a little guy so I scare somewhat easy and when I am scared, I growl and bark, which scares kids and I don't want the little kids to be afraid of me.

I will whine and bark for a few minutes until I can't hear you anymore and then I sit quietly or go to sleep. I am quiet when I hear you walk in the door, silently anticipating being reunited with you again! I am sleeping in my crate at night but I would much prefer sleeping with my person in a comfy bed.

CUTE QUIRKS: I love to burrow in blankets when I want to sleep :)

IDEAL HOME: Single family home as Rocko is pretty vocal in his crate at first. He gets loud for such a small dog so shared walls wouldn't work for this little guy. Someone who is home most of the time would be best for him. He gets very sad without his person. A family with older kids or a person/couple with grandchildren 5+ would be a great fit for him. He is very gentle with all children but should be supervised with children 5 and under if grandchildren are visiting.

I'm Khan , a good boy who loves to be active!

My fosters say I'm super soft and love-able. I absolutely love my people! In fact, I sometimes feel magnetized to them and will follow them around the house because I really love their cuddles, pets, treats and reassurance. I am the best combination of couch potato and play buddy!

I love to play fetch and am quite fast!

I don't like being kept in a kennel - I love my freedom! But can be in my kennel from time to time when needed. I am pretty antsy to get out as soon as I hear any commotion in the house prompting me to let me know that my crew is home.

When it comes to new dogs, I could use a bit of a slow introduction to them so that we can get acclimated to each other. I do love to go to the dog park and hanging out with new friends in a neutral territory. However, being an only dog in my previous home, I'm still trying to figure out how to have friends in the same house and may not know how to play and/or initiate play without coming off the wrong way. This awkwardness is getting better as I learn more about my foster fur sibings!

I've been in a family my whole life and looking to continue that family life with a family who will love me a ton! I lived with kiddos in my past life and was recommended to stick to older kiddos as I can get a bit jumpy and also love to do zoomies which can get a little intimidating for a little one. I did spend most of my time with kiddos though and I absolutely love them!

I'm house trained, can sit on command (with treats available!) and am learning to lay down on command. My fosters say I'm smart and want someone who can continue helping me out with this whole training thing. I am very food motivated and eager to please so with enough structure, I will become the best I can be!

My biggest weakness; however, is the darn car. (I don't get how some dogs get excited about this.) I can get motion sickness easily so will often drool more than normal during the car rides to ease my anxiety with these darn tin mobiles. This subsides as soon as we stop and am able to see our destination. My foster parents have learned to just bring a familiar blanket for the car to lay on and an extra towel so I can dry off quicker.

I look forward meeting you and giving you all the kisses. Adopt me? :)

Hey, it's me- Angell! I'm a 7 year old female rat terrier and I'm sweet as cherry pie! I am adjusting well in my new foster home. Though I didn't think I'd find myself in this situation, I'm doing A-OK! You see, I had a home, but I couldn't go with when my family moved.

I do use a crate at night and hardly make a peep. If I had it my way though, I'd choose to sleep with a human while snuggled up & covered in warm toasty blankets.

I'm learning how to \"get down\" and \"sit\" quickly! Shhh, don't tell my foster mom. I already knew those commands before I came. I'm developing more and more self confidence every day, which is helping me so I don't get so excited and urinate a little at your feet. Oops, I hate when I do that!! I do know how to go outside to potty, and a schedule without long periods helps me stay on track. I know I can get there. I just need someone to trust in me and help me develop my strong side!

I've been told I'm an absolute sweetheart. I love meeting new people and exploring the land on leashed walks. Car rides are a plus especially if we stop for a yummy treat! I'm not a picky eater but I might have some food allergies so my foster mom might recommend a special food. It's no biggie though!

Hi! My name is Jack, but my foster mom renamed me to Kai and I'm still learning my name either way. I'm happy to be at my new foster home and am excited to find a forever home. I love to play with stuffed squeaky toys, and will bring them out and toss them around. My foster mom gave up picking them up because I just get them right back out again. There's another dog here too, she's cool. We play together and sometimes wrestle. I wish she would play with the toys with me but she doesn't much, but that's okay. There's two small people here too, they are about my height. I'm gentle and patient around them, but I get a little nervous when I'm sleeping.

I LOVE squirrels, they say I'm obsessed. They just look like lots of fun to chase. There is a cat here too, he keeps his distance from me, but I get really excited when I see him. I cry, bark, and whine; it makes my foster mom nervous I think. I would probably do best in a house that doesn't have cats, or with a very patient one and a family that would take LOTS of time with a slow introduction. There was also a small dog here for a few days when I first got here, I did okay with him. I'm just big and don't really know my size. I didn't hurt him or try to hurt him. We got along well enough. I'm not much for snuggles, but when I get tired I do sometimes lay next to my foster mom on the couch.

When I especially want attention I will go rest my head on my foster mom's lap and she will give me pets, when she stops I just flip her hand back on my head for more... it seems to work well.

I like to go for walks, but I tend to pull really hard. My foster mom put on an Easy Walk harness on me, and that slows me down some. She says I walk better with it on. I could use some training for manners, like sit, heel, come, stay, etc. My foster mom is trying and she started using a clicker with me with treats and when I'm in the house I love treats and like to practice with the clicker. When we are walking though, I don't care for treats, I just want to run or walk fast.

My family is at work all day so I'm in a kennel which is okay. I think I like the resident dogs kennel better as she has pillows, a super soft pad, and is covered with a blanket...it's kind of like a den.

I can't wait to find my forever family. Will you be my family? I'm good with kids, all dogs, and I might be able to learn to ignore cats. I like to be outside, and I think I'm going to like this cooler weather come a lot!
