Hi there! My name is Doorknob but my foster family actually calls me Doorbell, silly huh? I can be a little distant with new people at first, but if you just give me some time I will be your partner in crime in no time at all! I am potty trained on a schedule, and crate trained if lead by a leash, score! I do really well with other doggy friends but sometimes prefer to just lounge around and coexist with them.I also live with a couple of these things called \"cats\" in my foster home and do very well with them. When I was first rescued down in Louisiana,I lived with lots of other chi's in a home that had a fire. However, I came in well fed (maybe a little too well;)). I currently am fed in the morning and at supper time with the correct amount of food per the instructions on the bag. I am happy to say that I've been living a much healthier lifestyle these days and have shed most of my extra pounds after a lot of dieting and hard work! I am fed next to two of my fosters dogs and have been known to try and take their meals when they are not looking. My foster mom makes sure we all eat out of our own bowls so I go and pout until she says potty outside. Those words are my favorite because we all run for the door. I do better off leash and going to the potty so if you have a fence that is a bonus for both of us. I will go potty while on a leash too. I just prefer to run to the door and go straight out side. My foster will be trying a lead in her back yard, come spring time (if I am still here) and she thinks I will do well on that because I will get to choose where I go potty. I have quirks due to my past but am able to live with my foster mom and three human foster siblings ages 15 to 7 without issues. I taught them everything they know on how to take care of me so I feel safe. The fosters know my cues and are working with me everyday to get better and better at being a dog. I do love my blankets and do not like people taking them from me but will share with you once I get to know you and you have the right moves :) I do love to snuggle on my terms (when I want it). I am not fond of being picked up like a baby but my foster mom can show you how to pick me up the way I like it. I have been known to bug my fosters for pets and give them some kisses. My big human foster sister loves to sweep and I cannot stand the broom so I go to my kennel for cleaning time. I can be very playful when I'm in the mood to be and am also known to tell a good story or two (bark) while doing it or of course if that doorbell rings. If I am not in the mood I am usually on my blanket or yours. If you are good at reading dog cues and willing to give me some love and patience I would really like you to fill out an application for me. I really hope to have a family of my own, could that be you?

In the meantime if you have questions or are interested in me, please fill out an adoption application at www.ruffstartrescue.org.

My foster mom says I'm doing great and she even gives me treats when I pass by a squirrel without trying to chase it. I will chase a cat too, so probably best if I am in a home without those. I would love it in a fenced yard where I could run some more and stay outside for longer and just be my goofy self! Overall, I am just not understanding the apartment life and I don't think it is for me.

I am very shy and meeting new people is tough for me, so with that being said, I will need a family that is willing to be patient with me and help me build up my confidence! I might bark when people come into the house but I calm down when they make themselves small and sit on the floor with me. I like to follow my foster mom around, and I always need to know where she is and what she is doing. I like to lay in my crate, but I don't like it when the door is closed for too long, I might bark a lot and try to get out. My foster mom leaves me out now when she goes to work and I do just fine! I do a happy dance and wag my tail in half when she gets home. I can be alone as long as I have things to stimulate me - I love to have the music on and I love to find toys and treats that my foster mom hides for me. I do well with smaller dogs but can get scared of big dogs and I will need slow introductions to them. Sometimes I play a little too rambunctiously (working on that too!), so I will also need practice being around any small children.

Whenever I am scared, or just too overwhelmed, my foster mom pets me for a while and tells me it is ok and I feel better. I think this is why they say all you need is love! Donnie was found on the side of the road on the Pine Ridge Reservation this past winter. He had been trying to make it on his own for far too long in the extreme cold temperatures and was picked up as a popsicle! He was treated for hypothermia and is now safe and warm in his foster home. He is about 50 pounds, our guess is that he is about 2 years old, as he has pearly white teeth. He is the sweetest boy ever. Despite his big head and large size, he fully commits to being a lap dog! He LOVES to cuddle with you on the couch. He is gentle to kids of all ages and gets along with dogs of all shapes and sizes. He really is just a total lover and does not have a mean bone in his body. He took a bath without making a fuss and gets right into his kennel when asked to. He just wants to please you and hear you tell him, \"he is such a good boy\". He is learning about life inside a home and also working his potty training. He loves treats and will be easy to train as he is food motivated. He has already learned that when he hears the fridge door open, he may get cheese if he sits really nice and waits. Donnie really is an all-around awesome dog, with so much love to share.

After lots and lots of tests... Donnie has a diagnosis. He has Reflex Dysnergia. meaning his urethra does not relax at the same time that his bladder contracts, making urination and emptying his bladder impossible at times. Having had this condition for so long his bladder has become distended and 4X larger than it should be. He will require catheterization likely a few times a month to drain his bladder. I did it last night (I'm totally not a vet)... he lays so still and knows relief is coming.

There has to be a home for him? Someone who can manage his condition? He's such a sweet boy!

Hello world they call me buckwheat at the rescue but my foster mom calls me taco! I came up from Texas so I'm a good old southern boy. I've had very minimal human interaction so I'm extremely shy and scared of people but my foster mom has been working with me and I actually go up and sniff strangers which is huge she said and praises me by jumping up and down and acting all silly that I went up and sniffed a stranger. She's kind of a weird woman but she's got a big heart and I sure do like her. Not much of my back story is known but my foster mom says that I will need a very patient person with a big huge heart like her that can see what she sees in me. She says I'm pretty good at house training and I go potty outside really well but I like to stick by her side so if she doesn't make sure I go potty outside when she's out with me then... I might have a little accident in the house right next to her. I really don't want to leave her side that's the thing! I haven't quite given kisses yet to my foster mom but I watch all the other pups here give her kisses and how much she likes them and I so want to do it, I'm just not there yet. She said she'll keep trying and eventually I'll give her kisses. I do kiss her on the hand when she's petting me and she praises me for that by saying thank you for the kisses. I'm a good little boy, I don't bark very much. I get along great with all my foster mom's dogs, she's got a big one and a bunch of small ones. Her son has friends over so they all come up and meet the pups and foster mom says I do really well with that by going up and sniffing them. I haven't let them touch me yet but I'll get there. I'm a happy little guy and I smile when I'm happy. When I'm being pet the sides of my lips curl up a little bit and my foster mom says I'm smiling which is super cute she says. I redirect very easily if I'm doing something my foster mom doesn't like she just says nope and I stop. I walk well on a leash but I'm afraid of everything so I will take some time to get over that. My foster mom has a fenced-in yard and I love running around and sunning myself on the deck. I kennel up super easy, all foster mom has to say is kennel up and I run right in. She always gives me a treat or I get a dental bone when she goes back to work from her lunch break. I sleep in the kennel at night and I don't make a peep. I ride pretty well in the car, no noise from me. If you have anymore questions please get ahold of my foster mom and she can explain more of me to you. I'm looking for someone patient that's willing to work with me through my fears and love me for the rest of my life.

Foster mom here, oh what can I say about little taco. He is absolutely adorable and such a great little pup. He looks to me for direction because he's not been taught very much. He was afraid of everything, noises, sudden movements, you name it. This boy has already come so far and he's got a little ways to go but oh my gosh is he so worth it! He bonds really hard to his person and looks to you for everything. His person will have to be supportive and understanding, patient and willing to do whatever it takes to help him, they have to be strong because he cannot take that role, he needs a leader and someone he can trust to get through this fear. He's never attempted to bite, he's just scared and he will hide when he gets scared. Baby talk has worked wonders and having other pups that he can learn from really helps. Having a brother or a sister pup for him would really help him a lot. He's not a big guy, I think he's only about 14 lbs so he's little. He doesn't like being under covers or blankets yet. Lol... I'm thinking one day he will though. I'm not sure how he does with small kids but being the fact that children can be loud and move quickly I think that would probably scare him and he wouldn't come out of his shell, it would only push him back. So I'm not sure if kids would be good for this little guy. I can't think of anything else right now but if you have any questions or want to know anything about little taco AKA buckwheat please let me know and I will answer anything and everything about him.

He's a Texas gem and he's got a second chance at life up here in Minnesota. This little guy will make someone so happy because he's such a funny guy once he trusts you and his heart is huge for love. Plus he's my favorite color black which never shows on your dress clothes and then to top it off he's got Doberman markings the black and tan so he's super cute and his ears stand up oh my gosh!!!

Buckwheat does need a home with another dog present and a fenced in yard

Thank you for reading and thank you for giving a pup a chance at a new life!

Buckwheat
was heartworm positive when he first joined rescue but has been treated and doing great!

description:

Toby Jacob AKA Toby joined Ruff Start Rescue after his forever owner passed away unexpectedly and the family was unable to afford his medical needs. He is affectionately known in his foster home as Toby Shark as well. He received that nick-name because when he first joined their home, he would walked around the house and make funny gremlin noises and would look up at them and bark with his teeth hanging out from his under bite. Toby is a super laid back gentleman and enjoys being with his humans and foster brothers all the time. Toby LOVES to eat, but does have skin allergies and requires a grain free dog food. He prefers a Raw Diet or wet dog food over dry kibble. He will play with stuffed animal toys from time to time, and loves playing tug-a-war with his foster mom when he gets in the playing mood. Most of his day though is spent resting (snoring) and following his foster mom and companion foster brother (Shih-Tzu) around the house or at the grooming salon that his foster mom works at. Toby does have separation anxiety and will need a home where he will either have someone home with him most of the time or will be able to join his family to work every day. Toby suffered from severe dry eye and extreme ear infections in both ears for an extended amount of time before joining Ruff Start. He ended up having his ear canal removed in his right ear and also gets multiple eye medication in both eyes twice a day now to help with his dry eye. Due to the severity of his ear infection, his facial nerve on that side of his face was damaged in surgery and he can no longer blink his right eye and his jowls are droopy in that side of his face. He does receive eye medications to help keep his eye healthy. Toby is mostly blind and deaf. He will need a one level home so that he will not fall down any stairs. Toby is house trained and enjoys strolling around the yard in the warm weather. He does need frequent potty breaks just because he has a harder time holding his potty because of his age. Toby grew up with multiple other large and small dogs and has interacted with cats in the past. In his foster home, Toby actually has a little shih-tzu that he uses a lot as his seeing-eye companion. He follows him around to make sure he is not going to bump into anything as well as his friend keeps in away from wondering off in the yard. He may do best in a new home that has another small laid back dog that he can bond with. Toby is good with children, but will need kids that understand not to be in dogs faces and not to be over bearing. Toby is all up to date on all his main vaccines, is neutered and heartworm negative. However, Toby has tested positive and has been treated for Lyme's disease. Lyme's disease can cause joint stiffness and minor lameness from time to time, his foster home gives him a daily joint supplement to help prevent this as well as to help with any arthritis he may have. Toby also has what is commonly called \"Old Dog Lung\" which is calcium build up in his lungs. It causes him to have difficultly breathing from time to time and may require further medical intervention in the future.

Toby's Needs

- Eye ointment in the AM and PM

- Eye Lubricant in right eye 4-6 times a day (as needed)

- Companion Animal

- Owner who is home most of the time or can bring him to work for frequent potty break and separation anxiety

- Frequent medicated baths for skin allergies

- No Stairs

- Grain free dog food

A good day to you! My name is Dacotah and I am an adult Husky mix looking for a human companion. I would consider myself a refined gentleman, I love long walks, hanging out with folks, and cuddling when the day comes to a close. Once in a while I will play with my younger foster siblings, but they can be so jumpy! I do prefer dogs whose taste more a lines with my own. Trying to talk to them doesn't get me anywhere so I find myself a good spot on the couch, curl in a ball, and plop right down to watch some tele.

I get along with pretty much everyone, I am very easy going. I like dogs, I get along with the resident cat, and children don't bother me either. I would prefer more respectful children if I am going to live with them for as I get older, I am more easily startled. I also like talking about my day, current affairs, all the like, so it can be off putting to younger ones if they aren't ready to chat with me. Another reason I prefer more mature small humans. They love talking to me!

I also like to play with toys! I love ball and tug ropes, so if you like playing I'd love if we could toss the ol' pig skin around. When I was a younger man, I moved a lot faster so you'll have to take it slow to start but once I get on a roll I'll play with you for hours!

This last part I am going to let my current human talk to you about; I don't fully understand why I get nervous about certain things so maybe she can help explain what I'll need. She does a great job of watching me so I bet she knows what will be best!

Hi there! My name is Taylor and I am Dacotah's current foster Mom. He has done an awesome job telling you about himself and covering the things he is so good at! Now I want to talk about something any new family considering Dacotah will need to know moving forward. I'm going to tell you where he came from, why he is the way he is, and what you can expect applying for him.

Dacotah's previous owner came on hard times but did what he could to continue to care for his pup even after they became homeless. Dacotah and him lived out of their car and they shared everything, from food, to water, to a living space. For this reason Dacotah is not used to confinement and is not accustomed to being alone. Being an adult dog, around 5-6 years old, these traits are something I find to be a part of him, not something I need to train away. I am looking for folks who are home more often than not and will have to leave him home for maybe a max of 2-3 hours a day. He does need a special type of kennel and this is something that his potential home will want to research prior to applying. It is called an Alcatraz kennel and it is made to be unescapable as the name may imply. Left out he can hurt himself and possibly your home if he becomes nervous or scared. This is not something that I as his foster parent take lightly. Watching him shake and cower away from me if I need to kennel him is crushing. Which is why I am looking to find a home that won't require that of him. He doesn't require a lot of exercise or grooming, just a lot of love! If you have the ability to bring a dog to your place of work or work from home, he would be an amazing match. He listens to commands extremely well and is a very people oriented dog that really looks to you for support. Any applicant's will need this information and I promise you, should you be able to meet these requirements, you'll come to meet one of the sweetest, gentlest, nicest dogs I have had the ability to foster.

Thank you for your consideration, Dacotah says he is excited to spend his life with you. Ready to go?

description:

Life is hard on the streets, especially when you look like I do. I'm an adult bully mix who is muscly, likes to growl, and likes to show my teeth. You'd have to stay with me a little while to see that's just my smile. To see my white muzzle. To see what I've been through. I've decided to call myself something approachable, I want to appeal to a wide amount of people. Call me.. Scooter!

I was found as a stray and brought into MACC, where folks at first weren't sure how I would do. As previously mentioned, I can come off as kind of hard. Then they let me out to play with some others dogs and.. well, I got to be me. I like playing with other dogs a lot but I like to meet my new friends slowly to make sure they're cool. I need to feel acclimated before I'm willing to offer friendship. The streets taught me that. I'm also kind of pushy, but I've been told most bully's are like that! (You may notice a reoccurring theme as I am pushy in some other departments too) I tend to play with my whole body so little children most likely will not be a good fit for me. Think, bowling ball. (See, pushy)

I met a kitty at my permanent foster home. She is a small creature, who stands her ground. I find her frightening and attempt to sneak up and sniff her when she isn't looking. This task is more difficult than it appears as she is very fast and harms my nose if I get too close. I bark at her. Then I hide. When she rests, I am respectful of her space. I do like her, although I have yet to confirm how she feels about me.. given the scratches on my nose, I would say she needs, possibly, more space? Will make a note for the future. (Too pushy?)

I would like to talk to you about how my true life's obsession. The thing that gets me up and out of the kennel in the morning, outside even when it's raining (I hate rain. I. Hate. It. It's too pushy), what even motivates me to listen to the humans I live with! It is the soft sphere they call, a tennis ball. This object is an amazing thing, I put it in my mouth and squeeze, it makes a sound that makes me JUMP with joy! I bring it to one of my humans, they are so silly they have no idea its value! They THROW IT! I bring the precious gem to them, only for them to do THE SAME THING AGAIN! These fools, eventually I stop bringing it back and just enjoy my ball alone.

I mentioned in the beginning of my tale, that I can be a tab quirky. That is a very true statement and my possible new humans will need to know these things about me, I find honesty is always the best policy. The streets taught me that.

I am a bed hog.

When I get on the bed, I roll around all over it first.

I snore really loudly.

I don't always listen when you tell me to drop the ball. (You're just going to throw it! You don't even know its worth!)

Sometimes I get really excited and pee a little. Just a little, I swear.

I drool when we play ball. That isn't a little. It's a lot.

I play in the water bowl. Only sometimes.

When you push me, I will push back against you with all my might. Even if I can see what you're trying to make me do, is definitely the right choice. (It's a bully thing, or so I've heard.)

I am scared of new people. I need you to take things slowly with me. When I was out there, alone.. it was terrifying. I did my best to stay strong, I knew someone would help me. They did! I'm learning that people aren't scary or out to hurt me, but sometimes I'll growl and tell new folks that I need space. My current humans have people meet me with my most favorite of the balls. Once I see they have that, I know my humans trust them which means they must be legit. Also, if they're willing to play ball with me they pass the test to be my friend.

Being on a leash is something that also stresses me out. I've never had to be tethered before, I think I can be taught, but that's something we'll have to learn together.. is that okay? Because if you're with me through this, I think we can do anything together.

In the meantime if you have questions or are interested in me, please fill out an adoption application at www.ruffstartrescue.org.

name: Delta
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.
Name: DELTA
DOB: 03/07/2017
Weight: 46
Adoption Fee: $125

I was born in Oklahoma but I claim Minnesota as my home. That's where my luck turned-around and I was truly rescued. A group of people in Minnesota finally convinced me... I would never be given-up on again. On a
cold day in December, the day after a lonely Christmas in a cage, I experienced the luckiest day of my life.

See... I had a really bad first year of life. No one really knows what happened to me. And I have no way to share it with them... although they can see my psychological scars periodically. They healed my physical ailments more easily. Well, 'easily' is probably not the best word, because I was very ill and it took many rounds of different medicines and several months to get my body healthy. I was a pretty sick puppy with worms and bacteria and parasites and wounds. I had all the ailments that a puppy growing up unloved and not cared for would have. I was given pills and shots, had blood drawn, and given more pills and shots. My body eventually healed, but only on the outside. My psychological ailments took longer.

In
my first year, I spent more than 100+ days in confinement in various cages at more than one facility. Through a series of good fortune I left Oklahoma and was transported to Minnesota. But months before my first birthday, even in Minnesota, my luck almost ran out. I was just days away from being euthanized. See... even
though I had been rescued and physically healed, I never made it to the \"adoption floor\" because I was too scared. I would shake uncontrollably and cower constantly. People tried to build my confidence and gave me lots of treats and spent hours teaching me things like... responding to my new name and how to sit. But regardless of their concern and best efforts, the metal cages, loud noises, strange faces and barking dogs kept me so unbelievably scared. And so I was labeled, \"rescue only\". Then two days before my 'down date' (my scheduled final day alive) a stranger came to my cage, picked me up, took me to a cold vehicle, wrapped me in a green blanket, took me home, put a goofy red dog coat on me, and held me for days while I adjusted to my new quieter surroundings. That was the luckiest day of my life.

A group of people saw passed my scared exterior and just wanted to give me a chance. Who
knew that it would take me more than 20 months of waiting to find my forever home. But, regardless of the passing months, the rescue people still haven't given up on me. I've gotten lots of love, snuggles, patience, treats, foster brothers and sisters and an annoying cat to bug me (ugh!). They taught me that houses are pretty awesome, and that doorways, stairs and ceiling fans aren't scary afterall. They've given me more training, and even surgery to help me with my eye lids (my eye lashes were turned inward and scratching my eyeballs -- ouch!). Nothing has made them give up on me.
They truly love me. And
trust me, ha, I
have really given them a run for their money. I still have some separation anxiety (which is understandable given what my first year was like), so I've chewed on a few dog beds, couch pillows, bedroom blankets, and more than a few pairs of shoes whenever I've been left alone. I am a work in progress and getting better every day, and I want to find my forever home. I am full of playful energy and lot going for runs and bike rides. I love car rides and long strolls on the... river. Kids are the only ones that still terrify me, so it's best that I not be around them.

I want to find my people (or person) that will be patient with me and understand what I've overcome so far. I want them to see the unfailing, unconditional love I have to give in return... because I have so much to be thankful for.

That's the story of my luckiest day... and my journey isn't over. If you want to meet me, drop my rescue people a line. And I'll see you soon. Oh please excuse if I'm a little cautious at first sight --- new places still make me a little nervous.

Oh, and also... I do need a side-kick brother or sister to help me adjust to new things. (But sorry, no little dogs cuz they just seem to bug me. )

Thanks for reading,

Delta

(P.S. My foster mom is going to ugly cry on the day I leave, so be prepared for that! No seriously... like really, please bring the Kleenex! No joke.)

Lucy's Interview

Tell me a bit about yourself? My name is Lucy and I am a fabulous Mature Bloodhound with the perfect dose of sass and silly antics.

Whats your favorite pass time? Where to start.. I love to spy on all my neighbors from the window. I also like to find a good chew bone, cozy spot on the couch and relax with my chew toy. I also enjoy walks and a dip in the kiddie pool my foster family got for me. I love to dunk my face in the water and take big drinks.

What would your ideal adoptive home be? My Adopters should have a home with a fenced in yard at least 5 ft plus. I like to run and chase small critters so it would keep me safe. I am good with baths, nail trims, ear cleaning, and vet visits!

I also love to steal rags and food off the counters! I think its super fun but my foster mom doesn't seem to think its as fun as I do.

What other things should we know about you? I am a super healthy gal but take medication daily to help me with urinary incontinence. That means I sometimes leak urine when hanging out or sleeping, but with my medicine I do not leak at all! Yay me! I am super a sweet girl and have been looking for my furever home for a long time now!

Zeena

is a gorgeous girl who is eager to please and has tons of love to give! She was found by her foster mom wandering the streets in pretty rough shape. Since she is so much happier and healthier now, she's so excited about life!

Zeena

is very playful and energetic and would make a good walking/jogging buddy, but needs to continue to work on leash training. She does well with SOME other dogs (she tends to be selective) and really loves to play with them when she finds a dog she can get along well with. A slow introduction will be needed and she tends to do better with male dogs. She has a prey drive so does not do well with smaller dogs and no cats or critters in the house for her. She would do the best with a fenced yard because she likes to chase squirrels and birds (hey who doesn't?) and should be supervised when outside as she has been know to scale a privacy fence to try to get a squirrel! Get out of my yard squirrel!

She loves to play and will always be up for a few rounds of tug-o-war. And when play time is over she likes to snuggle. She does great with the kids in her foster home (age 6 and 11) and loves to give kisses. I just remind them to be careful when playing with toys with her so that she doesn't get possessive of them.

Zeena

is crate trained, and knows a few basic commands (sit, recall-her name, wait and stay). Since she's so eager to make her humans happy, given time/patience and some dedicated training, I'm confident that she can learn more! This sweet girl developed some allergies and we have been feeding her Nutro (a limited ingredient diet) which seems to have helped. A 22lb. bag of Nutro is around $50 (should last about a month and a half). She also has some incontinence issues. She does go potty outside, but tends to have accidents inside as well. We've tried several medications for this and she has seen a specialist, but we can't quite pin point the problem. For now, she gets frequent outdoor potty breaks and wears a diaper indoors. Simple solutions diapers are about $11 per 12 pack of diapers (we use roughly a pack per 2-3 weeks, but this may vary depending on how long she's kenneled, how many potty breaks she gets, etc.)

Zeena is a great girl who has so much love to give. We know there is a family out there for her - we just have to find them! She looks bigger in her pictures but she is only about 35 pounds of sass, wiggle and unconditional love. She loves it at her foster mom's house but would love more than anything to find a forever home of her own!

Knox is not just another pretty face! He is a 4 year old double merle Catahoula Hound from Mississippi.  He is an amazing energetic smart boy who happens to be deaf. His deafness requires some special accommodations, but it doesn't hold him back from being a great companion and an active dog.  In fact, he is a better watch dog than his hearing foster brother using his other senses. Knox feels vibrations from cars, footsteps, & doors opening and smells his favorite people before they even enter the room. He knows the mail carrier is coming when the truck is still a block away! He will bark to alert you but settles down when he knows all is well.

Knox, like most deaf dogs, would do best in a household where someone is home most of the day and with a canine companion to keep him company. He loves to look out the windows or better yet hang out in a fenced in yard-in the sun anytime of year.  Knox walks well on a leash, loves car rides, and is house trained, and has used a doggie door, but does not do well in a crate.

 Knox LOVES other dog and LOVES kids - he enjoys playing  & cuddling with both. He doesn't have an aggressive bone in his body but he is a Catahoula Hound, with a bit too much prey drive, so a home without cats or other small animals is best. 

Knox has learned some sign language and would benefit from continued training. The ideal  home will have someone who can spend time with him working on reinforcing his training and taking him for long hikes and walks to burn off all of that Catahoula Hound energy. 

It takes a  bit to earn his trust but when you do, his love and loyalty are an amazing thing! Knox has been in foster care for over 3 years and is so deserving of a family of his own!  Please consider opening your home and more importantly, your heart to this gorgeous boy!

Our rescue partners knew it was too soon to have the puppies pulled from their momma so one of their employees went out and trapped her and convinced the girl that took the puppies to surrender them to the shelter so that mother Ramona could finish weening them. Bizzie is loving and very sweet!
She's one of those dogs who epitomizes canine forgiveness - you'll see this when you read her backstory. Fortunately for Bizzie, her future's looking ever so bright! We're thinking she's a blend of Chow Chow and Shepherd probably born sometime in 2014 or 2015. She has been fine with adult dogs and puppies; she has not been introduced to cats. She's been great with all adults, and though she has not lived with children, we think she would be okay with older, dog-respectful kids. House training and crate training are in the works, and she seems to do fine on leash. A dog who has lived on a chain for years, like Bizzie did, can have a tendency towards guard dog behaviors and though she has not shown any of these tendencies, her adopters will likely need to work with a professional trainer to help her accept strangers and work through any fears she might exhibit.

Bizzie loves to run and play with other dogs, people and toys! She rides well in the car while crated, she's very calm. Though a fenced yard would be great to get in some running and playing, daily leash walks for business, exercise and fun will work just as well to keep her happy and healthy. And to keep that canine mind sharp, think puzzle toys and games. Bizzie really just wants to find a forever home where she'll be loved and cared for. Could that be your home? Fill out an application today and her people will get right back to you!

Bizzie's Backstory: Bizzie truly deserves a wonderful life. Her first 3-4 years were very hard. She was from the south side of Jackson, Mississippi, and was tied out on a 6-foot chain to be used as a guard dog. Her shelter was limited to a carport, no matter what the temperature or weather was like. She often did not have food nor water, except when a neighbor was contacted for dog food. After that, the neighbor often checked on her and would feed her and give her water. We know that Bizzie had at least one litter of puppies that a rescue took, but Bizzie was left behind. However the rescue did provide a spay for her. Bizzie's friend finally convinced her owner to relinquish her. When the vet checked Bizzie, she did have heartworm, which has been treated and she is now clear. At first, this pretty girl was scared when anyone approached her with a leash - maybe she was afraid she would be tied out again. Of course, we know that this will never again be the case!

Medical Note: This dog has been treated for heartworm disease with melarsomine injections. Once treatment is completed and the dog tests negative for microfilaria, the dog will be cleared to resume normal activity and able to be adopted. Untreated heartworm disease can cause lasting damage to the heart, lungs and arteries, and can affect the dog's health and quality of life even after the parasites are gone, possibly presenting as medical complications and/or new conditions in the future. This dog showed no symptoms of heartworm disease before or during treatment. A good resource for more information on heartworm disease is: https://www.heartwormsociety.org/pet-owner-resources/ heartworm-basics. Please check with your vet if you should have any questions or concerns about this condition, and discuss any concerns you may have with your SOS Adoption Counselor.

name: Elvis
description:
On the heels of losing our sweet Gladys just weeks ago, we promised to follow up with some more information about her heartbroken son, Elvis.



Some of you may recognize Elvis from previous postings, but read on to learn a little more about what this soulful fellow has been dealing with recently. For those of you from other parts, Mississippi is the birthplace of American music, and Elvis Presley is one of her most favored sons. Presley had a hardscrabble upbringing in rural Mississippi - not so different from this fine dog - but he remained connected to his roots by his doting mother, Gladys. In the late 50s, as Presley began his meteoric rise to fame, Gladys fell ill and passed at the untimely age of 46. Here again, the parallels to our Elvis's story are heartbreakingly similar.



Elvis was rescued in 2009 - yes, nearly SIX years ago - along with a female dog that we believe was his mother. We named them Gladys and Elvis to signify their special bond; Gladys had tended to Elvis even after he'd lost sight in his left eye at a young age. The two were inseparable, and Elvis was distraught when complications from an infection took Gladys's leg. But even down one leg and one eye, this tough little family soldiered on, happy to have the company of one another and a roof over their head at ARF.



Knowing the strength of this bond, we were even more concerned than usual when we found a growth on Gladys's neck in late 2014. The growth was promptly removed, but years of hard living seemed to catch up to this sweet, 10-year-old girl. She had trouble healing in the months following the surgery, a fact that made more sense when we realized that the cancer had returned. Her good-natured demeanor remained, but it was clear that she was nearing the end of her road. Gladys enjoyed a beautiful final day in early February, laying in the warm Mississippi sun and leisurely watching the birds in a nearby park.



Much like his namesake, our sweet Elvis was devastated. We've made certain to give him lots of interaction with new friends in an effort to keep his spirits high, but we can't provide him with the one thing he truly needs: a family. He is a medium-sized dog that is full of cuddles and playfulness -- at roughly 7 years old, he definitely does not act his age smile emoticon Elvis is a sweet, friendly dog that needs a freshstart, and we know that the right forever home is out there. If you're looking to provide a new lease on life for one of our most deserving seniors, we'd be happy to provide more information about Elvis. And even if you're not ready to adopt, please consider coming to visit this handsome hound dog today -- he needs all the loving he can get.

Elvis, Labrador Retriever has been shared from Shelter Exchange - http://www.shelterexchange.org.

Iâve met people of all ages here at the shelter, but in my home, it would be best if I lived with older, dog-savvy children only. I really like being around people, and will do pretty much anything to be near them. Iâve been known to climb up and over my kennel door here at the shelter, which is why I shouldnât be trusted in a fenced in area left to my own devices. I will probably find a way out. The good news is that I love going for walks and playtime, especially with my favorite toy balls, so I promise you that weâll always have a good time. If youâre looking for a new canine companion that will surely bring lots of love and joy to your life, stop in and meet me today!

description:
Our sweet Raven has patiently been waiting her turn to come from Mississippi! She is roughly a 12yr old Pomeranian mix and weighs in around 24 pounds.

She may be missing a few teeth and have to be on thyroid medicine for the rest of her days but she sure is feeling better and is no longer in pain!
She is a very good girl at the groomer's, after so many years of neglect she enjoys the pampering! Raven is good with other dogs, but not sure how she is with cats since her foster home doesn't have any. Due to her age, she would do best in a home with NO smaller children, older responsible kids would be fine though! She loves to cuddle up on the couch and snooze while the humans watch TV. Raven's bedtime routine consists of sleeping on the bed with her foster parents as she is so deserving of.
Our adorable princess is already spayed, up to date on vaccines, current on preventatives and microchipped. She is looking to spend the rest of her life with a family that will truly adore her and give her the great life she obviously missed out on all these years

name: Ajax
description:
How I arrived to Northwoods: I came to NHS to find my furever home because where I lived there just wasn't enough room for all my energy, and there were small dogs I liked to chase.

I am originally from Missouri. I know a lot of commands like: sit, stay, lay down, shake, high five,  and hugs ( I will jump up you for this one).
I also know a couple of hunting commands like seek( use this one for things to eat only please). I also know Find it- if i have the smell of the item i will track and find it.
I am a natural born hunter and love to hunt. I need a little training and I will be a good hunter. Tho I am a little scared of loud noises right now.
I lived with 4 children and loved them immensely-  sometimes I would even sleep with one of them. I do forget sometimes I have grown larger and would accidently bump into them. I also love stuffed animals- they are so fun to chew! I also love to play fetch and love my exercise and just running! Sometimes if I don't get enough exercise I can be a little naughty tho and do things I am not supposed to do,.

I am kennel trained and will go willingly but I don't like it for long periods of time. I get sad and bored and will start to bark. I do need a wire kennel- I will chew right thru  the others. 

My favorite chew toys are Antlers, they keep me entertained for hours! I also love water so if my bowl isn't full I will drink from a toilet- I just don't know why people don't try it!

Good with kids: Yes
Good with cats:No
Good with dogs:lived with Beagle and loved him, but DO NOT LIKE smaller dogs at all.

name: Foster Homes Needed
description:
Every minute matters when it comes to rescuing a Shih Tzu. We may get a short notice that someone needs to surrender their dog or a puppy mill dog needs a temporary home. We can't help if we don't have families willing to foster, and we are always in need of more foster homes!

If you live in the Minneapolis/Saint Paul, Rockford or Chicago, IL areas and want to help save lives, please complete either our online Foster Sign-Up or download a word version here:

http://www.northstarshihtzurescue.org/foster/

(please note: neither dog pictured are available to foster or adopt, both are in their forever homes)

NorthStar Shih Tzu Rescue exists to benefit both Shih Tzu and Shih Tzu blend dogs and the people of our community. We operate as a no-kill rescue that provides rescue and adoption services, and meaningful outreach programs in order to advance the welfare of these companion animals, to serve and educate our community, and to make a positive, loving impact on the lives of both.

NorthStar, located in Excelsior, MN, actively works to rescue Shih Tzu and Shih Tzu blend dogs from dangerous environments and shelters with the ultimate goal of placing them in loving, permanent, adoptive homes. We rescue unwanted, abandoned, and abused dogs. We have them vaccinated, micro-chipped, spayed or neutered, provide other medical care, and rehabilitate them in carefully selected foster homes.

We also serve as a resource to our community and all pet owners by providing education and information on the benefits of adopting an animal in need as well as responsible pet ownership, including the importance of spay/neuter, good nutrition, and positive behavior training. We strive to increase public awareness about companion animal overpopulation, commercial breeders, and to offer solutions to end the killing of adoptable animals.

We work in alliance with local animal shelters, pounds, other rescue groups, and humane society organizations to ensure these animals are not forgotten.

name: Shane aka Vinnie
description:
OVERLOOKED AND MISUNDERSTOOD SEEKS SOUL MATE TO SET THE WORLD ON FIRE (or a good cuddle on the couch)...Please meet Vinnie!

Vinnie is an amazing three (3) year old, lab/terrier mix that wears his heart on his sleeve. Vinnie is a life-loving dog that would be the perfect compliment for an active owner or family (children over the age of 10 preferred). Vinnie LOVESto play (tennis balls are his favorite) and would thrive in an environment where he could be intricately involved with the daily activities of his new home! Vinnie will be an amazingly loving and loyal companion to the home that is open to his very special gifts!

We are determined to find the right home to make Vinnie's success story complete! Originally adopted out as a cute and happy puppy, Vinnie was (gratefully) returned to us after a concerned citizen stepped in; Vinnie's initial home was characterized as \"abusive\" and he was subsequently handed off to two separate acquaintances that were unfortunately ill-equipped to provide the structure Vinnie needed to regain his trust in people. Thus, poor Vinnie arrived back to us fearful and with a broken spirit; humans had let him down. For close to a year, we worked with Vinnie to regain his trust and rebuild his confidence in people. And, after a number of smaller \"baby\" steps, Vinnie was ready for some professional training and guidance. He made the journey to Golden Heart Canine in Montrose, Colorado, whereby he spent a full six weeks of intensive training to get back on track to being his best self! The transformation was amazing! Simply put, Vinnie was almost an entirely new dog from the moment we picked him up! Vinnie's former fear and mistrust had been replaced by love, comfort, and most importantly, faith in people. Vinnie has resided in the loving environment of a caring and supportive foster home since his return from Montrose, where he has continued to work on socialization and confidence building by visiting new places and meeting new people. Vinnie is now ready for a permanent family to callhis very own!

Vinnie loves to be the center of attention and doesn't at all mind acting \"goofy\" to get you to smile! Vinnie can occasionally geta little insecure on walks with unfamiliar canine companions, but has made great strides in making introductions at adoption events, whereby he has been in the company of many unfamiliar dogs at one time. Because he still exhibits moments of insecurity, we would recommend structured introductions with new canine friends in a controlled environment. Vinnie will, In fact, sit at the door to actively greet new people and dogs as they walk in!

Vinnie is house-trained, crate trained, sleeps through the night and just a ton of fun during waking hours! Vinnie also loves his crate, which can also serve as a great place for 'down time' as needed.

Sweet eyes, a big heart, and in great shape...Vinnie will be your trusted friend for life, if simply given a chance...all Vinnie asks for is love and a firm but gentle hand to reinforce the skills he has recently acquired.

If you are interested in meeting Vinnie and giving him the life he deserves, please fill out an application through our website!

*BSL Restrictions may apply.

According to my foster mom, \"TJ is a pure sweetheart and gets along with literally any and every dog he meets. He is always watching his people and loves to receive attention. He is a sweetheart and does SOOO good with baths. TJ is smart and is food motivated! He sleeps through the night in his crate without a peep!\"

Our fosters begin basic training, housebreaking, and leash walking skills to help pair you with the perfect pup for life!

We process all our applications in the order we receive them, and for that reason sometimes the dog or dogs in whom you are interested in may be adopted before your own processing concludes.

In order to apply for adoption and set up an individual meet and greet with one of our dogs, please visit us at www.HomeforGoodDogs.org. 

Find us on Facebook at www.facebook.com/HomeForGoodDogRescue.

name: PUPPY TANZIE
description:
Tanzie is a sweet and vivacious black Lab female puppy that is looking for a home with dog experience and training skills. This girl is a diamond in the rough that adores people, other dogs, would love a cat to be best friends with a cat too! She is 24 pounds at just 5 months old and will be a 45-50 girl when fully grown. She is loving and smart and almost housebroken with crate training down pat! She needs a fenced yard to run to her heart's content and would welcome a second dog in the family. She is NOT a Diva dog that needs to be the only dog. name: INDIE
description:
This precious 6 year old Yellow Lab girl is a victim twice now in her life. Her name six year ago when she came in to the Critter Cavalry Rescue program was Indie. A young yellow lab girl that needed a fresh and loving forever home. We thought we found one for herwe \"thought\". This is until we got a phone call from a local Nashville, TN shelter informing us that she was dropped off by the family saying they couldn't keep her any longer. They never in the whole six years of owning her, took her to the vet. Now, they were discarding her and not even trying to find the rescue who originally pledged their faith and support to this young girl. She was at the shelter for 4 more days as we scrambled to find a foster home for her at one of the most challenging times..holiday weekend of Labor Day. One of our faithful and trusted foster moms went to the shelter to bring her home. In the shelter she was shaking and shivering with fear and confusion as to why she was in this noisy, chaotic environment called a shelter. She didn't belong there and shame on that horrible family who didn't even try to find an alternative for rehoming her or calling our rescue. She is not trash folks. She is a loving and beautiful soul that needs a better person or family the next time around. We will dedicate all we have to finding that right place AGAIN. She is housebroken, good with other dogs, seems OK with the resident cat at the foster home and is good with children. She is not leash trained and she is strong. She would benefit from a fenced yard as that is what she had in the former home. She is 55 pounds and around 6-7 years old. Most like 6 than 7. But who is counting? She has lots of love and lots of years to give to a new beginning. Please email us at ccrtennessee@gmail.com Please help Indie find her forever place in life.

ADOPTION FEE REQUIRED. Contact ccrtennessee@gmail.com.

name: Kaiser
description:
Kaiser ~ Available...Kaiser is a handsome, male Rottweiler. He is approximately 3 years old and weighs around 80 pounds. He has a low-moderate energy level and is crate-trained and housebroken. He is good with kids, other dogs and cats!

For more information or to request an adoption application, please email us at adoption.mtgsr@gmail.com

ADOPTION: 
Training (for both the dog AND the family) increases the probability of a successful adoption. We feel strongly that training is an essential part of responsible dog ownership and we now require training for every dog placed through the MTGSR program. The cost of adoption is $500 which includes the $250 adoption fee and a training fee (payable to the trainer) of $250 is due at the time of adoption.

name: Fuli
description:
Fuli is one of six 6-8 month old puppies (all named after Lion Guard characters because that's what happens when the seven year old picks!) removed from a rural property in NC.  They were kept in cages and only Fed and watered once daily until animal control was alerted.  They are all gorgeous catahoula pups, and very sweet but will need continued socialization as they haven't been able to see much of the world!

Fuli is as fast and lithe as the cheetah that she is named after.  She's almost cat like in her ability to climb!  She's the smallest of the litter, and has the most beautiful stripey coat!  Her foster mom has dubbed her \"the barn manager\" as she loves doing chores and making sure everything is running smoothly.  Fuli is very sweet as well as smart, she watches and learns very quickly.  Fuli is nervous around kids, as the ex-neighbor's kids apparently used to jump on their crates.  At this time, we would not recommend her for homes with young children, as their quick movements still startle her.

The pups love to give kisses, gallop around the yard, and wrestle with their foster siblings.  Please email barkingbackrescue@gmail.com for an app.

name: Hearth (Tyson) - Massada pup 1
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs1066

Hello! My name is Hearth AKA Tyson. I am 7 years old and about 68 pounds. Don't let my age fool you I am an active guy! I LOVE walks on the beach and am learning that car rides can be kinda awesome. They say I'm a lab mix BUT I think there may be a shepherd in my family tree since I have this handsome fur. I was with my first family for a long time but they had to move and couldn't take me with them, so now I am hanging out with my foster Dad and learning lots of new and exciting things!! My foster Dad says I'm a pretty special guy. I am an expert level cuddler and love getting scritches and rubs! My favorite chew is this yak stick thingy. Yum! 

I would probably be best as an only dog or with a single calm, balanced doggie friend who could be my wingman if I get nervous.... but I am still not willing to share my nachos! Some things are sacred! Because I'm a big strong athletic guy (foster Dad says I'm just big boned) I need a human who has some experience and willingness to continue my training to help me be the best boy! 

Great Things about Tyson!
-Crate Trained
-House Trained
- Knows some obedience - sit, stay, down, paw, place, crate, heel
-LOVES people
-Been good with children I have met
- Affectionate
- Active but not high energy
- Loves chew toys
- Learning to like toys, especially this one that looks a little like p-o-o-p ;)


To adopt this dog, or any OPH dog, fill out the simple online application at https://ophrescue.org 
Operation Paws for Homes, Inc. (OPH) rescues dogs of all breeds and ages from high-kill shelters in NC, VA, MD, and SC, reducing the numbers being euthanized. With limited resources, the shelters are forced to put down 50-90% of the animals that come in the front door. OPH provides pet adoption services to families located in VA, DC, MD, PA and neighboring states. OPH is a 501(c)(3) organization and is 100% donor funded. OPH does not operate a shelter or have a physical location. We rely on foster families who open their homes to give love and attention to each dog before finding a forever home.

name: Diane von Furstenberg
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8549

 Diane von Furstenberg is a beagle mix girls who is about 5 years old and 27 lbs. Just look at those melting chocolate eyes and smooth long ears - talk about easy on the eyes. 

Diane, who is is fondly called Jolene by her foster family, is a pretty low-key dog. She is timid around new people and will need an adopter who understands that she's going to take some time to warm up. This is all so new to her, and we don't know her background, so perhaps she hasn't had a loving home before. She is very playful with the other dog in her foster home, and this is when we see her fun, quirky side come out. Say hello to Mia, a nine-month-old, 30-pound female Desi dog (a local term for street dog) from India. When Mia is comfortable she is a funny, happy, and athletic girl whos happy to spend a few minutes wrestling or racing with the other dogs in her foster home, and then a few more minutes snuggling with her foster mom. 

Mia thrives on routine and attaches very deeply to her household members. Although she would benefit from ongoing exposure to new situations and people, she would probably be happiest in a low-key household with one or two people, who can help her develop a sense of security and confidence. name: Zekke
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8390

Look into my eyes....you will be hypnotized by my charm!

Hello, my name is Zekke! I am six months old and estimated to be a husky mix. I arrived at my foster familys house after a super fun flight all the way from NC. Have you been on a plane ride? It was sure fun.

I've been hanging out with my foster family for a few weeks now and while its fun here, I would sure like to find my forever family as well. Below are some fun things my family wants you to know about me.

- I am crate trained. Im quiet in my crate and sleep the night away and know to keep it nice and tidy with my toys. Can't ask for more than that can you?
- I have kept my crate clean and dry. (If I bark in my crate its because I have to go out)
- I appear to be housebroken but foster Mom says accidents can happen in a new environment. Don't worry, we will both be learning when I come home with you but we will both quickly know how to talk to each other. 
- Ive just about mastered this whole leash walking thing. It was brand new to me when I arrived but I like to take walks so I'm learning how to walk like a good boy mom says. I still get excited sometimes and get tangled in foster mom's legs but we are working through it.
- Im learning other fun things too. I LOVE treats so teaching me things is pretty easy. Ive mastered sit & lay down and am trying REALLY HARD on stay (that one is tough, I like to be with mom when we are outside (she hides cookies in her pockets for me, how can I resist that)) 
 - I appear to be a roll with the punches type of pup. Ive liked everyone, 2 and 4 legged that Ive met so far. 
- Foster Mom says I am one of the easiest fosters they have had. I am quiet, keep the place clean and follow the rules. I think she likes me. :)
- I would do best in a home with older kids (over 12) until I settle down a bit more. Im pretty mouthy still, just like most teenagers. I am working on keeping this under control and am getting better each day. These foster family people don't take any back talk from me about this, they are tough. Mom says my forever people will have to continue to be tough and remind me about this until I fully outgrow it.
- I would be a great hiking or running partner with a little training. Mom & I are doing a bit of running and I LOVE IT! The foster kids started school so we have been super busy and unable to hike but we have talked about it and I'm pretty sure I would like that as well. I love to be busy.
- TOYS! I have discovered TOYS and love them. I am getting pretty good with fetch (I will bring the ball back most of the time, sometimes I get distracted) and love soft toys that make noise. Foster mom told me not to destroy them and I'm doing really good with it. I really am enjoying the toy box here. I like to take one outside each time we go. Silly foster mom picks them all up and brings back inside at bedtime every night for me to start again in the morning.
- I met cats, chickens, turkeys and pigs and am happy to report that I did not bother any of them or care about them.
- two new things we have discovered this week. I like to swim and I liked being in arlington for an event. 

Do you like my new pictures? I went to an event and there was a nice guy named Drew there who took them. I think I look pretty handsome (even if it was 100 degrees that day...whew!)

Anyway, Ill be hanging out in Nokesville, VA. I am able to go home with you as soon as you are approved to adopt. My foster family says someone is going to be very lucky to have me.

name: Mia Desi Dog
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8261

Say hello to Mia, a nine-month-old, 30-pound female Desi dog (a local term for street dog) from India. Mia has quite a rescue story her mom, Furry, was living on the streets of New Delhi with Mia and her three siblings when they were very young, but their mother was unable to feed them due to illness. Mom and pups were taken into Kannan Animal Welfare, a rescue group in New Delhi, and brought back to health. Furry has already been adopted here in the US, and now Mia is the first of her puppies to come in search of a home! 

Because Mia grew up in a rescue facility, life in a home is very new for her. That being said, theres plenty about it she loves! Walks, couches, grassy open spaces, and toys (even sticks will do!), have all been big hits. When Mia is comfortable she is a funny, happy, and athletic girl whos happy to spend a few minutes wrestling or racing with the other dogs in her foster home, and then a few more minutes snuggling with her foster mom. 

Mia thrives on routine and attaches very deeply to her household members. Although she would benefit from ongoing exposure to new situations and people, she would probably be happiest in a low-key household with one or two people, who can help her develop a sense of security and confidence. Those people will find in Mia a dog who is endlessly entertaining, unbelievably charming, and absolutely devoted!

name: Zekke
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8390

Look into my eyes....you will be hypnotized by my charm!

Hello, my name is Zekke! I am seven months old and estimated to be a husky/white shepherd mix. I arrived at my foster familys house after a super fun flight all the way from NC. Have you been on a plane ride? It was sure fun.

I've been hanging out with my foster family for a few weeks now and while its fun here, I would sure like to find my forever family as well. Below are some fun things my family wants you to know about me.

- I am crate trained. Im quiet in my crate and sleep the night away and know to keep it nice and tidy with my toys. Can't ask for more than that can you?
- I have kept my crate clean and dry. (If I bark in my crate its because I have to go out)
- I appear to be housebroken but foster Mom says accidents can happen in a new environment. Don't worry, we will both be learning when I come home with you but we will both quickly know how to talk to each other. 
- Ive just about mastered this whole leash walking thing. It was brand new to me when I arrived but I like to take walks so I'm learning how to walk like a good boy mom says. I still get excited sometimes and get tangled in foster mom's legs but we are working through it. *** UPDATE *** Zekke has this down. Has recently been out on a busy street and was perfect on the leash with his foster family and with others.
- Im learning other fun things too. I LOVE treats so teaching me things is pretty easy. Ive mastered sit & lay down and am trying REALLY HARD on stay (that one is tough, I like to be with mom when we are outside (she hides cookies in her pockets for me, how can I resist that)) 
 - I appear to be a roll with the punches type of pup. Ive liked everyone, 2 and 4 legged that Ive met so far. 
- Foster Mom says I am one of the easiest fosters they have had. I am quiet, keep the place clean and follow the rules. I think she likes me. :)
- I would do best in a home with older kids (over 12) until I settle down a bit more. Im pretty mouthy still, just like most teenagers. I am working on keeping this under control and am getting better each day. These foster family people don't take any back talk from me about this, they are tough. Mom says my forever people will have to continue to be tough and remind me about this until I fully outgrow it. *** UPDATE ***: Zekke has really gotten this under control. He has recently met children as young as 1 and did really well with them. He seems to understand they are small and to be gentle with them.
- I would be a great hiking or running partner with a little training. Mom & I are doing a bit of running and I LOVE IT! The foster kids started school so we have been super busy and unable to hike but we have talked about it and I'm pretty sure I would like that as well. I love to be busy.
- TOYS! I have discovered TOYS and love them. I am getting pretty good with fetch (I will bring the ball back most of the time, sometimes I get distracted) and love soft toys that make noise. Foster mom told me not to destroy them and I'm doing really good with it. I really am enjoying the toy box here. I like to take one outside each time we go. Silly foster mom picks them all up and brings back inside at bedtime every night for me to start again in the morning.
- I met cats, chickens, turkeys and pigs and am happy to report that I did not bother any of them or care about them.
- two new things we have discovered this week. I like to swim and I liked being in Arlington for an event. 
- I am super dog friendly. Honestly, I have not met another dog that I have not gotten along with.

Do you like my new pictures? I went to an event and there was a nice guy named Drew there who took them. I think I look pretty handsome (even if it was 100 degrees that day...whew!)

Anyway, Ill be hanging out in Nokesville, VA. I am able to go home with you as soon as you are approved to adopt. My foster family says someone is going to be very lucky to have me.

name: The Hobbit
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8481

 Meet The Hobbit - known fondly to her foster family as Lady Arwen or Lady for short. She is a 45-50 pound, one year old, beagle/spaniel/lab mix is our best guess. She has gorgeous creamy coloring and luxurious fur - hard to keep your hand out of it. And she doesn't mind the gentle petting and attention at all. She has her nose to the ground all the time - perhaps a nod to her beagle heritage? And she has long silky fur that one might associate with a spaniel. She is so gentle and sweet, and has done beautifully with children, other dogs and car rides. Each day we see more of her exquisite personality shining through. She's very loving and sweet. She's also smart and loves to cuddle. She's been really great with our 2 year old and our 12 year old twins, but our 7 year old is a little too rambunctious for her.

More about this darling girl:
- She is house trained in her foster home, and has visited homes of family members and remembered her house manners there as well.
- She is crate trained, and knows that her crate is her personal den and uses it at time to get some downtime, to relax and unwind. She is a smart girl understanding her personal space.
- She is working on improving her leash skills. She likely never walked on a leash before coming to her foster home, and she likes to pull. With training she is improving and to become really adept and walk on a loose leash, her adoptive family will need to continue the training process.
- She may be shy when meeting new people, but she has impeccable manners - not a jumper
- She is learning her house manners - she likes being on the couch which is fine in her foster home, but she may have to be trained otherwise in her adoptive home. She is very agile and has jumped up to get food from the table. She is learning quickly that is is not acceptable in her foster home. 
- She is generally quiet. She will alert at random times but it's few and far between.
- She is learning to trust humans more thoroughly and quickly, and her fosters are consciously socializing her to help her build confidence. She would rather people kneel down to pet her instead of looming over her. She gets nervous if someone comes up behind her too quickly and can startle if she is bumped into by accident. I think she needs more work on trusting humans in general. She shows no reactivity or aggression, but retreats to her crate if she feels overwhelmed. 
- She loves to run around in the backyard. She loves to play with other dogs. She seems to be a moderate energy dog and she is still trying to figure out how it all works inside a home.
- She loves to play with other dogs.
- She has not been exposed to cats, but her foster thinks she could do well with a confident cat. She's tried to go after squirrels on walks and birds get her attention.
- She will do best with a patient adoptive home where they can continue to show her that humans are a good thing and being apart of a family is where it's at. Possibly someone with another confident dog to help her to continue to gain confidence in a home.

This dog tested positive for Anaplasmosis before arriving to the rescue. Anaplasmosis is a very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Anaplasmosis is not contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get this disease is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

name: SKYE
description:
Beagle-dob: ~04/23/2016...weighs 19lbs.

Rescued from a kill shelter in western NC.

LOVELY personality! Sweet, friendly, out-going, fun personality, super-loving, 'social butterfly', happy, healthy and gentle. EXCELLENT with kids! Crate trained, rides well, walks well on-leash, gets along well with all dogs and older respectful & responsible children (must be 10y+). LOVES being with her people, but can allow her 'social butterfly' to emerge if not supervised OR if she becomes bored while outdoors unsupervised/person goes out gate...she wants to be with her person! Once outside, she will go exploring...not far, but ANY distance is too far, given this sometimes crazy world we live in.

NOT a good match for older seniors.

We will be happy to send you more pix & videos, upon request.

BEWARE! SKY is an 'escape artist'...she WILL climb chain-link & welded-wire fencing(anything she can get a foothold into). Therefore, we are seeking a stay/work-at-home person/walk on leash ONLY situation OR a home with a wooden/vinyl stockade fence with buried reinforcement wire(EXPERIENCED BEAGLE PEOPLE WILL UNDERSTAND!). She just wants to be with her PEEPS!

MUST have a secured fenced-in backyard (NO ELECTRIC FENCES=these are NOT compatible for scent hounds!) OR past INSIDE beagle experience and a regular walking/running/hiking regime and be committed to an 'ON-LEASH ONLY' exercise regime. Homes with children are REQUIRED to have a vinyl/stockade fenced-in backyard...NO EXCEPTIONS!

This pup is in & will remain in foster care in Rutherfordton, NC until her fur-ever home is approved.

Transport is available via 3 Rescued Pet transport svcs and their fees are: $125 from western NC to as far N as Long Island and Vince Lombardi svc plaza/NJTnpk, and $140 to all points along the I-95 corridor as far as ManchesterNH/BurlingtonVT & Albany/RochesterNY. Stops include: DC, MD, DEL, NJTnpk, RyeNY, JohnstonRI and ManchesterNH/BurlingtonVT, Albany & RochesterNY, & Allentown and CarlislePA on I-81.

Adoption fee: $175(includes spay, micro-chip, current health certificate, parasite-free, utd on 1st yr vax(Bordatella, Rabies, Parvo-Distemper & Lepto), all medical paperwork from day#1 at Howlin4Spirit(+ past shelter's records), beef knee cap bone, KONG or Nylabone chew toy, 1/2 gallon bag current dry food(Tractor Supply Store's '4health'-salmon & potato), 2 'pet alert' wallet cards, new Martingale collar and matching 6' leash, 'RESCUED DOGS ROCK' car magnet and 'SUPER PUPPY-The Best Dog You'll Ever Have' training booklet).

To apply to adopt this lovely little sweetie, please copy and paste the application in to a new email, complete all questions(the more detailed, the better your chances of being approved), and email to: howlin4spirit@gmail.com. MAKE SURE you provide us with EMAIL ADDRESSES for your 3 personal references and let them know we will be sending them a short questionnaire within 1 business day. Also, you will need to give your vet's office permission to release your pet's medical history to us, when we call them within 1 business day.

IF you rent, you will need to provide your property manager's contact info. We will be contacting them within 1 business day.

Thank you, for reaching out to a rescued pup in need of love, respect and a warm, safe place to call 'home'. We look forward to helping you find the right pup for you, your family, environment and habits, for a life-time of snuggling, unconditional love and adventures.

name: MADIGAN WAGS -RECOVERING FROM HER  PREVIOUS LIFE
description:
8/25/19

Hi! My name is Madigan, or you can call me Maddie. People say Iâm a pocket pit. Iâm about 38 lbs and 3 years old, so I donât really fit in your pocket, but Iâm smaller than most pit bulls. 
I had a rough start before I came up to PA. The people at Wags that rescued me say that I was most likely used as a bait dog, and then I was hit by a car! Can you believe it? But, oh how my luck has changed. Iâm living in a foster home and I love it! I have toys and chews and blankets and lots of treats. I love meeting and seeing people. I wag my tail and give kisses and they pet me. Itâs a win -win!
Now Iâm looking for my forever home. I like some dogs but I would probably be best as an only dog. If you have another dog, I would need to meet them slowly as I am a little particular, but with my past, do you blame me? Iâve never lived with cats but I could get tested to see how I do with them. 
I love my toys, especially the squeaky ones. I will play with them every day. I have so much fun playing I donât realize how excited I am and I might be a little too much for young children. Teens and up should be ok. I do well on leash with a harness but if you have a fenced in yard I think I would love playing outside. 
My foster mom puts me in a crate when she goes to work. Sometimes I bark when she first leaves but I donât carry on for long. And I havenât had any accidents in the crate. Iâm pretty good around the house. I like to find shoes and chew on them but I am getting better with correction. 
If you would like to meet me, please submit an application and your processsor can get you in touch with my foster mom. Bully breed criteria applies. 


7/23/19

Madigan (Maddie) is approx. 3 yrs old, a spayed Female petite pit mix. She was brought to PA from NC recovering from a broken pelvis, a CCL repair and an infection. She has recovered well and is feeling much better and is now looking for her forever home.  Maddie is very people friendly, adults and kids. However, she appears to be dog selective. She was known to be good friends with a Pom/Peke in training but does not appear to like some dogs. 
Maddie loves to be by her person's side and is getting more playful. She likes soft toys, chewies and antlers.  She has not been cat tested, but likes to chase rabbits and squirrels on our walk. She enjoys walks and will potty on walk or in backyard. 
It is believed that Maddie is a survivor from dog fights. She has some scratches and scrapes, but they donât bother her. She thinks they add to her charm and beauty. 
Maddie is crated while her foster is at work. She will cry and bark for about 10 minutes at first but then settles down. 


5/9/19

Madigen 

Madigen is our baby girl. She is approximately 3 years old and weighs 28lbs. Madigen came to Camp Chester on crate rest due to having her CCL and her fractured pelvis repaired after being hit by a car. She has recently been cleared for active duty and has been slowly learning to play again. Madigen is housebroken, crate trained, loves kids, could care less about cats, and LOVES ALL PEOPLE. She is so tiny you may be able to rock her like a baby, which is what she likes when she watches TV with you. As with all dogs, with slow introductions she has been accepting and playing nice. She loves playing with our resident dog Elsa, who is a 8 pound princess. 

Madigen has a very busy schedule here in Camp Chester, and it has been hard to interrupt her bust schedule for an updated photo shoot so stand by for pictures. 

So what exactly is âCamp Chesterâ? 

Camp Chester OR Wags at Chester WAGs at Chester is an institutional program that pairs incarcerated individuals with dogs to work on basic obedience, house training and socialization. Specifically, all the dogs work really hard to pass our Canine Good Citizenship Test! The Canine Good Citizen Program is a two-part program that stresses responsible pet ownership for owners and basic good manners for dogs. Every dog that arrives at Camp Chester, is given individual attention based on their needs, as every need is different.

Go to wagsrescue.com and click on adoption form. After you complete the application, you will be taken to PayPal so you can submit the $25.00 application fee. Thank you!

description:

name: Rowdy
description:
I am a beautiful boy with a heavy multi colored coat . My sister Muffin is here with me but has a short coat.  Maybe I take after my mother who is a Chow Chow and Muffin takes after our Daddy who is unknown but must be colored like me.

 We both lacked cartilage in our joints when we were born, probably due to our mother not having the proper nutrition when she was pregnant with us. But we are so much better now because our rescue mama has found medicine and a new food with things that we need and we can both run now without hurting our knees. We are able to go on walks but not jog. 

We are considered Senior dogs because on August 31st 2019 we will be 8 years old. But I act like I'm still a puppy.  My mama says the reason we have not been adopted is because we act afraid of people we don't know. I can't help it, I still remember being born under a strange house in the dirt and a man coming and taking two of my sisters away. name: Shyla
description:
Shyla is a very sweet young girl who loves attention and dog treats.  At first she can be shy but she quickly becomes affectionate.  She loves having a dog friend to play with, so we hope to find her a forever home with another dog,  and she's great around cats as well as children.   Shyla is crate trained. 

This sweet girl has overcome some big obstacles in her short life.  She was removed from a hoarding situation in NC,  brought to a kill shelter,  rescued by or group,  and spent many months im a foster home as a semi feral dog. She was terrified of humans, and all of her siblings were adopted long before she came around.  If you meet Shyla now,  you'll never believe this story because she's that sweet and kongs for affection.  

If you'd like to meet Shyla in her foster home i. Piscataway,  NJ,  please send an email to jerseygirlsanimalrescue@gmail.com for an adoption application.

She's medium sized and weighs about 50-55 lbs, is spayed and vaccinated,  housebroken and crate trained, although she doesn't need to be crated.   

Tina's issue is that,  sometime in her past, another dog or dogs weren't so nice to her and she is fearful.  Her defense is showing aggression towards other dogs.  She could successfully be walked on a leash in a park or neighborhood where there are other dogs,  and she walks very well on a leash,  but she will do best not having to closely interact with other dogs.  She,  therefore,  needs to be an only dog. She is a low-key, low maintenance  dog and will make her person or family very happy.  She also loves belly rubs!! 

If you'd like to meet Tina and get an application to adopt her,  please send an email to jerseygirlsanimalrescue@gmail.com.
