name: Lady Bunny
description:
Lady Bunny is a female double merle Australian Shepherd located in Fayetteville, NC.
She is around 6 months of age and is expected to be somewhere between 30-40 lbs when full grown.
As a result of being a double merle Lady Bunny is completely deaf, blind in the left eye but does have some vision on the right.
It's very important to remember that she was born this way so she doesn't realize she's any different and it certainly doesn't slow her down at all.
She is a rather strong willed girl, very smart and high energy!
She is very treat motivated which has made training a lot easier!
So far she is doing fantastic with the hand signals for sit, down, stand, come, stay and spin.
She walks well on leash too.
She is fully crate trained and is doing great with house training.
Lady Bunny would do best with someone that is willing/able to continue her training. 
Aussies are a very smart breed and love to learn.
Lacking some vision from one eye and hearing doesn't change that.
Training is also a great bonding tool!
She absolutely loves playing with other dog's and would do great with another doggie companion.
It would be best for any potential doggie friends to have a more playful/high energy personality because we feel Lady Bunny would be rather overwhelming for an older more laid back dog.
She loves her people and is very attentive, meaning she checks in frequently without being reminded.
She stays too busy to be a cuddler though.
We are recommending she go to a home without small children due to the fact that when she gets overly excited, she can bite down a little too hard.
Not aggressively at all but it does pinch.
Being an energetic young puppy at times she still finds it difficult to keep all 4 paws on the floor when greeting people.
Lady Bunny isn't a fan of sharing her food or high value treats with doggie friends.
We have been working on this and she has made great progress so it very manageable.
Foster mom can fill you in on what we have been doing to work on the issue.
Lady Bunny is spayed, up to date on all vaccinations, current on heart worm/flea tick prevention and she is also microchipped.
We are requiring a meet and greet prior to adoption.
This is just to help ensure we get the best match possible for Lady Bunny as well as the potential adopter.
With her high energy level and love for playing with other dog's, we feel any existing dog's will need to meet her as well to make sure they don't feel overwhelmed by her high energy playful self.
If you think you would be interested in meeting this adorable girl please follow this link to submit an application-

https://www.australianshepherdsfurever.org/adoption-applicaâ¦

Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home.

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption.

~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00

name: Murry Murdoch da Tank!
description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.

description:

He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

He had us fooled in the beginning but he will sit now nicely when asked (a treat helps) and he will need continued positive training to be the best pup he can be.

description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature.

name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

description:
Maddie is our little Miss Cutie Patootie! She is a short and stocky malamute girl with so much personality. She is guaranteed to make you smile every day with her paw up for high fives and zoomies. Maddie was born October 2011. She is easy and independent. She is called a little miss spit fire, because she is a tough little cookie! She is sassy and all malamute. She enjoys being in her crate and doesn't make a peep. Or hanging outside watching everyone and everything. She also enjoys hiking and just loves the outdoors! She is also happy just laying around on her doggy bed and just being in the same room as you. Don't let that adorable teddy bear look fool you, she isn't a cuddler and prefers her space, EXCEPT when salmon treats are involved. She will come right up to you, give you high fives and show so much excitement for treat time! Just give her space and time to get to know you. She had a very rough life and is hesitant to trust people. Despite this, she sits nicely to put her collar on before going on a walk. She also rides well in car but generally speaking, Maddie doesn't just do things willingly, which is why positive training works well for her. KronchUSA salmon treats really help us encourage Maddie to make good choices. She likes to protest a little bit just enough so she feels like she had a choice.  

She will roll over for belly rubs and come up to you for some love but when shes had enough she will leave and go about her business. She was potty trained at one time but will need a refresher. She does not like other dogs but can be around them. If given the chance she will let other dogs know she is boss and that's why we recommend her as being the only dog in the home. When you are out on a walk she won't get upset seeing another dog as long as they are behaving. She isn't dog aggressive but won't back down from a challenge either. 

In May 2017, Maddie had ACL surgery on her right knee and is doing well. Of note, she was debarked as a pup so she doesn't have her 'woowoo' but don't let that stop you from giving this girl her second chance. She needs a home with Northern Breed experience. She has a strict limited ingredient diet --- salmon only protein and fat. Typical malamute she cannot be around small dogs or pets including cats.

description:
Born in August 2014, Bucky has a great sense of humor and is full of personality.  He would love to be your hiking companion followed by a picnic with a chicken sandwich. He LOVES car rides and visiting the nearby pet stores where all the goodies are. Bucky is a very social Malamute/Husky mix and would love a family of his own. He is a free spirit who responds beautifully to pawsitive communication. He enjoys chasing and burying balls (especially squeaky balls) and really enjoys going out on hikes exploring. He has separation anxiety and would do best in a home with a stay at home human. He is an amazing boy with high predatory behavior that can spot any critter or find deer. With cheerful redirection, he will give up the chase to stay with his human.

Bucky is always ready for an adventure but we believe he is trying to find his furever home. Bucky will behave so well, then out of the blue it's like he has to celebrate being good and will surprise you with the fastest zoomies!  However, this is far and few these days. He enjoys just being where you are & hanging out. He has been receiving positive training and has learned to redirect his excitement by sitting for a treat and sitting so the car door opens for an adventure. Most recently he is learning to relax, which he enjoys with chicken sandwich bite size rewards. Bucky looks like a very tall Siberian Husky. Bucky would benefit from pawsitive reinforcement training classes and someone with a good sense of humor. Bucky just wants to have fun, so learning how to communicate being consistent & calm works great for Bucky, especially with a soft yummy treat. 

With so much to give, he definitely will make someone happy once he settles in and knows he's loved. He prefers to be the only pet in the home...who doesn't like to be the star of the show?!?!  We recommend reading, Positive Perspectives 2 - Know your Dog Train your Dog by Pat Miller.  This book will open your eyes from a dogs perspective & help you communicate & train in a pawsitive manner.  To know Bucky is to love Bucky. He is such a sweet boy who is searching for his furever home & hooman. Those who meet Bucky can't believe that he hasn't been adopted.

description:
Some of the most treasured places in America are the National Parks. At MatchDog Rescue, we are celebrating these fascinating places with a transport of pups named after our phenomenal parks. Just like the National Parks, each dog is unique and beautiful, to be treasured and admired. All of our pups are waiting to be discovered by you! Come out on October 5, 2019 and find your \"furever\" friend. Your adventure awaits!!

You don't have to travel all the way to Washington State to see this handsome guy! Meet Rainier- he is a 22 pound, two year old shepherd mix with a white body that will remind you of the snow capped mountains. Shepherds are loyal, highly trainable and have caring temperaments. Rainier is a friendly and happy pup,he just might be the sweetest dog you've ever met!Shepherds are very protective of people they love- will you be one of them? Rainier is 85 percent house trained and crate trained. He will be making the long climb from Texas to New Jersey soon so, if he sounds like the guy for you, fill out an application today.

If you think you are a perfect match for Rainier, please complete an application fully: https://www.petstablished.com/adoption_form/11415/generic

Rainier has been fully vetted, is up to date on all vaccinations and on preventatives for heartworm, flea and tick. We cannot guarantee breed information. You will find the price guidelines for adoption at matchdogrescue.org and can read about the whole adoption process and what MatchDog Rescue provides with each dog.

This gorgeous MatchDog is not yet in the state of N.J. and currently in our MatchPad in the great state of Texas. This dog will be going on a three-day road trip arriving to us here in N.J. on Sat, October 5th at Marlton PetSmart. For the very best chance of securing a meet for this dog on arrival in N.J you must be available all day on this date.

If you see a pending notification on this dog and the picture changed to black and white, it means we have informed the lucky family selected as the best match for this particular dog and they have agreed to come to the transport event as the dog arrives. Eventually go to their forever home. If for any reason this plan falls through, we will change the picture back to color and revisit other applications.

description:

name: Dexter
description: Dexter is looking for his furever home through Blue Ridge Bull Terrier Rescue! Dexter and his adorable floppy ear came into rescue from a New Jersey shelter. He was originally found as a stray and was adopted out from the shelter and, sadly, returned. He has now has been turned over to rescue so he can find his perfect furever home once and for all. Dexter is such a happy boy who is guaranteed to put a grin on your face! He has a very high energy level and is always on the move. He enjoys going for car rides, on long walks or running around a fenced yard, but most of all he LOVES to play with toys! He will play fetch or tug with his humans, but is perfectly happy entertaining himself by tossing the ball and chasing it down on his own. He lives for squeakers! Dexter is very smart and inquisitive. He knows how to sit and give his paw, and should pick up on new tricks quickly if someone were to spend the time with him; he loves cookies. Dexter also has a calm, sweet, and loving side, curling up on the couch for a good cuddle session. Due to his rambunctious energy level, kids in his home should be ages 10+. Dexter is reactive to other dogs and will need to be the only pet in his home. No dogs, cats, or critters. Dexter is a gentleman in the home; he is crate trained, housebroken, and nondestructive. He is a healthy boy who weighs in at 60lbs, is neutered, up to date on his vaccines, heartworm negative, and microchipped. He currently enjoys a grain-free diet. We have absolutely fallen in love with this guy. His floppy ear, paired with his soulful eyes will pull you in and melt your heart. If you are ready for the new love of your life to join your family, please apply here: https://www.brbtc.org/adoption-process/  Dexter is currently fostered in Hartsville, SC, but transport is available for the right home.

description:

We believe she would do best in a home with another confident dog who can help her.  Lula has a bit of separation anxiety but with the help of another dog and a family who spends more time at home than away, she will overcome it in time.  Lula is young and eager to please everyone she meets.  She is so excited to find her forever home where she can curl up on the couch and get endless belly rubs.

name: Freddie
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.FREDDIE

BOXER MIX MALE.

name: Patch
description:
This handsome smiley boy is Patch.  He was rescued from a crowded New Jersey shelter, where he lived for 18 months.  We can't even imagine this sweet soul living on concrete for so long.  He is now currently in a foster home and looking for his forever home.  Patch is about 3 years old, is loving, loyal and eager to please.  He enjoys car rides, especially if it means a trip to the pet store for some treats or a toy.  Patch craves attention and loves walking around the neighborhood looking for kids to give him belly rubs.  He told us children give the BEST belly rubs because their small hands make him ticklish.  He would do great in a home with children over the age of 10.  Since he is bigger and energetic we feel older children would be better!  His smile is infectious and all you want to do when you meet him is smoosh his big face.

If you are interested in adopting Patch, please go to bfdaaa.com to complete an application.

name: Lady Beaufort
description:
This Southern Belle has traveled all the way from South Carolina to find her forever home here in New Jersey. When you meet Lady it is obvious that she did at one time have a home where someone taught her the commands that she knows and how to play her favorite game of \"fetch\".

Lady has been in foster since 1/7/18. She has been a perfect houseguest, is completely house and crate trained. She goes right into her crate every morning when I leave for work and is sleeping when I get home. Lady loves her person, loves cuddling and to be pet. She is a calm dog that loves her toys and a good nap on the couch. On walks she doesn't pay attention to other dogs and walks calmly next to them when on pack walks. We do not know much about Lady's past, but she does scare easily, so she would do best in a calm household with older, respectful children, and not much traffic in and out of the house. She takes a while to warm up to new people but once she does she loves you. Lady is a very special girl that deserves a loving home of her own. She is silly, full of personality and one the sweetest dogs I've ever had the pleasure of fostering. She is so easy to love and will make a wonderful addition to the right household.

If you want to meet Lady go to EHRDOGS.ORG and submit an application. Don't forget to ask for LADY BEAUFORT - she is waiting so patiently at the kennel for someone to fall in love with her and bring her home. Could that someone be you?

name: Liutenant Dan
description:
Hey everyone! My name is Lt. Dan and I am a year old mixed breed dog. We think I might be an Australian Cattle Dog mix or something, but one thing is for sure: I'm 100% handsome! I'm even more handsome with three legs! Your eyes do not deceive you: I am tripawed and a lucky boy. I am awesome with other dogs but my foster mom says I'm not that great with cats because oh boy do I like to chase them. I'm pretty food motivated and will take all of the snacks you'll give me... but I need a new family to help me watch my figure because of my disability.

Truth be told, I did not have the best start in life. I was dumped on the side of a road where I searched for my family and had to fend for myself. While looking for my family I was hit by a car. I was scared and lonely and was hurt really bad. I was so scared of people and it took three big scary men to catch me. They brought me to a hospital where I met my foster mom. She gave me pain medication and advocated for me. This is where the amazing Mel said foster mom could bring me into the rescue and make me better. They amputated my leg and my foster mom slowly gained my trust as I healed. As you can imagine I am still very scared around new people and strangers. I need my new family to come meet me a few times before I can go home with them. It would also be great if my new family has worked with a fearful dog before. I am getting better with trusting my foster mom about strangers and ignoring them. I love playing with my foster brothers and sisters and can play all day. I have foster kitties in the house that I will chase if they run. I am going to go play with my foster siblings now and my foster mom will tell you more.

Lt. Dan is up to date on vaccines, heartworm negative, and on flea, tick and heartworm prevention monthly. He LOVES playing with other dogs and gets along with dogs of all sizes. He can live with dog savvy cats. Lt. Dan is fearful of new people and his adopter with be required to come to New Jersey a few times to meet him and spend some time with him before he can go to his new home. His adopters will also need to have experience with fearful dogs and will need to work with a positive reinforcement trainer. Once he learns to trust you, Lt. Dan will cuddle with you all day if you let him. He is a medium energy dog who just wants to be with his person. He will gladly occupy you on a long walk or cuddle on the couch all day with you. Because he had his leg amputated his adopters will need to be vigilant about his diet, weight and keep him exercised. Lt. Dan has had a rough beginning but with love and dedication he can overcome his past and be a loving member of a family. Could that be you?

SOHO is a 501c3 public charity focusing on rescuing herding dogs in crisis on the East Coast. Your pets will need to be up to date on vaccinations and heartworm preventative in order to be considered for adoption. Lt. Dan does have some additional adoption requirements: his foster mom would like a potential adopter to come and visit Lt. Dan a few times before taking him home in order to help him bond to his new family. Please note that Lt. Dan is located in HIGHLAND LAKES, NEW JERSEY.

name: Eliza
description: Time, patience and yummy treats is the winning combination for Eliza. Because she is shy and fearful, the best way to become her friend is to sit quietly in her room while offering her treats and letting her decide when she wants to approach you. Born in 2015, she came to Best Friends from a shelter in New Mexico. She is at her best when there are other confident, friendly dogs around to help her feel braver. When there are a lot of unfamiliar dogs and people coming and going close by, it is stressful for her. At Dogtown, Eliza is working on learning to trust through hand feeding. She is also working on leash walking, which she enjoys. Eliza is looking for a calm and understanding person or family. A quiet home with a predictable routine and other dogs who can help build her confidence would be best for her. She is considered a flight risk, so she'll need a secure space and someone who can watch over her and keep her safe while she learns about the world.

name: Fenway
description: Fenway is eager to be brave and loves to learn new things. She's shy and fearful with strangers at first but is working on her confidence. She loves water, so in the summer she sits in her baby pool for a good portion of the day. Because she also loves all things soft and fluffy, she likes to collect her blankets in one big pile to sleep on. Born in 2016, Fenway is a distemper survivor. She came to Best Friends from a shelter in New Mexico as a puppy mom. She loved playing with her puppies, and she now enjoys playing with other adult dogs. She also loves to do agility with her doggie roommate and will follow him around the agility course. She would do great in a home with another friendly dog who could help show her the ropes and help boost her confidence. Fenway is currently doing a lot of confidence and trust training at the Sanctuary. She is a willing learner, especially if you reward her with yummy treats, and she is learning that new people, walks and car rides are all good things. She has already picked up on leash walking and is learning basic training cues such as 'sit' and 'down.' Fenway would do best in a home with a person or family who understands shy dogs and can give her time to adjust and progress at her own pace. She is looking for someone who can give her a little guidance and show her that the world can be a fun and safe place.

name: Lotti
description: Lotti is one happy, energetic girl. Born in 2012, she loves running around with her toys and swimming in her pool. Lotti came to Best Friends from the animal welfare department of New Mexico. She can be a bit picky and in-your-face with her dog friends, so she'll need a home where she can either be the only dog or have a tolerant canine companion. Super smart and people-loving, Lotti is ready to learn about life in a forever home. Lotti is currently on a special diet and medication for environmental allergies. Lotti has a generous sponsor who will pay for her adoption fee.

name: Thor
description: Thor is a strikingly handsome boy with a full-body wag. He always has a smile on his face, and his silly antics often make his caregivers at the Sanctuary laugh. He is super smart and loves training. Thor will quickly show you his array of tricks he knows, including high five, down, shake, touch, and is always wanting to learn more! Born in 2009, he still has lots of life and love to give. Thor does prefer to live with female doggie friends. Thor came to Best Friends from a shelter in New Mexico. He's been working hard with Dogtown caregivers and trainers and is ready to find a home of his own.

description:

name: Lemon
description:
My name is Lemon, I am available for adoption through Colorado Canine Rescue (CCR) - a nonprofit dog rescue located in the Denver area. My vet and foster mom have guessed that I am around 2 years old and an American Pit Bull Terrier or \"pit bull-type dog.\" I was rescued from an overcrowded shelter in New Mexico. I will be available to adopt/go home after July 5th. I am currently completing a board and train program through High Drive Dog Company in Longmont, Colorado. Part of my adoption requirements include follow up training with High Drive (sponsored by CCR for 3 months), no other animals in the home, no children under 12, and no cities with BSL (breed specific legislation). It is preferred I am adopted to a home with a 6 foot wooden fence. These requirements are non-negotiable. Lemon would do best living with someone who has bully breed experience. Lemon weighs around 60 pounds, is crate trained, and doing well with housetraining. She can be vocal when she needs something, and is not appropriate for apartment/condo living.

Lemon had a rough start to life; being kenneled 24/7 for 2 months straight prior to arriving in Colorado was a lot of stress. Lemon has worked through a lot of reactivity issues. She actually plays well with a lot of dogs. She is NOT a candidate for dog parks. However, she is always welcome to attend supervised playgroups at High Drive (please see http://www.highdrivedogco.com/ for more details about the company). Lemon is not a coach potato. She is bold, eager to learn, and ready to take on the world. Lemon needs to be challenged physically and mentally. She is funny and affectionate. This pup may have started out as a lemon, but she is quite a peach.

If you are interested in adopting Lemon, please submit an application located on our website, www.coloradocaninerescue.org. We are asking for a $200.00 adoption donation. Lemon is spayed, up to date on vaccinations, and micro-chipped. Please note, CCR cannot guarantee the breed composition or ages of our dogs as we usually have no history prior to them entering the shelter. In addition, most dogs listed as potty trained will experience an adjustment period as they learn the routines in their new home.

name: Spot
description:
Spot is a six-year-old blue Doberman and came to us from a shelter in northern New Mexico. This gentle giant is such a loverâhe just always wants to snuggle and be right next to you, he will nudge his nose on your leg to get attention. He is very unaware of his size and is always trying to climb into his foster momâs lap. If you are laying on the couch or bed Spot will be right next to you and will make sure he can get as close as he can, so he gets lots of love.

He is crate trained and stays in the crate while his foster family is at work. He also sleeps the night in his crate just like the other pups in the house. Just say the word kennel and he will rush into his crate for that snack. He is very food motivated and is super gentle in taking treats. He knows basic commands like sit and down. He works well with snaps or a clicker when it comes to listening.

He gets along great with other dogs and can play all day with his toys and is always willing to give up his toy to the pesky puppies in the house. He lets these little girls crawl all over him and loves to play and chase them all over the backyard. You can tell he has been around lots of puppies in his life because he is as calm as it gets when these girl nibble and lick him to death. It did take him a while to open up to the other male dog in the house, but now they are buddies and you can see them lounging together on the bed or couch as well as running around to catch the puppies in the backyard. He is learning the leash but does get distracted easily and sometimes likes to pull when he sees something. But with work this can be broken. He weighs almost 80 pounds and has bald spots that unfortunately have not started to re grow even with proper food and care. But this is common with Blue Dobies and Spot doesn't know he is bald :)

name: Peanut2
description:
I live in Valencia County, New Mexico.

I was rescued from a hoarder in Las Cruces, New Mexico.

I have not been around people much, so they scare me. I need someone who has the patience to show me that people are not bad.

I have been micro-chipped.

At the time of this posting I am 5 years old.

name: Winnie: medical hold (NY)
description:
Winnie is diabetic and is currently on medical hold while she gets her insulin stabilized. She is being fostered in NY state. 

What we know about Winnie:
*sweet
*loves to be with people
*prefers her space with other dogs
*housebroken
*sleeps through the night

What Winnie's foster mom has to say about Winnie:
Who's that girl with the golden waves? It's Winnie! Winnie is a beautiful terrier mix. She's about 7 years old, and she's already quite the traveler! Winnie came to BDRA from a shelter in New Mexico, and she charmed hearts all the way from New Mexico to New York!

Winnie loves her people with all that she has. Her perfect day is a day spent with her person, giving cuddles and kisses and getting belly rubs. She tries very hard to be a good girl.

Winnie wants to be with her people at all times. She'll follow you from room to room, and will lay happily at your feet or in your lap as you work or watch TV. Sometimes she follows me so closely she actually steps on my feet. She can also be timid and submissive, and if she thinks she's in your way, she will do her best to avoid you.

Winnie has late immature cataracts, but has functional vision at this time. As her vision declines, she may be a candidate for cataract surgery. She receives eye drops every 12 hours and is an angel! She also has Anisocoria, which means her pupils are two different sizes. This does not affect her now, but will need to be regularly monitored. She is housebroken and sleeps quietly through the night.

Winnie can be tolerant of the other dogs (all males) and cats (one male, one female) in her foster home and may even sleep next to one, but more often, she does not like when another dog or cat gets too close to her. She'll give a warning growl, and if the dog doesn't move away, she will lunge. It does not escalate further than that. Out of the four male dogs here, there is one dog she likes very much (a blind poodle mix).

Winnie is diabetic and came into rescue underweight. She has since gained several pounds and is even a bit overweight! As she was an untreated diabetic, her diabetes is still being regulated, and so she will remain on medical hold. 
Blind Dog Rescue Alliance has voted against the use of electric fencing effective immediately.

description: Trinket is sweet girl flown in from New Mexico. She is good on a leash and knows basic commands. She gets along with most dogs with proper introductions. She loves to play or just snuggle with you. This girl is a really nice dog and will make a great addition to any family.

name: Kimy
description:
Kimy comes to us from New Orleans after her owners decided to move and dump her. She is a big girl, and enjoys to lean in for hugs. Kimy has had her Heartworms treated. This girl is about 5 years old! She is shy at first, but quickly warms up! She needs to be an only pet, and in a breed experienced adult home.

Kimy did have a bad knee but has had surgery to repair this, and should not have any issues!

name: Sebastien(dino)
description:
This little wild child is Sebastien! He loves getting the freedom to run and explore everything in sight! This sweet guy with his love for play can still be a bit shy to cuddling with new people but play some tug of war with him and he'll never want to leave your side! Sebastien had a long ride here from New Orleans after his old shelter got flooded from Hurricane Barry so he would love nothing more than to finally have a safe place to call home with people he can call family!

description:
Sandy is a beautiful senior girl who would love to sit on the couch and enjoy TV with you. Sandy is a senior so she does go out to the bathroom often. She loves to be outside in the yard and soak up the sun, she enjoys her walks too. Sandy is looking for someone she can enjoy her golden years with, someone who can just love her, cuddle her, and make her feel like a princess.

Sandy would do best in a home where there are no other dogs or a very submissive dog that is about her size. She would be an ideal match for a couple, maybe even an older couple who understand what it's like to be aging.Sandy is located in New Windsor, NY (not too far from Poughkeepsie). Why not visit her and see if there's a love match? If you have another dog, you will need to bring him/her along.

description: Cliff is a gentle, mellow giant who just wants to hang out with people and get lots of petting. He's easygoing and likes everyone he meets. Born in 2013, Cliff came to Best Friends from a shelter in New York. Never one to turn down a meandering stroll or a golf cart ride across Dogtown, Cliff truly does like to stop and smell the roses (ok, maybe sagebrush). Cliff also enjoys very sturdy toys and relishes his \"toy time\" with volunteers. He has allergies so he eats a prescription diet to control the food allergies and he takes allergy drops to help with the environmental allergies, as well as a few other medications and twice weekly baths. Cliff has had several play dates here at the sanctuary and seems to prefer female dogs. Because Cliff is a low-energy guy, he'd be the perfect dog for someone who wouldn't mind hanging out on the couch after taking a leisurely walk.

name: GINGER
description: Ginger is a beautiful one-year-old husky mix waiting to meet you! Ginger arrived here from an overcrowded shelter in the south; and after a long trip to New York, she's ready to find her forever family. She gets along well with all dogs and kids of all ages. However, she is a bit afraid of cats. Ginger is a moderate energy dog with a sweet, gentle personality. She is already crate trained and house trained, and knows her sit and down commands. Come meet this sweet girl today!

description:
Apple is a 2 year old female Jindo mix weighing 16lbs who was rescued from the Korean Meat Trade and brought to New York to find her forever home. She gets along well with other dogs, and loves running around in the yard with them. She is shy when first meeting new people, but with time and patience she gets comfortable and cuddly. She is currently working on her leash training and housebreaking. She will definitely need another four legged creature in the home and a quieter household without a lot of coming and going. A securely fenced yard is also a plus for this gal.

If you are interested in this dog, please submit an application directly to our website at www.ny-petrescue.org Only applications submitted directly to Pet Rescue will be considered.

name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home.

name: Murry Murdoch da Tank!
description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.

name: Lakota Mato (Bear)
description:
Lakota is a 2-year-old boy born July 2017 who came to us from a shelter where his previous owners dumped him. He was purchased as a puppy and lived most of his life outside. He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

Lakota would do best in a home with no young children. He did well when seeing other dogs on walks and we will continue to work with him and see how he does with a female companion. He is super smart and knows how to sit. He had us fooled in the beginning but he will sit now nicely when asked (a treat helps) and he will need continued positive training to be the best pup he can be.

name: Apollo the White Knight
description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature.

name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.   

If you are interested in adopting Finn, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

name: Winnie: medical hold (NY)
description:
Winnie is diabetic and is currently on medical hold while she gets her insulin stabilized. She is being fostered in NY state. 

What we know about Winnie:
*sweet
*loves to be with people
*prefers her space with other dogs
*housebroken
*sleeps through the night

What Winnie's foster mom has to say about Winnie:
Who's that girl with the golden waves? It's Winnie! Winnie is a beautiful terrier mix. She's about 7 years old, and she's already quite the traveler! Winnie came to BDRA from a shelter in New Mexico, and she charmed hearts all the way from New Mexico to New York!

Winnie loves her people with all that she has. Her perfect day is a day spent with her person, giving cuddles and kisses and getting belly rubs. She tries very hard to be a good girl.

Winnie wants to be with her people at all times. She'll follow you from room to room, and will lay happily at your feet or in your lap as you work or watch TV. Sometimes she follows me so closely she actually steps on my feet. She can also be timid and submissive, and if she thinks she's in your way, she will do her best to avoid you.

Winnie has late immature cataracts, but has functional vision at this time. As her vision declines, she may be a candidate for cataract surgery. She receives eye drops every 12 hours and is an angel! She also has Anisocoria, which means her pupils are two different sizes. This does not affect her now, but will need to be regularly monitored. She is housebroken and sleeps quietly through the night.

Winnie can be tolerant of the other dogs (all males) and cats (one male, one female) in her foster home and may even sleep next to one, but more often, she does not like when another dog or cat gets too close to her. She'll give a warning growl, and if the dog doesn't move away, she will lunge. It does not escalate further than that. Out of the four male dogs here, there is one dog she likes very much (a blind poodle mix).

Winnie is diabetic and came into rescue underweight. She has since gained several pounds and is even a bit overweight! As she was an untreated diabetic, her diabetes is still being regulated, and so she will remain on medical hold. 
Blind Dog Rescue Alliance has voted against the use of electric fencing effective immediately.

name: Mocha
description:
Sweet Mocha is a 6 year old Pit Bull who has come to our rescue all the way from Long Island in New York City!! Due to overcrowded kennels in the city poor Mocha was on the list to be euthanized. She was a favorite among the volunteers at the municipal shelter and they fought hard to find safety. After reaching out to dozens of no-kill shelters they finally found The Canine Rescue of Central PA and we were happy to make room for her! 

She is appropriately named Mocha as she has a beautiful coat that looks like a cup of Mocha with some whipped cream swirled in! And she's about as sweet as a Mocha treat as well! She walks well on a leash and has a good bit of energy! But also likes to cuddle and adores being with people. She has a small prey drive and would do best in a home without children, cats or small dogs. She could likely live with medium to large sized dogs.

Mocha is spayed, up-to-date on shots and housetrained. If you are interested in meeting Mocha or would like more information please leave a voicemail at the rescue 717-232-1644 or e-mail at adopt@crcpa.org.

name: XP Digby - New York City
description:
Digby is looking for a new home because his mom has severe allergies. He currently lives with his mom & dad as well as 3 children (14, 2 and 5 months) and a 14-year-old \"sibling\" named Pickle. As you can see in his photos, Digby \"digs\" children, even the littlest ones!

From his Mom:

Although he is 6 years old, Digby is still very much a young boy who has a lot of love and spunk left in him. He is a wonderful family dog and loves children, snacks, pets, and snuggles. He loves to eat and is very responsive to food as a reward for training. He does know several, tricks too!!

Sadly, like many other Pit Bulls, Digby does come with some emotional baggage. Since he was a rescue he has fear aggression issues only towards other dogs - never humans EVER - so he definitely would do great in a one-dog house unless someone has the patience to slowly introduce him into a home with another dog. We did it for 4 days at my in-law's house in Boston and by day 4 Digby was off leash and everyone was playing happily and he's lived peacefully with our Pickle dog since we got him.

Digby really is a wonderful family dog & we are hoping someone will give him a chance in a new family home. Digby is NOT with 11th Hour Rescue but we are helping his family with the rehoming process. If you would like to meet Digby or to get more info on him, please emailpalmares215@gmail.com or call Jennifer at 973 610 1201. Digby and his family are currently located in New York City.

name: XP Roo - NYC
description:
Roo is a 3 year old Pit Bull mix, full of energy and love. She's curious about everything and loves attention. She is very playful with her sister and absolutely loves giving kisses to any person or dog who wants them. I always joke around saying her ball is her pacifier because she has it with her the majority of the day and can be found sleeping with one in her mouth.

Roo is always looking for love by strangers and dogs when we are walking around the city. Although she loves interacting with dogs outside of the dog park she has no interest in playing with them at the park because of her ball obsession. She also loves sleeping on the bed and loves to cuddle! She loves to curl up and be held at night and is a big fan of covers but she's also okay if you leave her on the couch.

Roo has lived with a small Chihuahua as I fostered one for a month and Roo seems to know her size with other dogs. She really wants to interact with cats as well when we pass them in the bodegas in NYC. She even knows which bodegas have them and stops and wags her tail watching and hoping they will one day come say hi. She's good with every person she's met and loves kids as well but does try to jump and give kisses when she's overly excited.

Roo is NOT with 11th Hour Rescue but we are helping her owner with the rehoming process. If you'd like to meet Roo, please contact Lauren by email at lauren.wise@compass.com or by phone at 917-699-2380 - Roo is currently located in New York City.

name: Tone
description:
Tone is such a great dog!! He is eager to please, listens to direction and is ready for his furever too! He is currently living in a foster home and is an absolute pleasure. Housebroken and knows basic commands!! Are you his HERO?
REMEMBER TONE from NEWARK? Back in July 2017, we posted a plea for an emergency foster so we could pull him from the Newark, NJ shelter. He was very ill with pneumonia and he wasnât doing well. Kendell, a NYBC supporter made us aware of Tone and assisted with finding a foster. Mary, Toneâs foster mom, who now calls him Sam, has nursed him back to health and is giving him a stable home environment to flourish in. If you would like to adopt him, please submit an application today at www.nybullycrew.org

name: Vinny
description: Before you ask about Vinny please read the full description.  Vinny is NOT your typical easy  going sweet beagle.  I know the photo is misleading however he can be quite the charmer with MEN.  Vinny is a self-conscious type of dog and is very suspicious of human motives when approached.  We attribute this to unpleasant early life experiences.  Vinny will do well in a home with just one man or a couple with dog experience.  Although good a on leash we just don't trust his behavior if a child were to run up to him or a person wanting to prove all dogs love them bends over his head.  He'd be OK in a  fenced yard and walks taken where there is limited exposure to encountering others.  Nose to the ground in the country he's probably a great candidate as a hunting dog.  He's more of that type of beagle than a docile house pet.    His guesstimated age is about FIVE years of age and he was rescued from a Newark, NJ shelter. He weighs in the range of 25 pounds.   He enthusiastically runs to you when called,  sits politely for food, guarding a bone is another matter so no long lasting treats for Vinny.  He goes to his bed/crate when asked,  He opts to hide under a flannel blanket curled up so tight that you don't even know he's inside the blanket so of course he feels a little vulnerable when you wake him. He's a late sleeper and he grumbles when he doesn't want to get up but we all know someone like this! He's a very clean dog too that takes his business outdoors. Vinny likes car rides.   He's is OK with cats and great with other usually bigger dogs. Bottom line if you're a single male in a more suburban or country location, don't have kids; like to hike for long periods of time Vinny could really make a turn around  in his behavior.  I believe the key to his success is sufficient exercise to relieve his tension coupled with a protocol for rehabilitating his unwanted quirks.  To meet Vincent in Blairstown e:mail auntmarysdoghouse@yahoo.com or call 908-362-1333

name: Dustin
description:
Hello from our happy-go-lucky Dustin.  He is only 2 years old and a very sweet boy. He came to us from the Associated Humane Society in Newark, NJ where his future was not looking so bright. We took one look and couldn't leave him behind. 
Dustin is an extremely affectionate playful and cuddly guy!! He loves his walks and is overjoyed to go for a ride in the car. He is everything you could wish for in a dog. He is welcoming to people of all ages and greets everyone with a wagging tail but he would feel most comfortable in a home with no other pets. However, he has so much love to give, you will never need anyone else!! 
If you are interested in adopting ustin please go fill out the application today at www.nybullycrew.org

name: Cappuccino
description: CAPPUCCINO was transferred from Newark AHS. He is a 4 and a half year old friendly boy who likes other dogs and is a handsome boy. name: Sheba
description:
This spunky little lady is Sheba, a 4 year old pretty pittie that came to us from our Newark facility after being given up by an owner that just didn't want her anymore.  When you walk through the kennels and some dogs are barking, trying to get your attention, Sheba is the one sitting quietly, politely looking up at you, hoping you'll ask to meet her.  Politeness is one of Sheba's finest qualities!  Sure, she's a little powerhouse on a leash, but she is perfectly behaved.  She sits when asked and takes treats gently.  She takes a quick zoom around our exercise yard, chases after a few toys, then comes right back to stand beside you and get lots of attention.  She adores people and if she was any sweeter she would be made of sugar.  Sheba doesn't have much experience with other dogs but she is open to meeting them and seeing how it goes.  Come in and meet this little butt-wiggler.....you'll love her!  File#28915  3/5/19

name: Tank

name: Sadie & Jada
description:
A SPECIAL NEEDS BONDED PAIR NEEDS OUR HELP!

Update: Sadie and Jada will soon be seeing a veterinary ophthalmologist for a complete exam.

Five year old Jada and her best buddy, six year old Sadie, are a truly bonded pair - and they're both blind.

Although Sadie, a neutered male, is blind he always knows where Jada is - and she relies on him. When they go for leash walks with their mom, Sadie is the leader and he walks ahead of his mom and Jada follows behind her - it's quite the parade.

Sadie was especially attached to his dad who died a few months ago. He was his loyal companion and stayed right with him throughout his illness. He was also with him when he died.

Jada and Sadie's owner now can't afford to care for them and she's anxious to get them both to a veterinary ophthalmologist for a thorough eye exam and treatment.

Our wonderful volunteer took them both to be groomed and vetted the week of August 7th.

The groomers adored both dogs. \"Jada is a real sweetheart\" and Sadie was fine once he was lifted onto the grooming table (because he is blind he was a bit panicked by being lifted by strangers but he settled down quickly.) Now both dogs are clean and beautiful!

Our vet diagnosed Jada with juvenile cataracts and we hope they're operable and she can regain some sight. Sadie has cataracts and glaucoma, he's now on two eye medications to help reduce the pressure in his eyes.

The immediate need is to find a loving, caring adult only home for these two special cockers. CSRNE will pay for all ophthalmological care and medications. Our vet said both dogs are otherwise in good health.

Both Jada And Sadie were purchased from a Manchester, NH pet store at 12 weeks of age. They started going blind when they were about 4 years old. Their condition, juvenile cataracts, is genetic so the purchased them from an irresponsible puppy  mill that is breeding cocker puppies with the gene  for juvenile cataracts. But quite frankly the puppy mill doesn't care - they've already gotten their money and now it's Jada and Sadie who will pay the real price for the irresponsible breeding practices of mercenary puppy mills and the pet stores who so carelessly purchase their puppies.

We can only help dogs like Jada and Sadie if you, our friends, become their advocates. Do you know a special person who might be willing to give these two dogs the care and attention they so deserve?

We know we're looking for a rare individual who has the time to care for Jada and Sadie but we're hoping their cocker angel is out there somewhere willing and able to help these two devoted cockers.

We ask everyone interested in adopting to please fill out and send in our adoption application and restraint agreement before we invite you to meet any dogs.   Once your application is approved, we can proceed!

Here is a link to our application and more information: http://csrne.org/adoption/apply-to-adopt/

name: Fox
description:
Say hello to Fox - this handsome hound mix is approximately 11 years young. Fox's history is long and interesting. Once upon a time, he was part of a sprint racing sled dog team. Unfortunately, his owner passed from cancer a few years back which left Fox and several of his friends needing somewhere else to call home. Fox and his buddies made the trek from NY to NH and enjoyed being a member of our recreational touring kennel for a few years. Unfortunately and much to Fox's dismay, it was discovered that he had torn ACLs and for his safety and comfort shouldn't run too often. This newly retired sled dog is looking for a semi-active retirement home that will bring him on frequent walks and the occasional outdoor adventure. Fox gets along well with other dogs but would prefer a home without kiddos (they are a little overwhelming and make him a bit nervous). Fox is a sweet fella who would be happy to accompany you on daily errands or hang out with you on the couch enjoying the AC all summer long.


Things To Consider Before Inquiring:

- Our adoptable sleds dog are used to living in a traditional working kennel environment (ie: completely outdoors).This means that they will need to be house trained and exposed to house stimulus like stairs, cars, vacuums, wood floors, etc. Adopting an adult sled dog is similar to welcoming a puppy.

- Our adoptable sled dogs range from medium to high energy. In general they require multiple walks daily and engaging toys when inside the home. A bored/under exercised sled dog can be a destructive and anxious sled dog! 

- Our adoptable sled dogs are trained to run and are therefore in general are a high flight risk! We do require that they be on leash or within a fenced in yard at all times until proper recall training has been received. 

- While many of our adoptable sled dogs have befriended kitties in their new homes, we do not have cats at our facility to \"test\" them with. That being said, adopters are instructed to monitor all interactions with small animals as there is no telling how they may react.

name: Hermione
description:
Baby Hermione was dumped in the woods with her litter mates at 6 weeks old. Who does this stuff??? Terrible!  These are very lucky puppies. The woods is a very dangerous place for babies without their mother.  So, the first example of their luck started with two EMTs who discovered her and her siblings, have been loving them and will take care of her and her all eight of them until they are 12 weeks old. These EMTs truly knew how to care for them!  At 12 weeks they will have had their second vet visit including age appropriate shots/treatment which means they will be safe to travel from KY to NJ, arriving September 15.  She will not be housebroken at that time. She and her siblings are sweet, curious, playful and very ready to attach to a loving person or family. Some specs on their current weight will help determine adult weight, as for now they are small. The weight range for a medium sized adult dog is 26 to 60 pounds.  On 8/22 at 9 weeks old Jeanie was 11 pounds, Snape (male) 15.6 pounds, and Hermione 12.8 pounds.  It will be hard to predict their exact weights when full grown since we do not know either of the parents personally.  But their vet made some breed predictions. The rule for estimating weight is when it comes to medium and larger breeds, take their weight at 14 weeks and double it. Then add half of the original weight. (For instance, if your puppy weighs 25 pounds at 14 weeks, double this to 50 and then add 12.5 for an estimated adult weight of 62.5 pounds). They wonât be small dogs; some may be medium, or some large dogs. When they arrive at 12 weeks old they will of course be a little bigger than they are now but still little babies in need of love.  If you are looking for an elegant, fun, super good luck beagle/treeing walker coonhound please apply to adopt Hermione by visiting our website www.peace4paws.org

description:

She'll more than likely grow to be a medium size, isn't shejust a stunning gal? Yosemite is a sweetheart and very shy. She's still a pup and learning to come out of shell- do you know what's the recipe to helping her? Love, patience, play time and possiblysome traning. Yosemite needs a family that will love her and show her the ropes! She has known only a cold floor at a high-kill shelter and was lucky to have been saved by MatchDog. Yosemite is crate trained and 70% house trained. If you can picture her at your side during a walk around the neighborhood or justcuddling than why wait and place your app today!

If you think you are a perfect match for Yosemite, please complete an application fully:https://www.petstablished.com/adoption_form/11415/generic

Yosemite has been fully vetted, is up to date on all vaccinations and on preventatives for heartworm, flea and tick. We cannot guarantee breed information. You will find the price guidelines for adoption at matchdogrescue.org and can read about the whole adoption process and what MatchDog Rescue provides with each dog.

This gorgeous MatchDog is not yet in the state of N.J. and currently in our MatchPad in the great state of Texas. This dog will be going on a three-day road trip arriving to us here in N.J. on Sat, October 5th at Marlton PetSmart. For the very best chance of securing a meet for this dog on arrival in N.J you must be available all day on this date.

If you see a pending notification on this dog and the picture changed to black and white, it means we have informed the lucky family selected as the best match for this particular dog and they have agreed to come to the transport event as the dog arrives. Eventually go to their forever home. If for any reason this plan falls through, we will change the picture back to color and revisit other applications.

name: Lulu  urgent **Needs a Foster Home***
description:
Please check out Lulu's personal facebook page: I love Lulu

If you are looking for a dog that brings a smile to your face and makes you laugh, Lulu is the dog for you. Lulu has a wonderful attitude about life, she is happy and contented no matter what the situation. 

Lulu knows her basic commands: sit, stay, down, heel, off, look at me and crate. 
Lulu graduated from 2 positive training classes with Wonder Dogs in West Berlin, NJ All the trainers just loved her and she learned so fast. 

She would do best in a home with older children as she jumps when excited.
Lulu is a smart pup and a quick learner. She is even great with agility.  She also has learned how to walk on a tredmill for exercise.

When she is not enjoying a walk or some play time, Lulu wants to snuggle up close to you on the couch and give kisses. She's a real love bug.
While she enjoys an active lifestyle, she is crate trained and is not stressed out by spending time in the crate. Lulu is very housebroken.

Because she hasn't lived with another dog before we feel she would benefit from being the only dog. She can have neighborhood dog friends to Walk with and play dates at home with dogs once she gets to know them well, and if their play style is similar to hers. Lulu enjoys being the center of attention with the people who love her. 

Lulu is in need of a Foster Home, or an Adopter. She is living in one of our partner boarding kennels, since her family returned her because they were having a baby. 
She is taken care of by the staff and our volunteers everyday, but she misses being in a home with someone to cuddle with and a fenced yard to play in. 
We offer to anyone interested in fostering or adopting to start out with weekend sleepovers or day trips, to spend time getting to know each other. 

The adoption fee for Lulu is waived because it is sponsored.

If you are interested in fostering or adopting Lulu please contact us at wjvolunteers@yahoo.com.

name: Ember
description:
This is the story of the E Litter. Their mother, Coco, was found alone, abandoned in Barnwell, South Carolina. It was clear that she had been nursing quite recently however, at the time, none of her puppies had been claimed nor found. A week after rescuing Coco, Home for Good Dog Rescue got a call stating that Coco's puppies, now known as the E Litter, had been found. They were found by a good samaritan in the insulation of a trailer, all malnourished and dehydrated. They are all very very lucky to be alive. Once this litter arrived at Home for Good's Aiken, SC property, they receive all the attention, love, and care, they so truly needed. Within no time, these pups were all nursed back to a clean bill of health and are now ready to find the forever homes they so truly deserve!

They are now about 2 months old, 10 pounds each and the cutest Labrador Retriever/Hound mixes. They are a very playful and outgoing bunch despite their rough start to life - it is clear that they are all so happy to be given a second chance! These pups love other dogs, cats, and children. They would make perfect family companions. In their foster homes, they have begun to work on their crate, leash, and house training. Now, all they need are forever families to call their own.

Ember is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

description:

She is a very sweet and submissive girl, who enjoys spending her days hanging out in a kiddie pool. She gets along well with others, including kids, cats, and other dogs. Darby adores other dogs and would do great in a forever home with another dog. She walks nicely on a leash, is primarily housebroken, and is crate trained. This girl cannot wait to find her forever home!

Darby is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

description:

Scarlet is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

description:

Molly is NOT with Eleventh Hour Rescue but we are helping network her so that she may find a new home. If you are interested in meeting Molly, please contact Amber at 862-322-9789. Molly is currently located in Newark, NJ.

description:
Mace is NOT with Eleventh Hour Rescue but we are posting the dog on our web site to help his caretaker find a new home for him. If you are interested in meeting Mace, please call or text 973-223-0625.

Mace is an 8-year-old Mastiff whose owner can no longer care for him. He is up to date on his vaccines & he's currently located in Dover, NJ.

description:

Houston, Chicago, Raleigh, Seattle, Milwaukee, Boston, and Detroit have their bags packed and are ready to lay roots in their forever homes! They were all rescued from Loris, South Carolina.
