name: Martin
description:
Hi I'm Martin aka Marty for short,
I have a had a rough life and I am very misunderstood. Aside from my not so normal looks, I also have a unique personality. Do you remember the weird kid in school that would hang back and didn't have many friends... the one who was socially awkward... that's me. You see I came from Turtle Mountain Indian Reservation in North Dakota as a young guy, maybe 8 months old. Who knows but happen but I was likely shot in the face and took off and then found a wandering pokey animal humans call a porcupine. I was brought in with a face and mouth full of quills and an old fractured jaw. I was very scared and I stayed in the back of my kennel for weeks. Finally a nice lady took me in down in the cities. When I went to the vet for the porcupine quills they determined my kidneys were in rough shape. It could have been from some poison back home or I could have been born with issues. Either way the nice lady got me some special food and started me on medications. I had 3 separate procedures to clean up my face of quills and abscesses. I hate those pokey animals! I went to see a special doggy dentist about my broken jaw and they said it would not be worth rebreaking my jaw to reset it and that I just needed a couple teeth removed. We went back to the nice lady's veterinarian and I was neutered and had those teeth removed so they didn't hurt me anymore. That's when they discovered I had been shot. There are still shrapnel on xray. My crooked jaw doesn't bother me one bit. I do have to stay on the special food and one inexpensive medication for life for my kidneys but otherwise nothing special. I do get along with other dogs. In fact I love to play... but sometimes I don't really know how to go about interacting. Enter my socially awkward personailty... Due to my previous life of having to always be on guard and protect myself, I sometimes feel the need to flee. I am not a run away, in fact j love my foster people. If a dog is scary I want to run. If they are friendly so am I. I don't like strangers coming up to my fence though and making loud noises. I prefer meeting face to face without a barrier. I LOVE to run and play chase and tag. I love to play ball as well. I would really like to find a family or person that understands I am not like your all american lab. I have my quirks but I am a lover and I will be loyal to the end. I am house trained and crate trained and get along with kids as well.
Adoption fee is $225
Applications are available at rpaw.org

name: Sophia
description:
We are looking for a medical foster for Sophia starting in mid-September, she is currently being fostered in
Brandenton,FL (Manatee County).
Sophia was saved from a North Florida shelter. She was found abandoned with her two full grown puppies at an empty house. When we got her she was very lethargic, her gums were pale, and she could barely stand. We got her into the vet and after getting bloodwork done, she was diagnosed with AIHA, Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia. Evidently, this condition is prevalent in Spaniel dogs. The treatment is a medication called prednisone and she has responded well to it. We are continuing her weekly frequent blood counts until she is stable, then we will progressively decrease the prednisone. She has since perked up, and is able to get around without issues. She is the sweetest dog who wags her tail all the time. She loves to talk to you, which apparently is a trait of the Clumber Spaniel! She has not been crated but does go in one without issue. She is potty trained, uses a dog door, and gets along great with all the dogs in her current foster home. She loves to get belly rubs and has a big appetite due to the prednisone. Sophia still needs to gain some weight but she's slowly making progress on that end, she weighs about 35-40lbs but should weigh around 50lbs. Her blood count is coming up and although it plateaued last week we are hoping for an increase in the next few days. We are hopeful Miss Sophia will recoup from this. AIHA will always be present but with the appropriate medication dogs with this condition can live a healthy long life span. We are looking for a foster for this sweet girl who will continue to be able to care for her, get her blood work done, and would not be afraid of a challenge. Sweetest dog ever, she will be a project dog. Please contact us if interested in being a medical foster. All medicals are paid by us, and we will oversee her medical treatment plan. Sophia deserves a chance to live. Please look her up!!
We are a foster-based rescue organization with foster homes throughout the state of Florida. We predominantly save dogs from municipal shelters throughout the Southeastern U.S. Our rescue dogs live in foster homes - there is no central facility. If interested in meeting one of our wonderful adoptable dogs, please fill out an application at ewenityfarmsbch.com. Information on adoption donation amounts and our process can also be found at this site.

name: Rick
description:
It's hard to miss Rick when you walk our grounds. He's the handsome St. Bernard/Siberian husky mix sitting expectantly in his kennel for the fun to begin. Rick is originally from Macon County in North Georgia. He has lived in a house, done well in foster care, and would like to settle in a home of his own. At 52 pounds, three-year-old Rick is a fairly big boy. He likes other dogs, knows his commands, and rides in the car so exceedingly well that you almost forget he's there. In fact, as an occasional treat, we drive him around the block. 

Rick needs an adults-only home with dog-experienced people who can take him for walks and continue his training. He'll repay you with loyalty and love and then some. Come meet him.

name: Becky
description:
Becky is a 3 year old 45lb American Bulldog/ Boxer mix who was rescued from a North Jersey shelter after we learned that she at some point had 3 broken legs.  Becky saw a specialist who determined that her legs had already healed and were fused.  Therefore that meant that surgery was not an option.  Although she slightly limps sometimes, she gets around great and loves to run around and play.  Becky needs to go into a home without any children but loves to she loves to cuddle, sleep and get belly rubs from anyone who will spend time with her.  Becky has not had an easy life and we want her to be the only animal in the house so she doesnât has competition for affection as she can be very dog selective.  Becky can be described as a bit of a couch potato.  Give her a couch and some fleece blankets and she is a happy girl!!!  We would love for Becky to go into a home where she can go on walks every day to help make her legs stronger.  The more exercise she has the better it will be as she gets older.  Becky is crate trained, house trained and ready for a loving forever home.

If you are interested in Becky, please go to bfdaaa.com to complete an application.

name: Sugar
description: Meet Sugar! Sugar is a 10 week old Chihuahua/Terrier Mix. Sugar and her sister Spice came from a rural shelter in South Carolina and made their way North to Maryland just before a hurricane was projected to make landfall. Not only are Sugar's ears irresistible, she has the sweetest personality too! Sugar loves everyone and everything and is working on potty training in her foster home. Sugar is a little love bug! She enjoys playing and loves being held. This sweet girl would love to have a family of her own.

name: Brooks
description:
Meet Brooks. Brooks is a sweet, active and playful pup! He is 6 pounds of pure energy! This little guy has a severe heart murmur, but he has no idea as he only wants to play and have a great life! Want to adopt Brooks? Fill out our online adoption application by visiting our website: http://www.friendswithfourpaws.org/adoption-form.html

** It would be a great help to us if you can pick up your dog from transport, which is centrally located from Northern NJ and NYC, or foster home. 

**PLEASE INCLUDE YOUR PHONE NUMBER IN YOUR INQUIRY** We put a lot of time and energy into processing our adoptions to find our babies the best fit home for them. Please do not submit an inquiry if you are not serious about adopting. We are so excited to work with you to find you a new forever friend, and appreciate you working with us. For immediate consideration, please attach your application to the initial inquiry to help us expedite the process.Our adoption fee is $475. This includes their spay/neuter surgery, full (age appropriate) vaccinations, microchip insertion and registration, deworming, heartworm testing and prevention, flea and tick prevention and travel expenses. All of our dogs are rescued from local municipal shelters and the general public. Each dog is then placed in a foster home where it is kept for a minimum of 2 weeks for quarantine, to ensure if the dog gets sick it can receive proper treatment. After the 2 week quarantine time they are spayed/neutered and fully vetted. They are then placed on the website. We have foster homes in the NJ/NY area waiting to receive their fosters. Once an animal has received an application or there's an adopter interested in it, we make arrangements to pick the animal up from the airport or ground-transport to then meet with the potential adopter. Thank you in advance for your patience with our process and for making adoption YOUR option!

name: XP Jake - Northern NJ - URGENT!
description:
From his owner: Please help me find a new home for my dog Jake, an 8 year old German Shepherd/Lab mix who is great with kids and adults but no other animals. When he is happy to see you he actually smiles. Jake loves having his belly rubbed and loves to cuddle. He loves to sleep in your room close by and keep you safe.

Jake has been with his family since he was a puppy. He loves to go on walks and hang out in the backyard which needs to be fenced in. He is fully housebroken and has never ruined anything in the house. Jake is very friendly and loves people. He has no medical conditions and is not on any sort of special diet.

Jake needs a good home with no other animals. He is a great companion and friend and this is what he is looking for. Unfortunately Jake got into a scuffle with a neighbors dog and now animal control will only allow him to find a new home outside of Bergen County. We are heartbroken at having to surrender him, but we have no choice in this matter.

Jake is NOT with Eleventh Hour Rescue but we are helping his family to network him for a new home. If you would like to meet him, please contact Janet directly by email at elohrmann@dumontnj.org as soon as possible as his situation is urgent. He is located in Northern NJ.

name: Luke
description:
Luke's story is pretty incredible, we rescued him from a high kill shelter in Brooklyn, NY after he was found wounded, with scars and malnourished in a train yard. How he got there is unknown; he's pretty much the epitome of a Sarah McLaughlin commercial.  Political and sports commentator Keith Olbermann took a special interest in Luke and paid for a full medical and behavioral work up at a top notch Veterinary clinic in Manhattan, NY.  All results show Luke is pretty healthy considering everything he has been through.  He arrived to us in mid-June and despite his fear and timidness, he's coming out of his shell.  He has learned to sit, is potty trained and walks very politely on a leash. Luke is particular about his person and does prefer females, he has a hard time with males but can acclimate over time. Just know once he picks you , he is your Velcro dog for life.

Luke will need a very special and committed adopter. He had a rough beginning in life and he is still recovering, Luke has the doggy version of PTSD.  Due to this it takes him some time to warm up to new people.  Luke will need a patient person who is willing to continue to work with him to build his confidence and bond with humans.  Luke's past is unknown, it appears he has suffered trauma possibly from both the hands of humans and/or other dogs, but with love and patience he is a gem for the person who is willing to take the time to grow with Luke.  He is fearful of other dogs but could possibly adapt with the proper training and introductions.  Luke would benefit from a quiet household, with adults only; he is low energy and is most content just being with his person.  Luke is able to remain in his crate for hours in the comfort of his own home if he knows his person is nearby.  He is best suited to a home without children, loud noises or other dogs.  Luke has met one cat and appeared to have a healthy, non-predatory interest.

Luke will need slow introductions to meet new people; he does best when given space to come around on his own.  Luke will need a strong, confident leader and an experienced handler who will continue to focus on behavior training.  Luke is great on leash, a well behaved car obsessed passenger; and Luke's cuddles and kisses are extra special. He is approximately 5 years old and weighs 53 pounds.   Luke responds well to nicknames such as \"Lukey-baby, Sugar Monster and Mr. Handsome,\"  you should see his beautiful purple, gray coat! Despite a rough beginning in an unfair and cruel world, Luke has the potential to make someone an amazing pet and is a gentle soul looking for comfort and a place to call his home.

All of our puppies and dogs come up to date on vaccinations, microchipped, spayed/neutered and dewormed.

**PLEASE READ ALL BEFORE EMAILING**

If you are interested in adopting any of our dogs, the adoption fee is $495 (puppies) $375 (adults) which includes transportation from the South to NYC and we do suggest putting a 1st, 2nd and 3rd choice on your application if applying for a puppy with several litter mates.

**Please understand that we are a volunteer based organization.  While our volunteers try to answer all emails/questions as quickly as possible, below please find answers to some of our most frequently asked questions. We ask that you please read the FAQ's to see if your questions have already been answered before emailing additional questions:

-If a dog or puppy is listed on Petfinder, they are still available.  Please do not email asking if they are still available. If a dog or puppy is still listed, then we are accepting applications:-)  We do not go on a first come first serve basis, but on best fit for a family and most importantly the puppy or dog.

-We are taking our best guess on breed and size when fully grown(or already an adult), based on the puppy's/dog's physical appearance and what we might have learned about one or both parents depending on the situation. We rarely are able to tell the true or full breed mix of dogs as our information is limited most of the time.

-The way to start the process for any dog or puppy is by filling out an application,  Applications for foster or adoption can be found at www.snarrnortheast.org and by clicking either adopt or foster from the main menu.  If you fill out an application, please make sure you answer all the questions in as much detail as possible and that you receive a confirmation email, otherwise we did NOT receive it.

name: Peterson
description:
These little pudgey rolley poley puppies are just too cute for words !!! 
They have all been raised with their awesome Mama and are now ready to find a forever home. This family was dumped in a rural very high kill texas shelter and one of the puppies was very sick. We were asked to step in and said YES ! Everyone is now healthy and ready for their forever homes. 
Their adoption fee is $495 and these puppies arrive from Texas into NY on 7/11/19 and will be ready for adoption. They will be adopted out with a strict spay neuter contract. 
If they are still listed, then we are still accepting applications. 
Please fill out an adoption app at www.snarrnortheast.org

name: Pixie
description:
Hello from our sweet little Pixie!!  
We rescued Pixie in January from the NYPD 120TH  Precinct in Staten Island, NY. She was in very poor condition...starving, skin and bones, freezing and scared. She was microchipped but the owner claimed she gave her to her ex-husband and did NOT want her back even after learning she was emaciated and living on the streets!! How cruel!!
We were not able to actually take possession of Pixie until our great vet in SI did their due diligence. The Vet staff took great care of her while she had her stay and we are grateful for their assistance in keeping her safe. She otherwise would have most likely wound up in a kill shelter. 
Pixie has already gained 6 lbs but still needs some more healthy weight gain. 
This petite sweetie pie is super lovable, seems unphased by other dogs and just wants to snuggle and give kisses. 
Please consider applying to adopt or foster her by filling out the application at www.nybullycrew.org Thank you!

name: Nigel
description:
Hello it is me again Nigel the small standard poodle that was rescued along with many others from the bad breeding situation in NY. I am a small male standard at 33 lbs. and I am about 3 years young. I have always lived in very restrictive conditions and did not have a lot of interaction with humans. What does this mean, well I am fun loving, typical intelligent poodle who is curious but I have not learned too many manners yet (I am crate trained) I am also very shy when I meet a new human so this has made it hard for me to meet the right human for me. (I do love my foster humans as they are kind and patient with me) I will need an owner with Standard Poodle experience (please only apply if you are familiar with this breed) who can work with me and someone with a kind hand and patience to help to learn to trust you and who can use my energy in a positive way! I love other dogs but I am often too much for the little ones who just do not seem to want to play with me. I am not good on a leash yet, so I will need a fenced yard and you must live within a 3 hour drive of Richmond VA to be considered. If this sounds like you, Please fill out an application on the rescue's website
www.floprva.org 
Thank you for reading my story - I am so excited to find my forever home. 
Love, 
Nigel xo

name: Karmyn
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Karmyn is a sweet girl that came from a NY kill shelter. Karmyn was diagnosed with Cushings shortly after arriving at PPR and we have started treatment. She was spayed, had her dental, and had a hernia repaired. She will be having a consult on May 10th to repair her patellas, but we aren't sure what the surgeon will say since her back legs are so bowed and the Cushings disease makes healing difficult. Since starting treatment, Karmyn is now house trained and really just loves being with her people. She cannot do steps well so she is carried wherever her foster pawrents go. Karmyn is leash trained, rides perfectly in the car, and just wants to soak up all the love she can get! We really want to see Karmyn in her forever home soon and she would really fit in anywhere.

To adopt Karmyn, please complete an adoption application at PomPaws.org. The $250 adoption fee ($150 for senior citizens 65+) includes bloodwork, ACTH stim test, spay, dental, hernia repair, fecal, heartworm and Lyme test, core vaccines (Rabies, Distemper/Parvo, and bordatella), and all the love you can handle!

name: Shannon (NY)
description:
Hello, I am Shannon! I am a super sweet, loveable and CALM liver and white pointer. Iâm between 1-2 years old. Originally from Alabama, now in northern NY, I arrived in pretty rough shape, but thankfully my foster folks and the doggie doctors have helped to transform me.

Iâm really easy to live with because I love everyone â people especially, but also dogs and probably even cats. My foster folks tell me that Iâm the easiest foster theyâve ever had the pleasure of fostering. Iâm a happy girl, with a constantly wagging tail and a sweet, gentle and loyal disposition. All I need is a warm, comfortable dog bed, but I would much prefer to share your couch or your bed, if you will let me! I weigh just under 50 pounds, which is just the right size for snuggling. I definitely love cuddles and belly rubs. Being close to my beloved humans is my favorite thing. I could see myself being an excellent companion to a retiree or someone who works from home.

I am doing my best to be a polite houseguest and my folks report that I am exceptionally well behaved. The resident dogs have become fast friends. I know that the bathroom is outside and I have very tidy bathroom habits. I can be left alone in the house uncrated, although I will tolerate being crated if you insist. I walk wonderfully on leash at a heel. No pulling! I havenât made a peep since I arrived. I ride perfectly in the car. I give gentle kisses and take treats nicely. I donât go through the trash, counter surf, bark, or chew things that I should not. I am a Velcro dog and like to stick close to home, so I could adjust to apartment life or an unfenced yard easily.

You should know that I was found as a stray with a fractured pelvis and front leg, probably the result of getting hit by a car. These fractures are healed now and I get around just fine, including going up and down stairs, but overly boisterous little humans and dogs wonât be a great fit for me. I prefer a laid-back lifestyle that includes soft couches and cuddles instead of long runs or rigorous play sessions.

I am fully vaccinated, dewormed and heartworm negative. I have been spayed, microchipped, and put on monthly flea/tick and heartworm preventative.

name: Ginger Bean *URGT* NEEDS IMMED FOSTER*
description:
My name is GINGER BEAN & I'm a sweet and sassy 5 yr F Red/White Amstaff/PitbullX. I'm 50 lbs of  PURE BULLY LOVE. I was saved in the nick of time from a high kill shelter in NY. name: Yoshi
description:
This little guy is looking for a sidekick to call his very own. Your name doesn't even have to be Mario! If you're willing to be his best pal for all future adventures, Yoshi would love to receive your application!

In typical lab fashion, Yoshi is all heart and soul. Loving, comical, smart and all about relationships. He is happy to follow his people around, and is great with other dogs. Add some water, and any boring task becomes the most fun ever! A Chocolate Lab mix, Yoshi sports a gorgeous mocha coat and stunning hazel eyes. At 16 weeks old, he is working hard on house-manners 101, and promises to be an excellent student as you help him learn all a puppy needs to know to become an amazing adult.

Reason for being in rescue: Toby and his brother Caesar were pulled from a shelter in NY. This was their third time to the shelter when their owner was unable to care for them.

Special Needs? Yes, I need to go to a home with Ceasar.
Weight: 19 lbs
Height: 11 in
Spayed/Neutered: Yes

Adoption Fee: $200 for Toby and Ceasar together! We're a team!

Fence needed? No

What kind of home would be best for me? Toby is an experienced boy who needs an experienced owner. He is generally well mannered, but can be headstrong. Toby needs an owner who will show him consistency and love and teach him some basic manners.

What is my personality like? 3/29/19...update, we have a volunteer working at the farm this week and she took one look at Toby and said he is not a yorkshire terrier. He's a silky terrier. So we're changing his description and after reading the breed description, I agree with her. Toby, like most Yorkies, is full of confidence and spunk! He struts wherever he goes without a care in the world. Toby loves to play with toys but he can be a little stingy with them. He is fine with most dogs, but does not get along with other male dogs that are strong willed like him. His favorite things consist of going for walks, riding in a car, eating every treat he can and being loved on by humans! Toby is an awesome bed fellow who enjoys happily snuggling under the covers all night. He does need to learn basic commands and correcting his leash pulling. Toby can be a little temperamental and likes things on his terms. He has been known to growl and show his teeth if you try to make him do something he doesn't want to do. He needs a confident owner that will help redirect Toby and teach him appropriate manners for handling situations he may not like. With a confident owner who knows their way around dogs, he's a perfect angel. Toby and Ceasar are the perfect pair, you can have the best of both worlds!

How do I act when I first meet new people? Friendly, does not meet a stranger.

Other tips and tidbits: Estimated Birthdate: 2/2/2009. Toby is a loving boy but he's a terrier. He can be stubborn. No cats please. The pair gets along well with some cats and not with others.

House trained? Dogs can be house trained if they are in the right environment and are allowed to follow a schedule as long as a physical reason doesn't keep them from being trained. A dog house trained in my home may not be in yours. We will help you teach your new dog this necessary skill and based on your schedule.

Please note - we do not ship dogs. If you are interested in adopting, please take a look at the distance between the foster home location and your location and make sure you are willing to make that trip. Most of our dogs are at our farm in Pacolet, South Carolina.

To apply, please visit our webpage at www.carolinapoodlerescue.org and visit the tab on the left that directions you to the online application.

Please note that when screening applications, we look at the entire home and then make suggestions based on what would be a good fit for your home. You are not being screened for a specific dog although we are looking to see what type of dog interests you - poodles or non poodles, color, age, etc. Others here may be a better fit for you. It is very difficult to get to know a living animal from a picture and a short description. Since we are constantly getting in new dogs, this may be a dog not in our listings yet. We want you to be very happy with your new companion and will make suggestions based on what you tell us about you.

Thank you for considering CPR.

Basically, he is fearful most likely from being abused as a puppy, so needs a calmer environment in a home so he can feel safe. 

 
He currently lives in a home with several children and three other dogs (a lab, a golden, and a doxie mix). He does better as the dominant dog, but we have had success introducing him to other dogs in common areas. He was rescued as a puppy from Ohana animal rescue where his parents were told he was abused as a puppy.  

He walks best with a harness and he is a dog that tends to bark when seeing other dogs, but as previously stated, he is clicker trained. He enjoys the lake, hiking and playing outside. During the summer he also likes to lay outside. Please let Angie know if you have interest or any questions about Bear. He is a courtesy post for Valley Dogs Rescue.

name: April
description:
Aprilâs journey with Adopt-A-Dog began in October of 2015. She came from the Ross County Humane Society in Ohio, and as she settled in we saw how fearful April was and that she would need a lot of confidence-building in order to make her more comfortable in both a home and the outside world. Despite that, we were able to get April adopted within the month, with her family immediately beginning training with us we thought April landed in the right home. After a few months, the family contacted us and decided April was not the right fit for them. During her first couple of weeks back with us, we noticed some behavioral changes in April, including a more reserved and uneasy nature when it came to meeting strangers. Our main goal was to build her trust and confidence around people and once over that hurdle, we realized how desperately this gorgeous girl wanted to please her people. 

Coming back into our shelter was not the ideal environment for Aprilâs health, so we knew right away that we had to get her a friend. We matched her with Sora and now the best part of Aprilâs day is getting out in the yard with her best friend. This confidence boost of being around another dog led April to be placed in foster with one of our staff members. In that home, she was with three other dogs and we were able to really understand her hesitation with people. As her fosters gained her trust, April built more confidence knowing that they would not hurt her.  

For Aprilâs adoption, her new family would have to meet her several times and come to learn the excellent training she has learned here at Adopt-A-Dog. Along with her fear-based behavior, April does resource guard from other dogs and humans. Our trainer and Behavior Coordinator would equip any family with the training they need and we would follow up with training after adoption to ensure April and her new familyâs success.

 An ideal home for April would be one with owners who understand and have experience with fearful dogs and can help build a trusting and lasting relationship with her. We know that this home is out there and April cannot wait to find it!


Contact the Adoptions team at (914) 273-1674 or adoptions@adoptadog,org for more information!

The first step to adopting one of our dogs is to fill out our online adoptions questionnaire located here: http://bit.ly/2WpQHiY

name: ISABELLA
description:
ISABELLA is a 6 month old, female mini Eskie who loves to PLAY all day long.    
She does hang out with 2 other puppies at her foster home and has a blast.  She likes all dogs. We are not sure about cats. 
She and her Mom joined us from the puppy mills of Ohio.  
She is spayed, micro-chipped, vetted, crate and house trained. 
She is fostered near Cincinnati, OH


Please read the following comments below before applying to adopt one of our dogs. 
 
We do require that anyone wanting to adopt one of your dogs will have to come to Ohio.  We do not transport or fly dogs to any location.  We want to meet the new family and see the interaction between the dog and human(s). If you have a dog it is required that the dog(s) come with the family so we can see the interaction between the dogs.  
 
You will have to fill out an application to adopt one of our dogs. We require a Vet reference and home visit, that is mandatory.  
 
We will not adopt out to owners that have an invisible fence or doggie doors. It does not protect the dog from humans or other animals from harming the dog. 
 
If you do not practice proper care of your past or current dogs you will be denied.  We feel that the dog needs an annual wellness exam with the Vet. It is a state law all dogs must have a rabies shot.

name: Ariel
description:
Meet our little ARIEL!

She is 2 yrs old, 14lbs, likes to chew toys, enjoys trotting around the house, will make you wait till she decides to pee or poo in the yard, and does great with other dogs.

She is crate and potty trained.

Fostered near Indianapolis, Indiana.
We took her from a rural shelter here in Ohio. She is doing fantastic considering she lived her life outside in a wooden box.

name: Michael
description:
Meet our angel, Michael! 
(Standard male Eskie about 10 yrs old, and 40lbs) 
We took from a high kill shelter, here in Ohio. He joined us back in December in really rough shape. We are not sure, but who ever dumped him totally neglected our boy. He had tumors removed, all benign, a much needed dental ( only lost a few teeth) and a severe ear and skin infection. He has the best foster Mom and Dad that nursed him back to health. He lives with other dogs and enjoys trotting around the yard with them. One of his favorite things is hanging with man of the house. He is a gentle giant. He is house trained, fixed, and fully vetted. He is fostered near Cincinnati, OH

name: JULES
description:
JULES
Our little 2.5 yr old, black female Pom is about 4lbs. She joined us from the puppy mills of Ohio.  She sure does not act like a mill dog. She loves to play,and she just LOVES LIFE.  She is not afraid of humans. 
It is very hard to get a picture of her, she is grease lighting...ROFL  She loves to be on the go and loves her freedom.   She is so cute, when you pick her up, she wraps her front paws around your hands.  What a sweetheart. 

Due to her size of 4lbs, we will not adopt to families with small kids. 

She is a work in progress on potty training. 

It is mandatory to have a fenced yard for our girl. The yard will be check to make sure she can't escape.  She is not a dog to be left outside unattended. 

She is being fostered in Lebanon, OH

name: THOR
description:
Thor is absolutely adorable! This very mild mannered 3 year old Eskie loves to chew on toys and bones, cuddle with his people, and run in the yard! He is house trained, crate trained, learning basic commands, and very dog friendly! He is a happy little guy who loves to curl up and mellow out, preferably beside his people on the couch.

We took him from the Amish mills of Ohio. He is being fostered in Indianapolis.

He needs a fenced yard. 

Please email us at ohioeskierescue@outlook.com for an application.

name: TRISKY
description:
Our TRISKY of Ohio American Eskimo Rescue is doing great.

This 1.5 yr old, 16lb, female, tripod is up for adoption with Ohio American Eskimo Rescue.

She is a puppy mill survivor from the Amish mills of Ohio. She sadly had to have her leg amputated due to lack of medical care.

She is not a typical 1.5 yr old dog, she is learning to be a dog. So she needs a yard to run, not tied up or forced to learn a leash right now. She is working on walking and running on three legs. She is skittish, so we would prefer a family with older kids. She is a work in progress on house training, may have an accident if you are no watching her. .

No apartment life for her, or being left alone at home for 8 plus hours.

Email us at ohioeskierescue@outlook.com for an application.

name: Trevor
description:
Meet Trevor!  A 9 wk old cavalier boy puppy rescued from an Ohio Amish puppy mill.  He has been vet checked and has a clean bill of health (even his heart).  He weighs 4.4 lbs today and is growing fast.  He has a middle of the road personality, not timid, not bossy.  He is in a foster home in northern Vermont and you would need to be able to drive here to pick him up. If you can use our rescue vet in Waitsfield, VT the rescue will cover his neuter; if not you will get a $100 rebate with proof of neuter at your vet.   Trevor's adoption fee is $800.

Rowdy Yates is an 8 wk old cavalier boy puppy rescued from an Ohio Amish puppy mill.  He is very active and happy.  He has been vet checked and was found to have a grade 2 heart murmur. We're hoping he will grow out of this as sometimes happens.  He has had his first vaccine.  We call him Rowdy because he is the most active pup of the 6 we received. name: Glenda
description:
Glenda is a 6 yr old yorkie girl rescued from the life of a caged breeder at an Amish puppy mill in Ohio.  She is calm and sweet and a bit shy as she has been taken from the only life she knew.  She has had a grooming session and is microchipped.  She will be spayed and have a dental cleaning during the beginning of August and be ready to learn about life outside a cage. name: Chloe
description:
Chloe is a tiny 3 1/2 year old Maltese girl rescued from the life of a caged breeder at an Ohio puppy mill.  She has now been spayed and had a dental.  She is in a Vermont foster home and has been making nice progress, but she is still timid and will need ongoing patience and understanding as she continues to learn how great life can be outside of a cage.  She loves to snuggle with other dogs and is fine with cats.  We think she would do best in a home with another dog to help continue to build her confidence.

To apply to adopt her, go to https://cvcaninerescue.org/application
Her adoption fee is $400.  We are an all volunteer rescue and 100% of our fees go to the dogs.

name: Coco
description:
This lovely lady meatball came to us from an overflowing shelter in Ohio where she was running out of time to find a home. She is 1 year old and 55lbs, loves people and other dogs, and is very outgoing and affectionate. If you want to be greeted every day with instant wiggle-butt and do not value your personal space on the couch, Coco is your girl. She is pretty laid back most of the time save for the occasional bout of zoomies, but she is very curious and loves to explore outside so would love a fenced yard to roam, regular walks, and the occasional hiking adventure.

She loves playing with other dogs but she does tend to get jealous of other female dogs in her territory so should be the only dog in the home or placed with a compatible male. She will have to meet any resident dogs before adoption to make sure they get along. She has not been cat tested.

Coco's new family should be committed to providing the structure she has been lacking in her life and be willing to train her to be her best. With love and training, Coco will be a wonderful companion for a very lucky family.

If Coco sounds like a good match for you, please fill out the adoption application at k9orphans.org to meet her!

name: Honey
description:
My name is Honey and I'm just as sweet as my name.....and I have beautiful amber-colored eyes to match!  Iâm a boxer/pittie mix with a brindle pattern and I barely shed at all. I'm just over 1 year old and weigh about 60 lbs.  I have always looked at the bright side of life, even when I was just 10 months old, pregnant and homeless. I was still a very happy pup. I was blessed to be taken in by SOS where I was safely able to give birth to 8 beautiful and healthy puppies.  Now that theyâve all been adopted, I am hoping to find a wonderful forever home of my own.  I am great with kids (Iâve got natural mama instincts) but because of my size I'd do best with older, bigger kids. I'm young and still have a lot of puppy enthusiasm so I play too rough for little ones. I think other dogs are amazing to play with and  I'm a champion at Tug-O-War and fetch.  Iâll even bring my toys to share so that we can all have fun.  I am always up for a good snuggle.  Belly rubs and back scratches are appreciated as well.  I think cats are curious creatures. But, during the last storm, my foster mom gave me a treat every time there was thunder and it didnât bother me so much after that.  Basically, if it involves food, Iâm up for anything! I know I could be a perfect dog for your family; I bring a bit of extra sunshine wherever I go and Iâll love you unconditionally if you just give me the chance.  What do you say? My adoption fee is $150  fully vetted.

Bubba

name: Sammy
description:
Meet Sammie! He is a sweet, young boy that is full of energy. He loves going to the park, running, hiking and being outside. Sammie would spend all day playing fetch if he could. His favorite toys are volleyballs and soccer balls. Sammie has done well meeting and playing with other dogs and cats. He is crate trained and housebroken. Sammie is a smart boy and has done well learning simple commands and training. He will benefit from having a new owner that will continue to work with him and keep him active. With his energy level, he  can get rough when he plays and would not be a good match for young children. Sammie is a lovable boy and would be a great addition to an active family!

name: Buster
description:
Buster came to us from a small rural Ohio shelter as an owner surrender.   He appears to be mostly cattle dog with perhaps a little Jack Russell terrier thrown in  .  He is a little on the shorter side and weighs about 28 pounds.   
Buster has been neutered and vaccinated and is a wonderful little guy who just needs a few minutes to warm up before he goes into full play mode.   He is being fostered in Columbus, Ohio.   
If you are interested, let us know and once we get an approved application can move on to a meeting with this cutie!

name: Pebbles
description:
Pebbles is special senior mixed breed gal 8 9 years old and 25 lbs. She has a significant medical journey ahead of her. 

Pebbles came into our care from a rural Ohio shelter positive for Lyme, Ehrlichia, and Heartworm. She has been treated for Lyme and Ehrlichia and is in process of heartworm treatment.
She had her first immiticide injection already and will have the next 2 injection series in about 2&1/2 weeks. She has a slightly enlarged heart that was assessed by Medvet cardiology and requires no medication(just annual echos to monitor).

She also needs a dental, a small mass on her lower right eyelid removed, and an FHO for a right hip injury once she is confirmed heartworm negative so she can enjoy her golden years pain-free.

All of Pebbles previously mentioned veterinary requirements will be covered by Stop The Suffering over the course of her healing journey until she is medically cleared for official adoption.

Pebbles is an absolute sweetheart and loves people and LOVES the outdoors and walks.
She does get along with other dogs, but requires proper introductions and would not be a fit for a home with active and playful dogs. Other dogs would need to be laid back or senior companions. She has been good with kids, hasn't met cats.

Considering all she's been through and will be going through over the next several months, a quiet, stable home where she can rest, recuperate, and relax is ideal.


Her adoption fee is $195

Pebbles will require strict physical activity restriction while she continues heartworm treatment to prevent a pulmonary embolism; minimal exertion and on leash only activity in yard.

Are you the perfect foster-to-adopt family Pebbles is searching for? If so, you can apply for her now at www.stopthesuffering.org

Her adoption fee is $195 and includes spay/neuter, microchip, fecal/deworming, negative heartworm, vaccines and prevention up to date. Ohio residents only.

STS is a foster based, volunteer run, rescue. As such, we do not have a physical location or hours for you meet any foster dog and it does take time to answer each inquiry. All dogs are in homes and once an application is approved and a home visit is complete you are able to schedule meet and greets with available dogs.We encourage interested individuals to get approved prior to searching as it helps expedite the process. A petfinder inquiry is not a substitute for an application. For detailed information about our adoption process including fees please visit our website athttp://www.stopthesuffering.org.

name: Ethel
description:
Ethel is a stunning stunning girl. Rescued last year as what we thought was a hospice from an Ohio shelter; she was completely covered with mammary tumors from a life as a breeder dog. 
Our wonderful rescue vet did several surgeries and all tumors were removed; she also had a tummy tuck, was spayed, and is healthy, happy and patiently waiting now for her forever home.
She loves all humans....just the sweetest and most affectionate girl ever and will give you all the kisses you want. Great on car rides; great on a leash; crate and house trained and has never had an accident. Quiet and doesn't make a peep inside the home. Outdoors, she will bark and growl at neighbors dogs.
She is unpredictable around dogs so she is best suited, and we prefer, she go to an only pet home. She does ignore the lazy sleeping seniors she walks by to go on potty breaks, but does get a bit reactive around younger and the more active pups. Considering her life was a constant breed and motherhood cycle, it's probably why she reacts. 
She is the sweetest,  and most gentile couch potato and companion is that's what you're looking for. 
Ethel is located in Central Ohio. Potential adopters must be within a reasonable driving distance for initial meet and greets, and home checks.
To adopt; completed application,indoor home only, own your home, no other pets, vet and professional reference ; if approved, a meet and greet and home check will then be scheduled.

name: 1908-1683 Mac
description:
MAC - 11 years old, 80 pounds, house trained, very friendly, loves people, good with kids, cats & dogs, loves pizza, good on leash, severe allergies, lipoma (fatty tumor)

MAC had been with his previous family his whole 11 years. He had even traveled from Cleveland, Ohio to stay with them. It's almost tragic to think this boy had everything he knew torn away from him when he was surrendered to us at the Virginia Beach Animal Care and Adoption Center. You'd think a family who traveled so far with their boy would not give him up but whatever the reason, I cannot imagine it was an easy one to make. Moving on...I found Mac to be friendly and easy to handle although when I took too long to get him harnessed or give him a treat, he let me know by barking. Rude! But super cute! lol Mac's family supported my finding by telling us how wonderful he was with everyone from young children to adults to cats and even other dogs. He's an amiable boy who wants to just be at your side, outside walking and enjoying the fresh air or lying next to you at night. Mac is awesome. He is a bit older and we're told (and you can see) a decent size lipoma on his side/chest. A lipoma is basically a fatty tumor which doesn't have to be removed unless it seems to be hurting the dog. With Mac, his lipoma doesn't seem to get in the way at all. He is a good walker and had a blast in the yard! He still has lots of energy to expend but we need to be aware he may not walk as far or run as fast as some of his younger counterparts. Mac does have severe allergies so please be aware that this may mean there is an extra financial obligation to keep his allergies in check. Mac is a great boy who seems like he would be an easy fit into most homes. Please bring your resident dog in to meet him if you have one. Please bring your kids in to meet him! Let's find this senior a home so he doesn't have to live in a shelter cage. Mac is waiting in our large dog adoption kennel and his id number is 1908-1683. WE are located at 341 S Birdneck Road in Virginia Beach and are open daily except for Tuesdays. Thanks for considering adoption!

name: Merlin
description:
We pulled Merlin after being contacted by FCDS he was urgent for fear/bite issues. Merlin was an owner betrayal and as you can imagine, terrified after going from a home to the chaos of a shelter.
Although the shelter had him listed at 11-12 years old, he is estimated to be between 5-7...probably closer to 7. Because of his \"bite\" risk-and he has not bit anyone since rescued, no young children in any potential home...teens and up should be fine.
Merlin needs to be handled carefully only when he's getting his teeth looked at. It's the only time he gets nervous. He does have some age appropriate tartar. This guy is very food and treat motivated. He has two small lipomas on each side of his chest. They were aspirated and are not abnormal and merely fatty tumors. He does not like outfits and will react if you try to put a coat or sweater on him. He LOVES attention and is a great lap pup. Doesn't show well at events as he is loyal to his people which is his breed trait.
He is fully vaccinated, HW negative and neutered. He is cute as the devil, behaves like a perfect gentleman, does well with small to large dogs, listens well, house broken, obedience trained and loves car rides.
Adoption applications can be sent to you emailing us at: gratefulheartsseniordogrescue@gmail.com
Merlin has a small adoption fee.
Merlin is located in the Chillicothe Ohio area; adopters for him need to be a reasonable driving distance from us for initial meet and greets and home checks.

name: Larry
description:
Through no fault of his own, Larry's new family has had some serious setbacks and he is back in rescue.  He needs his own family! 

Sit. CHECK. Stay. Semi CHECK. I canât help that Iâm a puppy and want to play. I do like to learn though and my people think that Iâll be a great candidate for flyball or agility. Iâm definitely one smart cookie and love to learn. 

I donât remember a lot about my past. The folks at Hazeljaneâs Blessings pulled me from a shelter in Oklahoma. I am currently being fostered in New Jersey and made a trip across part of the country thanks to an awesome group of volunteers. Since being here, I have been learning how to trust again. There is definitely some setbacks for me, but Iâm very eager to overcome them with the right family standing next to me.

if you think Larry is the dog you've been looking for, go to www.hazeljane.com/adopt and fill out an application!

name: Jack (PA)
description:
Looking for a well behaved, gentle, trained companion dog that is good with young children? Meet Jack. He enjoys walks, snuggling, car rides, playing with toys, enjoys being close with his owner. 

Jack is a 10 year old, retired plantation hunting dog, approximately 55 pounds, heartworm negative on monthly preventative, and up to date on shots. He was neutered in August 2018 and microchipped. 

Originally from Oklahoma, currently living and a foster family in north western Pennsylvania, Jack has adjusted to the snow belt well. He can be tied out briefly to go potty and is not a barker. Jack knows the word no and promptly complies. 

He enjoys going on walks and sticks close to you in the yard. Jack is housebroken, crate trained, and very quiet. He is very quick to catch onto routines, follows them without any instructions, and goes right into his kennel knowing that heâs going to get a yummy treat. 

Jack should be in a cat free home. If you have another dog, the dog would just have to be chilled and very relaxed - not an Alfa type. A fenced yard would be best to keep Jack safe and give him the freedom to explore, but isnât absolutely necessary.

If you are loving, can supply joint supplements, good food, and an orthopedic bed , I will be forever yours. 

Please fill out an adoption application today!

http://www.pointerrescue.org/adopt.html

name: Goldie
description:
Goldie - Female Basset Hound/Labrador Mix (Bassadore) -- approx 40 lbs and born around Feb of 2018.

Goldie is a gentle soul. Goldie came from a rescue in Oklahoma who saved her from a shelter. Her background makes her a little sheltered from people. Her foster's families have been giving her patience and she will need some from her forever home. Being from a breeder, she's not sure how to be around people and how to interact with them. At first, she will take sometime to warm up to you. But once you share her with love under the chin and stomach, she begins to follow you and sit near you. She even starts whining to let you know she wants love!! Goldie is still learning to be on the leash, little by little she's improving but she still doesn't know how to be on it or what its purpose is. I am learning hand signals and I am exceptional at sitting for treats! Hand signals are how they communicate with me.

I can be a little apprehensive about some things, but I am learning so many new things. I'm slowly forgetting about my past. Ilove kids, other dogs and chasing butterflies! I have impeccable house manners and I will sit by the door to go out to potty.

I worked on my separation anxiety so now I politely settle down in my big crate with a chew toy.I quickly learned that everything is still okay and I am loved even when my humans leave.I don't mind being in my crate now andI love to sleep in late!

If you have a kennel with fluffy blankets,some toys to play withand love beingoutdoors then I amthe one for you! Did I mention I LOVE the water? Well, except for the water in the bathtub. It has soap in it! I talk walks through the creek with my foster family. It is so enjoyable.

name: Freddie
description:
FREDDIE IS BEING FOSTERED IN OKLAHOMA.  APPLICATIONS WILL BE ACCEPTED NATIONWIDE.

Greetings, from the great state of Oklahoma.  My name is Freddie, and Iâm originally from Pennsylvania.  I grew up on an Amish farm, but if Iâm being honest, my personality is a bit more suited to the English (thatâs all of you non-Amish folk) than to the plain life.  Letâs just say that I suffer from an excess of personality.  Ever seen Winnie-the-Pooh?  Well, Iâm Tigger!  Iâm bouncy, bouncy, pouncy, pouncy, fun, fun, fun, fun, fun!  At least, thatâs how I see myself. 

My Foster Mom says Iâm a punk, and that I need someone who will lay down the rules and make me follow them.  Câmonâ¦..look at this faceâ¦â¦can you believe someone would say that about little olâ me?  Waitâ¦.you can?  Oh, alright. I guess I COULD stand to learn a bit more self control, and Iâll even admit that I donât have the best dog-to-dog skills.  I mean, I LIKE other dogs, and enjoy playing with them, but apparently, some dogs think that Iâm just a bit much. My foster sisters have given me more than one good smack with a paw for being rude, so there might be some truth in that.

Despite my love of fun, I really do want to learn how to be a Good Boy.  My Foster Mom is laying the groundwork, but wouldnât you like to take over my leash and be my partner?  My ideal home would be one where my people will be patient with me and forgive my mistakes, but expect me to do better.  Iâll need a firm but loving hand, and consistent rules so that I donât get confused.  And of course, Iâll need plenty of play time, so that I can get my BOUNCE on!  

Folks say that Iâm strikingly handsome, but despite my good looks, Iâll be faithful and loyal, and love you with every bouncy ounce of my heart!  I just know that thereâs someone out there looking for a super fun best friend like meâ¦â¦is it YOU?????

If youâd like to meet me, or better yet, if you just KNOW that you want to be my BFF, please tell my friends at NESR!  I canât wait to meet you!

Love,
Freddie

description:
8/14/19 Ranch dog perfection! Meet \"Wrangler\" and \"Levi,\" the Denim Brothers! They are rescue dogs No. 275 & 276 that have come to us here at The HouseTop Ranch. Word is that they were born around June 10 and come from a ranch out by Burns, Oregon. The mix is supposed to be border collie, kelpie & heeler. One thing's fer sureâthey are all stock dog!

These cuties are currently enjoyin' themselves camping up in the Ochoco Mountains where they are learning about the great, big world out there. They are happily munchin' on horse an' cow turds, grasshoppers, sticks, and alfalfa pellets while explorin' further and further from camp everyday. Not much scares these lil' scampsâ not even big ol' angus cows and calves that wander by.

These boys have had their first shots, have been wormed and are chipped. They have been very-well socialized to two-leggeds and other dogs. Like all ranch-bred dogs they are smart, lively, and active. Stock dogs really do best when they have some sort of job to do EVERY DAYânot just weekends, even if its just horseback riding, supervising chores around the farm, agility sports, or real cow or sheep herding work. These pups will not do well in a small, urban yard where they get walked around the block once a day.

The adoption fee for each boy is $400 which includes a \"goody bag,\" his medical records and a free wellness exam from one of our local vet partners. In addition, there is a REFUNDABLE alter deposit which is returned after proof of neutering before the age of nine months. For more information contact Herd U Needed A Home Canine Rescue at 541-647-4080 or hunahapps@gmail.com. Fill out our application form here: http://herduneededahome.com/hunah-dog-adoption-applicationâ¦/ ~ct

PLEASE PROVIDE A PHONE NUMBER WITH YOUR INQUIRY. Note: preference will be given to working/herding situations, ranches, farms, large acreages, horseback homes, and agility/trial homes.
No apartment or condo living

There is a 200.00 REFUNDABLE spay/neuter deposit 

All stock dogs need lots of mental and physical stimulation to be happy and to stay out of trouble. A short walk around the block is not going to be sufficient. Herding breeds do best when they have a ''job'' to do which occupies most of their day. This can be herding livestock, horseback riding, hiking in the mountains or on the beach, mountain biking, playing extended games of fetch, or agility games. They are incredibly smart and love to learn tricks and solve problems. Be sure that you research this breed carefully before committing to living with a herding dog.

name: Panda ADOPTION PENDING
description:
We all know how we get that awww feeling when we see an adorable young puppy. They're so new and fresh with every possibility open to them. That's the case unless they're unwanted and at risk of homelessness on the scary New Mexico streets. 

We're so grateful for the efforts of our excellent rescuer in saving Panda...she could see that her temperament was so sweet and kind while so frightened with the turn her young life had taken. Farfel's was immediately contacted by Panda's rescuer...we were thrilled to welcome this loving and beautiful puppy into our rescue.

It turns out that Panda, at just about 9 weeks old and a tiny 3 lbs (expected to be approximately 8 lbs when full-grown) is so loving and so very sweet that it's been a fun and rewarding experience for her rescuer and foster mom.

Panda is like a blank slate...open and curious about everything around her and growing braver each day. If she continues her current regimen with her foster of socialization that promotes positive relationships with other dogs and bonding with humans...Panda will become a well-adjusted and very loving adult companion. 

Puppy Kindergarten followed by positive reinforcement/force free group obedience class will get this very smart puppy ready for a life of inclusion with her family. Through these classes, Panda will learn cause and effect in her relationships with other dogs. She will also view her people as her leaders, therefore developing a desire to please and to be partners with her family with her excellent behavior. Farfel's is happy to provide a list of approved positive reinforcement trainers in your area. 

Panda is a gorgeous and scruffy Poodle/Maltese puppy with a cottony-soft coat that speaks of her breed mix. Panda's coat will require a lifelong commitment to periodic grooming and great nutrition (a salmon oil supplement is an amazing life-long supplement for coat care and longevity). With this regimen, Panda's coat will always be super-healthy, SO soft and matt-free.

A family that loves Panda like crazy is exactly the type of folks we're searching for for this silly/fun, entertaining and very loving puppy. We also feel it's very important that she is provided with exercise and mental stimulation throughout her life. Panda will be overjoyed if her future holds walks along Colorado trails enjoying the sunshine. Socializing with other walkers and their dogs will definitely speak to the engaging nature of this super-friendly puppy.

We'd love a family for Panda that spends lots of time at home and chooses to include a fuzzy best friend in their activities. A family that is retired, works part-time or from a home office is an excellent choice for Panda.    

Panda can be taught that the car is a fun place that leads to great adventures out in the community. She can therefore accompany her family just about anywhere with the assurance that she'll be a social pup and therefore welcome everywhere a smaller and well-behaved dog is allowed .
  
Panda will be arriving in Denver unfixed due to her very young age. Once Panda is more mature, Farfel's is happy to cover all costs for her spay and microchip if one of our approved rescue vets is used.  

Panda will be arriving on transport in Denver in early October. Applications are currently being accepted for this  sweet and cuddly best friend. Apps can be found at http://farfels.com/farfels-rescue/adoption-form/. If interested, please fill out completely and submit.

**PLEASE NOTE: If you're truly interested in adopting Panda, please be sure to fill out our adoption application. It's the only initial tool that we have to determine a great match for this very deserving puppy. We're sorry, but in most cases, we're unable to get back to those that don't submit an adoption application. Thanks very much for choosing rescue.

Blu is fostered in the Tulsa area; all meet & greets at the foster home are scheduled once your application is processed. All GPRO adopted puppies under 6 mo old are required to be enrolled in a puppy level obedience class within 30 days of adoption. This is to insure this giant breed is successfully raised to be a good dog citizen, and is manageable and well-mannered when fully grown. We highly recommend all adopted dogs regardless of age attend an obedience class as it is a great way for adopters to bond with their new dog, continue building the dog's level of manners and skill set, have a local, professional resource, and also offer enrichment and socialization for the dog.

name: Jerry Lee
description:
Jerry Lee is a 7-year-old Terrier/Lab/Hound mix who weighs 47 lbs. He was one of 32 dogs rescued from another group in Pasco County. Since being rescued, he has gained 10 lbs and we have seen him slowly come out of his shell and has started to enjoy himself. He has a very special friend who takes him several times a week on walks in the park or on the beach. He even has done a sleep over with her. She describes Jerry Lee as \"loyal, smart, a lap dog and couch potato yet playful, sweet, affectionate, loves walks, gives lots of kisses and can be protective. He is still a little scared when meeting new people.\" Jerry Lee loves car rides. He loves them so much in fact, we have trouble getting him out of the cars after field trips are over. 

Jerry Lee has been neutered, microchipped and he's up-to-date with vaccines. he is nervous around kids and most likely would not do well with cats. He would need to do a meet and greet with other dogs but seems to do fine with other \"polite\" dogs. He wants to play with other dogs but is not sure how. We are continuously working on that. If you are interested in meeting Jerry Lee, well then, \"Great Balls of Fire\

name: Wednesday
description:
Our stunning Wednesday enters the room like an arctic blast of cold on a hot summer night and grabs your attention! This magnificent one and a half year old, black Labrador Retriever mix came to us from a big city Animal Control facility, where she spent some time after a lackluster owners abandoned her. She was rail thin and gaunt when she entered the city shelter system, and took some time to adjust to her harsh surroundings. 

When Wednesday came to our Rescue, she was a wild child, a Black Beauty in need of some firm, loving leadership. It was painfully obvious that her owners had missed all of her social development cues, and woefully neglected her manners and leadership training. Wednesday was as precocious as her Addams Family namesake, and seemed to feel that her opinion was warranted on just about every subject.

In no time, Wednesday has developed into a canine thoroughbred, brimming with potential. An energy and personality match is key to Wednesday's happiness. She is a high energy, athletic dog who needs alot of outdoor exercise. She would gleefully keep rigorous pace with an avid runner, hiker or powerwalker, and seems to thrive in the brisk country air. No doubt about it, Wednesday needs an active adopter, but, also one who is extremely proficient in leadership and obedience training. She is not a dog for the casual or inexperienced adopter.

Wednesday largely appears to be Labrador Retriever, but we also suspect some Border Collie in her DNA. She is a lean, tall dog weighing 47 pounds, and is extremely graceful and athletic. She runs with great speed, and could be an agility champion. Wednesday has the energy and intelligence that we see in this high strung Herding breed, as well as the mischievious and impertinent tendency that sometimes occurs when Border Collies are under exercised and bored! 

As a double dose of working dog, Wednesday definitely needs a job, and she is a natural at obedience work. She knows all her basic commands, and has passed many of the Canine Good Citizenship tests. She handles beautifully on lead, and heels nicely. Wednesday still needs some polish on her stranger manners, since she may, on occasion, greet someone rudely, but motivated adopters should be able to work her through any issues by employing her well honed commands. In the right hands, Wednesday will become a fantastic, well behaved companion.

Wednesday would fare best in an adult home, with adopters experienced in handling large, active breeds. She would overwhelm toddlers and seniors. She could easily join a multi-dog home, with another active, well trained dog, but sometimes, unruly and ill mannered dogs press her buttons. We have not had her around cats, but she would most likely chase them beyond their tolerance level.

Wednesday has respectable house manners and is mostly housetrained. She will need some finetuning on her potty routine as she transitions to a new environment. Wednesday is in good health, and has been spayed. She has been vaccinated for rabies, bordatella, and DHLPPC (distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvo, parainfluenza and coronavirus). She has had the 4dx test, and is negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. She has been microchipped and dewormed, and is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm treatment.

If you are interested in Wednesday, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738.

name: Hero
description:
Our magnificent Hero needs a hero of his own. This beautiful, robust boy is a victim of circumstances. His doting owner lost her home, and desperately tried to find housing to accommodate her beloved companion, whom she had raised from a pup. Hero's Mom took up temporary residence in a local motel, until she could get her bearings, but Hero was booted out by the motel manager. After a tearful goodbye, sad Hero was left in the care of a well-respected town shelter, who pled his case to us.

Hero appears to be a handsome mix of black Labrador Retriever and Border Collie. He has the physique and color of a black Lab, and the white tuxedo markings and black speckled white socks that suggest Border Collie. At 50 pounds, Hero has a solid, muscular build, and yet is easy to handle on lead. As a combination herder and retriever, Hero loves the outdoors, and has a hardwired work ethic that needs to be channeled through exercise and obedience work. 

Hero sometimes seems unsure of his place in the world, and needs to join a home with a strong pack leader, willing to provide the structure that he needs to to thrive. Hero gives the impression of caution at first, as he sizes up strangers, but warms quickly to a gentle touch. Adopters will need to be comfortable putting boundaries between Hero and strangers: he can become overzealous in guarding his person. He would be the ideal watchdog.

Hero seems subdued and intimidated at times, in the midst of our busy foster home, and we sense that a quiet, adult home would suit him best. He is not a big fan of change, and a steady, quiet routine will serve him beautifully.  Hero would be the ideal walking or running companion for an active single or couple. He loves the outdoors, can keep a brisk pace on a hike, and longs to make a one-to-one connection with a strong human personality. Hero could easily join a multi-dog home with another well-trained, calm dog, but cats are a definite no-go.

Hero has progressed nicely in his basic obedience training. The obedience work serves him as a job he can take pride in, and he performs the commands beautifully, either for praise or treats. Obedience training is key to providing the working breeds with the purpose and focus that they need to live happily in a domestic lifestyle.

Hero has good house manners and is house trained and crate trained. Adopters should have appropriate patience, and expect to troubleshoot the occasional accident that will inevitably occur during Hero's transition to a new home. He is in excellent health, and is at an ideal lean body weight. He has been neutered, and has been vaccinated for Rabies, DA2PP (distemper, adrenovirus, parvo and parainfluenza), and Canine Flu. He has been boostered as needed, and has had the 4dx test: negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. He has been dewormed, and microchipped. If you are interested in Hero, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738 for more info.

name: Bailey
description: Meet Bailey a 10 month old shepherd mix. She was an owner surrender that just didn't work out. She was originally adopted from a shelter in Pennsylvania that was unable to take her back. She is still young and very much a working breed. She needs something to do. She will do best in a home that has lots of time for her. She loves other dogs and children. She is very nosey when it comes to other animals. She did attend a training course but these skills will have to be implemented in the home.

name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home.

name: Murry Murdoch da Tank!
description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.

name: Lakota Mato (Bear)
description:
Lakota is a 2-year-old boy born July 2017 who came to us from a shelter where his previous owners dumped him. He was purchased as a puppy and lived most of his life outside. He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

Lakota would do best in a home with no young children. He did well when seeing other dogs on walks and we will continue to work with him and see how he does with a female companion. He is super smart and knows how to sit. He had us fooled in the beginning but he will sit now nicely when asked (a treat helps) and he will need continued positive training to be the best pup he can be.

description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature. 

If you are interested in adopting Apollo, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org
