name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

description: The Queen 17 are 16 puppies in age from 12 weeks to 20 weeks (from three litters) and one mother who were rescued from a Pennsylvania puppy mill. Some are hearing impaired and one is vision impaired but most are ok. Please submit a general application and the best match will be made for qualified applicants. The first step is to submit an application at www.findingshelter.org.

name: Lilly (PA)
description:
Hi, my name is Lil, or as my foster parents call me Lilly Lou. I grew up living in a home in North Carolina but after one of my people passed away the other got really sick and could no longer care for me. I was dropped off at a crowded shelter in the mountains of North Carolina. I wasnât really a big fan of being in the shelter and that is when Pointer Rescue Org showed up and I left with my foster parents. I had a long road trip from North Carolina to Harrisburg, Pennsylvania where Iâm now learning about lots of new things and am excited to find my new forever home. I am a very happy girl that LOVES to be around people and snuggle them on the couch. Every person I have seen I have wanted to meet. The same goes for dogs of all sizes. I enjoy soft, comfortable dog beds where I can get some sun but donât really like laying outside in the hot sun. Iâm not too sure about a lot of dog toys but I really like the soft, fuzzy ones that I can chew on. I get along with the other dog in the house but Iâm not a big fan of playing rough. Just laying around and being close to each other is ok with me. My foster parents tell me I walk well on a leash and donât pull and if I do I know to slow down to let them catch up. I know how to sit, especially if you have some yummy treats for me and will come when called. I LOVE Food and Treats and love to be in the kitchen anytime there is food being cooked. I was told Iâm not the best sous chef but Iâm probably the cutest one. I do like to check out whatâs on the kitchen counter but if you tell me Off I will sadly get off the counter. I enjoy going for walks and hiking but so far I donât like going into any water but I do enjoy a good mud bath. In my dream home I would be the only dog or have a brother or sister that is just as relaxed as me. Iâm a good sleeper and will gladly sleep all night in my kennel unless there is a thunder storm. Iâm not sure about those and if we have one I like to be under the covers in bed with my foster family. If you are looking for a relaxed, sweet southern girl, look no further!

Lil is a white English Pointer with some tan spots. She is around 6-7 years old, up to date on all of her shots (none due until July of 2020), spayed, microchipped, and tested negative for heartworms. She is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm preventative and has been strategically dewormed. She does well with ear cleanings and brushing but needs some coaxing to get a bath and would do best with a groomer or vet trimming her nails.

name: Jack (PA)
description:
Looking for a well behaved, gentle, trained companion dog that is good with young children? Meet Jack. He enjoys walks, snuggling, car rides, playing with toys, enjoys being close with his owner. 

Jack is a 10 year old, retired plantation hunting dog, approximately 55 pounds, heartworm negative on monthly preventative, and up to date on shots. He was neutered in August 2018 and microchipped. 

Originally from Oklahoma, currently living and a foster family in north western Pennsylvania, Jack has adjusted to the snow belt well. He can be tied out briefly to go potty and is not a barker. Jack knows the word no and promptly complies. 

He enjoys going on walks and sticks close to you in the yard. Jack is housebroken, crate trained, and very quiet. He is very quick to catch onto routines, follows them without any instructions, and goes right into his kennel knowing that heâs going to get a yummy treat. 

Jack should be in a cat free home. If you have another dog, the dog would just have to be chilled and very relaxed - not an Alfa type. A fenced yard would be best to keep Jack safe and give him the freedom to explore, but isnât absolutely necessary.

If you are loving, can supply joint supplements, good food, and an orthopedic bed , I will be forever yours.

name: Freddie
description:
FREDDIE IS BEING FOSTERED IN OKLAHOMA.  APPLICATIONS WILL BE ACCEPTED NATIONWIDE.

Greetings, from the great state of Oklahoma.  My name is Freddie, and Iâm originally from Pennsylvania.  I grew up on an Amish farm, but if Iâm being honest, my personality is a bit more suited to the English (thatâs all of you non-Amish folk) than to the plain life.  Letâs just say that I suffer from an excess of personality.  Ever seen Winnie-the-Pooh?  Well, Iâm Tigger!  Iâm bouncy, bouncy, pouncy, pouncy, fun, fun, fun, fun, fun!  At least, thatâs how I see myself. 

My Foster Mom says Iâm a punk, and that I need someone who will lay down the rules and make me follow them.  Câmonâ¦..look at this faceâ¦â¦can you believe someone would say that about little olâ me?  Waitâ¦.you can?  Oh, alright. I guess I COULD stand to learn a bit more self control, and Iâll even admit that I donât have the best dog-to-dog skills.  I mean, I LIKE other dogs, and enjoy playing with them, but apparently, some dogs think that Iâm just a bit much. My foster sisters have given me more than one good smack with a paw for being rude, so there might be some truth in that.

Despite my love of fun, I really do want to learn how to be a Good Boy.  My Foster Mom is laying the groundwork, but wouldnât you like to take over my leash and be my partner?  My ideal home would be one where my people will be patient with me and forgive my mistakes, but expect me to do better.  Iâll need a firm but loving hand, and consistent rules so that I donât get confused.  And of course, Iâll need plenty of play time, so that I can get my BOUNCE on!  

Folks say that Iâm strikingly handsome, but despite my good looks, Iâll be faithful and loyal, and love you with every bouncy ounce of my heart!  I just know that thereâs someone out there looking for a super fun best friend like meâ¦â¦is it YOU?????

If youâd like to meet me, or better yet, if you just KNOW that you want to be my BFF, please tell my friends at NESR!  I canât wait to meet you!

Love,
Freddie

description:
Forever Love Starts with a Wet Nose and Ends with a Tail...
Mason is a quirky guy. He is a 50 pound husky with a lapdog mentality. He will love you unconditionally and be your best friend. He loves to give kisses and is starting to do pretty well at the sit command. He plays hard and naps even harder. He does great at night, He has slept in both his bed, at the base of the bed, and up in bed with people. It just depends on his mood that night. He loves bones and jerky treats are his favorite. He likes his dinner wet, so we put some wet food on top of his dry food. He is also doing pretty good on a leash. We have been working with him and are seeing improvement. He does get excited when he sees other dogs. He will continue to be trained to be focused while walking, but overall does pretty well on a leash. He will need someone who has time to spend with him during the day or another dog to help keep him company when nobody is home since he does get very anxious being home alone. Fireworks and loud noises don't scare him however. We will send him with his crate, treats, a few toys, his harness, and his leash. His breed is known for high energy and needing a lot of exercise. He is doing great in his foster home. He loves kids and has even met and done well with cats.

name: Diego
description:
Forever Love Starts with a Wet Nose and Ends with a Tail...
HI, I'M DIEGO! DO YOU LOVE TO SNUGGLE AND PLAY? ME TOO!

It seems this sweet boy spent the beginning of his life living outdoors at the end of a chain. Oh, how Diego has blossomed in foster care! He adores people of all ages, including children, and and absolutely craves attention. He may be a little too enthusiastic for small children, so care will need to be taken in that regard. Diego hasn't gotten the memo that he's larger than your average lap dog, as he loves to get as close as possible to snuggle and offer pittie kisses.

This very smart pup will sit, shake, down and rollover on command; we're still working on 'stay' and 'come.' His leash manners could use some polishing, although a proper harness and additional training will be beneficial. Diego has excellent car manners and will often nod off in the passenger seat. Toys rock his world and this silly guy is always ready to romp and play. He'll chase a ball all day long but hasn't gotten the hang of returning it to you just yet. While Diego shares nicely with humans, he's not inclined to share toys, treats or food with other dogs and may act out in an aggressive manner. He's housebroken and crate trained in foster care and may just need a refresher course in his new home, as he gets the hang of a new routine.

Diego does not do well with dogs who make him feel challenged or threatened. He needs to be your one and only. He's also not a fan of kitties and there can be no cats in his home. If you can offer Diego the exercise, playtime and loving care he craves, he's ready to make your acquaintance. A fenced yard is would be ideal. He's had some hard knocks in life, but Diego has shaken off the dust and is ready for his happily-ever-after to begin.

name: Embry
description: Embry is a 4 year old female dog of medium size. She looks to have a couple different breeds in her. Corgi and rottie is what she looks like, but she only weighs 25 pounds, so maybe corgi and a small shepherd? She was rescued from the river bed in south Phoenix last year. She was so scared and so shy at the beginning, we don't think anyone had ever touched her kindly. She was maybe even a wild dog. She adores guys now,Â but has never been able to warm up to a woman. We think she must have been abused by a woman and it does not seem like she will ever get over that. With guys however, she will hang out with them, follow them around, and let them pick herÂ up and hold her after she earns their trust. She is a totally different dog with men. She is sweet and loving and seeks out their affection. She really needs an all male house. She is potty trained and kennel trained. At home in her own environment she is confident and does great, but she is still not interested in walks or car rides. With the right person we are hoping she will work up to that 1 day. This poor little girl seems to have been through a lot in her life and will take some understanding from her new owners. She just wants to hang out at home with her people she trusts. She enjoys being outside and feels like she has a job patrolling the yard. She gets along with other dogs and enjoys their company, but would also be fine by herself. She likes to chase cats, so no cats. She tries for the birds but her legs are too short to jump high enough to catch them. This poor girl is just looking for the right understanding guy to let her be her. If you think you might be the right match for Miss. Embry please call Jen #623-210-6578.

name: Noah
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Please contact stephodellfcr@hotmail.com for more information about this pet.Noah is an active 5 year old smooth coat male BC. He and his brothers came from Central Indiana and are being fostered in Plymouth, Indiana. If you would like additional information on Noah, contact Stephany at stephodellfcr@hotmail.com. For additional information on adopting Noah or any of the other CBBCR foster dogs, go to the CBBCR website at www.comebyebcrescue.org. Update January 18, 2016
Ty and Noah

These two handsome boys are brothers and are now about 4 1/2 years of age. It isn't required that they be adopted together but they would sure love that possibility. These boys are very sweet and affectionate boys. Ty and Noah need to be placed in a home without children.

They are initially a bit suspicious of people they don't know, Ty more so than Noah, but given a little bit of time to become familiar they are both loves. They are both good with other dogs and regularly interact with other dogs. They both love to chase along after my Border Collie when we are playing fetch.

Noah likes to stalk kitties and Ty could care less about them. They both enjoy riding in the vehicle but both are nervous when they are in an unfamiliar environment. They are both good in the house but are still crated when I am not home. Their crate behavior is much better now compared to when they were youngsters but still need the opportunity to go out for potty breaks often and shouldn't be left for more than about 4 hours at a time.

Their idea of a perfect home setting would be a quiet, country setting with a large fenced yard for them to play and have fun with their people and to have at least one stay at home parent. They would be best as home bodies and to go along places for ride alongs but are not the type of dogs that will enjoy going EVERYWHERE and being around lot of \"strangers\" on a regular basis. If they are not adopted together they would do best in a home with another dog because they do seem to feel safer when they are in the presence of other dogs.

Noah has been introduced to some agility obstacles and even though he is hesitant at first, when he is given a little time to get the obstacle figured out he seems to have fun learning how to maneuver the obstacle. These boys are looking for a patient person to provide them with a forever home. Someone who will love them for the soft, sensitive boys that they are and allow them to live in a quiet and predictable home.
*******************************************
Noah - This guy is a sweet boy that is typically very comfortable meeting new people when they come here for meet and greets. He likes toys but will shred soft, squeaky toys. He is foodie and enjoys learning. He did get to go to an agility open class once and very quickly found out how much fun it is to put his paws up on things ;) He is a very cuddly and affectionate guy. He does tend to have times in his crate where he salivates and has anxiety - but it is not all the time and seems to happen randomlynot because of one thing or another. He is good in the car, reasonable on leash. Good for bathing and nail trimming. I really like Noah and think he has the potential to be a nice companion level pooch for the right person. He gets a bit worried in new environments and is a soft, sensitive young guythat also will need a patient and understanding human. (9/24/14) *******************************************************
Oh, baby Noah.....he is sooooooooooooooooo cute and also a tennis ball junky! He loves, loves, loves tennis balls!!! He takes a bit longer than Spense and Jude to warm up to new people and a new evironment....he and his brother Ty are the most 'soft' of this litter born on September 16, 2013. He is a foodie puppy, and lots of ball drive, and once comfortable in his environment is such a fun boy. He very much enjoys playing with other dogs....was a barker at my kitties at first but now they are old news....he is very good in his crate...it is a rare day that he would have an accident in his crate....which again is awesome compared to how we started. I believe Noah will blossom into a wonderful companion level dog in the right home, that is patient and gentle and knows how to keep him safe and satisfied in his day to day adventures!! (3/28/14)

Noah likes to stalk kitties and Ty could care less about them. They both enjoy riding in the vehicle but both are nervous when they are in an unfamiliar environment. They are both good in the house but are still crated when I am not home. Their crate behavior is much better now compared to when they were youngsters but still need the opportunity to go out for potty breaks often and shouldn't be left for more than about 4 hours at a time.

Their idea of a perfect home setting would be a quiet, country setting with a large fenced yard for them to play and have fun with their people and to have at least one stay at home parent. They would be best as home bodies and to go along places for ride alongs but are not the type of dogs that will enjoy going EVERYWHERE and being around lot of \"strangers\" on a regular basis. If they are not adopted together they would do best in a home with another dog because they do seem to feel safer when they are in the presence of other dogs.

Noah has been introduced to some agility obstacles and even though he is hesitant at first, when he is given a little time to get the obstacle figured out he seems to have fun learning how to maneuver the obstacle. These boys are looking for a patient person to provide them with a forever home. Someone who will love them for the soft, sensitive boys that they are and allow them to live in a quiet and predictable home.
**************************************************************** Ty has come a long way from where he was at 5 months of age. He is now a sweet and cuddly boy that is very comfortable in his familiar environment. He is excellent with other dogs and fine with cats. He is typically a bit suspicious of unfamiliar people but if given a little space and time he warms up fairly quickly. Ty is a very soft and sensitive boy that is very effected by a change in his environment or routine. He is looking for a home with humans that are very patient and understanding and realize that he will need adequate time to become familiar with them and his new home.this will not happen in 1 week, or two weeks and likely not even 6 weeks. He is a wonderful doggie but wasn't allowed to have the best start in life and had no exposure to novel stimuli and very little interactions with humans until he was rescued by CBBCR at 5 months of age.He needs a forever home where he won't have to be crated for more than about 2-3 hours at a timeand a home that will give him plenty of opportunity to go outside for potty breaks..or someone that would have access to a doggy daycare where he could go daily while his humans are at work away from home. (12/6/14)*******
Ty is a very calm BC. One of the most, calm pups I've ever been around. He is an observer and likes to lay and watch what is going on and takes it all in. He enjoys lounging in the baby pool on hot days.he LOVES squeaky toys but will shred them. He also like to have a good chew on a hard bone while he is sunning himself in the yard. He doesn't like to chase the water hose but loves to chase other dogs while he is chasing the water hose. He is an affectionate and cuddly guy. Good for bathing and nail trimming and acts reasonable on leash. Again, a softie and is worried when out of his familiar environment. He is the biggest of his brothers but is still in the 40# range. He is a sweetie pie but is soft and will also need a very patient and understanding human in his life. When meeting new people, he is typically stand-off-ish..but is quiet. He does not bark at people he doesn't know and will warm up much more quickly than his brother. (9/24/14)********************************* Ty is the biggest pup of the litter and is just as sweet as he is big! description: Gia is a big girl with an even bigger heart. This Anatolian Shepherd was rescued from Tennessee, but is looking to find her perfect match right here at your Port Washington, N.Y. campus. name: Mario
description:
Hi! My Name is Mario. I came to my foster home in Central Ohio all the way from a shelter in Portage County. The shelter thought I would be better suited to be with Speak because they specialize in special need animal rescue. Oh yea, did I mention? I am deaf. But don't worry, that just makes me special, not different because I get to learn sign language. Right now, I know sit and come. I am eager to find my new family who will teach me more signs.

I like to run around too and play with other girl dogs. I am okay with boy dogs if girls aren't around. I am a gentleman and I like tend to be protective of girl dogs. My foster mom says I am what some people might call a \"velcro\" dog. I love to follow my foster mom from room to room and be by her at all times. I mean really, who doesn't like to hang out on the couch with their foster momma and watch TV?

I forgot to mention, I am great with kids too! I am okay with cats...I do like to sneak and get their food though. But I have to say I am super sweet boy and probably the most loyal dog on earth. I also give the best hugs. Hopefully we will have a chance to hang out sometime and I will give you one.

name: FOSTER HOMES NEEDED
description:
PLEASE NOTE - THE PUPPIES/DOGS IN THESE PHOTOS ARE NOT ADOPTABLE; THEY ARE MEANT TO SHOW THE VARIETY OF RESCUE PUPS IN OUR ORGANIZATION

Helping Paws Me is searching for quality foster homes in the greater PORTLAND, MAINE area.  Our foster families need to be within 1-hour driving distance of our Vet in case the foster puppy needs to be seen while in foster care.  We are unable to approve foster homes more than 1-hour from Portland at this time, but encourage you to reach out to your local animal shelter to inquire about foster opportunities.

We work with rescue groups in the Magee, Mississippi area to rescue unwanted shelter puppies & dogs and find them loving homes in New England.  Since we do not have a physical shelter, our network of foster families commit to taking a rescue puppy or dog into their home and give him or her love, care and attention.  The average foster period is a week, but can be longer.

Why foster?

Fostering a dog is one of the most rewarding experiences you can have.  By taking a dog in need temporarily into your home you are:
â¢freeing up a spot so our rescue group can take in another dog.
â¢giving your foster dog the time he needs to be ready for adoption.
â¢helping our rescue group learn more about the dog so he can end up in the best home possible.
â¢socializing the dog to a home environment and possibly getting him used to being around other pets and different types of people.

If you are interested in learning more about fostering, please e-mail our volunteers at helpingpawsme@gmail.com.  We do require all potential foster homes to complete our foster application which can be found at: helpingpawsme.org

name: Theon
description:
Name: Theon
Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 5 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

description:

Approximate Weight: 115 lbs

Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: good but cannot go to a home with children under 12 years
Currently Living at: DC area foster home

Meet majestic Gulliver! Surrendered at a SC shelter for not getting along with the resident dogs, Gulliver quickly proved that he is indeed good with most dogs... sometimes dogs just need a proper introduction. Although Gulliver passed his cat test, he is VERY interested in cats & may want to play with them. Obviously most cats wouldn't enjoy this so he may do better in a house with no cats. He does well with other dogs but he MUST have a PROPER introduction. He can only be adopted by an experienced (large breed) adopter who is willing to hire a trainer. Gulliver was not given any training in his first home so he needs a lot of work on his manners. If he were to go to a home with another dog, there should be 2 adults in the home. It is just too much for one person to handle Gulliver + another dog.

In addition to the above, we're looking for an adopter who doesn't have young children (under 12) & has a fenced (6') in yard. Please make sure you fit all of the above criteria before applying.

Gulliver is still somewhat of a puppy, but he is very treat motivated and smart, so training him should be a breeze. He already knows numerous commands after just a few days in a foster home.

Gulliver is a tad bit underweight if you can believe it, and we need to note that he is a bit of a resource guarder with food. Given his size, he needs an experienced adopter who will agree to work with a DC PAWS approved positive reinforcement trainer to address that issue and to generally teach him how to be a gentleman.

This pup is a rare rescue find (well, perhaps not THAT rare), and his previous guardian's loss can be your gain.

Please note that we anticipate A LOT of interest in this guy and we may not be able to respond to each application right away; we are an all-volunteer rescue of individuals with full time jobs and do our best to be responsive, but sometimes it can be overwhelming with popular breeds like this one. Our goal is to find a home and family that are the best fit for Gulliver, and vice versa. As such, applications will not necessarily be considered on a first come, first served basis. That being said, we anticipate a good match will be found quickly, but we always encourage applications since you never know when applications may fall through. 

Like most shelter dogs, Gulliver may need a refresher on housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Finding out the morning of the surgery, that she also has a luxating patella, grade 4, which (according to that particular vet) will also need repair after the hip is healed. The rescue had two more opinions, after her FHO surgery, and both of those vets (who we have previously worked with and trust more than the one(s) who did the surgery) agreed that taking off the knee cap and reattaching (because of the previous neglect) could make her unable to use her leg at all and make it worse. Therefore, we are opting to let her be the dog as she is very happy now. name: Yeti COURTESY LISTING!
description:
The following dog is not, nor has he ever been, part of our rescue.
We are listing him to help with his rehoming as a courtesy to his current owners.

If you are interested in finding out more about him, please contact the person listed at the end of the following set of notes (provided by his owner, Kenny):

His name is Yeti and his information is below:

1. He is 5 and his birthday is in November. He weighs about 65lbs.
2. He is Neutered. When I brought him back from South Korea, the Korean government required him to be neutered in Order to export him.
3. He is up to date on vaccinations as of May of this year.
4. He is not treated monthly for anything, as none of those are currently in my area and there are no signs of anything.
5. No known issues. Last Vet check was beginning of 2018 when I moved from Vegas to northern Reno.
6. He behaves normally around all. He doesnât like to be âtrapped/blockedâ in. I currently have him around my 2 other dogs whom my ex wife is taking. He is also around other animals from my ex wifeâs mom.
7. Normal routine consists of pretty much outside all day. I live on 40 acres and he runs around it all. He exercises outside all day with the other dogs. He only eats once a day, and it is currently at night around 2000 hours.
8. He is both an inside and outside dog. Does great with both.
9. He knows sit, down, come. He pulls slightly on a leash, but nothing over the top. When he sees other dogs, he is just curious. Wants to smell and normal stuff dogs do.
10. He likes to be pet and loved. The only sensitive part is his tail. When we found him in Korea, he had a rubber band around his tail. The doctors had to cut it to make it healthy. That is the only part about him that is sensitive. You can see it in the photos.
11. He rides in cars fine. Back of trucks too. He hates the vet. Doesnât like to get shots, but it is possible. Can be lifted. Just marks his territory a lot.
12. He has not bitten anybody or any other animals that I am aware of. I just came back from overseas after a year, and my ex wife didnât say anything.
13. No separation anxiety or behavioral issues that I know of. He is kennel trained and dog door trained.
14. I adopted Yeti while I was stationed in Korea. I rescued him from a meat market. He has had all American veterinary care in Korea and well as in the states. Up to date on all shots. The reason Iâm rehoming him is because I got divorced right before my deployment and now that I am back, with the divorce and child support, I can no longer keep a place that can an animal can accompany me. I have to downsize my current lifestyle and living expenses in order to keep my head above water. I have had Yeti since 2014 when he turned 1.
15. I have not contacted any other rescues as of this moment.
16. Best method of contact is 702.823.9275 or kenny032004@gmail.com
17. Address: Reno NV, 89510.

name: Logan (Courtesy Listing)
description:
Logan is very playful and has a outgoing personality. He enjoys being rubbed and likes to have a window to look out of. Heâs very submissive and enjoys doing whatâs asked of him especially when thereâs a treat. Logan has an auto immune disease called VKH syndrome ( https://www.marvistavet.com/vkh-syndrome.pml ) which affects the pigment of his skin and without immediate treatment can have a long term effect on the eyes and possible blindness. In terms of medical treatment,  He is currently on a steroid (prednisone) which helps suppress his immune system to stop it from attacking itself. Also on eye medication (prednisone, timolol, and dorzolamide). Pricewise the medications themselves are not costly. As of now, I havenât spent more than $70 dollars for his medications. The more costly things Iâve noticed was the actual exam fee. He has dog insurance which covers 90% of his medical expenses excluding the exam fee. Logan knows the sit, stay, lay commands. I'll ask him if he wants water or does he have to use the bathroom and heâll respond with a whine if he does. Same for food. The type of home I think that would be best suited for him is one where he can both be active and have some time to relax and receive a lot of love and just remain social, whether itâs with kids, other dogs, etc. He is house broken so he doesnât need to be crated.  

This Akita is located in Rochester, NY. If you're interested in him, please go to our website and fill out a online adoption application and we will get back to you shortly.

name: Romeo - Sponsored Adoption!
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.

GPMR does not have a shelter. All of our dogs are kept in loving foster homes. We must have a completed adoption
application on file before meeting any of our mastiffs.

GPMR adopts to the states of Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, Arkansas, Missouri, Louisiana and parts of Colorado.
!!!Any mastiffs being adopted out of the state of Oklahoma require a health certificate to be paid for by the adopter!!!

*** Romeo's adoption fee has been sponsored by Danielle and Andrea in honor of their friend Toni Howley! ****Romeo, Romeo...what a super sweet boy!! He is an absolute love bug. Romeo came through the rescue back in 2012 when he was about 8 months old. Unfortunately Romeo's family fell on hard times and then went through a divorce, which is when Romeo was returned. They sadly neglected his vet care and Romeo tested positive for heartworms. We've currently got him on medications for treatment.We thought back in 2012 that Romeo he may be a Mastiff mix. He is currently between 7 and 8 years old and is a healthy weight at 75 lbs, so possibly a Mastiff/Boxer but he for sure has the calm Mastiff personality. He is great with older kids 5 and up. Romeo, like his namesake, is a sweet boy with a lot of love to give! Romeo has shown to be selective about the dogs he likes, so we are searching for a home where he can be the only dog in the house. He would not be a good candidate for dog parks or other areas where dogs mingle off-leash. We don't recommend him for families with cats.Romeo's previous owner report he likes to try and escape from the house and yard, so he needs a home with a 5 or 6 foot fence, preferably stockade/privacy fencing.Romeo's adoption fee was donated by two of our supporters! He is being fostered in Edmond, OK.
Orginal Bio from 2012:Meet Romeo! He was rescued from a TX shelter. We are guessing his age around 8 months old. We think he is a Mastiff/Bullmastiff mix as he seems to have traits of both breeds. Romeo is good with other dogs and would be fine with older kids but he's too much of an active puppy for small children. Right after Romeo came into rescue, he got kennel cough so he's been staying at the vet's office, but he is back to good health and is ready to go into foster care. If you think you have room for this sweet pup in your home, please submit an adoption application for him today!Save a Mastiff...Adopt, Foster, Volunteer!

description:

Maybe you can give her that new start?

Come and meet her today!

Please stop by to see our adoptable dogs between 1pm-5pm Tuesday-Friday and 12pm-3pm on Saturdays. You are also welcome to contact us via email at emanimalhosp@aol.com. We hope to see you soon! 
 These are rescue dogs, and we do not have any further information regarding behavior, training or past experiences. 
 For the safety of the dogs, we need to verify residency for all adopters. Renters, please bring a copy of the lease showing that you are allowed to own a dog. Homeowners, please bring a copy of a mortgage statement proving you own your own home. We also require a copy of a utility bill with your name and address for all adopters. We encourage you to meet the pet you are applying for before submitting the application. Your application will not be approved until after you meet the pet. description:
\"Snoopy\" is a 70-lb, 1-yo neutered male GSD mix who is happy, loveable and a little goofy. Snoopy is friendly with everyone he meets but will likely be a good watchdog as well. I KNOW that Snoopy will be great with young children; he met two kids (ages 8 & 10) and was literally melting in their arms. Snoopy is very affectionate and loves to snuggle right next to you in bed.

Snoopy gets along fine with other dogs, but he does have a prey drive and doesn't seem to know what a little dog is; therefore, I am seeking a home with no small dogs. (I'm confident that once he realized that little dogs are indeed dogs, he'd be fine with them.) Snoopy prefers to receive attention from humans much more so than from other dogs, so he'd be fine as an only dog.

I have not seen Snoopy around cats, but since he went after a Chihuahua mix, I can't consider a home with cats for him.

Snoopy is housetrained and never had an accident in the house he's in, but he does occasionally get his paws up on the counter if there is food present. He responds well to the \"sit\" and \"lie down\" commands, so apparently he's received some obedience training in his young life. 

Snoopy walks very well on leash and rides calmly in a vehicle. He apparently enjoys water, as he took to the pond at GSRSV's rescue ranch fairly quickly.

Snoopy gets his name from his long snout and the somewhat comical overbite in his muzzle. I'm not sure if his overbite originates from another canine breed (Collie?) but it does not affect his ability to eat normally. 

GSRSV rescued Snoopy from the Stanislaus County Shelter on 6-23-18. He had been at the shelter since May 12; I imagine that he was a staff favorite at the shelter. Nonetheless, his time had run out and he was going to be euthanized so GSRSV appealed for donations to board Snoopy until he could be transferred to a no-kill shelter out of state. Three women came forward with donations to cover his boarding expense. (Thank you Danielle Blount, Diana Cheung and Alicia Navarro!) When I discovered what a sweet dog Snoopy is, I searched for and was able to find a foster home for him so that he wouldn't have to go back to a shelter. 

Snoopy is located in Sacramento. His adoption fee is $210.

name: Stella
description:
Stella.Aprox. 1 year old. 55lbs. Black Mouth Cur Mix

The story of Stella:

Stella came to us when we got an urgent plea from a good Samaritan to take a dog belonging to an estranged relative. This poor pup was being kept in a back room, chained to an old broken mattress, with no food or water for an unknown period of time. Being a large, energetic puppy, she was often difficult to handle, but rather than trying to train her, Stella had been beaten when she made mistakes. She was one of the saddest and most depressing examples of neglect we had ever seen.

Saving Stella:

The most urgent issue for Stella was giving her the nutrition her body desperately needed. Although it would be tempting to give a starving dog as much food as they can eat, it was important to strictly regulated and measured her food to avoid further health complications.

Sadly, when Stella started to feel stronger and more energetic, it was clear that she had suffered more than we knew. By locking her away, her family had robbed her of many crucial life experiences and exposure milestones that every dog needs to become a confident and happy adult. Although she was safe, Stella was still a tiny, confused and scared puppy in a big powerful body. Stella did not understand that she was not meant to walk across the dinner table, she did not believe that no one was going to use her leash to beat her, she could not trust that it was ok to move away from situations that overwhelmed her. Realizing that Stella needed expert help, we were lucky enough to get her a temporary place in a boarding and training facility where Stella has made amazing progress. She is learning how to enjoy being outside, walk on a leash, be around other dogs, basic commands and impulse control. We are now searching for the perfect foster home for Stella to learn how to live in a home.

Stella in training:

Stella's trainer says, \"While we still see the occasional unwanted behavior, it's more playful and quickly squashed. She is doing well - really has the cue down for fetch and tug, and knows Mine' for not grabbing toys when I pick them up. She wears a head collar pretty well, though still with the occasional tantrum. Doing great with dog play, and chooses avoidance when she can, which is a great trait to have.\

Apply to adopt McEnroe Lonestar at WWW.EHRDOGS.ORG!

name: Lilly "LuLu" Lonestar
description:
HI! I'm Lilly, I just made a very long trip from a shelter in San Antonio with my sisters Karolina, and Venus (who already found her forever home). Now I live with my foster family and I am learning my way as a family dog. I would do best in a home with another dog who can show me the ropes. When I'm not playing with my doggie friends I enjoy rolling around in the grass, getting the zoomies, playing with stuffed animals and laying on a nice warm bed/couch. I have lived with little people too, though it can take me awhile to adjust. I've never had a home of my own so I can be shy, but once I get to know you, I'm a sweet girl who will be your best friend.

Is my new home your home?

Apply to adopt LILLY DAVIS LONESTAR at www.EHRDOGS.org!

name: Ramps
description: from owner who surrendered him: Rampage we found while visiting my sister in San Antonio. We went to a San Antonio Rampage hockey game, and there he was, under our car at the SBC Center when we went to leave. We just had to take him home. He was very skinny and hungry and very scared. We brought him home October 26, 2013. He looks like a lab, but is not quite as big as most of the labs I have had. and his is brown with a white patch on his tummy. But my guess would be he has some lab in him. When we took him to the vet the following week, he estimated he was probably around 4 months old. So we approximate his birthday July-ish of 2013. Rampage still shows some signs of being abandoned or hurt by whomever left him in the SBC center parking lot. It took him a while to get used to people, and he scarfs down every drop of food when it hits the bowl. After being with us for almost 4 years, he has become very loving and comfortable. He is still scared of new people. He does not show aggression toward them at all, he just runs away and hides. However, he does show affection toward frequent visitors, such as our parents, siblings, and nieces & nephews. So we are confident he will become comfortable is his new home quickly. He does still eat all his food immediately, so we do not free feed him. He eats once a day and eats every drop immediately.  He is great with other dogs- submissive

name: Jedi
description:
Jedi is a very sweet, very shy, little boy we rescued from the euthanasia list from ACS San Antonio. He had little chance because of his fear in the shelter setting. HE wasn't our typical senior or hospice rescue but because he had zero interest, and was at serious risk, we just couldn't see this little guy not have another chance of a good life.
He is a small mix, probably beagle/pug or something along those lines. Perfect lap dog. His age is estimated between 5 and 6. He is very healthy, fully vetted, heart worm negative, and the perfect house pet. Ideal home for him is a calm, quiet older single or couple owners. He is very shy until he gets to know you. Zero aggression. Does fine with other low key dogs. 
Jedi is located in San Antonio Texas with the only foster and home he's known for the last couple years. He can be transported anywhere in the US, for an approved adopter, at cost to the adopter. Ideally we can find his forever home in San Antonio or a nearby location.
This one would be absolutely perfect for a mature person or couple looking for devoted love.
Interested applicants can email us about him.

name: L. Bonnie
description:
L Bonnie is a mature lady that ended up in rescue. She is 8 years old and has unfortunately lost her family. She does great on a leash, loves to go for rides, loves everyone she meets and is a perfectly house mannered girl. Bonnie has been going to work with me since rescue and we all forget she is there - she just snoozes and hangs out. She has done well with the dogs in rescue she has met. She doesn't always care for smaller dogs so no small dogs please. Because she is a little older I would suggest no small children - she is past babysitting age. She has met a horse, steer and goats with no interest. I do not know about cats. Bonnie really needs a home of her own to finish out her retirement years. Please apply at www.krrtx.org/forms. 

Please note all dogs are located in San Antonio, TX. We advertise out of state due to the critical pet overpopulation problem here in the south. We use Rescue Road Trips to transport the dogs to your area. They are all up to date and come with a health certificate. The fee is $170 adoption and $185 transportation = $355. Thank you for considering adopting a southern dog.

name: Adiva
description:
Adiva is a very special young lady . She clearly earns her name . 

She was saved from San Antonio's highest kill shelter . Adiva is a hound/shepherd mix of 3 years old. 

She is good with large dogs . With small dogs she can give attitude . She is not a fan of cats. 

She lives with a GErman shepherd and 2 kids . Please keep in mind that we do not adopt our adults out when children under the age of 10 are involved . 

Her best friend is a husky from a neighbor . 

This pretty sassy lady lives with her foster family in Huntington NY . 

We would like to see her going to her forever home where she will be adored 

To become Adiva  her new family please apply by filling in the adoption application to find on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com or email us and we will send you one

name: Antero
description:
Antero was saved from San Antonio's highest kill shelter . They told us that he is 3.5 years what could not be correct . He was a puppy and is now double the size since we pulled him . So we guess he is max 2 years old .

Antero was clearly abused and fears people . In his kennel he will bark everybody away but then tries to hide in his doghouse .

If you approach him slow and and with sweet words he will come to you . He just doesn't trust people after what happened to him .

This sweet teddybear is looking for a forever home . Where he will be loved , where they will have patience and where he can find peace on his mind .

Trust us , we have seen already miracles happen right after adoption.

Antero is dog friendly but not good with cats .

He is located in Middle Island NY .

(Please , only serious adopters)

To become his new family please apply today by filling in the adoption application to find on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com or email us and we send you one

name: Adiva
description:
Adiva is a very sweet shepherd /hound mix of 2.5 year old .

This baby was saved from San Antonio's high kill shelter as a puppy . Many people applied for her but nobody showed up .

Adiva stayed all by herself behind on our kennels until we could find a wonderful foster family .

Still she wants nothing more then a family of her own. Who will love and spoil her .

Even when Adiva is like a medium size dog , don't underestimate her .

This girl can keep up with the best runners .

Adiva is a great dog and it becomes time that we will find that perfect match for her .

She lives together with Amros who is a large shepherd but has a little bit of a Napoleon complex. She is the boss :)

Adiva does not like cats .

She is located in Huntington NY

To become her new family please apply today by filling in the adoption application on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com or email us and we send you one

name: Abdul
description:
Abdul is a 3 year old Rothweiller who was saved from San Antonio's highest kill shelter . 

Abdul came in with his brother and sister after a forced owner surrender by law . 

It was a severe cruelty case . Skin over bones and completely starved . 

The sister was adopted in the shelter and we took the both brothers . His brother is adopted but sweet Abdul is still waiting a rottie lover who knows the breed . 

Abdul is very sweet but he does not like other dogs or cats . He leans right away against your leg and shows his tummy . Yes he loves his belly rubs . 

This sweetheart is looking for a forever home where they will love him forever . 

Abdul is located in Huntington , Long island NY 

To become his new family please apply the adoption application to find on www.a-teameliterescue dogs or send us an email and ask one

name: Astro
description:
Astro is an adorable shepherd mix of almost 2 years old. This sweety was just in time saved from San Antonio's highest kill shelter .

Astro was terrified and did not understand that he was saved . It took him a while to trust people but he bloomed open with his wonderful foster mommies Shea and Amanda who foster also Asvina for us .

Astro is a little bit shy but will wag his tail when he understands that you are a good person.

Astro is good with dogs and cats . When you meet him he will stand a little bit frozen . You have to give him a little bit time to adjust to his new environment and he will act like the sweetest puppy .

Astro is ready to have a family of his own where they spoil him for the little prince he is .

He is located in Huntington NY

To become his new family please apply today. You can find the adoption application on our website www.a-teameliterescuedogs.com

description:

description:

She also loves burrowing under blankets, and is constantly showing off her goofy personality. Her foster mom can't stop raving about this sweet, funny girl. Roxy walks well on leash, and is curious about other dogs she meets. She does well in her crate, is super smart and a very quick learner. She will be the perfect companion to join someone on their daily activities!

Seattle Foster Updates:

name: Jason
description:
Animal Profile: Jason is an estimated 1-year-old, 62 lb \"Hound\" mix, who was rescued from a kill shelter in San Bernardino. Our volunteer says he has a great temperament, is happy go lucky and in good body condition. More information to come as he settles in!

Foster Update

We have taken Jason on fairly long walks and we are always tired before he is! He likes to go fast and it is better if you jog with him. He is interested in everything and pulls to investigate, but seems to be getting better each day. I think he is pretty smart, and he's friendly and playful! He will do well with a family that wants to continue training him as he loves to be challenged.

name: Snickers
description:
Snickers is a 6 year-old Chihuahua cross who is gorgeous.  He is a black and tan pooch with a good coat and body structure.  He was transferred from a local shelter where he was surrendered by his owner due to circumstances unrelated to Snickers.  

Snickers is shy yet friendly.  He likes being held after he's sniffed around and gotten to know you.  He would make a great pet for those who love Chihuahuas or small dogs.   We're not sure how he is with cats or children. 

Our kennels have quite a few visitors/volunteers, and most of our dogs have adjusted to all sorts of people who like to walk them and pet them.  Snickers, no doubt, will adjust to his new surroundings and fall in love with the perfect person. Won't it be YOU?

If you are interested in SNICKERS or any of our other canines, call our office at (831) 634-1191.  We are located in Hollister CA, about 100 miles south of San Francisco.  Sorry, we do not ship our animals.  

See all our animals on our website http://www.petfriends.org.

name: Bianca
description:
Bianca is a beautiful Shepherd mix who is about 14 months old. She is good shape but needs some basic training.  Bianca lacks the human touch that she will get here at Pet Friends before she gets adopted. 

If you are interested in BIANCA or any of our other canines, call our office at (831) 634-1191.  We are located in Hollister, CA, about 100 miles south of San Francisco.  Sorry, we do not ship our animals.  

See all our animals on our website http://www.petfriends.org.

name: Dagwood
description:
Dagwood is a senior (10 years old) Chihuahua who came with his litter mate/sister (Blondie) from a home that had an abundance of dogs.  The owner passed away and the dogs were transferred to a local animal shelter. They are very delightful and sweet.  

If you are interested in Dagwood or any of our other canines, call our office at (831) 634-1191.  We are located in Hollister CA, about 100 miles south of San Francisco.  Sorry, we do not ship our animals.  

See all our animals on our website http://www.petfriends.org.

name: Walton
description: Meet Walton aka Wally! Walton was rescued from the San Jose shelter. He has birth defect on his left back leg, it is shorter than his right leg. This doesn't stop him from getting around! Wally loves to play and he is dog friendly. He is house broken and will make a great companion for someone. His adoption fee is 200.00 and includes neuter, microchip, month of free pet insurance and being up to date on shots up to adoption. If you are interested in Wally please fill out an adoption application and put Walton as the header.

name: Hawkeye
description:
A Big softie in a rough exterior, Hawkeye is a real gem.  Hawkeye came from a severe hoarding case in San Miguel County, but right from the start he wanted to follow and be with people. He is a bit of a goofball, acting silly and playful quite often.  He has shown great manners with dogs and enjoys playing with polite dogs.  Hawkeye is still polishing his house manners.  He has likely had to be resourceful, so he tends to pick up items and carry them around, and is learning what a crate means. He is showing he is a quick study with house training.  Hawkeye really wants to belong to a pack and would like a home where someone is around more often than not.  Hawkeye is about 6 years old and we guess he is mixed breed of Rottweiler, Shar Pei, and other breeds.  He will fill out with good nutrition at about 90 pounds.  

Come meet this big dog with the big heart at adoption events.  Or inquire at julie@hart2heartcanine.com or call 703-254-6582

name: Janet
description:
Janet is as sweet as can be.  She is eager to follow and please.  She needs some confidence but will quickly progress into a nice outgoing, friendly dog.  Janet looks like a Doberman/Rottweiler mix of about 65 pounds.  She is slim and tall in build.  Janet was part of a hoarding case from San Miguel County (NM) and has been waiting a long time in the shelter for the case to be resolved so she can find her home.  She enjoys the company of other dogs and would do well with an outgoing friendly dog.  Janet is about 3-4 years old.  

Please inquire about Janet by emailing Julie at julie@hart2heartcanine.com

name: Blue Moon
description:
Blue Moon is a female, blue Miniature Pinscher/Chihuahua mix, Blue's estimated date of birth is June, 2016. She was rescued from the Sand Springs shelter as an unclaimed stray. Blue Moon has the prettiest blue coloring and intriguing personality to match her unique coat! She starts out a timid gal but warms up quickly because all she really wants is snuggles and attention! Blue will be a good lap friend. She did not get along with the other dog in her previous home, so she may be better as an only dog. She has been okay with cats. Due to her timid nature, she needs to go to a home with older kids only. You can meet Blue Moon at Bent Arrow Veterinary Hospital. Call 918-459-9100 for an appointment. She has a $150.00 adoption fee plus the cost of 6 months of heartworm prevention.  

Note: ARF reserves the right to deny any application that is deemed unsuitable for the animal. Please be aware that our animal adoptions are NOT on a first come- first serve basis. Our sole purpose is to find the best possible home for the animals that fall under our care. We do not ship our animals. All adopters are expected to come to Tulsa if approved

For details on how to adopt please visit http://www.arftulsa.org/adopt

name: Delina
description:
Delina is a female, 18.1 lb, red Dachshund mix. Delina's estimated date of birth is April 2014. She was rescued from the Sapulpa shelter as an unclaimed stray. She is a little shy at first, but is a super sweet girl with a lot of love to give! She would love to share a home with another dog for some four-legged companionship. You can meet Delina atMuddy Paws. Call 918-749-5255 for an appointment. Delina has a $150.00 adoption fee plus the cost of 6 months of heartworm prevention.

name: Violet
description: Violet is a bundle of sweet loving and playfulness. She came to us with a broken front leg, that has since been treated, and it never slowed her down, or altered her personality a bit. She is great with children, other dogs, will chase cats (only with the back up of her litter mates, otherwise they scare her).  She is about 9 months old, spayed, vaccinated, on HW prevention, and flea/tick free. She is located in Sapulpa and ready to find her forever home.

name: Max
description: Max is such a handsome fella!! He is about 9 months old, super chill, and such a pleaser. He is desperate to find his forever home. He's been neutered, vaccinated, on HW prevention, flea/tick free, and is microchipped. Max is located in Sapulpa. Adoption fee is $125.

name: Mia
description: Mia is a hound mix of some kind. She is about a year old. Mia loves attention and spending time outside with her fur brothers and sisters. She gets along well with other dogs. She is good with children. Mia has been spayed, vaccinated, on HW prevention, and is flea/tick free. She is also microchipped. Mitzi has been with the rescue since she was about 10 weeks old and would really love a family to call her own. She is located in Sapulpa. Her adoption fee is $125.

name: Rose
description:
Rose is a puller on the leash. Handler needs to learn how to control her while walking, and she would benefit from some leash training. She gets down and pulls hard.
She's bonded with her foster mom fast! But with her previous foster (also a woman), Rose exhibited jealousy. She's an 8.5 on the alpha scale. The lower dogs stay away from her but her foster mom's alpha, Sarge, likes her.
Rose is so smart and crate trained. She was rescued with two other dogs, Phantom and Muzzy. Rose and Phantom have to be separated at all times, even when being crated. Rose has figured out how to escape her collapsible wire kennel. Her foster uses plastic hay-baling twine to secure the front and rear panels. 
All 3 recovered nicely from their immiticide treatment, are taking a long course of twice-daily Doxycycline, and have had their first monthly treatment of Interceptor Plus Blue.
Rose is a 45 lbs American Staffordshire mix, and we believe she's 2-3 years old. She is currently in Texas, but transport can be arranged to an approved adopter!

If you're interested in adopting Rose, please fill out an adoption application on our website: www.safetails.org
If you have any questions on Rose, please feel free to message us via our rescue's Facebook page!

name: Theon
description:
Name: Theon
Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 5 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

description:
Name: Tyrion
Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 4 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Tyrion is the runt of the litter (ha ha)! This boy is by far the calmest and the quietest of the litter, but that can change when dynamics change and he is in a home of his own. He is a little more tentative about meeting humans, but he is warming up more and more.

He is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Tyrion will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Tyrion will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Tyrion, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization.

description:

I get along with other dogs but I get grumpy about my space and prefer to sleep solo. My hobbies include eating and napping on very plush bedding. I am maybe 5lb but I sure do enjoy my canned dinners and my foster mama even warms them up for me because my precious eyes convince her I require that. These hoomans that cater to me make me get up and walk around. I'll do best with a home with older kids that understand to give me space. I haven't been cat tested but by my chill level I don't see it even phasing me. 
And I think Iâm about 7 years old, but Iâm not sure. I will need a dental and to be on canned food only.

Please remember to bring a collar and leash with you the day of the adoption. 

Fill out an application online prior to arriving to our adoption event. This greatly speeds up the adoption process and will ensure that the animal you are interested in will be at the event. Not all adoptable dogs can make it to all events, because they are cared for in foster homes. Our adoption events are most Wednesdayâs from 5-7pm and each Saturday from Noon until 4 PM on Saturdayâs at 3602 Lafayette Blvd, Suite 102, Fredericksburg, VA 22408. There are circumstances that we will not have an adoption event, so please email or check our Facebook prior to coming to ensure we will be open. 

We do receive HUNDREDS of emails daily. The fastest way to get a response is to fill out an application on our website, NOT by submitting an inquiry. Online applications get priority over applications filled out in person.

Visit our website for an application to adopt.

Please be patient. Old Dominion Humane Society is a volunteer based organization. We are run completely by volunteers, who also have full time jobs and families.

Like us on Facebook

Old Dominion Humane Society adopts to Virginia and the immediate surrounding states. There is a $50, out of state fee.
