name: Johnny
description: If you are interested in adopting this dog, please fill out our dog adoption questionnaire and e-mail it to Mary at mj@mjcrain.com PLEASE VISIT THIS WEBSITE TO FIND THE ADOPTION QUESTIONNAIRE: http://www.homewardtrails.org/adopt-a-pet/adoption-forms/ \"Hello, my name is Johnny. I came to Homeward Trails from Scott County. I have been looking for my furever home for awhile now but for some reason, no one has grabbed me yet. My fosters think it may be because my fur i s little sparse and patchy but they assure me that there are plenty of people that won't judge me for that. I swear, my fur is looking better and growing out every day! I hear there is a saying that goes something like \"don't judge a book by its cover\" that applies well to me. Now, here are some of my favorite things: food, treats, naps, laying outside, sun bathing, butt scratches, chasing balls and playing fetch, and playing with other friendly dogs. Some things that are not my favorite things: Walks with lots of loud noises and baths. My ideal home would be with happy, calm, laid back people. I am fine if my people decided to have a kitty(ies) before me because I only show a mild interest in them and give them plenty of space. I would love to have a doggy brother or sister because they can reassure me when things may get scary. I would do best in a home has a fenced backyard for me to do my business in peace. It is scary to go to the bathroom when something could jump out at you at any moment! I don't jump on the furniture without permission and I love to just rest on my bed inside the house. Oh, I am a super good boy about not going to the bathroom in the house and sleeping in my crate at night! I do not like to get into the car but once I am inside I don't mind car rides. Well, what do you think? Could you be my soulmate?\" This guy is a champ that truly deserves a loving home where he can show what a great dog he is. Older children who are good with dogs would be best because loud noises can still be somewhat disturbing for Johnny. Do you have the patience and love to give Johnny the forever home he deserves? Please complete an adoption questionnaire so that we can arrange for you to meet him and see if he would be a good fit in your home. Adoption Coordinator: MJ Crain Breed Estimate: Shepherd/Golden Mix Gender: Male Approximate weight: 50 lbs Approximate age: 4 years Location: Foster Home in N. Virginia Cratetrained: Yes Housetrained: Yes Coat Type: Medium; red/chestnut/orange Personality: Shy but sweet; good with other dogs and cats The adoption fee for this dog is $375. This fee INCLUDES spay/neuter and microchip. If the animal you are adopting is not already spayed/neutered, you will be required to sign a contract legally obligating you to have the animal altered. Please contact your HT rep to learn about exclusive low-cost spay/neuter options made available only to HT adopters! Every adopted Homeward Trails animal comes with 30 days of free pet health insurance. We are proud to partner with the following veterinarians who offer a free first exam for your animal, exclusively for HT adopters: Caring Hands Animal Hospital, Palisades Veterinary Clinic, Sunshine Animal Hospital and Clarendon Animal Care and all VCA Animal Hospitals. Additionally, any VCA hospital will cover illnesses up to $250 at no cost to any Homeward Trails adopter. We also provide a 30-minute phone consult with a professional dog trainer at Fur-Get Me Not within the first 30 days of adopting - just for HT adopters in the Arlington/Alexandria area. Start your new dog out on the right foot with this valuable, expert advice and guidance FREE! You can save animals like this one by becoming a foster! Fosters are like way stations between high kill shelters and forever homes. We need fosters so that we can save dogs before they are euthanized at the shelters. If you are interested in becoming a foster, please check out our information about fostering by visiting http://www.homewardtrails.org/foster-a-pet/dog-and-cat-foster-program/

name: Crystal
description:
FOSTER NEEDED SUNDAY 9/22

Animal Profile: Crystal is a stunning estimated 1-year-old white German Shepherd, 61 lbs, who up as a stray and brought to Devore Animal Shelter. When our volunteer saw her she stopped in her tracks and said \"this girl is special.\" She was kennelled with another dog and with her positive energy helped that dog to come out of his shell. Apply online at www.DogGoneSeattle.org

Fosters provide a safe landing spot for dogs transitioning from the shelter environment and help prepare the dogs for adoption. Fosters do get first consideration for adoption, if desired.

Foster application: www.doggoneseattle.org/foster-application

description:

name: Sofia
description:
Animal Profile: Sofia is an adorable and petite 9 lb chihuahua mix who was just rescued from a high kill shelter in CA. She has the cutest smile that quickly won over our transporter! Sofia joined us in Seattle on 9/15 and we'll post more information as we get to know her.

Update from her foster:
Sofia is a sweet heart and one of the gentlest dogs i have ever had! She is trusting and wants to please. She loves her people, and it only took me about an hour to become her person, she loves kids, and she loves other dogs. She doesn't seem to have had a lot of training before but she is learning really quickly. We have started today with \"sit\" and \"leave it\" and she's is doing great. Being food motivated has helped a ton. She will work hard for a little piece of cheese. Sofia is definitely out of the puppy phase and does not chew on anything which has been great! She is great in the crate at night and is getting more and more comfortable in there during the day. But she would much rather be with you or a dog buddy while you're home. We are also working on house training and making great progress. If you are looking for a sweet buddy for yourself or a playmate for your dog, Sofia is your girl!

name: Hoshi
description:
Foster Update: Hi! My name is Hoshi which means Star in Japanese, and I am just that. I am currently living in a multi dog household, where I am learning to shine. I am friendly and get along with all of my doggy siblings. I am also learning; not everything is scary.

You see, when I first came; I wasn't sure who I could trust. I mean who was this lady? They kept calling her my foster mom and they told me to trust her!?! My siblings taught me quickly; she's ok. I now lay by her feet when she sits down and I know if I go over to say hi, she will give me a good scratch and or a snuggle. She isn't so bad after all.

If your looking for a well behaved guy to give belly rubs, hangout, snuggle or go on adventures, then I'm your guy!

name: Lizzy
description:
Animal Profile: Lizzy (and her sibling Lani) are 10-month-old female red Dobie mixes who were just recently rescued from a kill shelter in California. While these girls did not have the best start in life, they are in great spirits. She is a sweet and loving girl, friendly, playful and submissive with other dogs.

Seattle Foster Updates:
Lizzy

already learned her name, how to sit, how to go up stairs, and is working on other basic commands. She's still doing well with house training, crate training and some basic obedience training, like lay down and stay. She's not the best with cats, so probably in a house without any. She would do best in a home with another resident dog as she doesn't like being alone! She loves to be with people or other animals. She is extremely curious about everything.

Lizzy

likes lots and lots of exercise. Long walks, but mostly runs, 2-3X/day. Sometimes she just likes to run all over the yard or have you throw a ball. She's such a giant sweetheart and will lay down next to your feet.

Lizzy

is okay in cars and did great when we took her on a hike. After waking up in the morning, going potty and getting a good stretch, she loves to come in the house, run upstairs going into each kids bedroom to wake them up for school.

description:

While it's awful to think someone would try and perform this procedure at home, Lani is in great spirits.

She is a sweet and loving girl, friendly, playful and submissive with other dogs. She was kennelled with her s

ister in California, but to avoid littermate syndrome we placed the girls in separate foster homes.
Lani is a 10 month old puppy that can gently mouth when she wants affection or attention, but her foster family is working on this behavior. She is working on her leash manners, which includes not jumping for joy when she meets new friends. Lani is working on her crate training, and does better when the crate is located in the same room as her canine companion. She is too interested in small animals, such as cats and squirrels, so she is looking for a home without cats.

Seattle Foster Updates:

uper sweet and loves to cuddle. She is eager to please and very curious about the world around her. She loves every person she meets, is a quick learner and very food motivated!

description:

description:
Animal Profile: Nugget is an adorable chihuahua/dachshund mix who is an absolute gem of a pup! Originally rescued from a high kill shelter in CA, Nugget is now thriving in his Seattle-area foster home. His foster mom can't say enough good things about this little guy; from couch and bed snuggles to romping in the yard with his canine buddy, Nugget is a loving, affectionate, and sweet little guy. He loves treats, belly rubs, sun bathing, and any stuffed toy he can play tug-of-war with! He has done great around older kids and adults, walks great on leash, and does well in his crate. Nugget would love a canine buddy in his forever home, so he can continue to have a buddy to play chase with and snuggle up to during the day.

Seattle Foster Update:

Latest update: Oh my goodness.....I can't believe no one has snapped up this loveable little guy. He likes taking walks, playing with toys, cuddling, and hanging with my 10-year-old nephew. Nugget thinks cats are pretty cool and that any treat shaped like a stick is the only kind of \"real\" treat there is. Also......discovered a new talent over the past week. Little Nugget likes to \"sing!\" Cant wait to see what other new talents this little guy has! Third update: I just love this little guy! Toys and playing are now on the daily docket! He also has gotten to interact with a few older kids. He really enjoys the attention, belly rubs, and giving kisses. Second update: This little guy has come along way in 3 weeks. He hasn't had an accident in the house in 2 weeks, he knows \"sit\" and \"come,\" and he's working on learning other commands. He's started playing with toys, and is learning to play with other dogs. He does well on a leash and likes going to pet friendly stores and meeting other people. He does better with a playmate around, rather than being alone. First update: Nugget started off very shy and timid but quickly became the life of the party. He is a happy and inquisitive little pup. He gets along well with smaller dogs and is still getting used to seeing larger dogs in the neighborhood. He's good on a leash, loves going on walks, and doesn't mind his crate. And ... a big plus ... he gets along with the cats in our house. He has some separation anxiety, but it's getting better with each separation. Nugget loves to cuddle and is a real sweetie!

description:
Animal Profile: Berlin is a handsome and smart 3-year-old Shepherd mix who joined our rescue from California and is now in a Seattle-area foster home. Berlin knows all his basic obedience like sit, down, shake, come, heel and kennel up, is house trained and crate trained. He'd love to find a home with a yard where he can run and be free as that's where he is happiest. Berlin will make a great partner for hiking, jogging or long walks followed by snuggles on the couch. He's the sweetest boy with the best smile!

name: Brigid
description:
KID-FRIENDLY SWEETIE.

Animal Profile: Brigid is a 4- to 5-year-old female Boxer/Pit/German Shepherd mix (we had her DNA done) who was rescued in California. She is our rescue's longest resident and we're still looking for the right fur-ever home for her. She loves all people and is amazing with even very young children. She doesn't bat an eye at crazy antics or rough handling by toddlers, and is not mouthy whatsoever. All she wants in life is to be next to her people. Snuggling and following you around are her favorite activities. Brigid is crate trained and can be left crated for 8 hours without issue in a secure crate. She's house trained and knows sit, down and \"kennel up.\" She's not mouthy or food/toy possessive, and she takes treats gently. Brigid is anxious and reactive in the outside world, and needs slow introductions to dogs she doesn't know. She is leash reactive except when managed by an experienced handler, and will never be a dog-park dog. But she loves playing and cuddling with dogs of all genders and sizes in her own pack and will be fine living with other dogs after a slow introduction. (She needs to understand they are part of her pack before she accepts them.) Brigid doesn't need or want to go for walks for exercise but she does need a secure fenced yard to go potty. Bonus skill: She is treadmill trained!

Brigid's Story: Brigid was a stray in San Bernardino and ended up at high-kill shelter. She was put on the euthanasia list when she came down with kennel cough, so we rescued her in September 2016! She was not spayed due to her upper respiratory infection and when she arrived we quickly saw she was very pregnant! After giving birth she ended up with a very serious infection that required separating her from pups so she could get the veterinary care she needed. She had to have her mammary gland removed and was in intensive medical care for some time. This was likely traumatic for her and may explain some of her separation anxiety and excited/reactive behavior around other dogs. Since then, Brigid had an injury which required surgery (TPLO) and has since recovered. She has also had an extensive board and train so she is well trained. We are eager to find Brigid a wonderful home she can call her own. She has been through a lot so she will need a patient, loving and supportive family.

Adoption Info: Brigid's adoption fee of $150 includes her spay, all vaccinations (Rabies, DPPV, Bordetella) deworming, microchipping and transport from California to Seattle. Brigid's adoption will also include a home training session for her new adopters. Brigid's actual rescue costs are close to $10,000 so any donations to her care are greatly appreciated.

About Foster to Adopt Program:
Fosters provide a safe landing spot for dogs transitioning from the shelter environment and help prepare the dogs for adoption. You provide the love and structure, and we take care of everything else! We cover all vet care, and drive the adoption process. Average length of foster is 2-3 weeks. Fosters do get first consideration for adoption, if desired.

Apply to foster online at www.doggoneseattle.org/foster-application

Canadian adopters need to know that customs charge 15% taxes when entering into Canada.

If you feel that you have the heart and home to give this precious soul a wonderful life, please go to our website, under the APPLICATION tab, complete, then submit the APPLICATION. Once you have been approved, we discuss any questions in regards to the dog you are wanting to adopt, then you complete and submit the contract, make payment and then we can work out the pick up / transport arrangements.

If you would like to start the adoption our process is below:

Submit Application with two personal references and a vet reference.

If you have never had pets and do not have a vet, we will need THREE personal references.

Ensure references are people who know you and your lifestyle well.

Applicant MUST inform vet and references that someone from GaDaH will be calling.

As long as we are able to contact your vet and references, it takes just 1-3 days to process and hopefully approve applications.

If you rent we will need an approval letter for the breed of dog you are wanting to adopt from your landlord on official letterhead paper or email.

Rescue processes and hopefully approves applications.

Once approved, rescue invites applicant to come to the rescue to meet your chosen dog/s, spend time with him/her

and then hopefully take him/her home.

We do NOT hold dogs so if you are unable to come within a week or so of submitting your application the dog will still be available for adoption to other families.

Both of which are included in the medical file you will get when you adopt. (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/pet-travel/by-country/pettravel-canada)

Ensure ALL Fields are filled in, if something is relevant, then put n/a or something in so it recognizes an entry.

We do not recommend using a phone or ipad since these applications for some reason don't tend to come through and you will have spent a lot of time on the application for nothing as it will need to be re-done.

Once we have you approved we can schedule an appointment for you to come to meet

him/her at the rescue in Sebec, Mane and then hopefully take them home to start your new life.

I just have to work on an appointment basis as I run a boarding/day care business and the rescue and so am really busy, but by planning ahead of time I can be pretty flexible.

name: HUA-HUA - CHINA SAVE
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
HUA-HUA was saved from the legal meat trade in China in the Beijing area. He, his 10 siblings and mother were saved by a wonderful rescue lady in China and together we are working on getting them all to the safety of GaDaH-CHINA in Sebec, Maine. We pay to get these dogs vetted, tested, quarantined and all other requirements to import them to the safety of the rescue in Sebec, Maine. The adoption fee's vary slightly depending on the weight and size of the dogs. HUA-HUA adoption fee is US $550 and covers the costs we incur to save these precious souls.

HUA-HUA has been through the export and import quarantine requirements from China to the US. He has his rabies, core vaccines/lepto, heartworm, tick-disease and screw worm tested negative. He has been de-wormed, micro chipped and received any necessary monthly preventatives. He has an estimated date of birth of 2 January 2018 and he weighs around 24 pounds. His mother we believe is a Belgian Shepherd and so he is most likely a Belgian Shepherd Dog Mix, we have no idea what breed the father is. It is up to you to look at him and decide what breed you think he could be. He arrived in the United States on 23rd August 2018, landing at JFK and then was driven up to the rescue in Sebec, Maine. We are looking for families with knowledge of experience of working breed needs to ensure they get a good balance of mental and physical exercise.

HUA-HUA is a cautious boy, but once he has gained trust and feels safe he is very affectionate and loving. He likes to climb on your knee, or snuggle up on the bed, but has always been with his siblings. He will need time to get used to new people and new places, but once trust has been gained he is a great all round boy.

WE DO NOT HAVE CATS OR LIVESTOCK AT THE RESCUE SO ARE UNABLE TO COMMENT ON HOW HE WILL ACT NEAR OR AROUND THEM.

He does use the dog door to get in and out and does go outside to do his business. I do not know if he would let you know he needs to go out since he has 24/7 access to the outside, but he is extremely smart and do not think it would take long to learn, so a few initial accidents in his new home whilst he adjusts and gets used to his new routine and has his family teach him to let them know he wants to go outside should be expected. Until arriving at GaDaH, he had never been an inside dog.

He would benefit from a family who understands the importance of mental stimulation as well as physical exercise. As with all rescue's he needs guidance and training and we recommend families go through at least the basics of training with him themselves so that boundaries, personalities and body language can be learned from each other. He rides good in the car, but has only been with his siblings, never has he been alone. He gets on good with other dogs and would benefit from the companionship in his transition, so a family with another dog would be great, however, if that is not the case, then play-dates with other dogs would be extremely beneficial for him.

He needs an active family and one that will keep his mind stimulated and challenged. Lots of hikes and adventures, training tricks, or agility, dock diving or other fun, active, stimulating activities would be perfect for this boy when his confidence and trust has been gained. Although I have not seen him with children, given time and space his demeanor and personality I have no doubt that he would be great with them and I am sure they could keep each other entertained for many hours.Throughout all that this beautiful soul has been through, he has not once shown any kind of aggression.

HUA-HUA is available for adoption from Give a Dog a Home, German Shepherd Dog Rescue which is located in Sebec, Maine, for an adoption fee of $1,200. This fee is not negotiable and is used to cover the extensive costs of vetting, quarantine requirements, documentation, flights and such to get him from China to Sebec, Maine.

name: DA-HUI - CHINA SAVE
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
DA-HUI was saved from the legal meat trade in China in the Beijing area. He, his 10 siblings and mother were saved by a wonderful rescue lady in China and together we are working on getting them all to the safety of GaDaH-CHINA in Sebec, Maine. We pay to get these dogs vetted, tested, quarantined and all other requirements to import them to the safety of the rescue in Sebec, Maine. The adoption fee's vary slightly depending on the weight and size of the dogs. DA-HUI adoption fee is US $550 and covers the costs we incur to save these precious souls.

DA-HUI has been through the export and import quarantine requirements from China to the US. He has his rabies, core vaccines/lepto, heartworm, tick-disease and screw worm tested negative. He has been de-wormed, micro chipped and received any necessary monthly preventatives. He has an estimated date of birth of 2 January 2018 and he weighs around 19.6 pounds. His mother we believe is a Belgian Shepherd and so he is most likely a Belgian Shepherd Dog Mix, we have no idea what breed the father is. It is up to you to look at him and decide what breed you think he could be. He arrived in the United States on 23rd August 2018, landing at JFK and then was driven up to the rescue in Sebec, Maine. We are looking for families with knowledge of experience of working breed needs to ensure they get a good balance of mental and physical exercise.

DA-HUI is a cautious boy, but once he has gained trust and feels safe he is very affectionate and loving. He likes to climb on your knee, or snuggle up on the bed, but has always been with his siblings. He will need time to get used to new people and new places, but once trust has been gained he is a great all round boy.

WE DO NOT HAVE CATS OR LIVESTOCK AT THE RESCUE SO ARE UNABLE TO COMMENT ON HOW HE WILL ACT NEAR OR AROUND THEM.

He does use the dog door to get in and out and does go outside to do his business. I do not know if he would let you know he needs to go out since he has 24/7 access to the outside, but he is extremely smart and do not think it would take long to learn, so a few initial accidents in his new home whilst he adjusts and gets used to his new routine and has his family teach him to let them know he wants to go outside should be expected. Until arriving at GaDaH, he had never been an inside dog.

He would benefit from a family who understands the importance of mental stimulation as well as physical exercise. As with all rescue's he needs guidance and training and we recommend families go through at least the basics of training with him themselves so that boundaries, personalities and body language can be learned from each other. He rides good in the car, but has only been with his siblings, never has he been alone. He gets on good with other dogs and would benefit from the companionship in his transition, so a family with another dog would be great, however, if that is not the case, then play-dates with other dogs would be extremely beneficial for him.

He needs an active family and one that will keep his mind stimulated and challenged. Lots of hikes and adventures, training tricks, or agility, dock diving or other fun, active, stimulating activities would be perfect for this boy when his confidence and trust has been gained. Although I have not seen him with children, given time and space his demeanor and personality I have no doubt that he would be great with them and I am sure they could keep each other entertained for many hours.Throughout all that this beautiful soul has been through, he has not once shown any kind of aggression.

DA-HUI is available for adoption from Give a Dog a Home, German Shepherd Dog Rescue which is located in Sebec, Maine, for an adoption fee of $1,200. This fee is not negotiable and is used to cover the extensive costs of vetting, quarantine requirements, documentation, flights and such to get him from China to Sebec, Maine.

We post in other states and in Canada to ensure our saved dogs get as much exposure as possible and the perfect families are found. Canadian adopters need to know that customs charge 15% taxes when entering into Canada.

name: Macy
description:
Macy is an adorable young girl around 9 months of age who is believed to be a Shepherd Cattle dog mix. Macy came from a rural part of Kentucky where she was live-trapped after being born to a pack of Shepherds that were free-roaming on a farm. Macy had zero human contact prior to being trapped and has been very slow to warm up. She is considered semi-feral at this point and is still overcoming her fears. 

Macy prefers to avoid all human contact but has begrudgingly learned how to walk on a leash and tolerate being handled for daily living. Macy is a fear biter and if cornered - such as when she is in her crate and needs to come out - she will lash out in fear. If you move slowly with Macy she settles down and will allow you to handle her but she gets overwhelmed easily when rushed. Macy is going to require extensive ongoing handling, training, and socialization coupled with lots of patience as she continues to grow and bond. 

Macy connects with other dogs much better than she does people as a result of her early life in a pack. She does well meeting new dogs and is quick to follow their lead. She isn't at a place of comfort that she plays often but every now and then she will forget the people are around and start to play with one of the other young dogs. Macy has not been around cats or small dogs although she is relatively small herself. We do not know how she would do as there is not true way to test her given her discomfort on leash. 

Macy has a sweet soul and is trying her best to overcome her fears and bond with the people around her. Macy is searching for a home that can provide her a stable environment and ongoing work as she continues to grow beyond her past. 

If you have a place in your heart and home for Macy please email Tierhavenrescue@gmail.com for an adoption application or visit adoptapet.com/tierhaven for FAQ

description:

ABOUT OUR RESCUE DOGS: 
All of our sweet fur babies are being socialized daily with other dogs, adults, & most importantly, children. They are ALL in homes being cared for by people who LOVE them! All of our dogs are located in Connecticut, are spayed or neutered, up to date on vaccines, microchipped, dewormed, have had CT State health checks, & go home with a leash, collar, & packet of medical paperwork. 

BREED IDENTIFICATION:
Please understand that many rescue dogs are mixes of multiple breeds. Petfinder allows us to choose up to two breeds per dog. While the shelters and our rescue do our best in accurately identifying breeds, breed identification is not guaranteed. If there is a certain breed that you do not want, it is very important that you share this with our rescue when applying. When adopting a puppy, breed uncertainty plays a big part in the size/look of the dog as an adult. Please know that any puppy can be a wonderful dog, regardless of preconceived notions of certain breeds, but it is very important that the adopter has the dedication and patience to raise the puppy with boundaries, consistency, structure, & love. The more effort you give towards training & time you allow for exercise, your puppy will grow to be a HUGE source of UNCONDITIONAL LOVE, TOTAL LOYALTY, HAPPINESS, COMFORT & COMPANIONSHIP!

ABOUT OUR RESCUE:
We are a small rescue run by volunteers & focused on finding the right match for both our dogs & for you. If you are interested in adopting through our rescue, you first will need to complete an adoption application & be approved as a potential adopter before meeting any of our pups. No need to be intimidated by our application as it allows us to get to know you & your lifestyle. Of course, the more you can share the better! Please also note, while a fenced yard is fantastic, it is not required by our rescue, however, it may be required for a certain dog. Once adoption applicants are approved to become potential adopters, we offer private appointments where you can meet one or several dogs at the discretion of the rescue. We offer a unique & pleasant experience focused on finding the perfect match. It is extremely important to us that everyone is treated with respect & that NO ONE IS LEFT HANGING. WE WILL GET BACK TO YOU WITHIN 4 TO 5 DAYS of application submission. If there is a dog you are eager to meet, please email us before the 4-5 days! IF YOU DO NOT HEAR FROM US AT THAT POINT, PLEASE CALL US DIRECTLY at 203-241-2351 so that we can check the status of your application and move it forward immediately. We look forward to hearing from you and helping you find your new best friend!

HOME/RENTER INSURANCE:
SOME PROVIDERS HAVE VERY STRICT POLICIES REGARDING WHICH TYPE OF DOG BREEDS ARE ALLOWED UNDER THEIR COVERAGE. STATE FARM WAS SUGGESTED TO US AS THEY DO NOT PUNISH, DROP, NOR REFUSE YOU DUE TO DOG BREED SHOULD YOU RUN INTO ISSUES WITH YOUR CURRENT PROVIDER.

ABOUT OUR RESCUE DOGS: 
All of our sweet fur babies are being socialized daily with other dogs, adults, & most importantly, children. They are ALL in homes being cared for by people who LOVE them! All of our dogs are located in Connecticut, are spayed or neutered, up to date on vaccines, microchipped, dewormed, have had CT State health checks, & go home with a leash, collar, & packet of medical paperwork.

Please understand that many rescue dogs are mixes of multiple breeds. Petfinder allows us to choose up to two breeds per dog. The more effort you give towards training & time you allow for exercise, your puppy will grow to be a HUGE source of UNCONDITIONAL LOVE, TOTAL LOYALTY, HAPPINESS, COMFORT & COMPANIONSHIP!

ABOUT OUR RESCUE:
We are a small rescue run by volunteers & focused on finding the right match for both our dogs & for you. If you are interested in adopting through our rescue, you first will need to complete an adoption application & be approved as a potential adopter before meeting any of our pups. No need to be intimidated by our application as it allows us to get to know you & your lifestyle. Of course, the more you can share the better! Please also note, while a fenced yard is fantastic, it is not required by our rescue, however, it may be required for a certain dog. Once adoption applicants are approved to become potential adopters, we offer private appointments where you can meet one or several dogs at the discretion of the rescue. We offer a unique & pleasant experience focused on finding the perfect match. It is extremely important to us that everyone is treated with respect & that NO ONE IS LEFT HANGING. name: Star
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Introducing Star! This Star of the show was rescued from a South Carolina shelter. She is a gorgeous little girl with the most beautiful eyes and coloring. Star
is friendly with dogs, children and people of all ages and will make a wonderful addition to any family. She is current on vaccinations (age appropriate) and will be spayed prior to being placed. Will you be the lucky family that gets to love Star forever? If so, please fill out an application at

www.rescuedogsrocknyc.org

.

name: Kanaaq & Tapessa & Frankie- BONDED
description: These girls came to us from the same home in South Carolina. We've slowly tried to wiggle them away from each other but alas, we had to admit defeat. They LOVE each other! These girls are very sweet, playful and love people, dogs and kids. The problem? They're skittish because they are afraid so they don't show well at meet and greets. They require a solid FENCED in yard with zero vulnerability and a family that is patient with them. They want your love and affection, they just have to trust you first. Treats certainly help as they are all treat motivated! They love bones, rope toys, the pool and any kind of soft treat. They are incredibly gentle and deserve a chance to show everyone how amazing they are.

name: Doogie
description: You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Meet Doogie! Doogie is a 12 years young Beagle mix who was rescued from a shelter in South Carolina in the nick of time. Doogie is a sweet, quiet boy who is looking for a loving home where he can enjoy his retirement. He is friendly with dogs, people of all ages and especially LOVES children! Doogie will make a wonderful addition to any family. Doogie is up to date on vaccinations (age appropriate) and will be neutered prior to being placed. If the road to Doogie's happiness leads to your front door, please fill out an application at www.rescuedogsrocknyc.org.

name: Fred
description: Fred is a country boy from South Carolina. He is accustomed to a slow and steady lifestyle and can be spooked by sudden movements or loud noises. He will need a family that will help him overcome his fears and learn to just enjoy the world around him. He warms up very quickly and just adores attention. He wants to be pet and played with constantly. He enjoys toys and will chase a ball...he just needs to learn to bring it back! We think he would do best with mature children due to his nervous nature and abundant energy. We are unsure of how he would do with other animals at this time.

name: Beauty
description: You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Beauty was born in mid-2018 and, at approximately 30 pounds, is a petite shepherd mix. She came to rescue from a South Carolina shelter very pregnant. Now that her pups will soon be ready for their new homes, it's Beauty's turn to find her own forever family. She is a real love bug! She is great with people and loves to cuddle with her human foster sibling. Beauty also gets along well with other dogs. She is up to date on vaccines and will be spayed as soon as possible after her pups leave. To adopt Beauty, put your application in now @ http://www.rescuedogsrocknyc.org

name: Sawyer
description: You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Sawyer is a 5 year old male Beagle/Chi blend who comes to rescue from a shelter in South Carolina. He is up to date on vaccines and will be neutered prior to placement in his forever home. Sawyer is good with people and other dogs. Sawyer would very much like a human family of his own to adopt. The qualities he is looking for are: loving embraces, a soft bed, loyalty, understanding. If you are looking for those same qualities in a new family member, look no further because Sawyer is your fella! Apply here: http://www.rescuedogrocknyc.org

name: Amber
description:
Amber is a gorgeous pup  from South Carolina. She is around 7 months old, and weighs roughly 40 lbs. 
Amber is very intelligent, very alert, and very obedient! This pup is already hot stuff! She adores playing fetch with a ball and hiking, and could probably make a great running buddy! 
Amber totally  loves people of all ages, and is super friendly to everyone! 
She loves curl up close to her humans at night, and is a perfect sleeping buddy!
This girl will be a wonderful companion to any active household!

******IMPORTANT - PLEASE READ ALL THE GREAT INFO BELOW******

PLEASE read our website's ADOPTION PROCESS PAGE prior to submitting an adoption application. www.apupspizzazzrescue.com/adoption-process 
ADOPTION APPLICATION: www.apupspizzazzrescue.com/adoption-application 

ABOUT OUR RESCUE DOGS: 
All of our sweet fur babies are being socialized daily with other dogs, adults, & most importantly, children. They are ALL in homes being cared for by people who LOVE them! All of our dogs are located in Connecticut, are spayed or neutered, up to date on vaccines, microchipped, dewormed, have had CT State health checks, & go home with a leash, collar, & packet of medical paperwork. 

BREED IDENTIFICATION:
Please understand that many rescue dogs are mixes of multiple breeds. Petfinder allows us to choose up to two breeds per dog. While the shelters and our rescue do our best in accurately identifying breeds, breed identification is not guaranteed. If there is a certain breed that you do not want, it is very important that you share this with our rescue when applying. When adopting a puppy, breed uncertainty plays a big part in the size/look of the dog as an adult. Please know that any puppy can be a wonderful dog, regardless of preconceived notions of certain breeds, but it is very important that the adopter has the dedication and patience to raise the puppy with boundaries, consistency, structure, & love. The more effort you give towards training & time you allow for exercise, your puppy will grow to be a HUGE source of UNCONDITIONAL LOVE, TOTAL LOYALTY, HAPPINESS, COMFORT & COMPANIONSHIP!

ABOUT OUR RESCUE:
We are a small rescue run by volunteers & focused on finding the right match for both our dogs & for you. If you are interested in adopting through our rescue, you first will need to complete an adoption application & be approved as a potential adopter before meeting any of our pups. No need to be intimidated by our application as it allows us to get to know you & your lifestyle. Of course, the more you can share the better! Please also note, while a fenced yard is fantastic, it is not required by our rescue, however, it may be required for a certain dog. Once adoption applicants are approved to become potential adopters, we offer private appointments where you can meet one or several dogs at the discretion of the rescue. We offer a unique & pleasant experience focused on finding the perfect match. It is extremely important to us that everyone is treated with respect & that NO ONE IS LEFT HANGING. WE WILL GET BACK TO YOU WITHIN 4 TO 5 DAYS of application submission. If there is a dog you are eager to meet, please email us before the 4-5 days! IF YOU DO NOT HEAR FROM US AT THAT POINT, PLEASE CALL US DIRECTLY at 203-241-2351 so that we can check the status of your application and move it forward immediately. We look forward to hearing from you and helping you find your new best friend!

HOME/RENTER INSURANCE:
SOME PROVIDERS HAVE VERY STRICT POLICIES REGARDING WHICH TYPE OF DOG BREEDS ARE ALLOWED UNDER THEIR COVERAGE. STATE FARM WAS SUGGESTED TO US AS THEY DO NOT PUNISH, DROP, NOR REFUSE YOU DUE TO DOG BREED SHOULD YOU RUN INTO ISSUES WITH YOUR CURRENT PROVIDER.

name: Bo Peep
description: You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Welcome little Bo Peep! Beautiful Bo Peep, at 16 years old, comes into rescue from South Carolina. Due to no fault of her own and just because she's a gal in her prime, Bo Peep finds herself looking for a new home in which to enjoy her retirement. Bo Peep is a small Terrier mix who was an owner surrender. This gorgeous gal is good with people and dogs and wants to spend her days in the comfort of a nice soft bed and a loving home. If you have room in your heart and home for this sweet senior, please fill out an application to adopt Bo Peep at www.rescuedogsrocknyc.org

description: This big guy is our Theodore! He is about a year old, retriever mix, rescued from a high shelter in South Carolina! He's a playful, sweet, boy just looking for the right home! Theodore is proudly being sponsored by Linda & James Callihan.

name: Dillon
description:
Meet our handsome boy Dillon! Dillon comes to us from a kill shelter in South Carolina and was almost out of time when we were contacted. This stunning boy could not be sweeter! He walks well on a leash and is your typical southern gentleman. We are assuming he is a boxer/bull-dog/lab mix.  We're not too sure about his past, but Dillon had a skin infection when he arrived at our shelter which improved with antibiotics and medicated baths.

Dillon is estimated between 2-4 years old, and around 60 lbs. He is extremely friendly and would love an active, experienced home that can give him lots of love and exercise. Dillon is dog friendly when properly introduced and would do best in a home with older children.

GardenRescues.Org

name: Truffles
description: If you are ready for your newest best friend, Truffles is the girl for you. She's a 1 year old Terrier mix who was rescued from South Carolina. Truffles is really great with other dogs, and loves to play!

name: Sookie
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Sookie came to rescue from South Carolina. A good Samaritan had reported that they saw her lying in the grass on the side of her owners house, covered in fleas, and emaciated. Animal Control investigated and took her. Sookie is an 8 year old female Boxer blend. On intake, she was extremely underweight, and she has cataracts that make it difficult to see. It has been determined that she is also a diabetic, and a new family should know that she will require insulin as part of her daily care. In addition, Sookie had a small mass on her leg that was determined to be Mast Cell. She has had surgery with our vet to remove the mass and has healed wonderfully. She is now doing so great in her foster home but would really love a home to call her very own!
Her foster Mom says she is the perfect mix of couch potatoe and playmate
! Sookie is a vocal lady who definitely has her own hilarious personality to show you. When Sookie isn't curled up on your lap (Yes, ON your lap), in her bed, or on the floor next to you she is exploring her surroundings with her curious little nose or demanding your attention with her adorable little grumbles! To Sookie, there aren't too many things greater in life than cuddling with the nearest human or playing with a fun toy! Speaking of toys, Sookie loves a good game of tug-of-war or a round of squeaking her favorite squeaky toy. She also enjoys walks full of exploring and sniffing and is more than willing to accompany you on an easy hike with some more leash training.
Sookie is very tolerant of all kinds of petting, even some attention that might annoy some dogs. She does occasionally play a little rough so, supervision around the little ones is never a bad idea. She really
enjoys interacting with other dogs, especially those who want to play with her. Once introductions are done she is happy to play with her canine buddy or simply relax on the couch next to them.
Sookie has what some consider a complicated relationship with cats. She desperately wants to play with them but in true Boxer form, she doesn't seem to understand that hissing and swatting isn't playing. A kitty that loves playtime as much as her would be a dream come true to Sookie.
Sookie has made huge strides in her leash walking but, her cataracts do inhibit
her vision somewhat so unexpected objects in her path may trip her up.
In other areas she is a lady. She waits patiently (with the exception of a few grumbles) for her food and allows you to take it away with nothing worse than a pout. She is a pro at receiving her insulin and acts as if she doesn't even know you're there when administering it.
She really is the full package and any family would be VERY lucky to call her their own.
Sookie is up to date on shots and will be spayed prior to placement in her forever home. If you would like to adopt Sookie, please put your application in here: http://www.rescuedogsrocknyc.org

name: Donald

name: Birdie
description:
Birdie and her 4 young pups came to Simon last January from South Carolina.  She took good care of her litter but at 10 weeks the pups were vetted and quickly found adoptive homes. Adopters must have previous experience with challenging dogs.  Birdie absolutely loves her people so we looking for someone to love her and give her a great life, while helping her to make good choices.

If you are interested in adopting a dog, please submit an application to adopt on our website:  thesimonfoundation.org

name: Junior
description:
What a beauty Junior is.  At 23 pounds at a little over 3 months old, we expect him to be about 80 or so pounds when finished growing.  Super sweet, rescued from South Carolina and working on housebreaking and leash walking skills. 
 What a wonderful pet he will make.

Please note-we do require an application, found on our website, almosthomedogs.org, click on \"Adopt\" at top.

The adoption fee for puppies less than 6 months old is $350, which includes the cost of routine vetting, including age appropriate vaccinations, worming, flea/tick preventative and spay/neuter. Puppies under 4 months of age may go to adoptive homes before they are spayed/neutered. Adopters who choose to adopt a puppy that has not yet been spayed/neutered are subject to an additional deposit of $100 (refundable upon proof of spay/neuter.) Included in the adoption fee, the rescue will arrange spay/neuter by a partner vet at the adopter's convenience when the puppy is between 4-6 months of age. It is the responsibility of the adopter to bring the adopted puppy back to the rescue vet for spaying/neutering or to send verification from another vet that the puppy had been spayed/neutered.  All of our dogs will be microchipped.

Because our dogs are in foster homes, applications are required prior to setting up any appointments. Calling or emailing may delay your consideration. Find our application on our website, almosthomedogs.org, then click on \"Adopt\" tab at top

We are a non profit no kill 501 (c)3 rescue. Please understand that we do our best to describe our dogs but often we rescue them with virtually no information about them and often our best educated guess can be challenging. Currently check or cash is preferred payment.

name: Colt
description: Say hello to our little friend Colt! Colt is a six week old terrier mix. He came from a rural shelter in South Carolina and made his way to Maryland right before the hurricane was projected to make landfall. Colt is doing great in his foster home socializing with people and other dogs. He loves to play but loves cuddling even more. He is working on potty training and is doing well so far. Colt would love a family to call his own.

name: Bowie
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8094

Im Bowie! I am estimated to be a 6-year-old Catahoula Leopard Dog mix. Im a big boy, weighing about 75 lbs and I came to OPH from South Carolina, so Im a southern gentleman. Howdy-do!

My foster mom thinks Im awesome! She says Im crate-trained, I havent had a single accident in my foster home, and I only bark when the other dogs in my foster home bark to welcome someone home. I sometimes talk and sing when my food is being prepared, because I love mealtime! I also get very excited about going out and I spring about 3 feet straight up off the ground when its time to go! I am a strong boy, so I get walked on an easy-walk harness, which works well for me. My foster mom says Im smart to avoid obstacles and not get my leash tangled around them. Yay, me!

I am a people dog, so I love to be with my foster family and getting attention. I can get nervous and anxious around other dogs, so I would probably do best in a home as an only dog, but I think I would do well in almost any environment: apartment, townhouse, single-family home. As long as I can be part of the family and show my devotion, I will be a happy boy.

Come meet me!

name: Will Forte
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8330

Hi! My name is Will Forte. 

Im a Beagle mix and estimated to be about 1 years old. Im a sweet boy and I currently weigh about 32 lbs. I came to OPH from a shelter in South Carolina. I love it here with my foster family and have been hanging out, getting treated for heartworms (they are yucky) and learning new tricks. I've finished my heartworm treatment (yay!) and am ready to find my forever family. 

Some things about me:
* I LOVE treats. What's that mean to you? It means that I am very trainable to tag along with you during your daily travels and can likely learn lots of fun tricks with you.
* I LOVE to play ball. Hopefully you will too. It helps get my energy out as well so we can watch TV later. 
* I LOVE to get my zoomies out outside. My foster family has told me that's where we do this and we play nice inside and try not to run too much. 
* Do you like to explore? Hey, I do too! Let's go on hikes together and explore all that's out there in Virginia and beyond. 
* AHHH...my crate. It's my quiet and calm time and I don't mind it one bit. It's a pretty great place to nap. 
* I like everyone in my foster family so I'm sure I will like you too! They have older kids and I love being around them. 
* I hope you have some toys or that we can get some. I love to play with them. Wanna go to the pet store and pick some out?
* Here's the best part, are you ready? I have not had any accidents in my foster familys house. My mom says I may need a day to adjust to your house but shes assured me that I will quickly know your routine as well and not have any accidents there too.

I'm a super happy boy, my tail is always wagging. Let's find a time for you to meet me and see what a fun little guy I can be. There are some neat video's featuring none other than me below so you can see me in action. (I'm famous you know, I have my own videos and everything)


Click here and here to see me in action with OPH! 

Click here to see me playing with a foster friend. 

I'll be here hanging out with my foster family in Oakton, VA. Ask my foster mom for directions, she will be happy to share them with you. Don't wait! I'll be snatched up soon she says.

name: Bobby
description:
Bobby is a handsome catch who comes to our rescue from South Carolina.  When Bobby went into our care he was shut down and withdrawn.  Through time, patience and lots of love from his foster family, he has emerged a happy, friendly and playful guy.  His little nubbie tail wags, wags, wags when he greets you at the door.  Bobbyâs breed is anyoneâs guess.  He looks like he has some collie in him, and maybe a little lab.  We do not guarantee any breed mix/combo.   Bobby is approximately 5 years old, is 57 pounds and is housetrained. 

Bobby has transformed into a playful, cuddly, loving dog who is usually touching, leaning against, or curled up with you during downtime.  He loves, loves, loves the water.  Heâll play in hoses and irrigation systems, so heâs a lot of fun when youâre washing your car.  Bobby has been for a few boat rides and will get into the water freestyle when stopped at the favorite swimming hole.  He gets excited at just the sight of water and gives you no trouble when itâs bath time!  Bobby knows his basic manners and commands, and likes pleasing you and getting treats.  His favorite treat is Redi-Whip straight from the can!  He is a stuffed toy dog and will self-entertain by throwing around stuffed toys, which occasionally end up getting tossed onto countertops!  He likes to play tug-of-war and will do zoomies in the yard when heâs got a toy in his mouth.  

Bobby enjoys walks, and is great in the car.  Heâs just an all-around outdoor enthusiast, and we would love to see him adopted to people who will take him on outdoor adventures.  Bobby will need a little time readjusting to his forever home, so we are looking for a patient adopter who will commit time to training so he continues his transformation.  Bobby gets along great with other dogs and he is also great with cats.  He will actually snuggle up with his foster familyâs cat from time to time.  He would do fine as the only dog in the home or with other animals.   

Bobby has been fully vetted, is heartworm negative and is up to date on all vaccines.  He is neutered, microchipped, and on current heartworm prevention and flea prevention. Bobby does have a back leg that ever so slightly curves inwards.  The vet checked him out and said itâs fine.  It doesnât bother him at all, and it certainly doesnât hold him back from zoomies and swimming!

Precious is a fun little piglet who has adjusted beautifully to life in her busy foster home. She doesn't see well but likes to explore and is happy to make new friends. Her owner seemed to be taking good care of her, as she came to the shelter with extensive veterinary records, but for some reason she wasn't wanted anymore and was left there to die. Precious is diabetic and takes insulin twice a day, which is a difficult condition for the shelter to handle- they did not plan on being able to keep her there long, but luckily we had space and she made the long trip up from South Carolina. 
?
We've never had a pet with diabetes before and were a little nervous about keeping up with Precious' meds, but she takes her injections with no problems and the insulin is very inexpensive. Precious is also on a prescription food for urinary issues, but she doesn't eat much so that's no big deal either. All in all she has been a sweet, loving, and easy addition to our foster family, and we are so happy we were able to get her out of the shelter safely!

description:
This Southern Belle has traveled all the way from South Carolina to find her forever home here in New Jersey. When you meet Lady it is obvious that she did at one time have a home where someone taught her the commands that she knows and how to play her favorite game of \"fetch\".

Lady has been in foster since 1/7/18. She has been a perfect houseguest, is completely house and crate trained. She goes right into her crate every morning when I leave for work and is sleeping when I get home. Lady loves her person, loves cuddling and to be pet. She is a calm dog that loves her toys and a good nap on the couch. On walks she doesn't pay attention to other dogs and walks calmly next to them when on pack walks. We do not know much about Lady's past, but she does scare easily, so she would do best in a calm household with older, respectful children, and not much traffic in and out of the house. She takes a while to warm up to new people but once she does she loves you. Lady is a very special girl that deserves a loving home of her own. She is silly, full of personality and one the sweetest dogs I've ever had the pleasure of fostering. She is so easy to love and will make a wonderful addition to the right household.

If you want to meet Lady go to EHRDOGS.ORG and submit an application. Don't forget to ask for LADY BEAUFORT - she is waiting so patiently at the kennel for someone to fall in love with her and bring her home. Could that someone be you?

Thank you for your interest in dog who needs a new home. Adoption can be one of the most fulfilling experiences in your life and especially in the life of your new canine companion.

A note to those looking at CPR. We have no perfect dogs - but many of our dogs have proven to be perfect for a certain someone. Our job is to find those someone's. Our most successful adopters come to CPR not because they want a dog. They come to us because they want to give a dog a home. We urge all of our potential adopters not to fall in love with a picture. While we like to know what you like in looks, a dog is more than a pretty face. Our goal is to match you with the best possible pet for you and your home. We want to create furever families.

Our descriptions contain all that we know about this dog today. We'll update as more information is known.

Are you looking to adopt within the next 30 days? If so please visit our webpage at www.carolinapoodlerescue.org and complete the application. You'll find it in the menu on the left hand side. You'll also find a total listing of all our dogs available.

Just browsing but interested in poodles and poodle mixes? Please drop a note to applications@carolinapoodlerescue.org with your name, address and phone # and email. We'll add you to our mailing list.

thanks
the CPR Adoption team

Date into Rescue: 4/5/2019
Reason for being in rescue: VA shelter- allowed to run at large and picked up one too many times
Foster location: Dreamweaver Farms, Pacolet SC
Special Needs? Dood was deemed a dangerous animal in the state of Virginia. His previous owner would not keep him confined and he was allowed to roam at will. He is happy and gregarious and would run up to people and knock them down as a game. He's not shown any aggressive side to us at all but we all know how to tel him \"GET OFF\" and he's respecting that cue. He needs some training and someone with some common sense.
Weight: 99 lbs
Height: 26 in
Spayed/Neutered: Yes

Adoption Fee: $499

Fence needed? Without exception and it needs to be a solid, dependable fence and you need to plan to be in control of your dog. He's been failed by a human once before because of not understanding our dogs needs us to keep them safe and in places they can safely be, not roaming the streets.

What kind of home would be best for me? Dood's perfect owner will be someone with dog experience, who loves to take long, brisk walks and who would enjoy teaching, shaping and training their dog to be the excellent companion this dog has the potential to be. Dood is affectionate and friendly and longs for that companion that will be his partner, his friend and his guide through life instead of letting him run amuck.

What is my personality like? Dood is an even tempered and intelligent dog who has been allowed to run and roam and that got him on serious trouble. He was part of a pack with his sister Dette.

One of our temperament programs is to take our dogs off site for adventures. Dood is a perfect gentleman in the car just as he was in the trip from Virginia to South Carolina. He is attentive, likes to look out the window and enjoys seeing new places and learning new things.

How do I act when I first meet new people? Friendly. He's been known to bark at people but it's in a \"hi come on over and let's get to know each other\" way. But..as big as he is it is a deep bark and that can intimidate people.

Other tips and tidbits: Estimated Birthdate: 4/15/2015. Dood is a lot of dog with a lot of things going for him. He has been given a very bad rap and very nearly lost his life because his previous owner had no common sense. We are going to be extraordinarily picky about his next home to make sure it's his best home and his forever home.

Dood is NOT completely hypoallergenic. He does very lightly shed. We do not know his heritage but I am betting he is first generation so there is some shedding involved.

House trained? Dogs can be house trained if they are in the right environment and are allowed to follow a schedule as long as a physical reason doesn't keep them from being trained. A dog house trained in my home may not be in yours. We will help you teach your new dog this necessary skill and based on your schedule.

Please note - we do not ship dogs. If you are interested in adopting, please take a look at the distance between the foster home location and your location and make sure you are willing to make that trip. Most of our dogs are at our farm in Pacolet, South Carolina.

To apply, please visit our webpage at www.carolinapoodlerescue.org and visit the tab on the left that directions you to the online application.

Please note that when screening applications, we look at the entire home and then make suggestions based on what would be a good fit for your home. You are not being screened for a specific dog although we are looking to see what type of dog interests you - poodles or non poodles, color, age, etc. Others here may be a better fit for you. It is very difficult to get to know a living animal from a picture and a short description. Since we are constantly getting in new dogs, this may be a dog not in our listings yet. We want you to be very happy with your new companion and will make suggestions based on what you tell us about you.

Thank you for considering CPR.

name: Geneva
description:
GENEVA AMERICAN STAFFORDSHIRE TERRIER MIX TAN (RED)  & WHITE ARRIVED 9/4/19 ~46 LBS ~ THREE-YEARS-OLD FEMALE CHIPPED 

Geneva is one of five dogs that were rescued by PAWS from South Carolina during Hurricane Dorian. These lovely dogs are sweet, loving, lively and amazing! Elmore SPCA was happy to help a total of 14 dogs find their way towards their new beginning by being able to take in five of the fourteen dogs which made the transport possible. PAWS Rescue is amazing and so is Kershaw County Humane Society for keeping the faith that these pups would find new homes! 

Geneva  is a super loving staffie! She is very loving  and she loves to be pet and loves to be around her people once she gets to know you.  She seems to like the other dogs she has met in SC and here in NY! This lovely lady was very difficult to photograph because every time we pet her she closed her eyes and tried to snuggle in closer to us She is learning loose leash walking skills, but is pretty strong and will pull when there is something of high value available, ie food or a person to pet her.  She gets super excited when she is behind a barrier or a fence and she sees other dogs and does that pitty screech but it isn't an aggressive behavior. She is a bit shy of loud noises, door ways and fast and loud traffic. Although she is a bit wary and skittish at first, she has shown no aggressive behaviors.  If anything Geneva only wants a warm lap to curl up on and a loving hand to stroke her head. 

Geneva  is a great dog who has a ton of love to give. She would benefit from having a family who will help her gain some confidence and who will take the time to help her learn that not all humans are jerks!  Geneva is a love and seems to love everyone she has met here at the shelter, 

Geneva is current on rabies, distemper and bordetella vaccinations, has tested negative for heartworm, lyme, ehrlichia and anaplasmosis, is spayed and chipped and is ready to go to her new home! Come in and meet this adorably sweet and loving dog.

He came to us from the reservation in South Dakota were he and his brother had a bad interaction with a porcupine, but despite being in considerable pain when we got him he was still the sweetest most patient boy ever and is now ready to find his forever family.

He loves playing with his foster fur siblings and is good with all three of them, regardless of size. He also chose his 9 year old human foster sister as his person and is head over heels in love with her. He follows her all over the yard when she's outside playing and loves to snuggle with her. He has an 8 month old human baby foster brother and he pretty much doesn't pay any attention to him. He whines a bit when he first goes in the crate, but settles down shortly after and lays quietly. He walks fairly well on a leash, but could still use some practice with that to really get it down. Takoda would make the perfect addition to any family who is looking for a sweet, loyal companion.

name: Reba
description:

I would LOVE a family that likes to spend time outdoors hiking and walking as I have a lot of energy. name: Rogue (FL)
description:
Rogue ( formerly listed as Ashton ) comes to us from Georgia, where she was a stray in a packed shelter. Summertime is a big time for dogs to end up in shelters unfortunately so she needed help FAST. Fast forward to a ground transport from GA to South Florida, where our great transporters remarked on how sweet she is and how she looks for affection. Rogue came with some red areas on her skin from being loaded with fleas, and we can tell she has been a mama a few times.

Rogue is a calm girl, who politely asks for cuddles. She tries to be sneaky and counter surf when she thinks the coast is clear, but responds quickly to verbal correction and walks out of the kitchen. Rogue LOVES squeaky toys! She is good on a leash and loves companionship. Rogue is good with dogs and cats, and in general is a very easy going gal!

description: Lex is one of 400 German Shepherds saved from deplorable conditions in a puppy mill/hoarder situation in South Ga. Lex is slowly learning to love and trust. He actually walks great on a leash and LOVES people if you go slow and let him trust you. Lex will need a home with at least one other dog that he can learn from by example. No children please, as these dogs have proven to be VERY protective of their people once they bond with someone. Training will be a requirement for his new home, as we want success for all !! A secure fenced yard is needed to ensure his safety. description: Sophie is a sweet little Southern Belle who is moving to Colorado from South Georgia on September 8, 2019.  Sophie is about 3-5 months old and weighs about 20 pounds.  She is already learning how to walk on a leash and is doing great!  Sophie loves to play with people and other dogs.  She has spent time in a crate, so crate training should not be difficult. name: Courtesy Post: Princess Moonbeam
description:

name: Tater
description:
Meet Tater! This adorable little nugget was found abandoned on a property in rural Alabama with his buddy, Sparky, when he was only three months old. Thankfully, a Good Samaritan saw the pups, and brought them home to safety. This Good Samaritan is also the mom of one of our volunteers, so of course we wanted to help these adorable puppies find their way home.

We don't know if they are from the same litter or have different fathers, but they were lucky to have each other when they were out there on their own. They were a healthy weight when found, so we suspect they were not on their own for long.

Both puppies have been well cared for and initally lived in AL with 2 stay-at-home parents, multiple dogs to romp and play with, a cat, and two birds. They had regular play time with 2 teen grandkids, and were always great with the kids. Tater has a short coat, larger ears, and is the larger of the two pups. He's growing quickly and is very gentle with his doggy friends. Tater knows sit and lay down, and knows to ask to go out. He is already crate trained and well socialized with other dogs.

FOSTER UPDATE - 9/12/19

Tater arrived last week and is being fostered in Reston, VA. This adorable little nugget has really grown since our last update and arrived in N. VA just this past weekend. His brother, Sparky, was just adopted on Sunday, so now it's Tater's turn.

Tater has been living with other dogs, a cat, and two birds, and has had regular exposure to the grandkids while in Alabama. He's excellent with other dogs and would benefit from having a confident, social dog in his new home who can show him the ropes. He is a little unsure after being separated from Sparky and is adjusting to city life, so he's timid and tentative around new people. He was initially hesitant around his new foster dad, but he warmed up within two days, and once he's comfortable with you, he's a loving puppy who likes to snuggle up on the couch and nap on you. He's only been here five days, so he's still adjusting to a lot of change.

We are looking for a family who understands that Tater needs a little time and patience to settle in...as most puppies do! He's never aggressive and is still a puppy, and he just needs time to acclimate. His foster mom has been taking him to pet stores, and to get him accustomed to new people, she's had a dog walker come in the house and she introduces him to strangers . He's progressing every day and is ready to go home!

Apply today!

name: Scooter
description:
This handsome guy is one of a huge litter DCAWS agreed to take from the shelter in Houston County when they were overloaded with intake.  He was adopted when a young puppy.  In early June we received a call from an animal facility in St. Louis reporting that he was with them.  He had been brought in for observation at the age of 3-1/2 years because he had nipped a child.  When the 10 days were up he was not reclaimed by the family.  
Report from the facility is that this was a play nip and there were no ER or medical or police reports filed as this was a minor and non-vicious incident.  Since his return Scooter has been in a home with several other dogs and is doing well there.  He has shown himself to be affectionate, smart, playful and certainly of good nature, although he does still nip in play occasionally.  He is in need of a new home where he is corrected with training and is never abandoned again.
Born 12/25/12

name: Trish
description:
Meet Trish. Trish came to us in August of 2010 from Sister Pat at St. Anne's church in Carthage, MS. 

Sister Pat had some rescues at the parish and some thugs threatened to kill them if she and an older Sister didnt give them money. Sister Pat called the police on the boys and then called us in a panic. As soon as the young gang boys got out of jail, they were certainly going to come kill the dogs. ARF took in 18 dogs. Some have been adopted, some not. Trish is still a young dog, approximately 2-3 years old and weighs around 35 pounds. She's a bit skittish, and is still learning to walk on a leash. She LOVES to snuggle and just wants to be near you. 

Trish, Labrador Retriever & Terrier Mix has been shared from Shelter Exchange - http://www.shelterexchange.org.

name: Pixie
description:
Hello from our sweet little Pixie!!  
We rescued Pixie in January from the NYPD 120TH  Precinct in Staten Island, NY. She was in very poor condition...starving, skin and bones, freezing and scared. She was microchipped but the owner claimed she gave her to her ex-husband and did NOT want her back even after learning she was emaciated and living on the streets!! How cruel!!
We were not able to actually take possession of Pixie until our great vet in SI did their due diligence. The Vet staff took great care of her while she had her stay and we are grateful for their assistance in keeping her safe. She otherwise would have most likely wound up in a kill shelter. 
Pixie has already gained 6 lbs but still needs some more healthy weight gain. 
This petite sweetie pie is super lovable, seems unphased by other dogs and just wants to snuggle and give kisses. 
Please consider applying to adopt or foster her by filling out the application at www.nybullycrew.org Thank you!

name: Onyx
description:
Onyx is a well behaved friendly dog good with smaller dogs. She is good with dogs her size if they are friendly and not pushy. 

Kellen Rescue is located in California and almost always requires fenced yards and do not adopt out of State with the exception of sometimes to neighboring States. Our dogs are in foster homes and available to meet by appointment.

name: Panda
description: Panda is a senior (born approx 4.1.08) spayed female Akita. She is up to date on vaccines, on flea/heartworm prevention, microchipped, house trained, crate trained, and leash trained. Panda comes to us from the shelter in Suffolk, VA, where she found herself after she didn't get along with the family's new puppy. Panda still has lots of bouncy energy and loves meeting new people and is a wonderful breed ambassador! Panda has gone to daycare with some of the other fosters. She would like a retirement home as an only or with the right mellow male.

name: Waverly
description:
Waverly is a young (born approximately 10.19.17) spayed female Akita. She is up to date on vaccines, microchipped, heartworm negative, on flea/heartworm prevention, house trained, crate trained, and leash trained. MUST GO TO HOME AS ONLY PET.

Waverly comes to us from Suffolk, VA, where she was picked up by animal control, running stray. She is in very good condition and was found with a collar and Seresto flea collar. Clearly someone had been caring for her, but no one came to claim her. She is very people friendly.

name: Lincoln
description:
Lincoln is an adult (born approx 6.29.2013) neutered male Akita. He is up to date on vaccines, microchipped, heartworm negative, on flea/heartworm prevention, neutered, and leash trained. MUST GO TO HOME AS ONLY PET OR WITH FOSTER SISTER, SMUDGE.

Lincoln and Smudge came to us from the shelter in Suffolk, VA. Lincoln is a bit shy but very friendly. He is good friends with Smudge, and could be adopted with her.

name: Pinto
description:
Meet the Bean siblings! Navy and Pinto are 2-month-old Labrador Retriever mixes anxiously awaiting their forever homes here in New Jersey. They were originally rescued from Marion County, South Carolina and are very lucky to be alive. At the moment, they weigh all of about 7 pounds, however, they will likely be medium-large sized dogs once fully grown. Their foster moms say, \"These two pups are definitely the life of the party! They love to run and jump on each other playing. They are definitely attention lovers.\" They are working very hard on their leash, crate, and house training skills. In no time, these smart pooches will be masters of all three!

Pinto is neutered, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

name: Daisy

At first, she was wary of new humans, taking her time to warm up. It is evident that she had never felt the gentle hand of a human in her lifetime. However, day by day, Daisy has been coming out of her shell. She thrives in the company of other dogs and would truly love a sibling in her forever home. Daisy has the sweetest, most gentle temperament and loves to receive affection. She is 1 years old and fully grown at about 46 pounds. She is a Cattle Dog/Lab mix. Emotional Support Animals (ESA)
Emotional Support Animals are not required to undergo specialized training. They can be dogs, cats, exotics, birds. Their primary role is to provide their owners with emotional comfort. Emotional support animals can benefit a disabled individual psychologically. The basic gift of companionship and unconditional affection can be the therapy needed to counter a condition like debilitating depression or Post Traumatic Stress Disorder.
ESAs are protected under the Fair Housing Amendments Act (FHAA) and the Air Carrier Access Act (ACAA). People meeting the proper criteria are entitled to an ESA to assist them with life. The FHAA protects individuals by allowing ESAs to live with them regardless of breed (even with no pet policies). The ACAA protects individuals by allowing ESAs to fly with them in the cabin of an airplane without having to pay additional fees. ESAs are not required to be professionally trained. An owner can train the pet. A letter of need written by a mental health counselor may be required for those wanting to transport via plane or for landlords. For information regarding the legalities of ESA contact maggihall14@gmail.com.

My foster mom laughs at me when I knock over all the toy bins so I can add to my stash.  She says I'm like a toddler who scatters stuff all around but she loves me anyway!  I came from a Tennessee puppy mill where I didn't have toys or people to love me so I'm making up for lost time!  I'm only two years old and like to refer to myself as \"big boned\"; I do enjoy a good meal!  Mom's been trying to keep me on a diet but I steal the other dogs' food when she's not looking.  :-)   I am a bit mischevious but I think it adds to my charm!  Don't you?  I like playing with my doggy friends & exploring in the yard but I would be happy as an only dog as well as long as there were...can you guess?...toys!!!  My adoption fee is $200; I've been (gulp) neutered, microchipped and am current on vaccinations as well as heartworm/flea preventative.  You can find an application at waldosmuttleycrew.org.  Won't you be my \"furever\" family?
