name: Sprinkles
description:
**Please read Sprinkle's entire profile, which includes a link to the adoption application. Thank you!** 

Sprinkles is a 11-month-old, 50-pound Shar-pei mix gal.

Hello! Some people call me Coco, but I like my nickname âSprinklesâ better. Let me tell you a little about myself. I am from a southern Tennessee county, where there is no animal control and strays and unwanted animals are in abundance. My mom had me and my siblings last fall at a nice ladies house. One by one my siblings were given away until only I was left. I donât know why no one wanted me, I was just as playful and loving as the others. 

So, day after day I waited for my turn. Then, suddenly one day a strange lady drove up the driveway and I was put into the back of her car. I was really nervous because I did not know what to expect. She took me to her house where I met lots of dogs and cats who made me feel at ease. The kind lady told me that I was her new foster pup and that I would never have to live outside again and that she loved me. 

She LOVED me! It was so nice to hear! I am currently working on becoming the perfect family member.   I get into my crate with no problem and I am house trained.   I love playing with the other dogs.   I haven't been around kids but my foster thinks I will do well with older kids (only because of my size).  I am learning to be the best pup I can everyday! I am looking for a fur-ever family where I can continue to learn and grow.  Could you be my fur-ever family?
 

Sprinkles will be UTD on vaccinations and spayed or neutered at the time of adoption. Due to the young age of this puppy, he/she is not housebroken or trained. All puppies require professional training to become the best family member they can be.
To adopt or learn more about Sprinkles, you must fill out an adoption application. To find the application, copy and paste this URL into your browser: WWW.GDRNE.COM/ADOPTION-APPLICATION [Adoption Fee: $425]  **  PLEASE READ: If a dog is listed, then s/he is currently available for adoption. Their information is correct to the best of our abilities and the information we have been given as of the day of posting. Please note, GDRNE does not guarantee the breed of any dog or puppy unless stated that we have run DNA. All breeds listed are educated estimates. Our dogs are rescued from various situations. It is most likely that both their parents were strays and even if not, mixes of some sort and that their grandparents were mixes as well. The dog may have some genetic material of an American Staffordshire Terrier (pit bull). The dogs are usually mixes of many breeds, making them a breed all their own - a True and adorable American MUTT. If you are interested in this dog, you must submit an application. Great Dog is not a shelter so there is no building you can visit. Our dogs live in private foster homes until adopted. To learn more about our *shelterless* rescue, adoption fees, and procedures, review the list of Frequently Asked Questions on our website at WWW.GDRNE.COM.

I am a little on the shy side so I need a family with lots of patience so that I can take all the time I need warm up. Once I get to know you I am as sweet as pie! I love going on long walks and running around the big yard we have here. I really hope my forever family comes to adopt me soon. Call or visit the shelter with any questions. Petfinder inquiries will not be answered due to volume. Primary Color: Brown Secondary Color: White Age: 2yrs 3mths 1wks Animal has been Neutered

name: Ozzy
description: Hey guys! My name is Ozzy. I came all the way from Tennessee to find my forever family. Unfortunately I keep yelling for Sharon but she never comes to see me! Maybe my family will come find me before she does. I am a very handsome puppy who needs an experienced home to help me learn how to be the best dog ever! Maybe even going home with another dog will help me! Having a puppy is a lot of work so I hope my new family is patient with me while I am learning. If you are interested in me please come visit me at the shelter! Don't hesitate I heard puppies go really fast here at SAVE!! Call or visit the shelter with any questions. Petfinder inquiries will not be answered due to volume. Primary Color: Brown Secondary Color: White Weight: 20lbs Age: 0yrs 3mths 1wks Animal has been Neutered

name: Lemaster Steele
description:
Hi, my name is Lemaster Steele but foster mom calls me either Lemmy or Lem. She only uses my full name if I get into something that I shouldn't be messing with. I am a 2 year old border collie, boxer, lab mix from Tennessee. I am about 32 pounds and was born on July 2, 2017. I couldn't wait until July 4th for the entire world to celebrate my birthday so I came 2 days early.

When I first meet a human I may be a little quiet. When I become comfortable I will bark to let them know when a stranger comes near the house. I also will bark for a little while when my human leaves the house because I would much rather be with them than left home alone. If I have a companion dog I will feel a little more comfortable when my human leaves the house.

It wouldn't be good for me to go to a home with cats as they do not like me always chasing them around which is what I really love to do all the time.

I am very inquisitive so if you wouldn't like any edible items to disappear when you are not around, please don't leave them out within my reach.

My foster mom is teaching me the word \"Wait\" so she can open the door and go out and in before me so that I don't accidentally trip her by speeding out ahead of her. When she says the word \"Okay\" then I can join her outside or inside. I also have learned to sit and wait while my food dish is put down and then I start eating when the word \"Okay\" is said.

I am a very active little fellow so if my human lives in a house with a fenced yard to run around in, it would make me really happy.

I do occasionally enjoy just chilling on the couch with my family watching television or a video or just sleeping in bed with them. I also walk well on a leash, am house-trained, crate-trained, love chasing vermin in the yard, going on car rides and chewing on my Nylabone. I do like playing with toys but do not know how to fetch yet.

This is just a little bit about me. As you can see, I am an all around great guy who would love to find a loving family, preferably with another dog, who will welcome me into their home.

If you are intrigued by what I told you and would like to meet me, just fill out an adoption application at www.ehrdogs.org and don't forget to put my name, Lemaster Steele on it. When it is approved, it will be forwarded to my foster mom who will contact you and arrange a date and time for us to meet.

I am anxiously waiting to hear from you...

name: PUPPY KENZIE-FOSTER NEEDED
description: Sweet Kenzie is 1 of 9 puppies that were rescued from a very rural area in Tennessee where they were dumped and left to survive on their own. This 8-9 month old pup weighs 38 lbs now and will probably top off around 50. Thankfully a Critter Cavalry Rescue foster mom was notified of the NINE, yes NINE, dogs that were running loose and just trying to survive. Kenzie was one of the more socialized puppies that responded to love and kindness. She is really sweet and getting used to wearing a collar. This girl will be ready for walking and enjoying her leadership guidance from a family very soon. She is all puppy and will need just the basic training. She is a little shy but just wants to be part of everything. At the moment of 9/16, but she is not house trained. She is a Hound/Lab mix that just demonstrates the beauty and uniqueness of a MUTT! She will give you everything and expect nothing.

name: Annabelle (Puppy)
description:
Annabelle was rescued from a rural Tennessee animal shelter. 

To schedule a meet n greet please fill out this form https://tinyurl.com/keelysadoptionday

name: FRIENDLY FRANKLIN
description:
Friendly Frank is a handsome 7 year old American Bulldog/Beagle mix that has the most wonderful smile and sweet personality on the planet. This 40 pound boy has been in a family setting with his brother since he was just 4-5 weeks old. He and his brother were adopted together and have lived as a pair for the past 7 years with one major problem.his brother picks on him and beats up him almost weekly. Now with a new baby in the home and training advice that has not really worked. the mom and dad think that Frank needs a new home of his own so the fights don't continue and one day involve their human child. Frank and everyone else will live a much more peaceful life if he finds a great new home. The reason you should consider Friendly Frank is this.he is the BEST and HAPPIEST dog ever. Just look at his smile! He is a great combination of the Beagle joy and warmth and the chunky build and coloring of an American Bulldog with a little stubbornness thrown in for Bulldog good measure. He is perfection when it comes to housebreaking, sleeping all night in his dog bed (which he loves), good with other dogs (unless they jump on him) and he is just a loving soul that will bring good things to your life. It is best that Frank finds a new home where he does not live in fear of getting jumped on by his brother. This love bug deserves to have a family with children or maybe an empty nest couple that will enjoy his fun personality and playful nature and energy. Critter Cavalry Rescue wants to help this special family and special dog find some peace by rehoming Friendly Frank. Frank is fully vetted and neutered and just a happy and loving soul. This boy has many years ahead of him and if you are interested please email at ccrtennessee@gmail.com
PLEASE NOTE: Our dogs are transported from Tennessee to meeting places in the states where we have posted. Further information about us is given on our Adopt-A-Pet site. The adoption fees vary and will be provided as well as noted on the application you receive. Contact us at 615-661-5333 or ccrnewengland@gmail.com Sorry, we cannot adopt to MA residents.

name: PRINCESS NELL-FOSTER NEEDED
description:
Princess Nell is a young, 1 year old, Black and Tan Coonhound that apparently had puppies recently but we are sure about their fate. This girl was starved when we found her in a rural area of Tennessee running loose and very scared and hungry. We worried about where her puppies were and left her for a day or two in hopes she would lead us to her pups. That never happened. Her current weight of 40lbs is very very low for what her breed typically should be which is 65-70lbs. Aside from that, little is known about her previous life and so we will put that in the rearview mirror and go forward with great hopes for a miracle new home for her. She has taken to her foster mom and is good with other dogs and cats. She already has proven to have a desire to be loyal to those that love her and will even try to give a hug with her long thin limbs. She is the most kind and grateful and sweet girl who is desperately longing for her one and only forever family!! Now she is getting the care that she needs. Thankfully she is heartworm negative and otherwise healthy despite her low weight. We have promised her a loving home and a forever future with a committed person or family. Is that you!? She does need a fenced yard for safe exercise time and containment. Please email us at ccrtennessee@gmail.com She is ready to be adopted on September 13th and can transport northward from Tennessee.
ADOPTION FEE REQUIRED. Contact ccrtennessee@gmail.com.

name: Smokey
description:
Meet Smokey. He is a super sweet 6 year old boxer mix. He is an owner surrender from rural Tennessee. He is neutered and will be up to date with shots and heartworm tested before going home. He walks well on a leash and loves kids and other dogs. He currently being kept outside, but should pick up on house training fairly quickly!

To schedule a meet n greet please fill out this form https://tinyurl.com/keelysadoptionday

name: PETEE
description: Meet Petee a super sweet and shy little Chihuahua mix guy that is just 3 years old and weighs 12 lbs. This little guy came from a high-kill shelter in rural Tennessee. He was so lonely and so very scared in the shelter. He did not trust anyone. With some patience from his foster mom, he is starting to come around. He loves to play with other dogs and he is warming up to people. Petee is learning that people are nice and he really loves to be petted. He is still timid around strangers and is not sure about being picked up but he is a loving guy once he knows that you are not going to hurt him. Petee is fully grown. He needs a loving family to come to his aid and give him a the wonderful loving forever home he so deserves, He would be a great and loving little guy in the right home. if you have another dog to help show him the ropes and give him confidence that would be ideal. He would not be a good candidate for a family with small children. Petee would also be best in a home with a fenced in yard. He is smart and knows how to use a doggie door. He is also crate trained. Won't you consider adding the precious boy to your family!! To learn more about Petee please contact Vivienne at viviennejames@comcast.net or 615/943-7311. ADOPTION FEE REQUIRED.

name: XP Sami or Spanky in Tennessee - URGENT!
description:
URGENT! These 2 dogs are in Tennessee but are in desperate need of rehoming separately! The owner must leave her home on July 1st and these dogs still need places to go - a number of other animals in the home have already found placement but no one will give these dogs a chance. The owner does not want to drop them off at a shelter in Tennessee, if she can avoid it.

Sami is a senior Black Lab mix who is extremely skittish but lovable. He gets along with most dogs. Over the years he has gotten along with all the animals on my parents' farm except for Spanky.

We're not sure what Spanky is mixed with. He is about 5-7 years old. He is playful and lovable. He has gotten along with his playmate Si but does not like Sami. He loves to carry his blanket with him. He is a really good farm dog - he always knows when coyotes are on the property and is great at chasing them away from their goats. He is a drooler especially when he is happy.

These dogs do NOT belong to 11th Hour Rescue but we have been asked to help network them for separate adopters. If you can help at all, please contact Jesse directly at jess85_19@hotmail.com - the animals are currently located in Tennessee. These dogs should go to separate homes as they prefer the company of other dogs to each other.

There are also 5 cats in need of placement - they are siblings, male and neutered, about 3.5 years old. There are 2 beige, 2 with grey/white stripes and one all grey stripe. All are friendly although the all grey is still a little cranky but he is coming around. They are all indoor cats, they have never been outside. They are listed on EHR's web site under XP 5 Cats in Tennessee.

name: HANK
description:
Meet Happy Hank! A truly handsome 8 month old, 33 pound, strong and handsome Border Collie mix boy that needs a good B/C knowledgeable owner. He is smart and eager to learn and needs an alpha person in his life. He was found as a stray in a rural setting in Tennessee after he was seen being tossed from a moving car near a retail store on a highway. This boy is happy and healthy now and loves playing with other dogs. He loves to flip over for his humans to show submission to them and to beg for a good belly rub. He will pull at first on his leash walks but quickly settles down and stops pulling if you do it on a regular basis. He loves to play like most young herding dogs do. This boy needs to be with experienced dog owners or else his smart Border Collie instincts will take over and lead the household. He is food protective with other dogs. He needs to be fed separately as we recommend this for any multiple dog home during feeding time. Happy Hank would be an exceptionally good dog for Fly Ball training, agility or perhaps Dock Diving competition. The sky is the limit with this young and impressionable and moldable boy!
If you are interested please email us at: Ccrtennessee@gmail.com He is located in Tennessee and can transport northward at any time. Local Tennessee adoptions are welcome as well.

name: Ryder
description:
Ryder is a fun little Yorkie / Lab Mix (yes we know interesting mix .. mom was apparently a lab and dad was the Yorkie).  Ryder  was born on April 10, 2019 and is looking for his forever home.  We expect he will be a small / medium when full grown.

Ryder  loves playing with his siblings and toys.  He can be a bit shy at first, but warms up quickly. Ryder is up to date on shots, neutered, on heartworm and flea and tick prevention and is micro chipped as well.

Ryder is not potty trained, that is something that his new family will have to work on him with.  Preference will be given to those with a physically fenced yard, but Ryder we think will stay small enough to be suitable for apartment / townhouse living as well with the right outdoor space.

Ryder is currently located in Tennessee and the adoption fee is $250.  Transportation may be available to out of state adopters for an additional cost depending on the area. The first step in our process is submitting the application.  We are happy to set up a meet and greet once an application has been approved. If you would like to adopt Ryder  please fill out our online adoption application at http://safehaventn.com/ .

name: Nike
description:
Nike is a sweet mix pup that may have some Catahoula, cur or shepherd in him. Breeds are just a guess, we have no history to know what his parents were. He is about 30 lbs and 6 months old.

Nike was the runt of his litter and it took him a little bit longer to get his grown on!  He is a sweet pup who loves to play and cuddle.  He would love another dog to play with a fenced yard for his new family.  We expect he will be medium sized when full grown.

Nike is up to date on shots, neutered, micro chipped, on flea and tick and heart worm prevention.  Nike is working on potty training and this is something that he will still need help with as he transitions to a new family.

Nike is currently located in Tennessee and the adoption fee is $250.  Transportation may be available to out of state adopters for an additional cost depending on the area. name: Bojangles
description:
Bojangles is a fetching 7 month old pup and is about 55 lbs.  While we are not sure on breed, husky mix or GSD mix make our short list.  We expect he will be medium/large sized when full grown.  He is neutered, up to date on shots, micro chipped and on heart worm prevention.

We found Bojangles in a rural Louisiana shelter and he was listed as deaf and just 6 weeks old.  Luckily we had a local foster who was able to go and pull him and foster him for the first few weeks until he could make his way to TN.

Once here, we discovered that he does have some hearing ability.  He has been fostered with a dog trainer who has been working with him on both clicker, whistle and remote vibration collar training.  We don't know how his hearing will progress or digress as he gets older, so any family who adopts sweet Bo must continue working on his training.  His trainer has offered to help Bo's new family with training techniques and routines to help them get on the right track. We are working on potty training, but that is something that will need to be continued in her new home with lots of love and support.

Bo is a sweet and loving pup who is excelling in his foster home and with his training.  He is smart and eager to learn.  He is crate and leash trained.  He does well with other dogs, cats and kids and would do best with another young companion dog to play with.  To try to keep Bo as safe as possible, we are requiring a physically fenced in yard.  We also would prefer to adopt him out within a 2 hour radius of Cookeville, TN due to his special needs.

Bojangles is currently located in Tennessee and the adoption fee is $250.  Transportation may be available to out of state adopters for an additional cost depending on the area. The first step in our process is submitting the application.  We are happy to set up a meet and greet once an application has been approved. If you would like to adopt Bojangles please fill out our online adoption application at http://safehaventn.com/ .

name: Wendy
description:
Wendy is a sweet girl who we are thinking has some Catahoula or Aussie in her.  She is about 40 lbs, 6 months old and will be large size when full grown. She gets along great with her siblings and is always up for an adventure.

Wendy is up to date on her shots, spayed, micro chipped and on flea/tick and heart worm prevention as well.  We are looking for an active home with a physically fenced yard.  She is going to love being part of a home with activity and play.  She loves snuggling up on the couch with you at night.  She is house trained with a doggy door.

Wendy is currently located in Tennessee and the adoption fee is $250.  Transportation may be available to out of state adopters for an additional cost depending on the area. The first step in our process is submitting the application.  We are happy to set up a meet and greet once an application has been approved. If you would like to adopt Wendy please fill out our online adoption application at http://safehaventn.com/ .

name: Zeke
description:
Zeke is a little lover boy. Loves to give kisses. Enjoys Napping  and sleeping with his humans. Plays well with his other foster pups and dogs. He needs to have a fenced in yard. For he enjoys chasing squirrels, playing ball and chasing leaves.He is Up to date on his shot, neutered, flea and heart worm prevention. Not positive if that is what breed Zeke is that is a guess. We are looking for a physically fenced yard for Zeke and he would love a furry companion to play with!  He will be small/medium sized when full grown.

Zeke currently located in Tennessee and the adoption fee is $250. Transportation may be available to out of state adopters for an additional cost depending on the area. The first step in our process is submitting the application. We are happy to set up a meet and greet once an application has been approved. If you would like to adopt Zeke please fill out our online adoption application at http://safehaventn.com/

name: Mustard
description:
Mustard was part of a pair. He came in with Brit but after an evaluation period, we found them not to be a bonded pair. Mustard is 11 years
but acts like he is 8.
. Mustard is a friendly outgoing guy who is happy and a wiggle butt. he is on the tall side. He was owner by the same family all of his life but was made to live outdoors until they moved and then he journeyed his way from Texas to Las Vegas. Now he is looking for a home to spend the rest of his life in. He does well with other dogs but is also quite independent. We just had the holistic dentist clean up his teeth.

adoption fee is $200 Adoption fees go back to and cover all of the medical for all of the dogs. All dogs are spayed/neutered, vaccinated and micro chipped upon adoption and many have received further treatment for such things as lump removal, severe ear infections, leg injuries, etc..
For more information or to submit an adoption application, please visit our website at http://www.southernnevadabeaglerescue.com . We are also on Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/SouthernNevadaBeagleRescueFoundation . Come meet and play with our available dogs at Las Vegas area dog parks. Times and locations can be found at http://www.meetup.com/beagles-207/ . Contact us or check our Facebook updates ahead of time if you are interested in meeting a particular dog. All our dogs are in foster homes so not all are available to attend all our park meetups.
Our meetup group playdates allow you to socialize your beagle with his/her own breed at dog parks with large fenced areas where the beagles can run and play off-leash. Beagle enthusiasts, come bay with us..... AROOOOOOOOOOOO!

name: Edsel
description: You know a dog is really nice when her intake exam notes call her \"very sweet\". Edsel came to Best Friends in July 2019 from Texas and has been winning hearts ever since. Edsel has done excellent with a skin treatment that has greatly improved her coat condition. She has started duty as a tour dog, and meets and greets our afternoon visitors with a smile and a wag of her tail. Edsel is much more popular than the namesake car, and will make a great addition to your home.

name: Timmy
description: Gentle, affectionate Timmy is a hugger and a leaner. He just wants to be close to people, and he is happy to do whatever you are doing, whether it's lounging, hiking, training or running. At Dogtown, he has been improving his dog skills, and he's gotten along great with pretty much everyone. Timmy was born in 2016 and came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. He can be a little nervous in new situations, and he likes to jump up and offer hugs, so he is working on his manners and on keeping all four feet on the floor when he greets people. Timmy is crate trained and does great on walks. Because he is smart and loves learning, he has been doing agility training at the Sanctuary. Sweet Timmy is searching for an active home and is sure to make a wonderful companion. Timmy has a very generous sponsor who will cover his adoption and transport costs.

name: Aiden
description: With a wagging tail and a wiggly body, Aiden greets everyone he meets like they are his best friend. He is happiest when he is with people and getting lots of love and attention. Born in 2012, Aiden came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. He is charming and enjoys snuggling, cuddling and car rides. He has a lifelong medical condition, Intervertebral Disc Disease, and needs to have limited physical activity. Leashed walks that are long are fine, but he needs to refrain from running and jumping. Aiden needs physical therapy twice a day to help with his condition that will need to continue once he is in his forever home. \"The greatest thing you'll ever learn is just to love and be loved in return,\" seems to be Aiden's motto.

name: Daniel
description: Daniel is quite an affectionate guy and will climb right into your lap. Once he gets comfortable there, you may have to lure him off with treats. He is a loving dog who bonds strongly with people. Daniel is nervous during storms. He also has some sensitivity in his hind end, so he does not like to be handled there and will give clear signs that he is uncomfortable. However, he loves pets around the head and chest. An energetic guy, Daniel enjoys walks and would do best in an active home. Because he can jump fences, he will need a secure enclosure. He would also do best in an adult-only home due to the sensitivity of his hind end and the fact that he has bitten in the past. Daniel can be picky with his doggie friends, but he can live with other respectful dogs. Born in 2017, he came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. At Dogtown, he is working on crate training and name recognition. In the right household, this sweet and sensitive guy will make a great companion.

name: Dakota
description: Dakota is sweet and curious. She is shy and nervous when meeting strangers. However, she warms up quickly when treats are involved. She likes going for walks on the trails in Dogtown with new people, if they are respectful of her shyness and don't try to pet her too much too soon. Since she is a bit fearful of new people and other dogs, she will need to meet the residents of her new home first at the Sanctuary, as well as any other dogs that presently live in the home. Born in 2017, Dakota came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. She had heartworm disease and has finished up her treatment. She is very food motivated and enjoys enrichment activities with Kong toys and snuffle mats, which help her gain confidence. With a little patience, Dakota is likely to become a braver and more confident sidekick.

name: Tennessee
description: Tennessee loves toys and people. He is playful and gets along well with other dogs. Born in 2015, Tennessee came to Best Friends from a shelter in Texas. This little pocket pitty is always trying to make his human friends laugh with his silly antics. Tennessee enjoys having dog friends and is playful and full of life. Tennessee is currently working on crate training, loose leash walking and clicker training at Dogtown. Youthful and vivacious, Tennessee can't wait to show you how much zest for life he has.

name: Montana
description: You might find Montana perched on her chair inside her room in Dogtown. It's adorable to see, and it seems like Montana loves the view from higher up. Montana is welcoming and friendly, wagging her entire body when she sees a human friend. She is playful, silly, and really enjoys attention from people. When you enter her room, Montana will get down from her chair and be ready to snuggle. Born in 2012, Montana came to Best Friends from a shelter in Texas. She had heartworm disease and just finished up her treatment. She likes to play with other dogs here at the sanctuary, but she has been known to guard things from other dogs. She hasn't shown guarding tendencies with humans, though. Montana is currently working on clicker training, which she shows off when she happily greets the Dogtown tours. Stop by and meet Montana. She just might wag her way into your heart.

name: Mauve
description: If you want a dog who doubles as a blanket and is happy to cuddle with you 24/7, then Mauve is your girl. She's a gentle soul who wants nothing more than to be petted and snuggled for as long as possible. She will sit on your lap and ask for pets for hours if you let her. Mauve was born in 2012, and she doesn't do much running or playing. She's perfectly happy with short walks. She's very mellow but can get sassy and bark for attention. Mauve is so people oriented that she does not like to share people with other dogs. At Dogtown, she has guarded people and the gate from other dogs. She has some separation anxiety and has previously chewed on door frames when she was alone but could hear people nearby. Mauve came to Best Friends from a shelter in Texas. At Dogtown, she is working on crate training to help manage her separation anxiety. She is also on supplements to help improve her skin and coat. She would do well with a person or family who is home most of the time, so she does not need to be left alone for long periods. Mauve might be your perfect match if you're looking for a dog who'll love to veg out with you. Mauve has a generous sponsor who has covered her adoption fee.

name: Abner
description: Abner is a big, goofy hound who doesn't know much about life yet. Born in 2016, he came to Best Friends from a shelter in Texas. He is a bit nervous of new people and new situations and has the potential to be a flight risk if he gets really scared. Abner is just learning how to walk on a leash, so he often runs to and fro trying to see and smell everything. He can be reserved at times and playful at others. At Dogtown, he's getting lots of exposure to new things and new situations. As he's gained confidence, he has started seeking attention from his caregivers. Abner would love a home with a patient person or family who can help him keep building his confidence and finding his way in the world.

name: Kojak
description: Kojak is a genuinely nice dog to have around. He is friendly, engaging and loves getting attention from his caregivers. He has done well with all the dogs he's met at the Sanctuary and would likely be equally happy either in a home with other dogs, or being the only dog. He walks beautifully on his leash and is learning training cues such as \"sit, go to your \"place\" and \"wait\" (for a food bowl). Born in 2013, he came to Best Friends from a rescue organization in Texas that was closing its doors, and he would love to discover the joys of his very own home. Kojak has a generous sponsor who is covering his adoption fee.

name: Wynonna
description: Wynonna is a sweet girl who loves to be with her people. Though she is living as an only dog at the Sanctuary, she may be able to live with the right dog down the road in a home. Above all, she's looking for a patient person or family who can help her with her anxieties. Wynonna is afraid of stormy weather. Medication helps to calm her fears, though she still has a tendency to run away when she is scared. She will need a secure enclosure and someone who will watch over her. Wynonna was born in 2010 and came to us from Texas. She is looking for a safe and understanding home where she can relax and come into her own. Wynonna has a generous sponsor who will cover her adoption costs.

name: NIKO
description:
My name is Niko and if youâre looking for a feisty fireball, I am your guy!  I am three or four years young and around 60 pounds so perfect for someone w a small home or who loves Akitas but wants a smaller one.  What I lack in size, I make up for in personality.  I am happy and playful and ready to love.  A running buddy would be awesome too!  Since I am active, I would be best in a home without super young two legged kids, older kids who I canât accidentally knock over would be ok.  I do NOT like other animals and must be an only pet so that I can have all of your attention!

Some dogs were just left to roam and some dogs were kept in cages to breed.  The conditions for all were horrible and heart breaking.  Spaghetti was beyond skinny.  Her hip bones were protruding and her ribs were showing.  We knew we had to help her.  

Spaghetti made her way to CO to get the vetting she needed and the to start her second chance at life.  She was a little nervous at first, but she has really come out of her shell and started to act like a \"normal\" dog.  She gets along with the doggies in her home and is incredibly loving.  She loves to chase the toys the foster mom throws for her and after her bathes she gets a severe case of the zoomies.  More than anything she loves to snuggle. name: Hammy
description:
The best things come to those who wait . . .

I have no idea who originally said those prophetic words that aim to quell the impatience of humans, but for one special pup, Hammy, truer words have never been spoken. A fine bottle of wine must age for months, sometimes even years, before the liquid settles down and the oxygen fully dissolves and integrates with the wine. This period of time is called \"bottle shock,\" and the intoxicating prize rewarded to those willing to wait until a wine is properly aged is extraordinary.

Fortunately, sweet Hammy just needs a few days, not years, to decompress, integrate, and show you what an incredible, loyal, and intelligent pup she is. This beautiful canine soul has been neglected, went unsterilized and had a litter of puppies at the tender age of just 1 year, was likely kenneled for most of her life as she arrived terrified of stairs (she's mastered them now!), acquired easily-preventable heartworm disease which has since been treated, has healing sores on her hind end from who knows what, and, eventually, she was confiscated from her horrible owners in Texas. Hammy is more than ready to begin anew as a true outdoors-loving Coloradan and we hope you are the perfect person or family to help her forget that terrible life she left behind.

Initially, Hammy may be stand off-ish, reserved, and may even voice her displeasure at significant differences in environment. We call this Hammy's \"bottle shock\" period of time and inevitably it appears each time she moves to a new foster home (even if previously familiar) or experiences a significant change in her life. It lasts 24-48 hours during which time it's best to allow her to decompress by herself in a crate with a soft blanket, give her ample food and water, and leash her to take her outside to use the restroom.

Once Hammy recognizes that her new environment is non-threatening and loving, she will quickly warm up and show her true colors and, they are quite remarkable. Hammy is loyal, loving, and very intelligent. She is potty trained and crate trained although she prefers the company of her humans. She is motivated by food and treats but her true motivation is positive attention and reinforcement - she THRIVES on it. Hammy has a great sense of humor and will engage in play with dogs of all sizes by showing off a toy or ball and then running away, hoping they will give chase. Her favorites canines tend to be larger pups that enjoy a good wrestle in the yard. She enjoys car rides with her head hanging out the window and tongue flapping in the wind as much as a quiet, cozy snuggle session or vigorous belly rub. Most of all, Hammy just wants to love and be loved in return.

Like a fine wine, Hammy needs someone with a bit of patience, a confident demeanor that balances discipline and training, and a loving heart and home that is willing to allow this sweet girl to take her time acclimating to a new environment. Shiraz, Merlot, or Cabernet would have been a more appropriate name for this sweet ginger girl but her previous humans had no clue what a fine canine they missed out on because they never gave her the chance to shine. Will you?

description:
Shasta is available for adoption through Colorado Canine Rescue, a nonprofit rescue in the Denver area. He came from a crowded shelter in Texas where she was turned in as a stray. Since we have little history on him, we are estimating his age to be around five years old and guessing his breeds to be a Husky/Samoyed mix.

Shasta is a sweet, loving boy with beautiful blue eyes. He has had a rough life. He was picked up as a stray in Texas where he was likely hit by a car. His injuries were untreated and his pelvis healed on its own, so he struggles a bit on stairs. He is currently in a foster home where he is finally able to give and receive lost of love and attention. He is incredibly sweet with all humans.

While he is usually dog-friendly, he doesn't love all dogs and takes longer to warm up to some dog personalities. Given that, he will need to go to a family as the only dog. Due to his old injury, he has some minor urinary incontinence when he sleeps which has greatly improved with medicine. He is house-trained, and loves sleeping on hard-wood floors which makes his occasional incontinence easier to clean up! When Shasta came to CCR, he tested positive for heartworm. He's since completed the heartworm treatment and needs to be retested in October. If positive, CCR can cover cost of next treatment (antibiotics most likely) through our approved vets. He also had surgery to correct entropion and is healed from that. This sweet fellow is gentle, smart, and knows basic commands (sit, down, wait, etc). He has had a rough start to life and just wants someone to love him and smother him with cuddles.

If you are interested in adopting Shasta, please submit an adoption application located on our website, coloradocaninerescue.org. We are asking for a $100 adoption donation. Shasta is neutered, up to date on vaccinations and microchipped.

I'm 3 years old and weigh about 45 pounds. I'm house-trained, crate-trained and spayed. These days I'm all big smiles!

I'm always ready for adventure when out and about, but also love snuggling up on the couch with my people and relaxing. 

I love tossing around my fluffy duck toy, chewing on big bones and Kongs, and snoozing in the patches of sun around the house. I walk nicely on a leash (unless there are bunnies - but hey, who can resist bunnies!) and get good zoomies when I'm running around the yard. 

My foster mom says I'm the total package: able to keep up on adventures, trustworthy, snuggly, and adjusting very well. She says I'm super smart, eager to work, and really athletic. She thinks I'd love agility, treibball and freestyle! I've tried barn hunt, which is really fun, too! My ideal home would be one that's committed to giving me plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and positive training. 

I am trustworthy alone at home for reasonable amounts of time while my foster mom works, and sometimes she even takes me to the office with her, where I love getting attention from all her coworkers. Did I mention how much I love my people? It's not necessary for you to have another dog in your home, as I can go either way - both with other dogs and just on my own with you! Like many heelers, I can be dog-selective, though. Look, you don't like everyone you meet, do you? So introductions to other dogs must be done with knowledgeable supervision. I do go to daycare twice a week and everyone there LOVES me, but in big playgroups, I get a little worked up. Oh, and because of that bunny prey-drive thing, I probably wouldn't be the best fit for a home with small dogs unless you're willing to do very careful introductions.

Unfortunately, I didn't get the best start in life. I was found running around in rural Texas with a bullet wound in my hip! Can you believe someone would do that to such a pretty girl? My foster people think I was probably just doing what my breed is meant to do: chase cows! Isn't it fun to see them run and hear them go \"mooooooo!\" when you nip at them?? I was just trying to live my best life... 

So speaking of herding, I am really good at it. Like, amazing. I was born this way! So when we're out walking and a runner or bike or car passes us, I want to herd them... really badly... like really, really badly... My foster mom doesn't like this; she says I send her to the chiropractor every week because when I try to herd these moving things, I lunge to the end of my leash and bark and don't let up until they go away! (Don't worry, though, I watch carefully to see if they're coming back!) It's super fun, I don't know why she doesn't like it. Anyway, my people are teaching me to \"leave it,\" which is boring, but sometimes it's worth it for my paycheck - chicken!!! In the meantime, I don't go for walks in busy places with lots of bikes, like Marshall Mesa or Boulder Creek Path. My foster mom says I might be able to some day, with lots and lots of training and some maturity. Gosh, what do I need, a Ph-freaking-D??? (Yes, says mom.) She also says that giving me enough exercise is a delicate balance of just enough, but not too much so that I'm completely overstimulated, and things that tire out my brain, not just my body.

I'm also terrible on car rides. Usually, getting in the car means we're going somewhere awesome (a new place to hike, or maybe doggie daycare!!!), and I get so excited that I bark my head off and squeal (I have the most beautiful voice, if I do say so myself, and sometimes it's nice just to hear it!)... And sometimes I get frustrated and bark when we pass those pesky bikes. Come on, Mom! Just let me at 'em... I'm better if I can't see out of the car, though, so if you can crate me in the back of your SUV, I'm okay.

So you might be catching on to the fact that my first couple of years were a little rough. No one really taught me self control or how to channel my energy and instincts, so I just let my freak flag fly, and they sent me to the pound! Luckily, SDR took me in, fixed me up, treated my heartworm (whatever that is; all I know is that I feel MUCH better these days) and sent me on my way to my forever home. My ideal home would be in a quieter neighborhood (preferably rural - I'm a country girl from Texas at heart, after all) with people who are committed to lovingly helping me learn how to function better in the busy Colorado lifestyle. It would also be great to have a big yard with a tall wooden fence, too. If I can't see those bikes going by, then I won't try to chase them, and maybe I'll finally relax a little! (If you live in an apartment/condo or a busy area, please don't apply for Daisy unless you have plenty of heeler and/or dog training experience.)

Did I mention I like to snuggle? If snuggling was a Nobel Prize category, I would probably win it every year (and spend the money on bones). As for the other stuff, it makes my people really happy when I work hard at it, and I live to please my people, so I guess I'll keep at it.

Check out my very own video above made by Summit Dog's extraordinary videographers/editors, Molly Steele and Maddie Steele!

For more info and/or to apply to adopt me, go to https://www.summitdogrescue.org/meet-daisy.html

description:

Marlin is reactive to other dogs (and cats) but was acclimated to a foster home with two small dogs after very slow introductions. He is a little pushy with them but all live together peacefully the confident dog is very comfortable with Marlin but the submissive dog is intimidated by him. Because Marlin likes to learn and requires a lot of stimulation, he would do better in a house with no pets or children so he can get enough attention to nurture his talents and desire to work. Due to foot nipping and attention seeking, Marlin would not do well with young children. 

Marlin needs a structured home with a master who is patient, loving and willing to continue training at home or in the classroom. Marlin is crate trained and potty trained and loves to cuddle. He is a sweetheart looking for the right home and is willing to wait for the perfect match. Marlin wants to be a superstar and asks you to view his latest movie.

https://www.dropbox.com/s/7ccgatu8wkacpjp/Marlin%20PAWS%20New%20England%20movie%202019%20fall.mp4?dl=0

Name: Marlin
Breed: Terrier mix
Sex: Male
Age: 4 years old
Weight: 11 pounds
Spayed/Neutered: Yes
Vaccinations: Up to date
Heartworm: Negative
Microchipped: Yes


BASED ON OUR OBSERVATIONS: 
Dogs: Only with very slow introductions (small dogs)
Cats: No
Kids: No


Adoption Donation: 450.00

 
 
IMPORTANT INFORMATION:
Interested in a specific dog, please fill out an application if you are interested in a dog. The number of individual inquiries is overwhelming and we are finding it difficult to respond to each one. We cannot guarantee you will receive a timely response.
 
Paws New England is a rescue, not a shelter, and as such we do not have our dogs housed in one location - they are in foster homes both in New England and in our southern foster homes. If you're interested in a specific dog, please complete a short online application and you will receive a reply within 48 hours so you can ask questions.
 
At present, if a dog is listed on our website, the dog is considered still available HOWEVER, may have applications that have come in before yours but it's still too early to know if any are a good match; therefore we encourage you to apply.
 

NOTICE WITH REGARD TO LOCATION OF DOGS: Please note: Paws New England is a foster-based rescue. We do not have a brick and mortar building to house the dogs we rescue. We have found that dogs in foster homes are much more adoptable because they have been observed in a home setting. Dogs listed with Paws New England typically reside in various locations throughout the south (primarily Tennessee, Texas, and Arkansas) and New England (not necessarily in the state of Rhode Island). You will be notified by the adoption coordinator of the location of the dog you are interested in so you have the ability to decide whether to pursue adoption or not.

Dogs transported to New England are done so at a fee of $150.00 paid directly to the transporting company by Paws New England; no additional transport costs are responsibility of adopter. This fee is included in the adoption donation.

Adoption donations cover pre-adoption vet costs (including vaccinations, spay/neuter when age appropriate, and heartworm testing/treatment when necessary), a microchip, and transportation to New England if necessary.

Donations for our young, healthy puppies and dogs support their fellow canines of advanced age or suffering from injuries and abuse whose donations are reduced but whose veterinary costs are typically much higher. We appreciate your understanding that your dog will help others in need.

All known information about the animal is listed above. We do our best to give accurate information, but most of our dogs are rescues and do not come with a known history.

Paws New England abides by the dog importation regulations set forth in the states of MA, CT, NH and RI.

description: You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Gorgeous Hallie is a one year old Pit mix who weighs 30 pounds. She comes into rescue from Texas. She presented with some neurological symptoms. Hallie spent a few weeks at our San Antonio vet Partner and it was discovered that she was partially blind and deaf. She stumbled a lot and needed further diagnostic testing with a specialty hosp in NY. The specialist has determined that Hallie suffered from some type of trauma to the skull which is what is causing her issues. Sadly we think that she suffered this injury at the hands of humans or possibly suffered some type of brain infection that was never treated. Now we are dealing with her issues head on and she seems to be doing better. She has vision in one eye, and she stumbles less. name: Simba (TX)
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Handsome Simba, born in 2016, is a Chow mix weighing in at about 50 pounds. He comes into rescue from Texas. This sweet boy only knew a life of suffering and neglect and we are so happy we have the opportunity to give him the amazing new life he deserves! He really is a stunning boy with his fluffy coat and that cute black tongue that gives away the Chow in him! He can be shy and nervous with new people and surroundings and requires a slow and patient approach. Because he has a \"warm up\" period, Simba would do best in a home with kids 10 and up. He eats well and is very active, but does sleep well through the night. He really enjoys a nice belly/butt scratch session and is so appreciative to get some good loving! He is neutered and up to date on vaccines. If you are looking for a loving and loyal companion to add to your family, then Simba is the one for you! Lucky for this boy he is safe with us now and is currently in a loving foster home. Salvatore has been diagnosed with idiopathic epilepsy brought on by the trauma. He is on anti-seizure medication for epilepsy and has been seizure free for a while. He is not a fan of city traffic or noise and does not like car rides. He would do well in a quiet neighborhood. Are you the lucky family that can give Salvatore all the unconditional love that he is so deserving of? Despite the neglect he has endured and the pain he suffered, Salvatore is a very sweet boy. He is wonderful with people of all ages, other small dogs as long as they are more on the mellow side, and he even loves cats! He is a very chill and low key guy, is not destructive at all, is house trained, and will make the best new snuggle partner! name: Skyy
description:
Name: Skyy

Approximate Age: Approx. 2yrs old

Breed: Pit mix

Sex: Female

Special Needs: Allergies

Adoption fee: $300.00

Up to date on vaccinations/preventatives, spayed, house/crate trained, microchipped

I came to the rescue back in 2016 from a high kill shelter in Texas. The conditions werent the best to say the least and oh yeah, I was SUPER pregnant. Not a good place for a expecting mom. Thankfully, I was taken from there just in time and was able to have my puppies in a foster home. I was even thrown a huge baby shower by a ton of people who follow SNARR! I was so happy to finally have had my babies and be out of the shelter but my excitement quickly became tragedy. Not long after giving birth, almost half of my babies passed away- only 4 survived. 
Now that my remaining pups have gone to live their own liveshere I sit and wait. While I adore my foster mom, I want a home to call my own. 
Im confused on why I dont have my own home yet Im incredibly adorable and Im hands down the most wiggly tushed pocket pittie youll ever meet! I have never met a person I didnt like, however dogs.not too fond of dogs or any other furry little creatures. I blame that on my high prey drive and Im very smart when it comes down to it- I can be a pro stalker and Im lightning fast so its best that the temptation isnt there in forever home. Give me any kind of human though and its nothing but hugs (literally, I give hugs) and kisses! 
Due to having allergies, I take Benedryl and cannot eat chicken.

Transport to any approved home within the US can be provided at no additional fee
Currently Skyy is located in Lawrenceville, Georgia.


Please visit SNARRANIMALRESCUE.org to fill out an adoption application and our adoption requirements/process can also be found there!

name: Queenie
description:
Queenie is a spectacular pet in need of a home experienced with German Shepherds.   She is a protective girl who is not very stranger tolerant, so the meet-and-greet procedure with her must be more drawn out and she belongs only in a home comfortable with not allowing strangers to make direct contact with their dog.  Other than that, she is pretty close to perfect.  She can be in public settings where strangers are respectfully hands off.  Approximately four years old, she was pulled from a high kill shelter in Texas heavily pregnant and successfully raised a litter of puppies while being a wonderful mom.  She is now ready to move onto a forever ending of her own :)  She is purebred, although her ears did fail to stand, and a real deal GSD.   She is GREAT company - very playful, joyful and extremely affectionate.  If a German Shepherd can be merry, that would be her.  She is highly intelligent (both the good and the bad....she is an escape artist who can range from smart to daring), very responsible, forms a strong bond, and is an energetic girl with an extremely playful and fun personality.   For the breed, she is not a noisy dog, does great with other dogs, and is ok around cats. Older children only, please, as toddlers make her nervous.  

THE RIGHT HOME for Queenie needs to have breed experience.  Queenie is territorial and protective by her nature.  When displaced, she forms a strong bond, but meet-and-greets will require patience and understanding as she is not receptive to strangers.  This is a higher energy girl who belongs with someone active.  She crates well and is overall a good housedog, but if bored and under stimulated will be destructive.  She will do fine in a home with another  dog and has learned not to bother cats, but she should not be around smaller children - they are very foreign to her and she finds their movements unsettling.  If you need a dog who can thrive in social settings, she is not the dog for you as while she can be socialized better with strangers, her social circle being an elite group of knowns is inherent to both her and the breed itself.  If, however, you seek a adventurous companion, up for anything, who bonds strongly and is extremely loyal, she could be the dog for you.

Applications are available on the southpawsexpress.org website or by contacting Lucy at maramuser@gmail.com.  Her adoption fee is $450.

description:
Meet Waylon! He is approximately 4-5 years old and weigh around 65 pounds but needs to gain a few pounds. Waylon came from a VERY BAD backyard breeding situation in Texas. He was one of roughly 25 dogs living on a property with chainlink runs and nothing for shade but some blue plastic barrels tossed into the runs. (See photos). Waylon has definitely lived a life of neglect. He had fleas, hair loss, horrible infected ears and eyes and isn't quite sure what being pet is all about. He however has no desire to run from you and doesn't have a mean bone in his body. As each day goes by and he feels a little better he is getting more and more curious about being in a home and following his foster mom around. He's also training her about when he needs to go out by going to the door and barking. While Waylon has had a horrible life, he will know nothing but love, regular meals and a safe place to sleep from here on out.

Disclaimer: Please know this is a recently rescued dog that is still transitioning into a new home environment. Training, and even personality and energy levels are constantly evolving as the dog starts to feel better emotionally and physically. Your new dog will take days or even weeks to fully settle into his or her true self. What you read in this bio is a snapshot of this dogâs evolving personality. Additionally, the age listed is an estimate provided by the shelter and/or veterinarian. Different vets can provide different age estimates. So always consider the lab you are adopting to be within an age range of a couple of years of what is listed. Also remember, while we are a lab rescue, we do not have papers on these dogs, we cannot confirm any breed specific claims, and many of these dogs may be mixed with other breeds.

name: Max 0967
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Max is an amazing dog. He loves spending his days playing with his foster brother and sister and his evenings on the couch cuddled right next to you. He does well keeping up with our two Belgian Malinois as they are very gentle with him. Max is a little vocal and will bark if he feels like he isn't getting enough attention or he is too far away from his foster family on the couch. If it was up to him, he would be pet and cuddled all day long. If he goes home to a family with dogs, the dogs will have to be ok with Max always wanting the most attention.

Like any young puppy, Max is teething and loves to have a toy to chew on but does not chew on our furniture. He is crate trained and house trained as long as you are diligent about taking him out within reason. He is interested in our cats and wants to play with them. He would do well in a home with a cat who will not put up with his shenanigans.

Max does still have a limp but has adapted to his injuries very well. He can do the stairs but cannot jump on the couch by himself yet. Max will start physical therapy and will continue to show us how resilient and strong he is.

We have taken Max out to socialize and he does really well with children of all ages and other dogs besides our own.

Max was rescued from a high kill shelter in Texas after being hit by a car. Shortly after rescue the local ER told SSR his pelvis had shattered into his spine and he would never make a recovery. We were urged to euthanize Max, but we decided a second opinion was vital before making such permanent decisio
ns and sent him to San Antonio. Our vet there offered to take him home as a foster and we are so happy to report that he is 100% on the way to a full recovery! Per our surgeon, there is no need to surgically correct his injuries and to allow a natural healing process.

Max arrived in Virginia on July 25th.

name: Sheba 0725
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Hi there. I'm Sheba. I was picked up as a stray in Texas in July and brought to my foster home at the end of October. I am spayed and have never been pregnant so I was likely not a stray for very long. I am heartworm positive, but will he treated by SSR

I had an interesting first 24 hours with my new foster dad. He picked me up from the nice ladies who drove me all the way from Texas to Virginia and took me straight to a place where I got a bath. I was very good for my bath and allowed him to do all the things that he had to do to get me \"clean\". I thought I was just fine the way I was but the warm water was nice. I then met the 2 owners of the house, Duke who is a German Shepherd like me and Lily who is a Border Collie mix. They smelled Ok, I guess. I did not pay too much attention to them. I then had a look around the house. While I was doing that my foster dad got some food for me which I ate really quickly. He says I am \"overly enthusiastic\" when I eat and I try to see what is on the kitchen counters a lot, but I am just really hungry and it is hard to get over not knowing when your next meal will be. I slept in a crate all night and was so tired, I did not fuss at all.

I then went for a walk around the block. It was a nice walk and I just followed my foster dad. I don't usually pull on the leash but sometimes when I see a squirrel or fox or deer I want to chase them. I don't try too hard to do that because my leash and collar stop me and I don't want to pull too hard.

In the morning I went to the vet. I was very good for the doctor and let her do all the things she needed to. I did not complain at all.

I sometimes chase my tail and chew on it. I also have a bit of a hotspot on my back but that is clearing up. We are going to ask about my tail, though. I have chewed through much of the hair there.

I always like to be with my foster dad but sometimes he puts me in a crate. That is ok but I don't like it when I hear him but can't be with him. I try and jump around in my crate and make noises so he will come get me out. If he does not then I will stop after 5 minutes or so. I am good with being in my crate at night and when he goes out, though.

I understand a few of the words dad uses to ask me to do things. I know sit, stay (although for these I usually will expect a treat at some point), and come. There are others but he has not figured them out and I am surely not going to tell him what they are. Gotta make him work for it. I have gotten along well with my foster brother and sister so far. I have met dogs when we walk and they have seemed nice. I am not sure how I feel about cats but if they run I will chase them so dad does not think I would be good with them.

A couple of days after I got to Virginia there was something called Halloween. Not sure what that was but dad and I sat outside while a bunch of strange small people came up to the house. Dad said I was very well behaved and I let a lot of them pet me. There were some really small ones, too.

My foster dad tells me I am nice to have around and once I figure out that I will never have to worry about eating so I am not so enthusiastic about my food (and treats) and stop counter surfing, I will be a really awesome family member.

If you want to see more about my day to day progress, click this link https://trello.com/b/ce6g2fmk. It will take you a web page called \"Trello\" where you can read more about me and see pictures.

name: Donna 0864
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.

I was rescued from a high kill shelter in Texas. I was treated for Systemic Aspergillosis but recently tested negative; however, I
did test positive for Brucellosis which will likely require a lifetime of medicine, which can be covered by SSR. However, I'm such a happy girl, you'd never know!

Donna arrived in Virginia on August 9th, and was a little shy at first. I could tell right away that she had been on a hard floor for a long time because she loves the dog bed and cushy comforters. She took to small kids right away and I believe she would thrive in a house with children. However, with her current medical condition, it might make sense for her to be the only dog in the home, and in a home with mature kids. She's easy going and so so sweet. She would be happy lying around next to her person, but she also enjoys long walks and toys. She is not vocal. She runs around and plays but also enjoys down time on a soft surface. Her fur is soft and fuzzy and she is gaining weight every day.

Her safe space is a small bathroom (instead of a crate) and after a few weeks of a consistent schedule, she has acclimated to her environment. She is completely potty/house trained and just wants to be near her family. She will make some family very happy.

description:

BERNIE is a little thin-in-the-skin and could certainly use to pack on a few, but that shouldn't be a problem.  It's not that he isn't game, it's just that up until now he hasn't really had the option!

We'll have more information on him and better photos soon!

If you would like foster, foster-to-adopt, (in case you're not sure), or adopt young BERNIE, just fill out our online FOSTER/ADOPTION APPLICATION, which can be found in the main menu of our website or at the bottom of this page - simply copy and paste the link into your browser. EASY PEASY!

name: Jessie
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.
Jessie is a shepherd mix between 4-5 years old. She came to us from a shelter in Texas so she can't tell us how life was before Last Hope or explain why she is so shy and timid around new people, her fear of loud noises and quick movements, or her sometimes goofy interactions with her foster dog siblings. Jessie will need a stable and patient forever family to help her continue to grow into the wonderful dog she is becoming. Due to her fear issues, her forever home will require a fenced yard (at least 5'), an experienced dog family, and if there are any children, they should be over 10 years old.

Jessie is crate trained, mostly

housebroken, and very affectionate once she learns to trust. She loves to be around her family and is a big fan of sleeping on the bed with us at night. Jessie is in the process of leash training and basic commands. It is taking time but once she has confidence, we are sure she will learn quickly. If there is another dog in the home, it will need to be her size or larger, confident and very tolerant. Jessie is still learning how to be part of a pack. She has not been around cats and we do not feel they would be a good fit for her.

Jessie's adoption fee is $250 and includes her spay, microchip and current vaccinations. Last Hope's adoption process includes contacting references, vet(s), and landlord (if applicable), as well as a home visit. Last Hope requires all dogs are to be kept indoors and on heartworm preventatives year round.

name: Mr. Beans
description:
Meet our distinguished Mr. Beans! 
Mr. Beans is believed to be about 10 years young and thought to be a chi-weenie. He made his way up from Texas where he was rescued from an animal control facility. Upon arrival he was tested positive for heart worms. We have completed the treatment for these nasty worms and as of August he tested negative. Mr. Beans had heart worms bad enough that he began to go into congestive heart failure and needed meds. His last x-ray showed improvement and his medications are being lowered in the hopes he won't need them anymore soon! 
Mr. Beans is currently in a home with other dogs and has done well. He likes to be in your lap and at approximately 10 pounds he fits quite nice! He is very friendly with people and not picky about who gives him love...as long as he's getting it! He is housebroken and can be trusted to be left alone. He is not a fan of the crate and will make this known if anyone tries to leave him in one! He is a good boy and will not tear up anything but will snooze while he waits for you to come home. He is just the cutest and sweetest boy deserving of a family to love him. 
If interested in meeting or adopting our gentleman, please complete an application (see link below). We require an approved application before meeting a pet. We will review your application and be in touch for next steps if approved. Mr. Beans adoption donation is $175.

description:
Meet Choo Choo!

She's believed to be a 8 month old, Boston terrier mix. Choo Choo is blind. Most likely since birth. She was a cruelty confiscation case. We don't have much details about that situation. She was pulled from a Texas shelter by another rescue but she ended up here. Choo Choo is fully vetted, spayed, up-to-date on all vaccines, rabies, heartworm in Lyme disease tested negative, and on 6 month proheart.

Choo Choo has skin issues which have healed up pretty nice due to food allergies, so quality food is a must.

Being blind has 0 affect in her. She adjust just fine. She is dog and cat friendly and we believe she would do fine with children of all age although, older children probably be best.

Choo Choo does require consistency and routine. She is crate trained and house broken. Choo Choo truly is a sweet heart and enjoys cuddling but enjoys playing even more.


Choo Choo will do fine in a home with other playful dogs. She loves dog toys as mush as she loves to run, pounce, and wrestle. A fenced in yard is a must.

Choo Choo also enjoys her daily walks so much so her leash training is comming along great.

name: Mr. Worldwide
description:
Meet Mr. Worldwide, a 10 year old, 65 pound Pittie mix! This handsome fella came all the way from Texas to find his forever home! While he is blind in his left eye, he surely doesn't let it slow him down. He sees great out of his right eye and is able to navigate without any issues. Mr. Worldwide is both crate and potty trained! This low key boy is looking for a forever home with a matching energy level. He would do great with kids who are dog savvy, and he does great with the other dogs in his foster home. However, he'd like a cat-free home. Mr. Worldwide is a sweet senior boy who is full of wiggles and tiny tail wags! He'd love a forever home to live out the rest of his golden years.

My adoption fee is $150.

name: Duke
description:
Duke was saved minutes from death at a high kill shelter in Texas. He is a handsome Rottweiler mix, 70 lbs and about 8-9 years old. He is crate and appears potty trained. He is a people's dog. He has never gotten into playing with any other dogs, he really just wants to be with his family or person. He knows how to sit, lay down, shake and walks great on a leash. He rides so well in the car. He doesn't like kittens at all, so we don't think he'd do too well with adult cats. He would do best in a home with no other pets. 
Duke is currently with a wonderful foster in Texas, but transport can be arranged to an approved adopter!

If you have any questions on Duke, please feel free to message us via our rescue's Facebook page.
If you're interested in adopting Duke, please fill out an adoption application on our website: www.safetails.org.

name: Ellie looking for a loving family!
description:
Ellie is from Texas where she was saved from a high kill shelter and was in a foster home.  She loved attention from her foster parents and played with the 2 dogs in her home.  She would go for daily walks in a residential area.  She rode well in the car.  She learned to use doggie door and is crate trained. 
   
Ellie traveled by ground transport from Texas to the Boston area to a foster home.   She did not realize Boston was such a big city with so many people, cars and just normal Boston life.   While she did great at her Texas home, she was not sure how to act in the big city.   She figured out she is not socialized to the city environment.   This new life caused her to be fearful of new things.   We found help for Ellie with a wonderful trainer at Atlantic K9 Training!  They are the best and are helping Ellie overcome her fears and she LOVES them!

The right home for Ellie would be one that is calm and in a nice residential area with a fenced yard.   She would love another dog or two so she has a buddy for playing!   She needs a person who will be her pack leader and will continue her training.   She really wants a loving family who will give her the time and patience to become the loving dog she wants to be.  No children please.

Ellie Mae is a pretty brown/blonde Shepherd/lab mix who weighs about 45 pounds and is two years old.  She is spayed, micro-chipped and up to date on vaccines.   She is located in the Boxford area.    For an app, please email rhondabarron@earthlink.net

name: KRATOS
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
KRATOS was saved from a high kill shelter in Texas where dogs have just 3 dogs to be saved and transported to the rescue in Sebec, Maine. KRATOS is neutered, core vaccines, rabies, heartworm and tick-disease tested negative, de-wormed, monthly preventatives and micro-chipped. He has an estimated date of birth of 24 February 2018 and at the time of rescue in the end of August 2019, weighed around 28.00 pounds. The shelter has a breed listing of Husky Mix. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

KRATOS was adopted from the shelter but returned the day after as the family didn't have time for him.

KRATOS will be arriving at the rescue on Thursday, 12th Saturday and we will update when he has been here and settled so we can give a more accurate description of his personality and mannerisms. As time permits, we will take more pictures. You are welcome to complete and submit the adoption application if you are interested in giving him a forever home.

WE ARE NOT ABLE TO COMMENT HOW HE WILL BE AROUND CATS OR LIVESTOCK.



RATOS is available for adoption for an adoption fee of US $550.

This fee is not negotiable and is used to cover the rescue costs of pulling, vetting, health certificate, transport from Texas to Maine, monthly preventatives, supplements, food, general day to day cost of running a brick and mortar rescue and anything else that is needed. Canadian adopters need to know that customs charge 15% taxes when entering into Canada.

If you feel that you have the heart and home to give this precious soul a wonderful life, please go to our website, under the APPLICATION tab, complete, then submit the APPLICATION. Our process takes around 2-4 days, and ensuring your references are aware that we will be calling, could speed up the process. Once you have been approved, we discuss any questions in regards to the dog you are wanting to adopt, then you complete and submit the contract, make payment and then we can work out the pick up / transport arrangements.

Please do NOT submit an application if you are not looking to take home a new best friend within the next few weeks.

http://www.giveadogahome-sanantonio.org

ALL Dogs are LOCATED AT THE RESCUE IN SEBEC, MAINE. We post in various states along the east coast and Canada where we have had lots of successful adoptions to enable more exposure for these beautiful saved souls. Families will need to be prepared to travel to the rescue to meet and take home their new best friend. Sebec is located just outside the towns of Dover-Foxcroft and Milo (approx 8 miles) and approx 45 miles from Bangor. There are also lots of hotels, motels, pet friendly accommodations and wonderful camp-sites for the more adventurous families and what a great way to get to know your new best friend.
Give a Dog a Home, German Shepherd Dog Rescue

187 Downs Road, Sebec, Maine, 04481

giveadogahome@live.com

All pets adopted will be spay/neutered, micro-chipped, de-wormed,heartworm tested, rabies and relevant vaccinations.

NO DOG WILL BE ADOPTED TO BE AN OUTSIDE DOG!

If you would like to start the adoption our process is below:

Submit Application with two personal references and a vet reference.

If you have never had pets and do not have a vet, we will need THREE personal references.

Ensure references are people who know you and your lifestyle well.

Applicant MUST inform vet and references that someone from GaDaH will be calling.

As long as we are able to contact your vet and references, it takes just 1-3 days to process and hopefully approve applications.

If you rent we will need an approval letter for the breed of dog you are wanting to adopt from your landlord on official letterhead paper or email.

Rescue processes and hopefully approves applications.

Once approved, rescue invites applicant to come to the rescue to meet your chosen dog/s, spend time with him/her

and then hopefully take him/her home.

We do NOT hold dogs so if you are unable to come within a week or so of submitting your application the dog will still be available for adoption to other families.

For Canadian adopters, all that is needed to get them across the border into Canada is a current rabies certificate and proof of adoption, which is the adoption contract. Both of which are included in the medical file you will get when you adopt. (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/pet-travel/by-country/pettravel-canada)

Ensure ALL Fields are filled in, if something is relevant, then put n/a or something in so it recognizes an entry.

We do not recommend using a phone or ipad since these applications for some reason don't tend to come through and you will have spent a lot of time on the application for nothing as it will need to be re-done.

Once we have you approved we can schedule an appointment for you to come to meet

him/her at the rescue in Sebec, Mane and then hopefully take them home to start your new life.

I just have to work on an appointment basis as I run a boarding/day care business and the rescue and so am really busy, but by planning ahead of time I can be pretty flexible.
