Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
HUCKLEBERRY was saved from a high kill shelter in Texas where dogs have just 3 dogs to be saved and transported to the rescue in Sebec, Maine. HUCKLEBERRY is neutered, core vaccines, rabies, de-wormed, monthly preventatives and micro-chipped. He has an estimated date of birth of 24 May 2019 and at the time of rescue in the end of August 2019, weighed around 33.00 pounds. The shelter has a breed listing of Blue Heeler /Pointer Mix. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

HUCKLEBERRY will be arriving at the rescue on Thursday, 12th September and we will update when he has been here and settled so we can give a more accurate description of his personality and mannerisms. As time permits, we will take more pictures. You are welcome to complete and submit the adoption application if you are interested in giving him a forever home.

WE ARE NOT ABLE TO COMMENT HOW SHE WILL BE AROUND CATS OR LIVESTOCK.



HUCKLEBERRY is available for adoption for an adoption fee of US $550.

This fee is not negotiable and is used to cover the rescue costs of pulling, vetting, health certificate, transport from Texas to Maine, monthly preventatives, supplements, food, general day to day cost of running a brick and mortar rescue and anything else that is needed. Canadian adopters need to know that customs charge 15% taxes when entering into Canada.

If you feel that you have the heart and home to give this precious soul a wonderful life, please go to our website, under the APPLICATION tab, complete, then submit the APPLICATION. Our process takes around 2-4 days, and ensuring your references are aware that we will be calling, could speed up the process. Once you have been approved, we discuss any questions in regards to the dog you are wanting to adopt, then you complete and submit the contract, make payment and then we can work out the pick up / transport arrangements.

Please do NOT submit an application if you are not looking to take home a new best friend within the next few weeks.

http://www.giveadogahome-sanantonio.org

ALL Dogs are LOCATED AT THE RESCUE IN SEBEC, MAINE. We post in various states along the east coast and Canada where we have had lots of successful adoptions to enable more exposure for these beautiful saved souls. Families will need to be prepared to travel to the rescue to meet and take home their new best friend. Sebec is located just outside the towns of Dover-Foxcroft and Milo (approx 8 miles) and approx 45 miles from Bangor. There are also lots of hotels, motels, pet friendly accommodations and wonderful camp-sites for the more adventurous families and what a great way to get to know your new best friend.
Give a Dog a Home, German Shepherd Dog Rescue

187 Downs Road, Sebec, Maine, 04481

giveadogahome@live.com

All pets adopted will be spay/neutered, micro-chipped, de-wormed,heartworm tested, rabies and relevant vaccinations.

NO DOG WILL BE ADOPTED TO BE AN OUTSIDE DOG!

If you would like to start the adoption our process is below:

Submit Application with two personal references and a vet reference.

If you have never had pets and do not have a vet, we will need THREE personal references.

Ensure references are people who know you and your lifestyle well.

Applicant MUST inform vet and references that someone from GaDaH will be calling.

As long as we are able to contact your vet and references, it takes just 1-3 days to process and hopefully approve applications.

If you rent we will need an approval letter for the breed of dog you are wanting to adopt from your landlord on official letterhead paper or email.

Rescue processes and hopefully approves applications.

Once approved, rescue invites applicant to come to the rescue to meet your chosen dog/s, spend time with him/her

and then hopefully take him/her home.

We do NOT hold dogs so if you are unable to come within a week or so of submitting your application the dog will still be available for adoption to other families.

For Canadian adopters, all that is needed to get them across the border into Canada is a current rabies certificate and proof of adoption, which is the adoption contract. Both of which are included in the medical file you will get when you adopt. (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/pet-travel/by-country/pettravel-canada)

Ensure ALL Fields are filled in, if something is relevant, then put n/a or something in so it recognizes an entry.

We do not recommend using a phone or ipad since these applications for some reason don't tend to come through and you will have spent a lot of time on the application for nothing as it will need to be re-done.

Once we have you approved we can schedule an appointment for you to come to meet

him/her at the rescue in Sebec, Mane and then hopefully take them home to start your new life.

I just have to work on an appointment basis as I run a boarding/day care business and the rescue and so am really busy, but by planning ahead of time I can be pretty flexible.

BOOMER is a handsome Foxhound who is neutered, just had his 3 year booster rabies vaccine, core vaccines, heartworm/tick disease tested negative, de-wormed, monthly heartworm and flea/tick prevention and micro-chipped He has an estimated date of birth of 25 August 2018 and weighs 65 pounds.

Following his neuter on 9th September 2019, Boomer went home to stay with a foster family who live in the Litchfield, Maine area, just south from Augusta and is acclimating well and the foster family adore him.

Notes from his foster family:

BOOMER is a GREAT boy he is very affectionate, knows a few basic commands and loves to play. He definitely has that \"hound\" personality

and likes the company of other dogs, children, and adults and is heartbroken when left alone. Boomer has not been acclimated to cats but I think he would do fine. Hounds need a lot exercise and the foster family is currently working on leash and obedience training. Boomer is house trained and will let you know by whining or scratching at the door.

At 65 pounds, Boomer is a strapping young hound and basically mild mannered in the home. Hounds can be independent and stubborn in nature, particularly if their nose is in pursuit of an outdoor smell. Boomer is lovable in nature and will definitely win you over with his charm, love and loyalty.

On intake from the rescue.

I was informed by the family giving him up that Boomer has lived with his sibling, another dog, two small children and his mum and dad and was a wonderful part of the family. He has never shown any aggression, was well behaved, house-trained, he would go on long walks, play frisbee, chew on bones and a Kong and LOVED people.

When Boomer arrived at the rescue he was clearly stressed, upset and unsure what was going on. He has never been away from his brother and of course being left by his dad whom he has lived with since he was a small puppy caused some anxiety. He did settle down after a while and met some of the dogs. Not being fixed when he arrived he was a bit \"frisky\" with some of the dogs and so it was best to keep him separate until he has been neutered. He is in the house with the dogs, just living at the other end, but he does lie and sit next to the gate dividing them and is doing great making friends this way. He is definitely a social boy and I am sure when neutered there will be no issues, his family said he was never a problem around dogs, animals or humans and had two very small human siblings whom he adored.

BOOMER needs a family that lives in the country or are very outdoorsy and active, where he has a lot of places to explore, however, working on training and recall would be extremely important before he is allowed to run loose because being a hound, he will most likely be very easily distracted and would most definitely chase after squirrels and wildlife. A family that can take him on daily runs in rural areas, would be a great for him and with no distractions of people or other dogs an enjoyable activity. He is used to living with a family and so when alone, he does have that loud hound bark/howl, so plenty of interaction and mental stimulation. BOOMER loves toys, if they have a squeak in all the better, he will play for hours happily and I am sure the puzzle toys for dogs would help keep him entertained.

name: MARGIE-G-AR
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
MARGIE-G was saved from the high kill shelter in Texas in early 2018. She was extremely emaciated and in rough condition, but she was so loving and affectionate. At the rescue she settled in great and it wasn't long before she was playing grandma to a female German Shepherds 3 week old pups.
MARGIE-G has a date of birth of 15 February 2009 and is fully vetted.

After being here a few months, gaining weight, starting to enjoy life and enjoying playing with other dogs, she was adopted in May 2018. Unfortunately in the middle of August 2019 I received a message that Margie-G, who had been renamed Maggie, needed to be returned as she had become extremely protective of her home and her owner.

Upon talking to her owner and just by knowing Margie's personality and of course the breed it became clear that she had been allowed to become \"alpha\" and so with being alpha comes naturally responsibility for dogs, as with humans. They must protect their family (their pack) and they must protect their home (their territory). Aggression like this doesn't happen over night and she would have taken control gradually, with growling, hackles up, barking and such - and had this been stopped and her made clear this behaviour was not needed, nor would be tolerated, there would have been no problems and she would have accepted that she was not alpha of her humans and so no need to protect her family and home. However, it wasn't stopped and it progressed to where the owner was scared of having anyone in her home and so returned her.

Since being at the rescue Margie has shown no signs of aggression or even wanting to be alpha, she has settled back in, although is still stressed and clearly missing her family life, but she is good being amongst other dogs, although not ideal for her age. She is a very sweet, loving, affectionate girl, who when allowed to come in my bedroom, will jump up on the bed and settle into a deep sleep. She will give kisses and just enjoy getting lots of love and affection.

Margie is 10 years old and with age comes health problems, she does have severe arthiritis in her hips and knee, she is on pain medications and I have some natural supplements that I am giving her to help with the joints and general health. She had been fed Alpo with her family, however, since this is an extremely low quality food we immediately switched her over to a high quality senior diet of both dry and wet food mixed together - she seems to enjoy it. She is house trained and will let me know when she wants to go out.

Considering her hips are in such bad shape she gets around great, she does jump up on the bed and climbs stairs without hesitation, however, this is not encouraged and only done when absolutely necessary, or without me knowing.

Margie really needs a quiet home and family where she can relax and enjoy her old age. The rescue is very loud and busy with lots of dogs running and playing and having fun and it can be stressful for her.

We are looking for someone who has experience with GSD / Working Breed dogs. They must be confident in being in control and not allowing the dog to think they need to be in control. As mentioned above, she became very protective and that needs to be not allowed anymore. She needs to be not only taught that it is not needed, nor acceptable behaviour, but precautions need to be taken, she needs to be either crated when people come round, put in a secure room, or have a leash and muzzle on - when dogs become protective there really is no leeway giving them opportunity. This will also show her that you are in charge and can see she is not needed. Having her under control any sign of growlng or negative behaviour can be corrected immediately and so she will learn quickly.

With the right family I do not think her protectiveness will be difficult to get under control, experience, and consistency is what is needed.
Then of course she has her arthritis so we are looking for a family that is financial stable to get her any treatment needed in the future and be strong enough now and over the next few years to be able to support her hips when she needs to go outside. Maybe a belly support will be needed, or even the possibility of a wheel-chair - all possible options that the family should be willing to consider and move forward on should it help her in the future.
At least annual x-rays and senior blood panels need to be done to keep on top of her health since she a senior girl and although she is a tough cookie, I would think she has a few more years at the most, but it is critical her health is monitored regularly. So a family that understands that and is willing to make her last few years the best ever and do what is needed, at whatever cost for her comfort.

She needs a high quality diet to suit her age, breed, any medical needs and of course ability and ease of eating. Home cooking would be PERFECT for her, but a high quality senior diet is needed.

I know there is a perfect family out there - she doesn't need LOTS of exercise, but she does need to get out and move her hips so that they don't seize up and be even more painful.

If anyone is interested in adopting her - think seriously about the commitment and her issues - it is easy to fall in love with a sad story and want to make it right - but please be sure you are able and 100% committed to her FOREVER.

name: MARGIE-G-AR
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
MARGIE-G was saved from the high kill shelter in Texas in early 2018. She was extremely emaciated and in rough condition, but she was so loving and affectionate. At the rescue she settled in great and it wasn't long before she was playing grandma to a female German Shepherds 3 week old pups.
MARGIE-G has a date of birth of 15 February 2009 and is fully vetted.

After being here a few months, gaining weight, starting to enjoy life and enjoying playing with other dogs, she was adopted in May 2018. Unfortunately in the middle of August 2019 I received a message that Margie-G, who had been renamed Maggie, needed to be returned as she had become extremely protective of her home and her owner.

Upon talking to her owner and just by knowing Margie's personality and of course the breed it became clear that she had been allowed to become \"alpha\" and so with being alpha comes naturally responsibility for dogs, as with humans. They must protect their family (their pack) and they must protect their home (their territory). Aggression like this doesn't happen over night and she would have taken control gradually, with growling, hackles up, barking and such - and had this been stopped and her made clear this behaviour was not needed, nor would be tolerated, there would have been no problems and she would have accepted that she was not alpha of her humans and so no need to protect her family and home. However, it wasn't stopped and it progressed to where the owner was scared of having anyone in her home and so returned her.

Since being at the rescue Margie has shown no signs of aggression or even wanting to be alpha, she has settled back in, although is still stressed and clearly missing her family life, but she is good being amongst other dogs, although not ideal for her age. She is a very sweet, loving, affectionate girl, who when allowed to come in my bedroom, will jump up on the bed and settle into a deep sleep. She will give kisses and just enjoy getting lots of love and affection.

Margie is 10 years old and with age comes health problems, she does have severe arthiritis in her hips and knee, she is on pain medications and I have some natural supplements that I am giving her to help with the joints and general health. She had been fed Alpo with her family, however, since this is an extremely low quality food we immediately switched her over to a high quality senior diet of both dry and wet food mixed together - she seems to enjoy it. She is house trained and will let me know when she wants to go out.

Considering her hips are in such bad shape she gets around great, she does jump up on the bed and climbs stairs without hesitation, however, this is not encouraged and only done when absolutely necessary, or without me knowing.

Margie really needs a quiet home and family where she can relax and enjoy her old age. The rescue is very loud and busy with lots of dogs running and playing and having fun and it can be stressful for her.

We are looking for someone who has experience with GSD / Working Breed dogs. They must be confident in being in control and not allowing the dog to think they need to be in control. As mentioned above, she became very protective and that needs to be not allowed anymore. She needs to be not only taught that it is not needed, nor acceptable behaviour, but precautions need to be taken, she needs to be either crated when people come round, put in a secure room, or have a leash and muzzle on - when dogs become protective there really is no leeway giving them opportunity. This will also show her that you are in charge and can see she is not needed. Having her under control any sign of growlng or negative behaviour can be corrected immediately and so she will learn quickly.

With the right family I do not think her protectiveness will be difficult to get under control, experience, and consistency is what is needed.
Then of course she has her arthritis so we are looking for a family that is financial stable to get her any treatment needed in the future and be strong enough now and over the next few years to be able to support her hips when she needs to go outside. Maybe a belly support will be needed, or even the possibility of a wheel-chair - all possible options that the family should be willing to consider and move forward on should it help her in the future.
At least annual x-rays and senior blood panels need to be done to keep on top of her health since she a senior girl and although she is a tough cookie, I would think she has a few more years at the most, but it is critical her health is monitored regularly. So a family that understands that and is willing to make her last few years the best ever and do what is needed, at whatever cost for her comfort.

She needs a high quality diet to suit her age, breed, any medical needs and of course ability and ease of eating. Home cooking would be PERFECT for her, but a high quality senior diet is needed.

I know there is a perfect family out there - she doesn't need LOTS of exercise, but she does need to get out and move her hips so that they don't seize up and be even more painful.

If anyone is interested in adopting her - think seriously about the commitment and her issues - it is easy to fall in love with a sad story and want to make it right - but please be sure you are able and 100% committed to her FOREVER.

If you would like to start the adoption our process is below:

Submit Application with two personal references and a vet reference.

If you have never had pets and do not have a vet, we will need THREE personal references.

Ensure references are people who know you and your lifestyle well.

Applicant MUST inform vet and references that someone from GaDaH will be calling.

As long as we are able to contact your vet and references, it takes just 1-3 days to process and hopefully approve applications.

If you rent we will need an approval letter for the breed of dog you are wanting to adopt from your landlord on official letterhead paper or email.

Rescue processes and hopefully approves applications.

Once approved, rescue invites applicant to come to the rescue to meet your chosen dog/s, spend time with him/her

and then hopefully take him/her home.

We do NOT hold dogs so if you are unable to come within a week or so of submitting your application the dog will still be available for adoption to other families.

For Canadian adopters, all that is needed to get them across the border into Canada is a current rabies certificate and proof of adoption, which is the adoption contract. Both of which are included in the medical file you will get when you adopt. (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/pet-travel/by-country/pettravel-canada)

Ensure ALL Fields are filled in, if something is relevant, then put n/a or something in so it recognizes an entry.

We do not recommend using a phone or ipad since these applications for some reason don't tend to come through and you will have spent a lot of time on the application for nothing as it will need to be re-done.

Once we have you approved we can schedule an appointment for you to come to meet

him/her at the rescue in Sebec, Mane and then hopefully take them home to start your new life.

I just have to work on an appointment basis as I run a boarding/day care business and the rescue and so am really busy, but by planning ahead of time I can be pretty flexible.

description:

LACEY-1 is spayed, core vaccines, rabies, heartworm & tick disease tested negative, de-wormed, heart worm and tick disease tested negative, monthly preventatives and micro-chipped. She has an estimated date of birth of 19 June 2017 and at the time of rescue in the middle of June 2019, weighed around 43.00 pounds. She is listed as an Pit Bull Mix. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

LACEY-1 was saved with her 3 puppies,Taylor, Spot & Holister who have been adopted and although she is doing great, she was sad and looked for them for several days after they had been adopted.

LACEY-1 is a great girl, she is fun, full of life, happy, playful, active, loving, affectionate, boisterous and a good all round girl. When she first got here with her pups she was a little apprehensive, but soon settled and took on the role of surrogate mum to some other pups that was here.

As the pups got adopted she did start to get a little anxious looking for them and whining, however, since she was living with lots of other dogs she soon was able to be distracted with play and fun with them and so she adapted and is now as happy as can be.

When I took Lacey for her spay surgery she rode like a queen in the car and was friendly and affectionate to the vet staff. She will bark at strangers coming in, but she is in a high energy environment and dogs tend to feed of each others energy. She doesn't bark excessively and will stop when told to do so.

She is a young girl and so an active lifestyle would definitely be of benefit to her. She needs a family that is familiar with the breed and understands that there is a lot of negativity towards pit-bulls and many places unfortunately do not allow the breed and people are of course quick to judge and condemn them. So we are looking for a Pro-Pit-Bull family.



She would be a great family pet, she is so much fun, so loving and gentle. She is always friendly and happy to see me or the volunteers that come occasionally come over.

As with all dogs she will need basic and advanced training so that so she can learn her families rules, boundaries and expectations. She is very responsive and I feel that she will be easy and fun to train and will be eager to please. She is a gentle girl and I think would make a great family dog.

Lacey-1 would be great in a family environment but as with all dogs, she must understand that she is not in charge and that rules and boundaries must be followed, she is confident and so I am sure she would push and test the boundaries. She is young, fun and would be great for an active family to take her on long walks and adventures.

name: TILLY-AS - $300
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.

IMPORTANT - READ ALL INFORMATION PROVIDED


TILLY was saved from a high kill shelter in Texas in May 2018, where dogs generally have just 3 days to be saved before they are killed for space. TILLY is spayed, core vaccines, rabies, de-wormed, heartworm tested negative and micro-chipped. She has an estimated date of birth of 18 April 2010 and weighs around 14.20 pounds. She has been listed as a Cairn Terrier Fox Terrier Mix. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, so it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

At the beginning of June 2018, Tilly was adopted and went to start her new life. Unfortunately in the middle of March 2019 I received an email from the family saying that she would need to be returned to the rescue. The problems the family had was that Tilly had started to get protective of her chair, and her home, she would bark and growl at people coming into the home. The family took her to the vet who recommended a training program and then anxiety medications. Tilly's negative behaviour continued and the family again reached out to the vet wanting her taken off the medication as there had been no significant improvement, the vet, even knowing that the rescue would take her back offered euthanasia as an option. Tilly had not bitten anyone and she had not a recent physical exam or blood panel done to rule out any medical issues for her personality change. Thankfully the family brought her back to the rescue.

When TILLY first got back to the rescue I noticed how over-weight she was. I put her in the bedroom which is off the main living area where there is a gate installed so she could come out of her crate and get to know the dogs and start to decompress slowly. She was at first growly with me which I tolerated for the first day back, on day two I shouted at her, pointing and telling her \"no, this behaviour was not acceptable\". I sat on the floor and within minutes she came belly-crawling over and turned over next to me to let me scratch her belly. That has been the extent of her aggression.

description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
CHIP-L was saved from a high kill shelter in Texas with his 3 buddies, all feral and had been scheduled to be killed the day we saved them. CHIP-L is neutered, core vaccines, rabies, heartworm and tick disease tested negative, monthly preventatives and microchipped. He has an estimated date of birth of 20 April 2016 and at the time of rescue in May 2018 weighed around 11 pounds.

CHIP, PRINCE, MILO & PIXIE were all saved together. When I had informed the shelter I would take them into rescue, they informed me they were scheduled to be killed that day because they were feral. I had committed to them and so I couldn't back out.

When they got here I let them with the other dogs and just left them to it as I think it is important for dogs to decompress and figure out what has happened to them the last week, being picked up by animal control, taken to a large city kill shelter, having surgery and all the vetting then on a transport up to the rescue for 3 days, then getting here - it is so much for them all in such a short time.

name: BETSY-AS - Reduced $250
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.BETSY was saved IN March 2018, with her son, Bobby from a high kill shelter in Texas both with severe skin infections and demodex mange, which was treated and a clean bill of health given. BETSY is spayed, core vaccines, rabies, de-wormed, heartworm tested negative and micro-chipped. She has an estimated date of birth of 10 March 2016 and wheighs around 50 pounds. Betsy has been listed as a Pointer Mix, however, we are not able to say for sure what breed she is, it is up to you to look at her pictures and decide what you think she looks like.

BETSY was adopted in October 2018, however, in March 2019 I received an email from the family saying that they was having problems and eventually BETSY was returned to the rescue on 3 April 2019.

BETSY was living in a family home with a fenced in yard and was happy go lucky girl. She loves to give and get snuggles and was great with the children, although concerns were with her high energy she might accidentally knock small children over. She loved being outside as she did at the rescue chasing squirrels and wildlife. She went on a run with her dad and she seemed to enjoy it and was able to keep up and it was a great way to burn off some of her excess energy. On walks certain noises would scare her and she would refuse to continue to walk that way. She did shows signs of separation anxiety in a form of barking if she was not in the same room as her family, which was not possible due to the family cats living in the upstairs of the house. BETSY was not good on a leash when other dogs or animals were around and she would bark in an aggressive manner. She apparently also got very agitated when people walked past their home and she would bark and jump up at the fence until they passed. The family tried CBD oil with limited affect, then family vet prescribed her Trazadone for a period and then changed her to Prozac which both are an anti-depressant to help with her anxiety. I asked that she be weened of this drug before being returned to the rescue.

When BETSY came back to the rescue I brought her into the house to live with me and 20 other dogs. She settled in well and has been great with the other dogs, but being a hunting breed dog she is constantly on the go and rarely keeps still. She will run and play outside but really needs to be taken on long runs and places where she can smell and dig around to stimulate her brain. She is a very smart girl, but can be easily distracted, again a trait of a hunting breed. BETSY needs to be kept on the go, she needs to be mentally stimulated and being able to go out and run and tire herself out. She is the kind of dog that needs a \"master\

description:

We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

Since being at the rescue BUSTER has lived amongst a lot of dogs of all ages and sizes ranging from small chi's, middle sized dogs up to adult German Shepherds and so he is very dog socialized and very confident. He is friendly with people and has enjoyed cuddles from a friends 7 year old granddaughter.

We do not have cats or livestock at the rescue so cannot comment on how he would be around them.

BUSTER is young and used to being around lots of dogs so we are hoping for a family who either adopts another rescue or who has other pets at home. He is a young pup and so chewing is very much to be expected. He does use pee pads but also at times does use the dog door to go outside. He will need house training along with all basic training, manners and general behaviour. His personality is still developing and so it will be up to the family to ensure he stays a loving, gentle, playful, affectionate pup whilst growing into an adult dog.

Since being at the rescue he is totally loving life, he loves to play with toys, chew on hooves and horns, wrestle and chase with the other dogs and get lots of love and cuddles as much as he can. He is high energy and he feeds of the excitement of the other dogs, but does calm down and settle after a while. He is a great boy who has never shown any kind of aggression in any way.

As with all rescue's he needs guidance and training and we recommend families go through at least the basics of training with him themselves so that boundaries, personalities and body language can be learned from each other. BUSTER is very responsive and training would be fun and easy as long as proper training techniques are followed and are consistent.

We do not recommend dog parks for several weeks, if not months, it is so very important for families and dogs to form a strong bond and get to know each other before exposing them to the potential dangers of dog parks. Although all GaDaH dogs are very well socialized with other dogs, lots of other dogs have not had the benefit of this socialization and do not always know how to play and act with other dogs. You also do not know the control the other families have over their dogs and you should always have a good recall for your adopted dog before going to dog parks.

He is going to be a medium / large dog and so we are looking for an active family who goes out and about and intends to take their new family member as many places with them as possible.

BUSTER would benefit from a family that goes on walks and adventures and road trips together. name: Ari
description:
Ari did not get the best start in life, but is learning that it feels good to be loved, and that snuggling on the couch is fun. Ari came all the way from Texas to find his forever home!

He is a bit timid and skittish, but will jump up on the couch to be petted and to give kisses. Ari loves any kind of food, and will sometimes eat two bowls. He is a very sweet boy and is happy to see you when you come home.  He is right at the door to greet you.

Ari lives with seven other dogs in his foster home and gets along great with all of them.  He even cuddles with one of them and eats out of the same bowl with her. Ari uses pee pads, but still marks in the house.  He is still working on potty training.  His foster mom thinks he had never seen a leash, so he didn't understand what it was at first.  He's gotten lots of practice and has made good progress.

Ari likes to snuggle.  He will lay by his foster mom's shoulder, or under the blanket by her legs.  He has to be touching her. He is a very loving dog and loves praise and affection. Ari was heartworm positive, but has had his first and second rounds of meds.  He did very well and has now been neutered.
 
Ari is a very happy dog and listens to commands. He is up to date on his shots and flea prevention. Ari will make a great pet and will be fun to have in your home.

**Ari is currently being fostered in Ada, MI**

I'm still learning to be a gentleman on a leash and if you are not watching, I will chew through the nylon ones. Mom was not happy...Overall though, I have been told that I am the absolute sweetest. I hear it every day so it must be true! I am a super chill pup that enjoys lounging on the couch or in my dog bed by my people. I am a gentle fella and I like to take my time when eating. I am crate trained and never potty in the house. I am learning the basic commands so that I will be the best boy for my new family. Hello world they call me buckwheat at the rescue but my foster mom calls me taco! I came up from Texas so I'm a good old southern boy. I've had very minimal human interaction so I'm extremely shy and scared of people but my foster mom has been working with me and I actually go up and sniff strangers which is huge she said and praises me by jumping up and down and acting all silly that I went up and sniffed a stranger. She's kind of a weird woman but she's got a big heart and I sure do like her. Not much of my back story is known but my foster mom says that I will need a very patient person with a big huge heart like her that can see what she sees in me. She says I'm pretty good at house training and I go potty outside really well but I like to stick by her side so if she doesn't make sure I go potty outside when she's out with me then... I might have a little accident in the house right next to her. I really don't want to leave her side that's the thing! I haven't quite given kisses yet to my foster mom but I watch all the other pups here give her kisses and how much she likes them and I so want to do it, I'm just not there yet. She said she'll keep trying and eventually I'll give her kisses. I do kiss her on the hand when she's petting me and she praises me for that by saying thank you for the kisses. I'm a good little boy, I don't bark very much. I get along great with all my foster mom's dogs, she's got a big one and a bunch of small ones. Her son has friends over so they all come up and meet the pups and foster mom says I do really well with that by going up and sniffing them. I haven't let them touch me yet but I'll get there. I'm a happy little guy and I smile when I'm happy. When I'm being pet the sides of my lips curl up a little bit and my foster mom says I'm smiling which is super cute she says. I redirect very easily if I'm doing something my foster mom doesn't like she just says nope and I stop. I walk well on a leash but I'm afraid of everything so I will take some time to get over that. My foster mom has a fenced-in yard and I love running around and sunning myself on the deck. I kennel up super easy, all foster mom has to say is kennel up and I run right in. She always gives me a treat or I get a dental bone when she goes back to work from her lunch break. I sleep in the kennel at night and I don't make a peep. I ride pretty well in the car, no noise from me. If you have anymore questions please get ahold of my foster mom and she can explain more of me to you. I'm looking for someone patient that's willing to work with me through my fears and love me for the rest of my life.

Foster mom here, oh what can I say about little taco. He is absolutely adorable and such a great little pup. He looks to me for direction because he's not been taught very much. He was afraid of everything, noises, sudden movements, you name it. This boy has already come so far and he's got a little ways to go but oh my gosh is he so worth it! He bonds really hard to his person and looks to you for everything. His person will have to be supportive and understanding, patient and willing to do whatever it takes to help him, they have to be strong because he cannot take that role, he needs a leader and someone he can trust to get through this fear. He's never attempted to bite, he's just scared and he will hide when he gets scared. Baby talk has worked wonders and having other pups that he can learn from really helps. Having a brother or a sister pup for him would really help him a lot. He's not a big guy, I think he's only about 14 lbs so he's little. He doesn't like being under covers or blankets yet. Lol... I'm thinking one day he will though. I'm not sure how he does with small kids but being the fact that children can be loud and move quickly I think that would probably scare him and he wouldn't come out of his shell, it would only push him back. So I'm not sure if kids would be good for this little guy. I can't think of anything else right now but if you have any questions or want to know anything about little taco AKA buckwheat please let me know and I will answer anything and everything about him.

He's a Texas gem and he's got a second chance at life up here in Minnesota. This little guy will make someone so happy because he's such a funny guy once he trusts you and his heart is huge for love. Plus he's my favorite color black which never shows on your dress clothes and then to top it off he's got Doberman markings the black and tan so he's super cute and his ears stand up oh my gosh!!!

Buckwheat does need a home with another dog present and a fenced in yard

Thank you for reading and thank you for giving a pup a chance at a new life!

Buckwheat
was heartworm positive when he first joined rescue but has been treated and doing great!

name: Elina Lonestar*
description:
Hi, my name is Elina Lonestar, but my foster mom calls me Ellie. I am a Shepherd mix about 1 year & 3 months old. I came from Texas where I lived outside all the time with several other dogs.

I'm in NJ & living with a really nice foster mom and her 8 year old female Husky mix named Tess. At least that's what my foster mom says she is, but to me she just looks more like a beige German Shephard. I love the crate that was set up for me with a bed inside and a few toys and chew bones. I like going into my crate and will do so just to get away from any hustle and bustle even though there isn't that much here in my foster home,

I like going on car rides but still don't understand why I can't constantly kiss my foster mom even if she is driving.

I am even being taught a word called \"wait\" so I can let my human go in and out of the house first. I am a little scared and get startled easily by new things but with patience and care I know I will get over this. When Tess is outside with me I am a little more comfortable as I know that I am not alone and I know that she and my foster mom would not let anything happen to me. It's just that everything is new to me. Not the fact of being outside but the fact that there really are people and dogs in this world that really do care about me.

I love the company of dogs - in fact, I love dogs so much that foster mom says I need to go to a home with at least one other dog who can help me gain confidence. But I am too active for cats so I need to go to a cat-free forever home.

I also am cautious when meeting new people so you need to go slow when you first meet me. I would be more comfortable with older children, probably 10 years or older, as the speed at which some smaller children run and act might scare me.

I walk pretty good on a leash with my foster mom (she asked me to walk easy as she and her knees are not that young anymore. I don't know what she means by that because she looks pretty young to me) who congratulates me whenever I don't pull.

I do like playing with toys but I need to get comfortable with the person playing with me or else our fetching sessions will be one sided with my owner throwing the toy, me starting toward it and then the owner having to go fetch it themselves. This not only goes for toys but for tennis balls as well. So, unless you want to go a great distance to retrieve a ball you throw, I suggest you start out throwing it close at least at first.

I also love to jump up next to my human if they are on the couch and just snuggle up. If my human allows me to I would also really like to lie close to them on their bed because it's so comforting to me to be able to sniff their scent where I will be laying. If I could also have a companion dog to keep me company it would make it a little easier for me to adjust to my new surroundings.

This is just a little bit about me. If you would like to know some more and possibly meet me in person, just fill out an application at www.ehrdogs.org and don't to forget to put my name, Elina Lonestar on it. Once it gets approved, my foster mom will contact you to schedule a time to meet me. By the way, I am so much cuter in person than I am in my pictures. Just wait and see.

She was treated for heartworms and has completed her treatment.   She is spayed, microchipped and up to date with her vaccines.  She will make a great companion. She does not like being crated and will do best with older children.  She loves to play with small toys.

description:
Please do not inquire or apply through Petfinder. Please apply directly with bigdogrescueproject.org/adopt. Dogs will be transported from Texas upon approved match.

Buddy is about 2 years old and is a total sweet boy. He is a typical happy-go-lucky lab who has done well with the other dogs in his foster home. It takes him a little time to get over his shyness and then he is happy as a clam!

He met a cat at the vet office and had no problems. Buddy has not met many kids at this time!

When Buddy went in for his neuter, his pre-op blood work showed that he is in kidney failure. This was obviously unexpected news, particularly given the fact that he is such a young boy. He has since started on Benazepril, which will promote healthy kidney function, and a kibble recommended for dogs with kidney issues. Benazepril is an inexpensive medication - our vet has quoted us $8 per month. While we are currently working on a plan for his future care, it is impossible to say what to expect long-term. Some dogs do not live a full life, and others do. Buddy will need to have his blood work monitored once or twice a year and at some point could need subcutaneous fluids to flush his kidneys. As long as he is eating and drinking well, with normal activity, he is considered to be stable for a dog with his condition.

Currently, Buddy is doing really well. He does consume a lot of water which is actually a good thing, per our vet. Drinking plenty of water will help him stay hydrated and keep his kidneys flushed. Because he drinks more than the average dog, he needs more frequent potty breaks but other than that, he is a normal pup. His appetite is great, he is a happy guy and he really enjoys playing with the other dogs in his foster home.

name: Baby Jade
description:
Stare deep into those baby blues, and tell us it's not love at first sight!

Baby Jade is an absolutely stunning American Staffordshire Terrier puppy that had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. Baby Jade is currently in Houston, Texas and available for transport through our rescue partners. 

This little girl has been in foster care for about 3 months and has  trained quickly. She is smart, learns quickly and has grown to become confident dog with a playful nature. She has learned to walk on a leash, crate train and house train quickly. She is very food motivated and will require a home that will work with her on basic obedience and gives her guidance. Baby Jade can be a little stubborn and her favorite activities include stealing peaches off the trees and searching for pecans in the grass. She can be a little stubborn at times and tends to run off and explore on her own, while the other dogs play. She plays in a group daily with other dogs, both male and female, ranging from young pups to adults, and does great with all of them. She loves to wrestle and roughhouse, if the other dog will allow. When another dog sets boundaries with Baby Jade by barking, growling or correcting her with a bite to the neck, she will back down and go into puppy mode by running away. Baby Jade is dog friendly and great with kids.

She is about 50lbs now and still growing. She recently had a growth spurt and is in that awkward puppy stage where she has skinny body and long, lanky legs. Baby Jade will be a large dog when fully grown, from 80-90lbs, and has an incredibly sweet temperament. She is medium to high activity, and would be an amazing companion for runs, hikes or just a nice casual stroll around the park.

Baby Jade is at an age where she needs guidance and would thrive in an environment with another assertive and more confident dog. She does well with dominant female dogs and takes correction well, however may persist in roughhousing until her human steps in to correct her as she is all about playing. This girl is a tomboy and lives for mud puddles and water- don't let her good looks fool you into thinking she is a girly girl! She is also extremely vocal and \"sings\" when she is hungry, displeased or bored, so be prepared to always have someone talking to you and letting you know how she feels! 

Baby Jade has a high prey drive towards rodents, such as squirrels, rats and possum outdoors. We have not tested Baby Jade with cats, but she is very calm and submissive. She could likely be trained to accept cats, with strict reinforcement.

Background: 
Baby Jade had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. She was found with a broken tail and infected, butchered ears from an amateur crop job at only 6 months old. She came to us as a stray, found by a Good Samaritan who saved her life after seeing a man beat and kick her on the street for approaching his dog while on a walk. He said she was vicious and tried to throw her into oncoming traffic. 

Vetting: Baby Jade has received the standard DHLPP vaccine, rabies vaccine and Bordatella vaccine. She is spayed, microchipped and heartworm negative. We recommend that all rescue dogs coming from Texas remain on heartworm preventative for 6 months after arriving in Washington, as a precaution.

Ideally, dogs should be pottied every 4 to 5 hours. Dogs cannot be left alone for 8 hours per day. Home check and plan must be carefully thought out and presented at time of interview.

Hi my name is Rascal and I'm a 3 year old Chiweenie. My past is not a happy one and is one that was filled with a lot of abuse, that involved hitting and slapping me and yelling at me. I am so thankful to be given a chance to be adopted by someone who will love me and give me hugs and kisses like my foster Mom. Due to my abusive past, I don't like for someone to look me directly in my eyes while holding me as it scares me. When my foster Mom would do this, I would smile at her showing my teeth. I would not bite and have no bite history, but that's how I showed I was nervous. After a couple of months, I learned my foster Mom would never hurt me and I replaced my smiles with lots of licking and kissing my foster Mom; and now I smile with my eyes. I have never known love or how good life could be.

I'm told I'm a very good watch dog. I'm the first to hear if someone has walked up to the door and I promptly let my foster Mom know.

I love to jump, run and play and love toys. I love car rides and sit like a gentleman in my foster Mom's lap and look out the window.

I don't like to be around other dogs and I do like to harass cats. But I just tease them. If it's time to be kenneled, while I don't like it, I will be a good quiet boy and lay down to sleep. Unless I hear something outside like a knock on the door, then I might bark.

Thank you for reading my bio. I'm hoping that a nice family will adopt me and love me so I can have the life every dog deserves.

name: Teddy (formerly Summer)
description:
Teddy needs a new home!
As much as we vet all of our applicants with questions, screenings and home visits, we don't always find the right home the first time. Some people say they will make a lifetime commitment but when push comes to shove, they can't or won't follow through. This beautiful boy was returned after 8 months in what he thought was his forever home because he is protective and guards his people. He is back in Maryland and up for adoption. Only applicants with husky/chow experience or experience with these types of behaviors will be considered. If you think you are the forever person for this guy please apply today. He is so sweet - he just needs a firm handler!
The adoptive family must commit to ongoing training, visits to a behaviorist and medication if called for. This breed needs to stay busy - they love having a job and must be exercised thoroughly.

Here is Teddy's original bio from 10/2018:
Summer originally came to us in October 2018 as one of 7 dogs MMR took in via an emergency request from The Humane Society of the United States due to the devastation in Houston, Texas when thousands of animals were displaced from their homes and shelters.
He is a gorgeous blend of MUTT and it would be interesting to know what he is. Mostly we see Chow, Shepherd, Husky and Collie but it's a guess. No matter what he is, we can tell you this handsome boy is very sweet and friendly. He likes all people - big and small. We think he is about year old and he weighs in at 50 lbs. He is working on potty training and has improved immensely since in foster care but still has a way to go. He's ok on the leash, he doesn't pull much but we can tell he might make a good running partner. He also lives with some cats and although he is interested in them he doesn't seem to care about them one way or the other. Like most of us, this boy is not without his quirks. He really hates the crate and whines and gets agitated while inside. He stands down to the female dogs in the house but can be reactive to the males - we hope this will resolve itself after his neuter. Last but not least he is a little food aggressive - not necessarily with dog food but if a person has food, is preparing food or even has a wrapper or container in their hand he will try to grab it. We think with some good training he will overcome this as well but for right now we won't place him with kids under 13. He is not at all aggressive if you touch his food while he's eating, he doesn't race to move the other dogs in the house away from their bowls and he doesn't even growl if they come near while he is eating. He really is very friendly otherwise and he is looking for a home where he will get the training he needs and a human who will love him and allow him to snuggle with them. He will be available for adoption after his neuter. *Since this was written he is potty trained and crate trained. He has been living in a home with no other pets but has been fine on walks and at the dog park.
My adoption fee is $350, which covers the cost of routine vetting, rabies and distemper/parvo vaccinations, deworming, spay/neuter surgery, heartworm testing, my microchip, monthly heartworm prevention, monthly flea/tick prevention, and any transport costs if applicable. If you can't adopt me, consider sponsoring my care and being a rescue angel. Click on the DONATE button below and chip in what you can. Your donation is tax deductible and helps us save more lives!

To fill out an adoption application, go to: http://muttsmatterrescue.com/adoption_app.html
You can save animals like this one by becoming a foster home for a dog in need! Fosters are like way stations between high kill shelters and forever homes. We need fosters so that we can save dogs before they are euthanized at the shelters. If you are interested in becoming a foster, please check out our information about fostering on our website: http://www.muttsmatterrescue.com/foster_faq.html
MMR covers the vet care, food, and tools to get started. You supply the love. Fostering saves lives. Sometimes a foster home is the only thing standing between life and death. 9/16/19 8:12 PM

name: Mr T
description:
Updated 8/7/19 - Mr. T is a 10 year old Jack Russell Terrier/Beagle mix (but acts more like a 4 year old).  He can be very active or just chill out .   Mr. T was rescued from a hoarding situation in TN.  He was lucky enough, along with 19 other dogs, to find his way to PA.  Unfortunately, none of the dogs were socialized and were very shy and afraid of just about everything.  Mr. T was the most shy of them all.  After spending over a year in a shelter receiving daily personal interaction, Mr. T got the opportunity to enter the Hounds of Prison Education (HOPE) Program.  He was very afraid of all the noise and commotion in the prison and subsequently moved into a foster home at the beginning of 2018.
 
Mr. T has made significant progress being in a quiet home with his canine foster friends.  He now seeks out his foster Mom to cuddle on the couch during TV time.  He likes to go for walks and walks well on a leash, (he pulls once he knows he is headed home so he can get there as fast as possible).  Mr. T doesn't particularly like the sounds he hears on a walk in the neighborhood, such as garage doors, a car door slamming,  or strange people walking toward him.  He has gotten past most of that and now is starting to really enjoy his local walks.  His favorite activities include going for car rides and running around the dog park.
 
Mr. T is still very wary of strangers and takes time to feel comfortable with strangers.  He likes to take his time trusting and will require a ton of patience in a new home.  He is a really, really sweet boy that just needs love, patience and understanding.  He needs a person or family that will help him unpack all of the baggage he carries from his former life.  Mr. T would do best in a quiet home (no apartments) and one that has at least one resident dog.  At this point, Mr. T has not been \"cat tested,\" but that can be done before being placed in any home with felines.

Mr. T is crate trained and housebroken.  
 
Adoption application, home visit and adoption fee required. If you would like to apply for adoption, please complete the online application at www.furryfriendsnetwork.com. Look under ADOPT tab. Please also read Our Expectations prior to applying.

Foster Homes are desperately needed in order to help more animals like this one. Please consider opening your heart and home to a homeless animal. To find out more about becoming a Foster Parent, see our website at www.furryfriendsnetwork.com. Look under VOLUNTEER tab.

name: Tango
description:
Update 8/6/19  Tango is an adorable, adoptable cuddle bug who likes to snuggle while watching TV.  He is approximately 9 years old and weighs about 25 to 26 pounds.  He is one of the terriers saved from a hoarding situation in TN when the ASPCA went there to rescue animals during flooding.  Tango and 19 others made their way to a PA shelter.  He was one of the most shy and scared dogs of the group.  After being in the shelter for over a year, Tango moved into the Hounds of Prison (HOPE) Program where he received obedience training and given the confidence he so badly lacked.  After graduation from the program, he was placed in a foster home to continue to work on his social skills.
 
Tango has made a lot of progress living in a quiet foster home environment with 3 fur siblings.  He follows his foster Mom and wants to be with her as much as possible.  He also enjoys cuddling and sleeping beside her and enjoys car rides and exercise at the dog park.  Tango has not been \"cat tested\" at this point, but will be prior to any decision to be placed in a home with a feline.  Although Tango likes other dogs and gets along well with them, he could be an only dog.  He is more eager to spend time with his foster Mom than anyone.  However, having another dog(s) is preferable since Tango has never lived without a buddy or two.
 
Tango is now at the point where he will go up to someone who has been a frequent visitor in the home, but still shies away from new people (unless they have a special treat which he is more than glad to snag).  He also does not like a lot of commotion, so apartment living may not be the best fit for Tango (this, of course, depends on the apartment and noise in the neighborhood).  A quiet household with a person or family that has patience to spare would be best.
 
Tango is a very sweet boy who is ready to find a forever home .  He needs an understanding family who will give him space to settle in at his own pace.  Since he is very treat oriented, the fastest way to this guy's heart is through his stomach.

name: Celeste
description:
Celeste and Gideon came to us from a neglect situation involving 10 dogs in Tracy, TN.  I have included their intake pictures so you can appreciate how far they have come.  They went from semi-feral to sweet dogs to run to give me kisses now when they see me.

We don't know their breed or relationship, other then they are for sure a bonded pair and must go and stay together.  We think that Gideon is about 7-10 years old, and Celeste is about 5 years old. Both are fixed, heart worm negative (and on prevention), up to date on shots and micro chipped.  They are newspaper trained and have had dental cleanings done recently.

Celeste and Gideon do very well with each other, and would prefer to be the only dogs.  They are ok with some small dogs similar in size to them, but not bigger dogs.  If you have other dogs, a meet and greet is required.

You MUST have physically fenced that is very secure.  They are diggers and can Houdini their way out at their choosing.  For the most part they have remained inside and just going on newspapers for these reasons.

They travel well in a crate and are very friendly once they get to know you a bit.  They are very food motivated.  Celeste walks well on a leash, Gideon currently needs to be carried, he is not as leash savy.  Both are around the 25-30lbs mark.  Neither have any current health issues that they are being treated for.

Their ideal home would be someone who is home all day who can bond with them and vice versa.  A nice retired person or couple who is looking for some companions would be perfect.  They will need their own room/space as well so that when you go out, they are in a safe space. 

Please contact us if you would like more information about Gideon and Celeste.  Our email address is info@safehaventn.com and you can fill out an application on our website if you are interested in offering these 2 dogs a forever home.  They have been through a lot and have come a long way and are now socialized and ready for a forever family.

name: Tyra
description:
Hello world, my name is Tyra, yes like the super model.  My foster mom says I should be called Sweetie because that is what I am. I am 6 years old, which is a perfect age! I am not a crazy puppy, but I am still an active girl who loves to play! I was due to be euthanized and my two legged guardian angels came to my rescue. I am up to date on all of my vaccines (no cooties here). I am house, crate, and leash trained. My crate is like my own happy place. I like to go there to unwind from all of the playing. I greet everyone that I meet with a big smile and tail wag. I try to sneak a kiss in there every once in a while, but hey I like giving lovingâs. I really like to play with my four and two legged friends all day. I am great with other dogs no matter the size.  I even get along with cats (shocker I know). I am not food or toy aggressive at all. We can all share. I do know how to sit, lay down, and give paw. I do have a tiny spot on my nose that I am seeing my friends at the vet for. I will be getting it removed shortly.

I am currently located in Trenton, OH. If you would like to adopt me please go to www.sophiasgracefoundation.org and fill out the application. I cannot wait to meet my forever family and start the next chapter in my life!

name: Trooper
description:
Trooper is a super super sweet 3 year old Shepherd mix looking for her forever home. She weighs 37.6 pounds and is full grown. Trooper originally came to us from Tuba City and had been found pregnant, skin and bones and covered in ticks. She has since watched all her puppies grow and find their own homes, while she was being treated for tick fever. Now she is tick fever free, has gained weight and is in great shape! This girl is very lovable and adores human touch She is house broken, and rarely barks. Trooper is cautious in new environments until she feels comfortable and trusts the people she is with. She is good on a leash but is still wary when cars pass her. Trooper is happier around smaller dogs compared to larger dogs. She will need a home with a securely fenced backyard and would benefit greatly from having a smaller canine companion to help her build her confidence. description: Roxy just turned three years old. She is a very friendly happy well-behaved girl that you canât help but love! name: Artie
description:
Artie is a very sweet bundle of energy! His owners had taken him from a friend to care for him when he was found as a stray in Tucson over a year ago. When he was found, flyers were posted and attempts were made to find his original owners with no luck. They kept him and took great care for him over the course of a year until he landed here with us.

He is so sweet and likes to try to climb up on you to be pet, and will rest his head in your lap if he thinks he isn't getting enough attention. For the most part he is very curious and affectionate. He does great with other dogs too! He has been to the dog park frequently and loves to run and play. He also loves food and treat, and will get super excitable when you offer him treats! He knows how to sit for them too.

With his excitability, we would recommend no children under the age of 10 for this guy. We also think he would do best in a house that has another dog, and where he isn't left alone for too long, as he is very social and just wants companionship and love.

Please let us know if you are interested in giving Artie a forever home!

Please fill out an application if you want to meet him: http://azhuskyrescue.com/adoption-application/

name: Ganny
description: Ganny is a 2 year old Doberman with a crop n' flop. He was rescued from euthanasia at a Tulsa shelter, and surrendered a couple months later. While he tested negative for Heartworm Disease at the shelter, he was not placed on preventative and was infected with Heartworms. He will be under treatment for three months and will be adoptable during treatment (with DHDR covering the cost). He is sweet and very laid back, although he may gain more young-boy energy after his treatment is complete. He does well with large and small dogs, but not cats. Ganny adores affection and people. He is housebroken, does well in the car, and does great with handling. Ganny has a great nose and would enjoy Barn Hunt or Nose Work. While he heals, he is also working to drop a couple lbs.

name: Samantha
description:
Samantha is a sweet girl who had a rough twist of fate last year. The man who had adopted her several years ago passed away and family members were unable to properly care for her. Samantha came to us infested with fleas, coat in terrible condition, large tumor on her shoulder, and very depressed. We treated the fleas, had the tumor removed (benign!), gave her great care so her coat grew back healthy, and helped her get her good spirits back. Happy and healthy now, she'd love to find a new home where she can relax and enjoy life. She's good with other dogs and a total sweetheart. Very calm and easy to have around, but plenty of spunk left too. Seniors are such great, grateful companions. Samantha deserves her happily-ever-after!

He walks nicely on a leash and pottied outside so there's a good chance he'll be an easy house train. Charles was quiet on the ride to the vet. name: Max in NH
description:
PLEASE DO NOT USE PETFINDER'S \"ASK ABOUT\" BUTTON.  We are very sorry, but those get lost in our process and are difficult for us to manage. Questions about this puppy should be directed to melissa@caninecommit.org.  Anything else may delay the process. (Submitting an application or mini-application is the only way to hold your place.)

Max is a one year old retriever mix. He's a super friendly boy who loves to play with other dogs. Max was rescued from Tupelo Lee Humane Society in Tupelo MS. He's about 45 pounds and is currently doing well with crate training. He is neutered, up to date on vaccinations, and microchipped. His adoption fee is $475. Applications and information about our adoption process is available on our website at www.caninecommit.org. Email melissa@caninecommit.org. 

PLEASE READ:
Again, questions about this dog should be directed to melissa@caninecommit.org. Not e-mailing Melissa directly may delay the process.  Thank you!

YES, ALL OF OUR DOGS ARE IN NH! Canine Commitment does not post any dogs as available until they are here, in NH, and available to meet before committing to adopt.

HOURS:  We operate out of our personal homes so appointments are required to meet our pups.

PROCESS:  www.caninecommit.org.  Click on Adoption FAQ.

OUR LOCATIONS: Canine Commitment has two licensed shelter locations (at our private residences) in the state of NH, abiding by all state and federal import and quarantine laws. We are a 501c3 not-for-profit organization run by volunteers who just want to help save some lives.

IF THE LISTED CONTACT IS MELISSA@CANINECOMMIT.ORG, that dog or puppy is at our Manchester location or being overseen by Melissa.  Melissa is only available via e-mail; the person answering the phone at our published phone number will not have up-to-date information about that dog's availability.  All visitors to Melissa's home must have submitted an application prior to scheduling an appointment.

Thank you, so much, for considering rescue.  Please remember that the reason it can be hard and can take some time and patience to adopt a dog or puppy in our area is that we do not have debilitating overpopulation and we are not euthanizing hundreds of unwanted dogs in our local shelters.  Please also remember that we are two volunteers who give up the privacy of our personal homes, along with dozens upon dozens of volunteer hours each and every week, just to help save some dogs' lives.  We do it of our own free will and do not do it for any kudos or recognition, but kindness and patience are much appreciated as we do our very best to juggle all of the demands on our time.  It takes all of us to make a difference and we appreciate you!



A NOTE ABOUT HOUSETRAINING:  We can tell you about our experience with a dog in our homes and in the fosters' homes down south (prior to arrival in NH).  Please keep in mind that we do this with a lot of pups -- dogs go directly outside when they come out of their crates and usually are not given free range in our homes without supervision.  ANY dog may need time, patience, and consistency to learn your home, your routines, and your expectations of them.  Be patient, buy a bottle of carpet cleaner just in case, and give this new relationship some time and TLC.  Most pups have been in at least three locations prior to going to your home.  They may be confused, unsure of themselves, and looking for cues ... and understanding.  They are living, feeling beings who should not be expected to be perfect instantly. (Sometimes, they are.  Bonus!)

A NOTE ABOUT LEASH WALKING:  In our homes, the pups are in fenced areas. In most cases, volunteers have walked the adult, larger dogs at some point and we have some information from them about the dog's behavior on leash.  Most often, we do not.  Our experience with them on leash is limited to transfers to/from the car, into/out of the vet's office, etc.  Some dogs behave just the way they do in group settings when they are on leash.  Other times, they do not. Do not ask too much of a new, adult dog in your home.  Give them time to adjust before introducing them to other dogs.  Introduce them slowly and with forethought (feel free to ask us for some resources -- we are happy to provide those!).

Join us on Facebook for more photos and to join our community of dog lovers!  https://www.facebook.com/caninecommitmentnewengland

name: Sutton
description: Hello! My name is Sutton! I was transferred into the shelter from Turtle Mountain Area Rescue! I am a very sweet boy! I am still young so there is a lot that I have to learn about being a \"good boy! I get along with some other dogs, I would do fine with children, and if I have some time to get used to them I could like cat too! I just love to play with toys and I would like to have a bunch of them that I can pick from so I don't get bored. I do like to go for walks with you but I could use some more training on the leash, I get excited and I will pull on it! I can't wait to meet you to see if I am the boy for you! Come in and give me a chance! I am sure that you will be so happy that you did!

name: Norah
description:
Name: Norah
Breed: Labrador retriever
Age: Approx. 3 Years as of April 2019
Sex: Female
Good with Dogs: Yes
Good with Cats: Unknown, but can test for approved applicant upon request. Based on her temperament, we suspect she would be fine with kitties!
Good with Kids:  Yes
Heartworm Status:  Negative

Norah came to us with what we are guessing is her biological family member, Margo in mid-2018 from what was initially described to us as a hoarding case in Twiggs County. As we learned more about their origination, our hearts broke for these poor mama dogs. Because when they came to us, they did indeed have three puppies between them, all three of which were approximately 6 weeks old. Norah and Margo have been through a personal purgatory that if a person had gone through, they would be hailed as superheroes. They and 36 other dogs of similar breed and ages were on a property under what from all reports has been described as a den of horrors. None of them had any sort of medical care, all were living in pens outside with little to no shelter. Many had teeth rotten from a steady diet of white bread. Little to no human contact was given to any of them.

Despite all of this, they were the best moms to their puppies. The puppies grew up and have since found forever homes of their own where they are loved and cared for. Norah and Margo both have spent extra time with us learning about people, socializing with other dogs, and getting plenty of medical care and a steady diet of good food. They have both been so appreciative. Itâs truly been a wonder to see their personalities blossom! 

Norah is a flirt. She likes to give you a big puppy smile and dance away from you just out of reach when you go to tickle that little pointy face of hers. Her zoomies are the best; sheâs like a blonde tornado of glee. She likes treats and to dance with Margo. Sheâs a rough and tumble tomboy that likes laid-back personalities in her canine companions. She gets along great with our small dogs and plays in the yard with them every day. She does fine with other big dogs as long as they arenât overly dominant. Despite her horrific past, she has no problems with things like food or resource guarding. Sheâs a soft, gentle, big bottomed girl that is still learning about how nice it is to be part of a pack that includes people. She is not a fan of the camera shutter sound and pretends to be a walrus with big eyes when itâs around.

Norah is still learning the ropes of walking on a leash completely comfortably, and she is making good progress. Her ideal family would include someone that appreciates her courage and is willing to give her the patience and love she needs to bridge that last gap of going from rescue dog to full fledged, comfortable member of a family. It may take her a couple of meetings with her potential family to really get a good sense of her goofy personality; this will be determined by our manager on a case-by-case basis. Norah tips the scales at approximately 60 pounds. 

----

Although our rescue dogs share a common bond with one another, no rescue story is the same (even when similar). Vetting costs vary depending on their health conditions. For us, it is never about the money. We are a non-profit. Thank you for your love and support! All of our dogs are fully vetted: up-to-date on annual shots, spayed/neutered and microchipped with a lifetime registration. We look forward to hearing from you!

name: Baxter
description:
A super sweet 5 yr old Black Lab Mix & 70 lbs of pure baby love.  This sweet boy has seen some tough times but has come through and is doing great.  He was found as a stray nearly starved and no hair on his back. He had raw sores on his neck, head and back. It was also evident by his raw neck that  he had been kept on a chain. 

With the gracious help of a rescue and foster family, Baxter has made a tremendous recovery over the past 2 months.  He is LOVING dog life~ he plays like a puppy & loves his bone and toys. He gets along with our other dogs (took slow introductions and a little time). He also gets along with cats. Mostly just curious but doesnât chase.

Baxter is still somewhat fearful of the outdoors at times. He still gets skittish and nervous when on walks but is getting better over time.  He is also nervous around unfamiliar people. He will need a patient and loving person / family to help continue with his rehab and recovery. Most of his fur has grown back and he is looking so beautiful.

He would do well with a home where someone is home during the day and he would also do better with a home that has  another furry dog companion. He is not aggressive but loves to run, play and engage in dog play. *We wouldnât recommend Baxter go to a home with small children. 

The foster family is willing to help with introductions and transition. They are located in Union County in the Charlotte area.

description:

DOG'S DESCRIPTION
Forest is a very handsome husky mix with two beautiful different colored eyes! He came to us from rural VA where he was found as a stray. No one came to reclaim him so we scooped him up to give him his second chance! Forest gets along well with other dogs and loves attention from humans! He is a large dog who prefers to be a part of a pack and would prefer to go to a home with another canine buddy. He exhibits strong husky behaviors and would be better suited for somebody who has experience with the breed. He would be happiest in a home with a fenced-in yard.
Your new pet will require a refresher in house-training. K-9 Lifesavers strongly recommends all new adopters enroll their new pet into obedience training. This provides for an easier transition into a new home, ensures the dog remains well socialized, and helps form a bond between the dog and the new family.
Adoption fees cover basic vetting, spay/neuter surgery (for dogs over 6 months old), rabies, distemper/parvo vaccinations, treatment for worms, heartworm testing, monthly heartworm prevention and monthly flea/tick prevention (while the animal is in our care), and transport costs from high-kill shelter. Please note that on average, K-9 Lifesavers spend significantly more on each dog than their adoption fee. Adoption fee for HW positive dog also covers heartworm treatment at our partner vets.
Foster Program: Foster homes provide for the temporary care of a rescue until the dog is placed into a loving, forever home. For more information on becoming a foster parent, and our Foster Program, visit http://www.k-9lifesavers.org/foster/ or email our Foster Coordinator at foster@k-9lifesavers.org
Sponsor Me! Make a tax-deductible donation today by visiting us at http://www.k-9lifesavers.org/donate/ . Donations help us offset boarding costs and additional medical treatment for those dogs who need it. K-9 Lifesavers receives NO federal funding and survive with your generous support!
