name: Layla (GREAT Family Dog)
description:
While this photo from her at the SC shelter that saved her, is not a good photo, Layla is a GREAT and beautiful dog. She is 3 years old and 55 lbs of love and affection and she loves to play. Layla is good with dogs and kids and cats. She is just so sweet and just another great Labby girl, in need of a forever home. A must meet, for she will steal your heart for sure. (If you do not hear back from us within about 6 hours, send us your phone number, for there might be something wrong with your email!) 
Lovable Mutts Adoption Center is a private, in home, all breed rescue/adoption facility, specializing in all ages and sizes of dogs.  We exist only on the kindness of your donations and adoptions!  We pride ourselves on being an HOLISTIC center and feed only holistic grain free foods and give daily, various, vitamins and supplements to all of our dogs. 

Our dogs are well socialized, very friendly, well mannered, affectionate, and in wonderful health. While some might be timid or shy, we work with our adopters in any way we can, to help them to work with their new family member. We give training tips and behavioral tips and even board for a very reasonable fee. Our dogs are extremely well cared for - most even know how to use a dog door by the time they leave us, know basic commands, and are crate trained!  We stand by our pups/dogs, and give 10 days for a refund and almost always take our dogs back at any age of their lives (can sometimes depend on the dog)! 

Lovable Mutts Adoption Center has an application screening process.  All applicants are asked to provide vet references, personal references, and a home visit.  We pride ourselves in matching up the right dog with the right home.  Sometimes this happens quickly and sometimes it might take awhile.  We hope you understand and are willing to wait for the perfect pup for your situation. We reserve the right to turn applicants down and to change our mind about a suitable match, for we are only concerned about what is best for our dogs.  Also note that we arrange our visiting hours around your schedule, as this is a private, in home facility.  We respond to all inquiries promptly, so if you have any trouble sending us an email, or have not heard back from us within 24 hours, please, CONTACT US AGAIN and check your spam!  (We all know how emails can be at times!)

Our dogs are spayed or neutered (if old enough), up to date on vaccines, wormed, heartworm tested, and free of fleas and ticks.  We temperament test our  dogs and they are all suitable for many family situations. Our dogs are well mannered,  and are in our family/home situation at this time (not kept in kennels or crates), and are worked with daily.  All of our dogs do well with other dogs and many do well with cats, and we can cat test. Adoption donations vary with age, breed, vetting, and training of the dog, and range from $250 to $500. This donation helps to pay for shots, de-wormings, spays, neuters, flea protection, heartworm/Lyme testing, treatments, and other vetting/issues that might be needed, for dogs in our care.  (We do not tend to place puppies or small dogs with kids under 6 and reserve the right to match who WE feel would be the best homes for our dogs.)  
Please, come adopt one of our Lovable Mutts - you will be so glad you did!

name: Irene
description: Irene was rescued during Hurricane Harvey and later came to Best Friends from a humane society in Utah. At first, shy and fearful with strangers, but now she warms up quickly and turns into a silly goofball. Her little body wiggles with joy when she sees her human friends. She loves to play with other dogs at Dogtown, and she has been a good role model for her doggie roommate. Irene loves to have weekly play dates with new dogs! She even passed a cat test at the Sanctuary.

name: Kenya
description: When Kenya sees someone she knows, she does a happy dance, wiggling around and folding her body in half. Then she'll sit at your feet and ask to be petted. Born in 2006, Kenya came to the sanctuary from a Utah shelter. Here at the sanctuary, she and her trainers have been working hard on some behavior issues. Although she is calm and friendly when meeting people on a leash, she is protective of barriers and can seem a bit fierce on the other side of a fence or gate. She has bitten before, so she needs a very understanding person who is willing to work with her on her barrier issues. Although she loves to play with toys and with people, she does not get along with other dogs, so she would do best as an only pet. Kenya is looking for a home with a dog-savvy person (or people) who can see her potential and will continue to work with her. She would be thrilled to meet you if you think she might be a good fit! Kenya is part of our Single Pets* program! That means that she is eligible for a free flight home and waived adoption fee! *Single pets do best as the only dog or cat in the home.

name: Pita
description: Pita was saved from a horrible high kill gas shelter in Utah. He is about a year old male that is very sweet and cuddly. He will be flying to Maine for foster within the next month. If you would like to fill out an application, please go to www.underhoundrailroad.org.

name: Yahtzee
description: Yahtzee is a 10 year 29 pound beautiful fawn color Cocker Spaniel. CAWS pulled Yahtzee from a Valencia, NM shelter where he was found as a stray, and hitched a ride on a transport back to Utah. He arrived very sick and lethargic. Took him to the vet within a couple days and learned he had pneumonia and bad ear infections. He was placed in isolation for a few weeks to get over his illness and regain his strength. Once he was able to get out and be a part of the family pack, hes been thriving ever since. Our little man was a fighter who wanted to live and now be part of the good life! Yahtzee has had a dental with 12 extractions. He has arthritis in his back legs and hips so will be on pain medications for the rest of his life. Due to this arthritis he should be in a home with very minimal steps or none at all. Yahtzee can totally be trusted in the home when his 2 legged people arent home. He is dog door trained. He loves his 4 legged siblings, male and female, small and large. He doesnt sleep on the couch or bed, he prefers a bed on the floor. His sight isnt 100% but he sees enough to get around. His hearing might be a little less than stellar as well. He is a very nervous little man, he will pace at times and his legs shake with nervousness. Yahtzee will play with chew toys on the floor every once in a while and he loves to tear up empty paper towel and toilet paper rolls. With his big floppy ears he comes to share after hes had a drink by dragging his ears across you, so cute, well okay, really kind of not that cute, but it goes with the territory. He will need regular grooming. This precious and sweet little man is pure as they come. Now its his time to find his forever family that will show him the unconditional love he deserves! He will surely melt your heart. Due to Yahtzees nervousness he needs to go to a home with no children, or at least older. He also needs a home with a fenced yard and no stairs, or very minimal steps due to his arthritis in his back legs and hips. Yahtzee is not a barker, very occasional yap. If you are interested in adopting a CAWS pet, please fill out an online application at http://caws.org/adoption-application

name: Iggy - Amazing, Amazing!
description:
Meet Iggy! He is incredible! He is deaf but that bothers him none! He knows 9+ signs, is super smart, loves tennis balls and with a proper intro to other dogs, can be so happy!

Iggy loves to play. He has waited forever to find a home and since he is new to us, we hope to find him a great home in the Pacific Northwest. Originating from Best Friends in Utah, we are so excited to have him here.

His local coach has worked with many deaf dogs, curiously most have white coats. They are the best.

He is a big snuggler, loves to play tug of war, chase balls and going for a walk, hike or run is all on his bucket list!

He is now updated on all shots, neutered and will be chipped. His adopt fee is $395.

We cover the medical to prepare the pet for adoption and the adopt donations go directly to cover those costs and range from $295-$495. Thank you for stepping up to save a life!

To expedite to meet with this dog, please go to our site at www.savinggreatanimals.org and fill out an application. We look at the first applications to arrive, so we hope to hear from you soon!

name: Ryder
description: Ryder is your guy! He is approximately 2 years old and a Golden Retriever/Border Collie/Heeler mix-best guess. He is a beautiful strawberry blond and has a long lean body with a docked tail. He loves being part of a pack and gets along well with other dogs. He was found as a stray from the Ute reservation in Cortez, NM, and is so glad he caught his freedom ride to Colorado. This smart goofy guy rides well in the car and hopes to become your favorite adventure buddy. He can be a little reserved at first, but once he becomes comfortable, he is affectionate and enjoys shadowing your every move. Ryder is housebroken and does well in his crate, although he prefers to be outside or free roam in the house. He is learning how to live in a house and once he masters his leash skills, he will make an awesome running buddy. Ryder is UTD on shots, neutered, and microchipped. He will do best with an active home, and someone that will be willing to continue his training. He would love a home with a companion dog, and older kids would suit him fine.Ryder is being fostered in Littleton. Want to meet Ryder and fall in love? Apply to adopt at rezdawgrescue.org

name: Camelot
description: Camelot was found abandoned, however we did find the owner.  Unfortunately he is being deported and is not interested in helping to find Camelot a home. name: Hearth (Tyson) - Massada pup 1
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs1066

Hello! My name is Hearth AKA Tyson. I am 7 years old and about 68 pounds. Don't let my age fool you I am an active guy! I LOVE walks on the beach and am learning that car rides can be kinda awesome. They say I'm a lab mix BUT I think there may be a shepherd in my family tree since I have this handsome fur. I was with my first family for a long time but they had to move and couldn't take me with them, so now I am hanging out with my foster Dad and learning lots of new and exciting things!! My foster Dad says I'm a pretty special guy. I am an expert level cuddler and love getting scritches and rubs! My favorite chew is this yak stick thingy. Yum! 

I would probably be best as an only dog or with a single calm, balanced doggie friend who could be my wingman if I get nervous.... but I am still not willing to share my nachos! Some things are sacred! Because I'm a big strong athletic guy (foster Dad says I'm just big boned) I need a human who has some experience and willingness to continue my training to help me be the best boy! 

Great Things about Tyson!
-Crate Trained
-House Trained
- Knows some obedience - sit, stay, down, paw, place, crate, heel
-LOVES people
-Been good with children I have met
- Affectionate
- Active but not high energy
- Loves chew toys
- Learning to like toys, especially this one that looks a little like p-o-o-p ;)

name: Jenny
description:
Jenny is a small female terrier who is estimated to be about two year old.  She is about 8 lbs, and is looking for a forever family who will not abandon her anymore. 

In a very remote part of southeast part of Korea, Jenny was found on the street abandoned by her human family.  We do not know how long she has been living on the street, but she was very thin, and also tested positive for heartworm.  She was relocated to a near by shelter, but we had to rescue her out when it was time for her to be euthanized to a nice foster home who was willing to take her in while she was being treated for HW,  Her personality was really blossoming while she was with the foster family, and we realized she is just another loving pup who likes to be petted, loves going for a walk, and plays with her toys.  She also loves people, and furry friends at the foster home.  We were told she is not much of a barker, which would make her a perfect city dog where she can live in an apartment, and gets to go to a nearby dog park to play with other dogs!  Now, she has to take is the monthly HW meds just like any other dogs, but other than that, she received thumbs up from the vet, and she is ready for his forever home!

We believe people who adopt rescue animals because they are willing to accept a bit of imperfection, and willing to embrace, work/ train and love them no matter what baggage the animal had in the past. It can be challenging, but extremely rewarding. We have seen amazing transformation in our adopted dogs who have been with loving families, and it is our goal to provide all of them with the opportunity. We are at our happiest when we see photos of our adopted animals smile with the new adoptive family, and we hope to find Jenny a loving family who would do the same. 

Please consider adopting Jenny and making her part of your family! If you would like to apply to adopt Jenny, you can download an application here: 

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1u_YTSKWFVkNYLUcJbCVvfyQnguL-gHi8JGG59XOIIog/edit 

You can MEET Jenny upon request or at one of our adoption event in the near future.  We will post the exact date once we finalize the plan.  Please refer to our facebook page for more info:

https://www.facebook.com/Band4Animal/

 *NOTE* We have a 30-mile radius limit from Fairfax, VA for adoption.  We require a completed application & home check to adopt. An adoption fee o$500 applies. All dogs are spay/neutered and have all shots prior to adoption. We will not respond to anyone who has not filled out the application, but request to meet the dogs. Thank you!

name: Tom
description:
Tom is a male Maltese who is estimated to be about two year old.  He is about 11 lbs, and is looking for a forever family who will not abandon him anymore. 

In a very remote part of southeast part of Korea, Tom was abandoned in a crate along with his playmate, a small 7lbs Pomeranian by his previous owner near a high kill shelter.  We do not know why, but incidents like this happen all the time to our furbabies in Korea, where the dogs have been part of the family for some time, and one day, they become disposable.  Tom and his friend were rescued out of the kill shelter when it was time to be euthanized, and now that he feels that he is safe with us, his personality is really blossoming.  He loves people, and loves getting petted.  He does not like it when other dogs try to take the attention away while he is sitting on your lap, and would growl, but he never attacks.  He is relatively very calm, and not hyper.  He plays well with other calm dogs but stays away from dogs that are more jumpy.  When he was rescued, he tested positive for heartworm, but he has been treated for HW since then. name: Doodle Dandy
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8551

2-3 year old Male beagle about 15lbs. Was found in a southern Virginia shelter by a volunteer. 

This dog tested positive for Ehrlichia before arriving to the rescue. Ehrlichia is a very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Ehrlichia is not contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get this disease is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8549

 Diane von Furstenberg is a beagle mix girls who is about 5 years old and 27 lbs. Just look at those melting chocolate eyes and smooth long ears - talk about easy on the eyes. 

Diane, who is is fondly called Jolene by her foster family, is a pretty low-key dog. She is timid around new people and will need an adopter who understands that she's going to take some time to warm up. This is all so new to her, and we don't know her background, so perhaps she hasn't had a loving home before. She is very playful with the other dog in her foster home, and this is when we see her fun, quirky side come out. Her foster family is working on slowly socializing her, and helping her to build confidence so her true personality can shine. She is working on her house-training, and does well in a crate - no accidents there, and she is a quiet sleeper. And she walks well on a leash. She is just the sweetest little thing, and we will update her profile as she comes out of her shell more.

This dog tested positive for Ehrlichia and Anaplasmosis before arriving to the rescue. These are very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Neither is contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get either is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

name: Lulu
description:
Lulu, who is a terrier/ Maltese mixed female terrier is about 9 mo puppy. She and her sibling Lucy (who was happily adopted in VA) were both rescue from a temple in the remote southeast part of Korea. Their mother, Star, who is a small Maltese belonging to a man who works at the temple, was raised as an outdoor dog, tied up to a post. In Korea, the winter weather is very harsh, and they get a lot of snow, and we have no idea how a little Maltese survived all those years! The man decided to give up these two pups, since they have no place for growing family, and after much resistance from the man, we were finally able to convince him to also surrender Star to us. Star will also be joining us soon here and hope to be reunited with her babies!

Lulu is such a friendly pup, and plays well with other dogs and people. She is very loving and sweet, and weighs around 9 lbs currently. We believe she will be under 15 lbs even as a full grown. She loves playtime, treat time, kiss time, naptime, and did I mention playtime and kiss time?? She is a perfect small terrier who is fun and friendly, but because she is mixed breed, not designer breed dogs, she has a zero chance to be adopted in Korea. Since she was with our foster's family, we are happy to report Lulu has mastered the potty training, and she is on target 95% currently. We would love to provide a family who already have a small furry friend in their because Lulu likes to play with other dogs. Other than that, she received a clean bill of health from the vet, and she is ready to be adopted! 

We believe people who adopt rescue animals because they are willing to accept a bit of imperfection, and willing to embrace, work/ train and love them no matter what baggage the animal had in the past. It can be challenging, but extremely rewarding. We have seen amazing transformation in our adopted dogs who have been with loving families, and it is our goal to provide all of them with the opportunity. We are at our happiest when we see photos of our adopted animals smile with the new adoptive family, and we hope to find Lulu a loving family who would do the same. 

Please consider adopting Lulu and making her part of your family! If you would like to apply to adopt Lulu, you can download an application here: 

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1u_YTSKWFVkNYLUcJbCVvfyQnguL-gHi8JGG59XOIIog/edit 

You can MEET Lulu upon request or at one of our adoption event in the near future.  We will post the exact date once we finalize the plan.  Please refer to our facebook page for more info:

https://www.facebook.com/Band4Animal/

 *NOTE* We have a 30-mile radius limit from Fairfax, VA for adoption.  We require a completed application & home check to adopt. An adoption fee o$500 applies. All dogs are spay/neutered and have all shots prior to adoption. Thank you!

description:

Say hello to Mia, a nine-month-old, 30-pound female Desi dog (a local term for street dog) from India. Walks, couches, grassy open spaces, and toys (even sticks will do!), have all been big hits. When Mia is comfortable she is a funny, happy, and athletic girl whos happy to spend a few minutes wrestling or racing with the other dogs in her foster home, and then a few more minutes snuggling with her foster mom. 

Mia thrives on routine and attaches very deeply to her household members. Although she would benefit from ongoing exposure to new situations and people, she would probably be happiest in a low-key household with one or two people, who can help her develop a sense of security and confidence. description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8261

Say hello to Mia, a nine-month-old, 30-pound female Desi dog (a local term for street dog) from India. Walks, couches, grassy open spaces, and toys (even sticks will do!), have all been big hits. When Mia is comfortable she is a funny, happy, and athletic girl whos happy to spend a few minutes wrestling or racing with the other dogs in her foster home, and then a few more minutes snuggling with her foster mom. 

Mia thrives on routine and attaches very deeply to her household members. Although she would benefit from ongoing exposure to new situations and people, she would probably be happiest in a low-key household with one or two people, who can help her develop a sense of security and confidence. Those people will find in Mia a dog who is endlessly entertaining, unbelievably charming, and absolutely devoted!

Her life started out a bit rough, she was surrendered with her siblings who all were undernourished and scared. She made her way to OPH and has grown so much both physically and mentally. Please note that because she is so young, she has only received 2 sets of the required 3 sets puppy vaccinations. This is very IMPORTANT because it means that her immune system will not be fully functioning until about 16 weeks of age. She MUST stay out of public places where she could be exposed to the germs of many other dogs for another 6-8 weeks after she goes home. These no puppy zones include all pet stores, dog parks, and for apartment dwellers, areas used by other dogs. These requirements are strictly for the puppys medical safety and longevity.

name: The Hobbit
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8481

 Meet The Hobbit - known fondly to her foster family as Lady Arwen or Lady for short. She is a 45-50 pound, one year old, beagle/spaniel/lab mix is our best guess. She has gorgeous creamy coloring and luxurious fur - hard to keep your hand out of it. And she doesn't mind the gentle petting and attention at all. She has her nose to the ground all the time - perhaps a nod to her beagle heritage? And she has long silky fur that one might associate with a spaniel. She is so gentle and sweet, and has done beautifully with children, other dogs and car rides. Each day we see more of her exquisite personality shining through. She's very loving and sweet. She's also smart and loves to cuddle. She's been really great with our 2 year old and our 12 year old twins, but our 7 year old is a little too rambunctious for her.

More about this darling girl:
- She is house trained in her foster home, and has visited homes of family members and remembered her house manners there as well.
- She is crate trained, and knows that her crate is her personal den and uses it at time to get some downtime, to relax and unwind. She is a smart girl understanding her personal space.
- She is working on improving her leash skills. She likely never walked on a leash before coming to her foster home, and she likes to pull. With training she is improving and to become really adept and walk on a loose leash, her adoptive family will need to continue the training process.
- She may be shy when meeting new people, but she has impeccable manners - not a jumper
- She is learning her house manners - she likes being on the couch which is fine in her foster home, but she may have to be trained otherwise in her adoptive home. She is very agile and has jumped up to get food from the table. She is learning quickly that is is not acceptable in her foster home. 
- She is generally quiet. She will alert at random times but it's few and far between.
- She is learning to trust humans more thoroughly and quickly, and her fosters are consciously socializing her to help her build confidence. She would rather people kneel down to pet her instead of looming over her. She gets nervous if someone comes up behind her too quickly and can startle if she is bumped into by accident. I think she needs more work on trusting humans in general. She shows no reactivity or aggression, but retreats to her crate if she feels overwhelmed. 
- She loves to run around in the backyard. She loves to play with other dogs. She seems to be a moderate energy dog and she is still trying to figure out how it all works inside a home.
- She loves to play with other dogs.
- She has not been exposed to cats, but her foster thinks she could do well with a confident cat. She's tried to go after squirrels on walks and birds get her attention.
- She will do best with a patient adoptive home where they can continue to show her that humans are a good thing and being apart of a family is where it's at. Possibly someone with another confident dog to help her to continue to gain confidence in a home.

This dog tested positive for Anaplasmosis before arriving to the rescue. Anaplasmosis is a very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Anaplasmosis is not contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get this disease is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

name: Cardi
description:
Hello, my name is Cardi, although my foster mom usually calls me \"Sweet Girl\" or \"Pretty girl.\" I came to ODHS from a hoarding situation, and when I got to my foster house, I wouldn't even come out of the back of my crate for the first 2 days. Since they had me come out of my crate, they've been working with me a little more every day and they tell me how proud of me they are for making progress every day. I've been with my foster family for about a month now and I've gotten much more comfortable with them. I love to follow my foster mom around the house everywhere she goes. I wag my tail and do my happy dance when I see my foster family now. I went from being scared of them, to loving getting pets and treats from them. I love treats! I hardly ever run into my crate when they are home now, because I enjoy being out in the house with my foster fam. I do great with going potty outside in my little puppy pen. I stay in a crate when my humans leave the house and at bedtime. I have 3 human siblings (ages 7-11) in my foster family and 2 canine siblings that are both close to my size. I have done well with my human siblings because they are very calm and patient with me. I don't think I would like to be with young kids that don't know how to be patient and calm with me and give me my space to build up trust with them. I now love playing with dog toys and chasing balls. I love running around and playing with my 2 year old canine brother.  I'm not a big fan of my older canine foster brother though. I have come a long way during my time in my foster home, so although I'll have a transition period to go through in my new home, I know I would blossom with having a fur-ever family. I would love a family that understands that I will need time and patience to build up trust and know that they are good and love me and help me to understand that the world isn't so scary. Will you be that family?

My first adoption event will be 9/25, which is also my \"go home\" eligible date.

description:

name: Belle (& Taco)
description:
This sweet bonded pair, Taco & Belle, have had unfortunate luck in their very short lives. They lost their original owner suddenly to a stroke and were passed around to different family members for a few months. They ended up with the 80-year-old grandmother who was legally blind and taking care of her disabled son, so she didn't have the time or bandwidth to take on two young dogs. A family member reached out to Worthy Dog for help, and we gladly took them in.

The duo came to N. VA and were adopted in February by a very sweet couple, and we thought they had found their forever home. Sadly, their current mom, Lynn, who is only in her 30's, is going through a significant and unexpected health challenge, and suffering from kidney failure. She had a kidney transplant 18 years ago and was in great health when she adopted the pups. The couple was so very excited to have these dogs, and even started an Instagram account for Taco & Bell to share updates

About two months ago, Lynn's kidney started failing, and she ended up in the hospital for weeks. She is now on the transplant list waiting for a donor and has to do dialysis 3 to 4 days a week. She travels from VA to MD to a military facility for treatment, and the dialysis wipes out her energy when she gets home. Lynn has been the primary caregiver for the pups and had the flexibility to work from home. Her husband is active duty, and travels frequently, so he's not home during the day to help. Her mom and friends have been helping out, and kept Taco & Bell when she was hospitalized, but it's not a long-term solution.

In the interest of the dogs, Lynn has made the difficult decision to rehome them. She feels they aren't getting the time and attention they deserve, and with another transplant surgery in her future, she may be out of commission for an extended period. She wants to find a home for them before transplant surgery, and have peace of mind that they will be well taken care of. She is fostering them until a great family can be found.

TACO & BELLE

Taco & Belle have been together their whole lives and are a bonded pair. Taco is more timid, but loves his buddy Belle, and looks to her for reassurance. Taco needs a little more time to settle in and trust, but once he connects, he's very trusting and affectionate. Both dogs fancy themselves lap dogs once they get to know you.

This adorable duo loves to play and will keep each other entertained during the day. They are crate trained, enjoy their daily walks, and are potty trained, but do need regular potty breaks. Belle lets you know she needs to go out, and Taco will follow her lead once he settles in. Initially, Taco was prone to marking or excited peeing when he was unexpectedly picked up, but that was more about nerves. They used a belly band to settle him in, and both dogs have been trained on pee pads. Lynn will leave them gated in the kitchen when she goes in for treatment, and has a dog walker or her mom come in when she's out of the home for more than 5 or 6 hours.

These two pups are very connected, so we will only adopt them out as a pair. They are buddies who love to play and nap together and keep each other entertained. They are both afraid of loud noises and strangers and need time to acclimate to visitors, but once they know the person, like grandma, they are all excitement and kisses.

We feel a quiet, calm home is the best fit for them - an adult or senior couple, or empty nesters would be ideal. If you are looking for two little pups who will add joy and much entertainment to your life, please apply today. They are long overdue for their forever home.

Breed: Chihuahua
Weight: 12 lbs (needs to lose a pound or two)
Age: ~ 2 to 2.5 years
Gender: Female
Adoption fee: $500 (pair)
Vetting: updated on vaccines, dewormed, spayed microchipped.
Location: Gainesville, VA

FOR MORE INFO OR TO ADOPT: Please go to http://adopt.worthydog.org and complete the application.

You can also help save dogs like this one by becoming a foster, providing a rescue dog with a temporary home and giving them the love and care they need until they are permanently adopted. Every person who fosters is directly responsible for saving the life of a dog, because we can only save as many dogs as we have foster families available to welcome them into their homes. A family member reached out to Worthy Dog for help, and we gladly took them in.

The duo came to N. VA and were adopted in February by a very sweet couple, and we thought they had found their forever home. Sadly, their current mom, Lynn, who is only in her 30's, is going through a significant and unexpected health challenge, and suffering from kidney failure. She had a kidney transplant 18 years ago and was in great health when she adopted the pups. The couple was so very excited to have these dogs, and even started an Instagram account for Taco & Bell to share updates

About two months ago, Lynn's kidney started failing, and she ended up in the hospital for weeks. She is now on the transplant list waiting for a donor and has to do dialysis 3 to 4 days a week. She travels from VA to MD to a military facility for treatment, and the dialysis wipes out her energy when she gets home. Lynn has been the primary caregiver for the pups and had the flexibility to work from home. Her husband is active duty, and travels frequently, so he's not home during the day to help. Her mom and friends have been helping out, and kept Taco & Bell when she was hospitalized, but it's not a long-term solution.

In the interest of the dogs, Lynn has made the difficult decision to rehome them. She feels they aren't getting the time and attention they deserve, and with another transplant surgery in her future, she may be out of commission for an extended period. She wants to find a home for them before transplant surgery, and have peace of mind that they will be well taken care of. She is fostering them until a great family can be found.

TACO & BELLE

Taco & Belle have been together their whole lives and are a bonded pair. Taco is more timid, but loves his buddy Belle, and looks to her for reassurance. Taco needs a little more time to settle in and trust, but once he connects, he's very trusting and affectionate. Both dogs fancy themselves lap dogs once they get to know you.

This adorable duo loves to play and will keep each other entertained during the day. They are crate trained, enjoy their daily walks, and are potty trained, but do need regular potty breaks. Belle lets you know she needs to go out, and Taco will follow her lead once he settles in. Initially, Taco was prone to marking or excited peeing when he was unexpectedly picked up, but that was more about nerves. They used a belly band to settle him in, and both dogs have been trained on pee pads. Lynn will leave them gated in the kitchen when she goes in for treatment, and has a dog walker or her mom come in when she's out of the home for more than 5 or 6 hours.

These two pups are very connected, so we will only adopt them out as a pair. They are buddies who love to play and nap together and keep each other entertained. They are both afraid of loud noises and strangers and need time to acclimate to visitors, but once they know the person, like grandma, they are all excitement and kisses.

We feel a quiet, calm home is the best fit for them - an adult or senior couple, or empty nesters would be ideal. If you are looking for two little pups who will add joy and much entertainment to your life, please apply today. They are long overdue for their forever home.

name: Wink
description:
VIRGINIA AREA -- Wink is a perfect little sweet companion estimated to be about 9 years old, neutered male who weighs about 10 lbs. Wink is a miniature poodle that went through so much before he came to us.  When Wink was rescued, he was in terrible condition and every square inch of his body was pink and he was itching constantly.  Vet examined Wink and diagnosed him with scabbies, chronic ear infection (which explained why he was snappy when someone try to pet him in the head) and in addition, he was heartworm positive.  It was obvious that such a tiny guy was an outdoor dog in someone's house in the past, and his hair/ skin/ general health condidion was not managed at all.  While he was getting vetted to get the proper medical treatment, he was in the middle of a fight amongst dogs at the shelter, and due to the shock and trauma, one of his eyes popped out which gave him a permanent damage (blinded in one eye).  The ER vet was able to place the eye back in. but not able to save the vision sadly.

But, Wink is a survivor! He completed his heartwarm treatment and fully recovered from scabbies. He still has eczema on his skin, and will need to receive monthly injection of Cytopoint a few more months to be permanently cured of his skin condition, but that is easily obtainable, our foster mom thinks.  Wink was seen by a cardiologist since his arrival in the US, and the symptoms for his heart is also controllable with daily heart meds (Vetmedin, 1.25mg x2 daily).  We were told he does not need to be on Lasix, as long as his breathing is monitored visually.  Wink did however developed symptoms for diabetes since his arrival, and now, he is currently receiving insulin twice a day at his foster home which makes things a bit more complicated.  What a life Wink has..

With so much that Wink went through, we are looking for a family that will shower Wink with love, trust and belief.  Wink is doing his best, but he is afraid of the insulin shots, and he does not know why he is getting poked every day.  His foster mommy is working with a trainer, so that Wink is being less sensitive of his shots currently.  This is a life long commitment, and BFA does not take it lightly.  Wink is still a great companion, and has so much love to give to his family.  Once you get the routine down, giving daily insulin shots won't stop you from loving Wink, because Wink is really that special...(ask his foster moms in the areas, we have a several of them!) We also have to look into whether the adopter is able to afford Wink's medical expanses too since Wink has a several special needs conditions what need routine check up, and will need to be given medicines for life.

If you think you have a small space in your home for a dog that definitely need your help to survive, please consider Wink.  Wink is easy to take care of because he is potty trained, does not exhibit any separation anxiety, and easy to get along with people and other dogs.  We are very sure that Wink will be forever thankful to you and your family, and show you his unconditional love.  

We believe people who adopt rescue animals because they are willing to accept a bit of imperfection, and willing to embrace, work/ train and love them no matter what baggage the animal had in the past. It can be challenging, but extremely rewarding. We have seen amazing transformation in our adopted dogs who have been with loving families, and it is our goal to provide all of them with the opportunity. We are at our happiest when we see photos of our adopted animals smile with the new adoptive family, and we hope to find Wink a loving family who would do the same. 

 Please consider adopting Wink and making him part of your family! If you would like to apply to adopt Wink, you can download an application here: 
 https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1u_YTSKWFVkNYLUcJbCVvfyQnguL-gHi8JGG59XOIIog/edit 


You can MEET Wink upon request at our foster home.  Please refer to our facebook page for more info:

https://www.facebook.com/Band4Animal/

 *NOTE* We have a 30-mile radius limit from Fairfax, VA for adoption.  We require a completed application & home check to adopt. An adoption fee of $500 applies. All dogs are spay/neutered and have all shots prior to adoption. Thank you!

name: Betsy
description:
This dog is part of our shelter outreach program where we take dogs from overcrowded shelters in hopes of finding them a forever home here! We generally do not have much background info on them and cannot guarantee they are housebroken. They are all up to date on vaccines, spayed/neutered and microchipped.
Betsy (32lbs) and Frack (49lbs) came up from VA. They are part of a hoarding situation where they lived with dozens of dogs. This brother and sister pair have lived in the same 15x15 kennel for their entire lives. A rescue group in VA has worked with the owner for the past year trying to spay and neuter and remove dogs from her property. The owner loved the dogs but sadly things got out of control. The rescue group asked if we could help with these 2. Betsy and Frack are 8 years old and a bonded pair so need to go home together. They will need a fenced in yard and a home with love and patience. Betsy is the more nervous of the two. Our staff and volunteers are working hard with them to get them used to other people and different sounds and surroundings. They are making progress and seeking out attention. If you think you may have the right home for these 2, please stop in or call our facility. Fenced in yard required.
Kids 14+*Per JSAC policy, puppies and kittens under 6 months will not be adopted to families with children under the age of 6 years.

name: Felix
description:
Felix and his brother Oscar came to us from a rural shelter in central VA.  They were surrendered along with 3 siblings and from what we are told, all 5 of them had been kept in cages outdoors.  We were also told that Felix is 11 years old, although that is hard to believe when we see him playing with the young puppy in his foster home.  Felix is timid, but does not act like a dog who was kept in his cage for his entire life, so at some point he probably had a home where he interacted with his family.  Hopefully he can find a home like that again.  He is sweet and loving with his foster mom and dad.

Unfortunately, Felix does not get along with all of the dogs in his foster home and would probably do best as the only dog in the house, despite his fondness for the pup that he plays with.  He is extremely interested in cats and it would not be a good idea to leave him alone with one.

Oh, and Felix is missing a foot.  He gets around so well that I often forget to mention that!  If you look closely at the last photo, you can see that his right back leg is just a stump.  Sometimes he limps on 3 legs and sometimes he actually walks on the stump.  He doesn't seem to know he has a \"handicap\".

Felix was very matted when he came to us so we shaved his hair.  Now that it has grown out, he looks exactly like a large Yorkie (he weighs about 15 lbs.)

If you think you might be the one to give this sweet little dog a home for the rest of his life, please email cosmozcause@gmail.com

name: Panda
description: Panda is a senior (born approx 4.1.08) spayed female Akita. She is up to date on vaccines, on flea/heartworm prevention, microchipped, house trained, crate trained, and leash trained. Panda comes to us from the shelter in Suffolk, VA, where she found herself after she didn't get along with the family's new puppy. Panda still has lots of bouncy energy and loves meeting new people and is a wonderful breed ambassador! Panda has gone to daycare with some of the other fosters. She would like a retirement home as an only or with the right mellow male.

name: Athena
description:
Athena is an adult (born approx 5.5.15) spayed female Akita. She is up to date on vaccines, microchipped, heartworm negative, on flea/heartworm prevention, house trained, crate trained, and leash trained.

Athena comes to us from the animal shelter in Spotsylvania, VA. From what we can gather, she has already had at least 3 homes before ending up in the shelter. In March 2018, a family acquired her from someone who was giving her away. In May, they surrendered her to the Stafford County Animal Control because they were moving. A few days later, she was adopted by another family. She did well with them for a while, but then she began to guard her pregnant human and show teeth at the other little humans in the house. They surrendered her to the Spotsylvania Animal Shelter on Nov. 1, 2018. 

Athena is SUCH a good girl, the shelter was very persistent about asking the Akita rescues to take her. Finally the stars aligned and we had a space open for her! She is fantastic in the crate in her foster home and regularly goes to doggy daycare! She would be happy in a home with a large male to play with or as an only pet. No children under 10 years of age, please!

name: Waverly
description:
Waverly is a young (born approximately 10.19.17) spayed female Akita. She is up to date on vaccines, microchipped, heartworm negative, on flea/heartworm prevention, house trained, crate trained, and leash trained. MUST GO TO HOME AS ONLY PET.

Waverly comes to us from Suffolk, VA, where she was picked up by animal control, running stray. She is in very good condition and was found with a collar and Seresto flea collar. Clearly someone had been caring for her, but no one came to claim her. She is very people friendly.

name: Yin
description: Yin is an older (born approx 6.20.10) spayed, female Akita. She is heartworm negative, on flea/heartworm prevention, microchipped, up to date on vaccines, house trained, crate trained, and leash trained. Yin came to us from the shelter in Chesapeake, VA, where she was surrendered because her family could no longer care for her. She had a bad skin infection on her back and was reported to have gotten into a tussle over food with the female Rottweiler she previously lived with. In true girl-fight fashion, all she did was hold the Rottie down and pull out her hair. ? Yin is a sweet, older girl looking for her retirement home

Both were in pretty sad shape with horrible skin which we were told was allergies, but good hygiene and nutrition, plus flea eradication, has allowed the skin to completely clear.  Paperwork from the previous veterinarian indicates that most care was declined.

With good care and her small size, Sadie should live a very long time and enjoy life!  Sadie loves being a lap dog. Introducing Rigby, a cute little mixed breed dog who is about 3 years old and fully grown at 15 pounds.    The first question most people ask is what the breed of the dog is, and the truth is, we haven't a clue!  We see dachshund, Jack Russell terrier, pug and chihuahua, but your guess is as good as any!  Rigby is a happy, healthy dog who would love to have a home of his own!

Rigby is in good health.  He has been neutered and microchipped, given all his vaccines and has had blood tests to rule out heart worms and tick borne illness.  Rigby will do best in a home with experienced pet owners who have a secure environment.  He is good with other dogs his age, but may be better suited to a home without small children.

name: Yahtzee
description: Yahtzee is a 10 year 29 pound beautiful fawn color Cocker Spaniel. CAWS pulled Yahtzee from a Valencia, NM shelter where he was found as a stray, and hitched a ride on a transport back to Utah. He arrived very sick and lethargic. Took him to the vet within a couple days and learned he had pneumonia and bad ear infections. He was placed in isolation for a few weeks to get over his illness and regain his strength. Once he was able to get out and be a part of the family pack, hes been thriving ever since. Our little man was a fighter who wanted to live and now be part of the good life! Yahtzee has had a dental with 12 extractions. He has arthritis in his back legs and hips so will be on pain medications for the rest of his life. Due to this arthritis he should be in a home with very minimal steps or none at all. Yahtzee can totally be trusted in the home when his 2 legged people arent home. He is dog door trained. He loves his 4 legged siblings, male and female, small and large. He doesnt sleep on the couch or bed, he prefers a bed on the floor. His sight isnt 100% but he sees enough to get around. His hearing might be a little less than stellar as well. He is a very nervous little man, he will pace at times and his legs shake with nervousness. Yahtzee will play with chew toys on the floor every once in a while and he loves to tear up empty paper towel and toilet paper rolls. With his big floppy ears he comes to share after hes had a drink by dragging his ears across you, so cute, well okay, really kind of not that cute, but it goes with the territory. He will need regular grooming. This precious and sweet little man is pure as they come. Now its his time to find his forever family that will show him the unconditional love he deserves! He will surely melt your heart. Due to Yahtzees nervousness he needs to go to a home with no children, or at least older. He also needs a home with a fenced yard and no stairs, or very minimal steps due to his arthritis in his back legs and hips. Yahtzee is not a barker, very occasional yap. If you are interested in adopting a CAWS pet, please fill out an online application at http://caws.org/adoption-application

name: Gaby
description:
\"Gaby\" is an approx 1-yr old, 50-lb handsome neutered male Terrier mix (perhaps Jack Russell/Pit Bull?) who is exceptionally mellow, affectionate and well-behaved. Gaby is friendly with people of all ages and would be appropriate for very young children due to his calm nature. (Yes, he takes treats gently from hand.)

Gaby is great with other dogs and very playful with select dogs. His foster caretaker has four other dogs and Gaby rough houses constantly with the one female dog. However,  Gaby does prefer hanging out w/ his foster caretaker. See a video of Gaby interacting with  a few other dogs at GSRSV's rescue ranch elsewhere on this page.

We have not seen Gaby around cats but my hunch is that he'd be OK with them. We'll consider a home with cats for Gaby.

Gaby is fully housetrained and very well-behaved inside. He's never had an accident indoors even though it's likely he was kept as an outside dog previously. Gaby does not know  even the \"sit\" command, but I was able to get him to sit in just a minute or so with a biscuit as incentive. Oh--Gaby loves treats, so he'll likely be very easy to train. 

Gaby is good on leash and has great recall off-leash. He does not wander far when off-leash. He rides well in a car; in fact, Gaby LOVES to go for car rides!  

Gaby showed up at an RV park/marina along the Sacramento River in June. All efforts to find his owner failed so the man who found him (a friend of GSRSV's) offered to foster him until we could find him a home.

Gaby is located in Verona (small town along the Sacramento River in south Sutter County). His adoption fee is $210.

name: Luna
description:
This petite princess is Luna!  She is about  7-8 months old and weights 35 lbs.   She gets along great with other dogs, loves people, and is good with cats. She was rescued from a city shelter in Vicksburg, MS.  

Luna is housebroken and crate trained. She sees her crate as a safe place and likes to bring toys inside to play with. At night she brings a special toy or two up to bed to chew or cuddle with. She enjoys sleeping all curled up right next to her foster mom and will do best in a home where she can continue to enjoy this bonding experience.  

We donât know her past, but we donât think Luna had a chance to experience a carefree life as a puppy.  Her play consists of what is expected of an 8 month old with sporadic bursts of young puppy-like activity. Luna is focused, does well on car rides and loves a good belly rub. 

She is very smart and will thrive with experienced dog owners who will be able to take her on adventures that continue to work her body and mind.   

We do not provide DNA testing which is the only way to know with certainty which breeds are in her genetic background. Our best guess is that she is a Whippet mix with her long, slender build and markings. She may have White Shepherd in her family tree and Catahoula. We expect her to reach about 40-45 pounds as an adult, but we can not guarantee size at maturity. 

Highlights about Luna:
- Enjoys playing with other dogs  
- Is good with cats
- Housebroken
- Crate Trained  
- Friendly, Affectionate 
- Up-to-date on vaccines
- Super Smart!!
- Food motivated
- Well socialized
- She was tested in August for Heartworm and is negative
- She has been spayed  

Our adoption fee is $375 which includes age appropriate vaccines (such as Distemper, Bordetella, Parvo, Rabies), spaying, worming, micro-chipping, and health exam. Discount vouchers for training, grooming and similar dog related products and services are provided.

name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home. 

If you are interested in adopting or fostering Winter, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Gracie #3
description:
Gracie #3 is an almost 2-year-old spayed black female lab. She weighs 44 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Gracie is a happy but shy girl, who loves adorably once she trusts you, but will take a bit of time and some caution to earn that trust. She absolutely loves other dogs, and has never met one she doesn't like. For this girl, the more dogs in her world, the better. If you are giving affection to another dog, her curiosity will get the better of her and she'll almost immediately come up to investigate. She can be a bit hand shy, even once she trusts you, so just needs humans that will go slow and understand to give her time. When she's in her element, she is silly, rolling on the grass, spinning around and zooming as fast as she can to play \"tag\" with the other dogs. And she's REALLY fast. She enjoys napping on the couch, and will allow herself to be a pillow for the other dogs. She also likes to sleep in bed with her humans and is incredibly silly in the mornings as she considers the bed a safe zone - she'll roll on her back and beg for belly rubs and play bitey-face. She especially loves when the other dogs join in the fun. She's excellent in the crate, and foster mom has spied her sleeping in the crate belly up while she's at work. Gracie prefers to eat alone, and will quickly eat her meals in her crate, or in a separate room, but is nervous eating in front of humans, unless it's people food that you are sharing with her (which she loves!). Her leash skills are pretty good, but she would prefer walking on quiet streets and not on a busy road. Gracie is a shy dog, and is always going to be a bit shy. She warms up to new people, but prefers them in small groups and not making a lot of noise, please. She's not the dog for you if you have rambunctious teenagers (or adults), throw parties often, or if you're looking for a dog to take everywhere with you. She started her life sheltered in a pen, and didn't get the socialization with humans she should have at an early age, so they make her a bit nervous. She's incredibly sweet and loving, and will reward you with her sweet, happy, silly self if you give her love, patience and understanding.

description:
Kayla is an 8-year-old spayed chocolate female lab. She weighs 81 pounds but needs to lose about 5 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Kayla is a happy chocolate girl who likes belly rubs and running in the yard. She has been a loving and attentive mommy to multiple litters of puppies and now she is ready to take her turn in the spotlight. Sheâs a friendly girl with lots of energy who would do best with a family that will give her plenty of playtime outside, long walks, and lots of love. Kayla is good with dogs, but not cats and approved for kids 10 and up. Kayla is from a rural area and has not been exposed to traffic, noise, or groups of people. If dogs are overwhelmed by their environment, they can exhibit behaviors like excessive barking. To avoid this, for now we are limiting placement to stand alone single-family homes or townhomes in a suburban neighborhood or rural area. As we learn more from the dog's time spent in foster, we will evaluate if placement can be expanded to include a more urban environment and send out an update. 

Foster family reports: Kayla has a vivacious, energetic personality. After spending much of her life outdoors, she is excited to be in her foster home. Her tail has not stopped wagging! She thinks she's a lap dog and would crawl in your lap with the slightest encouragement. She introduced herself to the resident lab with play bows and ran zoomies with him. She is friendly without being either dominant or submissive. Kayla had no problem navigating the hardwood floors. She can zoom up and down stairs. She likes watching TV, especially animal shows and Litter Robot advertisements, which bring her to her feet everytime. (Must be the cat!) She also enjoys watching squirrels outside. This former breeder girl had a litter quite recently and still has enlarged mammaries. She weighs 80 lbs but should weigh ~75. She shows interest in meeting children (approved age 10+). description:
Baby is a 6 month-old spayed female black lab. Baby weighs 30 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Baby is the most charming, sweetest little pup. She is fearless and loves everyone and everything. She especially adores water! Baby is learning to use the ramp to go down the short grouping of stairs outside to the yard, and is getting better at it! She is also learning to go up the big staircase in the house and doing great! To avoid this, for now we are limiting placement to stand alone single family homes in a suburban neighborhood or rural area. As we learn more from the dog's time spent in foster, we will evaluate if placement can be expanded. 

Foster family reports: Update We know that Marley is not her real name so we're trying different names. Right now we're calling her Penny, so we'll see. A couple more facts about Marley/Penny. We're not sure how she got to be so large but she's the most food-unmotivated lab! She may or may not eat her breakfast and she's really not into fruits or veggies. Her thyroid has been tested and is fine. We've never had a pup take treats so gently. We're used to the \"you may lose your fingers\" type of lab. Marley/Penny will go to the door if she needs to do her business. She would like a family who's willing to take the time with her to help her feel comfortable and loved. She'd also like a couple walks a day to help her build up her stamina and lose some of those pesky pounds. She recently visited with a friend for a weekend sleepover and met two very dog-savvy cats. She initially appeared to want to play with them but that was more effort than she wanted to expend and she laid back down. Marley/Penny found the toy basket, and although she is not a huge player or retriever, she periodically picks up a tennis ball and brings it to you or gnaws on one of the many bones all over the house. She LOVES her walks she doesn't go far and not too fast but she loves all the smells and all the people and dogs met so far. Marley/Penny is a very easy dog that requires little more than a place to sleep, a few pats on her head, some belly scratches and some food. Do you have room in your heart and home for Penny?

name: Murry Murdoch da Tank!
description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.

description:
Regina s a 1-year-old spayed female fox red lab. Regina weighs 26 pounds and is up to date on shots. She is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Regina is a very sweet and slightly shy girl. She is a bit slow to warm up to people but once she does she will show you just how sweet she is. She play bows and wiggles her entire body when she sees foster mom. Once she is comfortable with you she will surprise you by stealing kisses when she can. She would benefit most in a somewhat quieter household and a patient one so she can blossom at a more relaxed pace.  Regina gave birth to a rainbow of girls 8 weeks ago. Now that the girls are weaned she is looking for her fur-ever home. All of Regina's puppies have been adopted, and Regina has adjusted very well to life without little ones. She sleeps in a dog bed in the master bedroom. She loves to chase toys and will toss them up into the air with joy. She now tries to engage the resident dogs in play with lots of play bows and quick dashes away. She still LOVES to be outside as much as possible. Currently, she refuses all treats and loses all interest in other activities when strangers are around (this is a change from just a few weeks ago when she settled down nicely with female guests). She continues to change and make progress each week, so it may be a phase that she works through quickly. Her adoptive family will need to be patient while she adjusts to the changes in her life. She still needs to gain a few pounds - she is a picky eater, but will happily munch a dose of Philadelphia cream cheese:). 

Regina is from a rural area and has not been exposed to traffic, noise, or groups of people. If dogs are overwhelmed by their environment, they can exhibit behaviors like excessive barking. name: Papi
description: Papi is a sweet 7 year old (think he is older--he was a previous rescue from a shelter) weighing 9.4 lbs. He is neutered, heart worm negative, and had a recent dental. He doesn't see well out of one eye possible cataract). Something approaching on that side can startle him easily. Papi came to us from a veterinarian in southern Virginia. Papi's owner left him with the vet because he was too much trouble and didn't want him any longer. Papi was at the vets for severe skin allergies which had been an issue on a yearly basis.  Initially when he came to me he didn't have much hair but it has all grown back and looking healthy. He has been doing well with medication and prescription skin shampoo.  Papi usually needs a belly band even though he goes outside. He is usually very timid although he gets excited sometimes especially for a treat. He would do best with a family where someone is home most of the time. If you feel you can love this precious boy with his issues, please submit an adoption application to the American Maltese Association Rescue at wwwe.americanmalteserescue.org. He is being fostered in Bristow, VA.

name: Blake
description:
Blake is a 5-year-old neutered yellow male lab. He weighs 62 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Blake is a sweet, happy boy. He is good with other dogs and used to live with two others in his previous home. We don't know how Blake is with cats. He is very curious and is quite interested in all the daily activity of the suburbs. He loves to look out the window at home and in the car. He has been fascinated by joggers and was completely mesmerized by a sprinkler. He has been very interested in everything the family is doing. He likes to lay in the kitchen while we are cooking and eating dinner, but never begs or gets into the garbage. Blake does not bark and does not jump on strangers. He has not had the opportunity to learn basic commands but has demonstrated he can learn quickly and responds when you correct him. He went from crazy dog on a leash to a calmer and responsive walker on the harness. Blake will make a great addition to a family and will quickly bond. He has loads of personality and has perfect house manners.

UPDATE from Blakeâs foster family:  Blake is a sweet, sweet boy and is doing great in his foster townhome. He is housebroken and has free reign over the house when his foster needs to be gone. He has not been crated; he did scratch at the door when left alone initially, but calmed after a couple of days. His foster works-from-home, so he does get a potty break every four hours. Blake is great with the fosterâs teenager. He knows sit, and he quickly learned paw! He is a great eater, is not protective of his food, and sleeps through the night. He gets excited when you first get home and tends to jump, but that is something that can be trained. Blake is a love bug and loves snuggling in your bed or the sofa - he would a family that will let him on the furniture:) 

Blake is a playful guy and walks ~4 miles each day to expend his energy. He is very strong, and his handler needs to be prepared for him to pull hard if he senses something he wants to investigate. He is learning to walk on a leash and doing MUCH better, but ongoing training is needed. He wants to meet people and dogs on his walks and does well; he has not spent time alone with other pups while with his fosters. Blake is a cuddly, fun-loving boy and is the perfect match for a family willing to give him the exercise and ongoing training he needs. 

Blake is from a rural area and has not been exposed to traffic, noise, or groups of people. If dogs are overwhelmed by their environment, they can exhibit behaviors like excessive barking. name: Chops
description:
Chops is a 10-month-old neutered male yellow lab. Chops weighs 55 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Chops came to us as a very scared pup, but his foster has been working very hard to socialize him and let him know that people and the world are not so bad. He has been building his confidence a little at a time. He is good with dogs but is still a puppy at heart, so can be a little annoying to the older, less playful dogs. He has become much more attentive to people and has started to show more affection and enjoy human contact more. name: Sheba 0725
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Hi there. I'm Sheba. I was picked up as a stray in Texas in July and brought to my foster home at the end of October. I am spayed and have never been pregnant so I was likely not a stray for very long. I am heartworm positive, but will he treated by SSR

I had an interesting first 24 hours with my new foster dad. He picked me up from the nice ladies who drove me all the way from Texas to Virginia and took me straight to a place where I got a bath. I was very good for my bath and allowed him to do all the things that he had to do to get me \"clean\". I thought I was just fine the way I was but the warm water was nice. I then met the 2 owners of the house, Duke who is a German Shepherd like me and Lily who is a Border Collie mix. They smelled Ok, I guess. I did not pay too much attention to them. I then had a look around the house. While I was doing that my foster dad got some food for me which I ate really quickly. He says I am \"overly enthusiastic\" when I eat and I try to see what is on the kitchen counters a lot, but I am just really hungry and it is hard to get over not knowing when your next meal will be. I slept in a crate all night and was so tired, I did not fuss at all.

I then went for a walk around the block. It was a nice walk and I just followed my foster dad. I don't usually pull on the leash but sometimes when I see a squirrel or fox or deer I want to chase them. I don't try too hard to do that because my leash and collar stop me and I don't want to pull too hard.

In the morning I went to the vet. I was very good for the doctor and let her do all the things she needed to. I did not complain at all.

I sometimes chase my tail and chew on it. I also have a bit of a hotspot on my back but that is clearing up. We are going to ask about my tail, though. I have chewed through much of the hair there.

I always like to be with my foster dad but sometimes he puts me in a crate. That is ok but I don't like it when I hear him but can't be with him. I am good with being in my crate at night and when he goes out, though.

I understand a few of the words dad uses to ask me to do things. I know sit, stay (although for these I usually will expect a treat at some point), and come. There are others but he has not figured them out and I am surely not going to tell him what they are. Gotta make him work for it. I have gotten along well with my foster brother and sister so far. I have met dogs when we walk and they have seemed nice. I am not sure how I feel about cats but if they run I will chase them so dad does not think I would be good with them.

name: Apollo the White Knight
description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature. 

If you are interested in adopting Apollo, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

description:
