name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.   

If you are interested in adopting Finn, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Pepe
description:

name: Pokie
description:
Pokie is a 9-year-old neutered male chocolate lab. Pokie weighs 61 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Pokie is an exceptionally loving, sweet boy that adores all people and his toys. This silly boy has a toy on him at all times - so much so that we've had to teach him to check his toy at the door before he goes outside. Pokie has exceptional house manners. He is fully house trained and has full run of the house while we're out. He also loves going for rides in the car. Pokie is quiet and only lets out an occasional bark when there's someone at the door. Pokie is partially blind due to complications from diabetes, but he does see shadows and gets around just fine. He loves running around the yard and playing ball (he listens for the bounce and is quite good at locating it). His diabetes is well controlled with two injections a day that are quite easy to do. Pokie's other passion is food and he equates getting his insulin with a biscuit, so he eagerly sits in anticipation of getting his injection and treat. He would do well as an only dog or have a laid back doggy companion. No kitties. Pokie has so much love to give his forever family. He is such a sweet gentleman, LOVES people, toys and catching some rays. Pokie is mostly blind due to diabetes, but runs full speed around the house. He has excellent house manners and is a complete sweetheart. Pokie would do great as an only dog or with another super laid back companion. 

Foster family reports: Pokie is a wonderful companion. He loves to play with people and is getting along with the pack. Pokie adores everyone he meets and is very affectionate. Pokie loves to play ball (he tracks very well with his hearing). He is perfect in the house - he has never had an accident or gotten into anything he shouldnât. His thyroid and diabetes management have remained very stable. He would probably do best with a quiet doggy sibling or on his own.

name: Maui
description:
Updated 1/27/19 - Hey everyone, itâs me, Maui. I know itâs been awhile so I thought Iâd let you know how Iâm doing here in my foster home. Itâs been great. We had a nice Christmas and foster mom was very impressed that I didnât try to potty on the tree. Really mom??? I know better than that. All my business is done outside.
I have been a very good boy. I now have run of the house and only go into my crate when I want to, not because I have to. I like to follow my foster dad. He is my buddy. He calls me his shadow. Guess that is a good thing. I only bark when I see something outside or my foster sisters bark. Iâm a pretty quiet guy. And I still love my belly rubs!
My foster sisters are fun to have around. Buttercup and I play in the yard and I help Violet track rabbits. Thatâs not as much fun as playing. 
As much as I am having fun here, what I really would like is a home of my own. I know my forever home is out there. If you meet me, I know you will just fall in love with me. Iâm that kind of a guy. 





UPDATE - 23 OCTOBER 2018: Hey there, Iâm Maui. And I just have to tell you that I love being in a home!! I have been with my foster family for over a week. I have a real cool Mom and Dad and 2 awesome sisters. I have several warm and comfy beds to choose from. Or on occasion, I may curl up on a chair. I get 2 meals a day and a yard to run around in. Life is good!! Especially when I get belly rubs, which I ask for often. I will roll over on my side or back and Mom will rub my belly. She thinks itâs cute.

My Mom says that I am a good boy. I do all my business outside and I keep my crate clean and dry during the day. I enjoy running in the yard with my sister. And we like to play and rough house. Itâs so much fun.

Now donât get me wrong, I really like it here. But what would really be even better is if I had a forever home of my own. That would make my life perfect.
 So if you are looking for a fun loving, easy going good boy, check me out. I wonât disappoint.

description:
Courtesy Listing!
Courtesy dog listing, please direct all inquiries to the information provided within the bio below (CBCR does not warranty any information provided about courtesy dogs listed)

About Waylon:

Sex: Male
Age: 9 years, 4/2010
Coat: Black, long
Weight: 60 lbs
Activity Level: Companion
House Trained, Neutered, Current on Vaccination
Prefers a home without: Small Children

Biography:
My Uncle Joe passed away last summer and left his dog Waylon behind. Joe was a bachelor and adopted Waylon as a puppy.   They were bosom buddies and Waylon would come with Uncle Joe when he came to Williamsburg to visit from southwest Virginia. They hiked together and generally hung out. They lived on about an acre and Waylon had free range with a wireless fence he was well trained on.

After he passed, my sister brought Waylon home to Williamsburg with her husband and three teenage sons. The boys bonded with Waylon and they also had an elderly lab that Waylon got along with.

Does the dog have any history of aggression such as growling, lunging, snapping or biting any adult or child?   Yes
Please explain the aggression history.
My sister noticed him snapping at people. We originally chalked it up to younger kids getting in his face or messing with his tail. He recently snapped at one of my nephews and scared him and my sister. She decided that it made her too anxious and needed to find him a new home.

Reason for re-homing?
We think Waylon will do better with a dog loving person with less coming and going activity in the home. He was used to a pretty standard schedule and limited in and out- especially children.

Location & Contact
Ridge is located in Williamsburg VA.  For more information, reach out to Molly at mollythiel@hotmail.com or 757-345-9781.  Please text first so I know to pick up or feel free to leave a message and I will call you back.

name: Scooter
description:
When we named Miss Nellie, we thought that she was on the verge of being a senior dog. Now that she is healthy and happy; we can confidently say that she has a long way to go before she is a senior. We now call her Scooter; which better describes her personality and her propensity to get frequent attacks of the Zoomies.

She came to us from a rural shelter in southwestern Virginia. She was malnourished, infested with intestinal parasites, and her fur was coming out in clumps. We were also concerned that she may be pregnant. During her wellness check, it was discovered she was indeed pregnant, but the vet felt something was wrong. An ultrasound was preformed and we found out her babies were not viable.  She needed emergency surgery.  If we had waited few more days; she may have not survived.  After a few weeks of recovery at her new foster home in South Carolina; the real Scooter showed herself.. Her coat is soft, full and beautiful. She loves to run around her wooded fenced property chasing away squirrels and any other critter bold enough to trespass.  Due to this, we think she would do best in a home without cats.  She likes going for leash walks and really loves to snuggle with her foster mom.  Scooter gets along with her big ACD foster brother, but is not very fond of other female dogs.  

Scooter is deaf, She may hear really low and high pitched loud sounds. For this reason, we feel a fenced yard is really important for her safety.  She is learning some sign language.  Like most ACD's Scooter is wary of new people until she gets to know them; then she quickly warms up for petting and treats.. She is a goofy, happy girl.  She is crate trained and likes to go for car rides. She has been a very good girl at all of her vet visits and with everyone she traveled with on her journey from Bristol, VA to Richmond, VA and onto Summerville, SC She is still learning about toys, squeaky ones are really fun.

We think Scooter is about  4yrs old, and 35 LBS, She is Heartworm negative, up to date on her vaccinations, crate trained, house trained, spayed, and being fostered near Summerville, SC

If you are interested in adopting Scooter, please visit the Adoption Process page on our website â http://carolinasrescue.com/Adoption_Process.html. You can download our Adoption Questionnaire there, then email it to us at adoptions@carolinasrescue.com. That will start the process.

name: Dood
description:
Thank you for your interest in dog who needs a new home. Adoption can be one of the most fulfilling experiences in your life and especially in the life of your new canine companion.

A note to those looking at CPR. We have no perfect dogs - but many of our dogs have proven to be perfect for a certain someone. Our job is to find those someone's. Our most successful adopters come to CPR not because they want a dog. They come to us because they want to give a dog a home. We urge all of our potential adopters not to fall in love with a picture. While we like to know what you like in looks, a dog is more than a pretty face. Our goal is to match you with the best possible pet for you and your home. We want to create furever families.

Our descriptions contain all that we know about this dog today. We'll update as more information is known.

Are you looking to adopt within the next 30 days? If so please visit our webpage at www.carolinapoodlerescue.org and complete the application. You'll find it in the menu on the left hand side. You'll also find a total listing of all our dogs available.

Just browsing but interested in poodles and poodle mixes? Please drop a note to applications@carolinapoodlerescue.org with your name, address and phone # and email. We'll add you to our mailing list.

thanks
the CPR Adoption team

Date into Rescue: 4/5/2019
Reason for being in rescue: VA shelter- allowed to run at large and picked up one too many times
Foster location: Dreamweaver Farms, Pacolet SC
Special Needs? Dood was deemed a dangerous animal in the state of Virginia. His previous owner would not keep him confined and he was allowed to roam at will. He is happy and gregarious and would run up to people and knock them down as a game. He's not shown any aggressive side to us at all but we all know how to tel him \"GET OFF\" and he's respecting that cue. He needs some training and someone with some common sense.
Weight: 99 lbs
Height: 26 in
Spayed/Neutered: Yes

Adoption Fee: $499

Fence needed? Without exception and it needs to be a solid, dependable fence and you need to plan to be in control of your dog. He's been failed by a human once before because of not understanding our dogs needs us to keep them safe and in places they can safely be, not roaming the streets.

What kind of home would be best for me? Dood's perfect owner will be someone with dog experience, who loves to take long, brisk walks and who would enjoy teaching, shaping and training their dog to be the excellent companion this dog has the potential to be. Dood is affectionate and friendly and longs for that companion that will be his partner, his friend and his guide through life instead of letting him run amuck.

What is my personality like? Dood is an even tempered and intelligent dog who has been allowed to run and roam and that got him on serious trouble. He was part of a pack with his sister Dette.

One of our temperament programs is to take our dogs off site for adventures. Dood is a perfect gentleman in the car just as he was in the trip from Virginia to South Carolina. He is attentive, likes to look out the window and enjoys seeing new places and learning new things.

How do I act when I first meet new people? Friendly. He's been known to bark at people but it's in a \"hi come on over and let's get to know each other\" way. But..as big as he is it is a deep bark and that can intimidate people.

Other tips and tidbits: Estimated Birthdate: 4/15/2015. Dood is a lot of dog with a lot of things going for him. He has been given a very bad rap and very nearly lost his life because his previous owner had no common sense. We are going to be extraordinarily picky about his next home to make sure it's his best home and his forever home.

Dood is NOT completely hypoallergenic. He does very lightly shed. We do not know his heritage but I am betting he is first generation so there is some shedding involved.

House trained? Dogs can be house trained if they are in the right environment and are allowed to follow a schedule as long as a physical reason doesn't keep them from being trained. A dog house trained in my home may not be in yours. We will help you teach your new dog this necessary skill and based on your schedule.

Please note - we do not ship dogs. If you are interested in adopting, please take a look at the distance between the foster home location and your location and make sure you are willing to make that trip. Most of our dogs are at our farm in Pacolet, South Carolina.

To apply, please visit our webpage at www.carolinapoodlerescue.org and visit the tab on the left that directions you to the online application.

Please note that when screening applications, we look at the entire home and then make suggestions based on what would be a good fit for your home. You are not being screened for a specific dog although we are looking to see what type of dog interests you - poodles or non poodles, color, age, etc. Others here may be a better fit for you. It is very difficult to get to know a living animal from a picture and a short description. Since we are constantly getting in new dogs, this may be a dog not in our listings yet. We want you to be very happy with your new companion and will make suggestions based on what you tell us about you.

Thank you for considering CPR.

name: Fergus & Jamie #2
description:

Fergus & Jamie would like a home with a family that will give them lots of love and has a yard where they can play. He is still leery of other dogs, mostly those that are \"in your face\" type dogs. He does well with dogs that just coexist with him and do not try to initiate too much. He gets a little intimated if shown too much attention by another dog. Dagwood has lots of good points. He is good on leash and loves to go on group walks. He is affectionate and well behaved. He is housebroken. He also presents his challenges. He is terrified of a crate and will try to break out. He is an escape artist with containment, possibly from his formative years of having to live in a pen with MANY other dogs. He would be best placed with someone who is home most of the time or where he could go with them a lot. We do not have any cat history on him and he is approved for kids 10 and up.

name: Baby
description:
Baby is a 6 month-old spayed female black lab. Baby weighs 30 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Baby is the most charming, sweetest little pup. She is fearless and loves everyone and everything. She especially adores water! When foster mom was cleaning and refilling the pup pools in the yard, Baby had so much fun chasing the water and carrying the hose. She loves to cuddle and will fall asleep on the couch snuggled up with the other dogs, or next to foster mom. She loves playing with the big dogs and does her very best to keep up with them. She's curious about everything and loves to explore. Baby was born with a neurological condition that affects her movement. She sometimes weaves or stumbles when walking, and needs to be watched near stairs. She is on a low dose of Prednisone and 5mg of Omeprazole once/day to prevent an upset stomach. But this delightful girl still approaches everything full of excitement and joy. She is looking for someone who has a huge heart and maybe a friendly resident dog that will be her buddy. If you have a place in your heart for this sweet, sweet girl, her love will reward you ten-fold.

UPDATE from Babyâs foster family:  Baby's favorite thing to do is play with other dogs and snuggle with them or her humans. She often is found sleeping belly up, as close as she can get to the other dogs or foster mom, and snoring... She loves the new dog bed that she can nuzzle up in as well. Baby is learning to use the ramp to go down the short grouping of stairs outside to the yard, and is getting better at it! She is also learning to go up the big staircase in the house and doing great! She has found her voice and foster mom affectionately refers to her as \"bossy\" when she barks because she wants to do something and hasn't quite figured out how yet. She also likes to bark at the big dogs to get them to play bitey-face with her on the couch. She's a sweet, silly, special girl, who is looking for forever humans that understand her limitations and help her break down the walls when she can.

description:

Marley is a very sweet girl. She would love to meet you so she can give you love and attention. She loves to be with you to play and get petted which I don't think she had a lot of until she came to us. She enjoys being outside playing with other dogs but thinks being inside with people is better. She is not interested in running around outside retrieving but will go get treats which she takes very nicely. She likes to go on walks which is good as she has to lose some extra weight. We see a vegetable and fruit diet in her future! Marley would like to meet a family that will give her love and attention. Kids 10 and up as we don't have history. Good with other dogs has been out with other LR pups at the kennel with no problems. No cat history. Knows sit, come and sometimes down. Not bad on lead, better when walking with an Easy Walk Harness. Crate trained, probably house trained as she is keeping her room clean at the kennel. If you are looking for a laid back, gentle soul, consider Marley. This dog is from a rural area and has not been exposed to traffic, noise, or groups of people. If dogs are overwhelmed by their environment, they can exhibit behaviors like excessive barking. To avoid this, for now we are limiting placement to stand alone single family homes in a suburban neighborhood or rural area. As we learn more from the dog's time spent in foster, we will evaluate if placement can be expanded. 

Foster family reports: Update We know that Marley is not her real name so we're trying different names. Right now we're calling her Penny, so we'll see. A couple more facts about Marley/Penny. We're not sure how she got to be so large but she's the most food-unmotivated lab! She may or may not eat her breakfast and she's really not into fruits or veggies. Her thyroid has been tested and is fine. We've never had a pup take treats so gently. We're used to the \"you may lose your fingers\" type of lab. Marley/Penny will go to the door if she needs to do her business. She would like a family who's willing to take the time with her to help her feel comfortable and loved. She'd also like a couple walks a day to help her build up her stamina and lose some of those pesky pounds. She recently visited with a friend for a weekend sleepover and met two very dog-savvy cats. She initially appeared to want to play with them but that was more effort than she wanted to expend and she laid back down. Marley/Penny found the toy basket, and although she is not a huge player or retriever, she periodically picks up a tennis ball and brings it to you or gnaws on one of the many bones all over the house. She LOVES her walks she doesn't go far and not too fast but she loves all the smells and all the people and dogs met so far. Marley/Penny is a very easy dog that requires little more than a place to sleep, a few pats on her head, some belly scratches and some food. Do you have room in your heart and home for Penny?

description:

Blake is a sweet, happy boy. He is good with other dogs and used to live with two others in his previous home. We don't know how Blake is with cats. He is very curious and is quite interested in all the daily activity of the suburbs. He loves to look out the window at home and in the car. He has been fascinated by joggers and was completely mesmerized by a sprinkler. He has been very interested in everything the family is doing. He likes to lay in the kitchen while we are cooking and eating dinner, but never begs or gets into the garbage. Blake does not bark and does not jump on strangers. He has not had the opportunity to learn basic commands but has demonstrated he can learn quickly and responds when you correct him. He went from crazy dog on a leash to a calmer and responsive walker on the harness. Blake will make a great addition to a family and will quickly bond. He has loads of personality and has perfect house manners.

He has not been crated; he did scratch at the door when left alone initially, but calmed after a couple of days. His foster works-from-home, so he does get a potty break every four hours. Blake is great with the fosterâs teenager. He knows sit, and he quickly learned paw! He is a great eater, is not protective of his food, and sleeps through the night. Blake is a playful guy and walks ~4 miles each day to expend his energy. He is very strong, and his handler needs to be prepared for him to pull hard if he senses something he wants to investigate. He is learning to walk on a leash and doing MUCH better, but ongoing training is needed. He wants to meet people and dogs on his walks and does well; he has not spent time alone with other pups while with his fosters. Blake is a cuddly, fun-loving boy and is the perfect match for a family willing to give him the exercise and ongoing training he needs.

description:

Ginger is a sweet, smart, gentle lady who enjoys snuggling, swimming, and going for walks. This pretty brown-eyed girl has good manners in the house, sleeps all night in a cozy dog bed, knows multiple commands, and walks well on a leash. Sheâs pretty close to perfect! Ginger is a fun, active girl who doesnât need much and is ready to find a family that has room for a laid-back love bug in their lives. Sheâs generally fine to be left alone for about 6 hours, but she needs a home where she won't be alone for a long work day. There are just a few things Ginger canât do in her golden years - like stairs. Sheâs okay on a few, but a whole flight is too much for her. She also needs help getting into a car. Ginger LOVES to sleep in the bedroom. She gets along with all of the resident dogs, and even the resident cat. Sometimes she doesn't like to share her toys, so as long as there are plenty of toys to be had, she will be a happy camper! She has been learning to take treats gently and responds to \"easy.\" She'll be a great addition to someone's home. She's such a nice dog with a great spirit and energy!Â 

UPDATE FROM FOSTER: Beautiful Ginger is checking in with a smile! Her foster family adores her and states that you cannot help but but smile and love her!! Ginger has great house manners, loves to go for walks, enjoys car-rides, is thrilled with lots of attention and will sleep quietly at your feet. All of these good things are wrapped up into a 13-year-old girl who is truly young in heart and spirit! Ginger is a gem of a gal who is always wagging her tail and is always excited to start her day, giving no thought or worry as to what will come her way -- A lesson to learn!! Ginger has so many good qualities and is good with other dogs who will respect her space - AND when she gets to know the kitty's in her life, she respects their space and won't chase or bother them. Ginger is not good on steps, but she has great house manners and knows all the basics. Added to this, she also has great eye-mouth coordination to catch treats, loves car-rides and lots of attention and of course mealtimes! All these good things wrapped up into a beautiful 13-year-old girl who is young in heart and spirit and has so much love to give!!

History: Rosa comes from a local Washington shelter. PUP was asked to help and we are happy to help her find her forever home!

Notes from Rosa's Foster Home: If you are a fan of the chihuahua personality and spunk, then Rosa may be the pup for you! She has been delighting us since joining our home and we truly love this girl!

Rosa really enjoys getting out and about. She loves neighborhood walks as well as exploring a wooded trail. She is a 'regular' at Home Depot and has fun with her friends at the local pet food store. She can be shy when meeting people and likes to have an opportunity to meet new folks at her own pace. She would love to be your sidekick!

Rosa's house manners are excellent! She is crate trained, house trained on a schedule, and has mastered many commands. Rosa will alert bark at times but quiets quickly with correction. When not snoozing in a comfy dog bed, she is busy playing with toys, running and retrieving, or playing tug with our 75 lb dog (don't tell her she only weighs 7 lbs!). She can be quite comical when chasing squirrels in the yard, chasing a ball, or running in the yard for the sheer joy of it! Come evening, she looks for a warm and welcoming lap. She is just loaded with personality and this tiny-but-mighty dog makes us laugh every day. And did we mention her cute little zig-zag tail?

Rosa has 'bladder struvite crystals'. Crystals are concentrates of naturally occurring minerals in a dog's urine which can occur due to abnormal urine pH. The good thing about struvite crystals is they can be managed easily by keeping her on an inexpensive prescription food (approx $15/month). She needs to have water available at all times, as well as the opportunity to get outside frequently. Despite this diagnosis, Rosa behaves like all happy and playful young dogs.

Because of her size and shy nature, she will do best in a home with adults and older, dog-respectful children (12+ yrs) She also needs to have opportunities to go 'out' several times during the day. She loves other dogs and would really enjoy having a playful canine buddy in her new home or a playmate nearby. She will require strict adherence to her dietary needs.

This extra-special pup is looking forward to finding her new, extra-special family!

name: Baby Jade
description:
Stare deep into those baby blues, and tell us it's not love at first sight!

Baby Jade is an absolutely stunning American Staffordshire Terrier puppy that had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. Baby Jade is currently in Houston, Texas and available for transport through our rescue partners. 

This little girl has been in foster care for about 3 months and has  trained quickly. She is smart, learns quickly and has grown to become confident dog with a playful nature. She has learned to walk on a leash, crate train and house train quickly. She is very food motivated and will require a home that will work with her on basic obedience and gives her guidance. Baby Jade can be a little stubborn and her favorite activities include stealing peaches off the trees and searching for pecans in the grass. She can be a little stubborn at times and tends to run off and explore on her own, while the other dogs play. She plays in a group daily with other dogs, both male and female, ranging from young pups to adults, and does great with all of them. She loves to wrestle and roughhouse, if the other dog will allow. When another dog sets boundaries with Baby Jade by barking, growling or correcting her with a bite to the neck, she will back down and go into puppy mode by running away. Baby Jade is dog friendly and great with kids.

She is about 50lbs now and still growing. She recently had a growth spurt and is in that awkward puppy stage where she has skinny body and long, lanky legs. Baby Jade will be a large dog when fully grown, from 80-90lbs, and has an incredibly sweet temperament. She is medium to high activity, and would be an amazing companion for runs, hikes or just a nice casual stroll around the park.

Baby Jade is at an age where she needs guidance and would thrive in an environment with another assertive and more confident dog. She does well with dominant female dogs and takes correction well, however may persist in roughhousing until her human steps in to correct her as she is all about playing. This girl is a tomboy and lives for mud puddles and water- don't let her good looks fool you into thinking she is a girly girl! She is also extremely vocal and \"sings\" when she is hungry, displeased or bored, so be prepared to always have someone talking to you and letting you know how she feels! 

Baby Jade has a high prey drive towards rodents, such as squirrels, rats and possum outdoors. We have not tested Baby Jade with cats, but she is very calm and submissive. She could likely be trained to accept cats, with strict reinforcement.

Background: 
Baby Jade had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. She was found with a broken tail and infected, butchered ears from an amateur crop job at only 6 months old. She came to us as a stray, found by a Good Samaritan who saved her life after seeing a man beat and kick her on the street for approaching his dog while on a walk. He said she was vicious and tried to throw her into oncoming traffic. 

Vetting: Baby Jade has received the standard DHLPP vaccine, rabies vaccine and Bordatella vaccine. She is spayed, microchipped and heartworm negative. We recommend that all rescue dogs coming from Texas remain on heartworm preventative for 6 months after arriving in Washington, as a precaution.

description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

description:

She is a beautiful and spunky 4 yr young 75 lb lab mix, spayed, current on all vaccines and no health issues and perfectly house trained. Juliet adores people and kids (because of her energy and strength she should be watched around small children). She is the biggest lover of people - loyal, affectionate, intelligent, highly trainable, protective, energetic, strong, sweet, in need of human love and interaction, good listener, senses emotion, loves to hang with her owners, needs daily exercise, needs routine, needs alpha management. She is a wonderful protector of home and family and will bark loudly and menacingly at strangers who approach the house until she officially meets them. She is anxious away from her owners and does not do well in kennels, she needs in-home boarding (at owner's home or in home of sitter.)

Juliet is an alpha dog and needs a firm and consistent hand which is not possible in her current situation. Juliet's ideal owner would be an experienced and alpha dog owner (single person, couple or family with children experienced with dogs) who could love and spend time with her, manage her firmly, and keep a routine for her. She does fine when home alone during the day as long as she knows her owners will return after work. She will do better with fewer handlers who can use the same training methods with her (e.g. we have too many handlers -- nanny, babysitters, housekeeper, dog walker, husband, wife, kids) Active owners - and with a yard - would be ideal.

Juliet cannot be with other dogs at this time - while she loves certain dogs that she knows, she has shown aggression with other dogs. She loves flirting with cats on walks, but it is unknown how she would do with a cat in the home. She shows aggression towards large dogs and needs active training before any further interaction with dogs. Juliet should not interact off leash with dogs until further training. Her current dog trainer located in Washington, DC has offered free training to the new owners.

name: Sparky
description:
It's been over 10 years since the water rose up in Waveland, MS. Over 3,500 days since the hurricane cracked the skies open and drove the sea right into town. If you have to ask which hurricane, well, then you probably aren't from around here. Katrina made landfall at Waveland, MS, a small town of 7,000 just an hour east of New Orleans, on August 29, 2005, and you'd be hard-pressed to find any of God's good creatures in Waveland that don't remember. Destin and Sparky remember.



Chaos is too simple of a word to convey what that time was like, but it's the closest thing we've got. Fortunately, there were a few clear minds that day, including Doll Stanley and In Defense of Animals. The organization recognized the doom bearing down on animals in the region, petitioning courts to release captured animals in the pound. Destin was one such animal, languishing in the pound as the storm bore down on the Gulf Coast. At the 11th hour, a judge granted the request, forcing animal control to release the animals to safety. When they reached Destin, the water was already up to her neck. Destin and 34 other animals were rescued that night, but, sadly, thousands more souls lost their lives all along the coast. Destin and Sparky, who was discovered after the storm, were some of the lucky ones.



A number of animal rescue facilities went to work in the aftermath of Katrina, and ARF was one of the organizations born from the rubble. The 35 dogs from Waveland made the trip north to Jackson, and a few more groups soon followed. Destin and Sparky were placed together in their new home, and quickly became inseparable, sharing a bond that few of us can scarcely imagine. Yet over 3,500 days after the storm arrived, these two remain with ARF. Every one of the other 35 dogs has moved on, either adopted to a wonderful home or crossing the rainbow bridge. We've twice attempted to adopt Sparky individually, but both dogs immediately grew depressed and stopped eating. Their bond is unique and irreplaceable, and so even though we know how challenging it is to adopt two older dogs, we know that they need to be together. They are sweet and spunky, despite their advanced age. But the wisdom in their eyes is surely enough reward for providing a forever home.



Katrina had an impact that still reverberates throughout the region. As we think of it, we still mourn for those that have been lost. Yet we also recognize the events that catalyzed the creation of ARF, and are reminded of our mission. If you can't adopt Destin and Sparky today, then please continue joining us in this mission. Stop by sometime to walk these wonderful dogs. The lifeblood of this organization is our supporters, and we're grateful every day that you've helped us make it this far.

Sparky, Hound Mix has been shared from Shelter Exchange - http://www.shelterexchange.org.

name: Reilly Virginia
description:
Senior Dog Alert - Sweet, sweet senior

Reilly is a cocker girl we've rescued from West Virginia and she is as sweet as she is pretty - she is blind at this point in her life secondary to what we think is either cataracts or glaucoma - she will have an evaluation at a veterinary ophthalmologist when we get her to New England and are hopeful we can perhaps restore some sight to this girl.

Reilly was found on a porch in West Virginia - the gentleman couldn't get in his house as she was sleeping - he called the local animal control who came and picked her up - knowing our love of seniors we were asked if we'd take her - and the rest is history!!
Reilly gets along with other dogs at the shelter - she does get startled easily until she knows her surroundings but she does not show this in any aggressive fashion. When found she was covered in fleas and flea dirt - the staff at the shelter were able to get her groomed and she looks (and feels) so much better.

Our plan is for Reilly to come to New England the weekend of 9/27 - we are hopeful you will want to adopt er with the full knowledge of her eye condition however we will cover the evaluation with a veteran ophthalmologist - either one of the ones we partner with or if there's one you know of, we can certainly work with them if possible.

Reillly deserves a place to land, forever. She shouldn't need to ever roam around without a home.

Breed: Cocker Spaniel
Sex: Female
Age: 8 years 0 months
Weight: 25 lbs
Spayed/Neutered: Veterinarian examined and found spay scar.
Vaccinations: Up to date
Heartworm: Negative 
Microchipped: Yes

BASED ON OUR OBSERVATIONS: 
Good with Children: Unknown - small children may not be great for her with her eye sight issues.
Good with Dogs: Has done w/ the dogs she's met - interested - does not play.

If you're interested in a specific dog, please complete a short online application and you will receive a reply within 48 hours so you can ask questions.

At present, if a dog is listed on our website, the dog is considered still available HOWEVER, may have applications that have come in before yours but it's still too early to know if any are a good match; therefore we encourage you to apply.

We have found that dogs in foster homes are much more adoptable because they have been observed in a home setting. Dogs listed with Paws New England typically reside in various locations throughout the south (primarily Tennessee, Texas, and Arkansas) and New England (not necessarily in the state of Rhode Island). name: Lucy
description:
Meet Lucinda aka Lucy!!! She came to us heavily pregnant from West Virginia. Her pups have all been adopted and now momma need a home!! She is a small terrier mix (15-20lbs) about 1-2 years old. She has terrier tendencies and because of this we think a home with older children would be best.

Here is what her foster has to say:
Lucy is lovable and cuddly and cute as the dickens. She likes to be around people, usually snuggled up next to them. She loves riding in the car and being outside. She likes to chase balls and other toys. A tennis ball is the perfect size for her. She loves to jump and can walk and hop on her hind legs.

Lucy chews paper and slippers, but not shoes. She is crate trained, but not totally house trained yet. She has to learn to tell you when she needs to go outside. She play nips at you to get your attention, and we are working to break her of this habit. She barks at people to get their attention so they will love her. She also barks at every dog and cat she sees on the street. Lucy does not like the cat in her foster home and would do best with more submissive dogs. She thinks she rules the roost. ??

If interested in Lucy, apply online!!!

name: Oliver
description:
Oliver is a very sweet hound/beagle mix from West Virginia. He is friendly, playful and well behaved.  He likes being with his people and tends to stick close to them. Cuddling and laying on the couch with his family are among his favorite things to do. He rides great in the car and walks well on his harness. He loves walks, being outdoors and being cuddled.   Oliver gets along well with other dogs, but chases cats so a home without cats is a must. 

Oliver is deaf and has some separation anxiety, however, he does well being alone with another young dog. Oliver is house broken and prefers not to be in a crate.

Due to his deafness, Oliver startles easily. Although he loves children, he would do best in a quiet, all adult home with another dog.  He is about a year and a half and weighs about 43 lbs.

name: Chatter
description:
The first thing you notice about Chatter is that she can't stop, well...chattering. She is a talkative lady which is true to her breed and is always ready to let you know what is going on with her distinctive Hound bay. Her moniker is fitting in more ways than one as she loves to chatter and to chat with her human friends. Being a Hound means that Chatter's nose is always on the go and she always knows when you have recently had lunch and will sniff out any crumbs left over. She is pretty much a canine vacuum, and we say that with fondness, and her nose is sniffing out the next treat it can find!

Chatter isÂ a recent transplant from our rescue partner in West Virginia, and from her physical state it seems as if this lady had recently had a litter or puppies or had had previous litters. For a dog as clever and driven as Chatter is (usually for food), we would love to see her put those mothering days behind her and be spoiled in her very own home. Special note to all of our Hound fans; she is as beautiful in person as she is in her photos and just as chatty!Â 

Come meet this Chatty Cathy today, and foster or adopt her! You will never run out of things to talk about with Chatter around!

name: Mr. Pricklepants
description:
Not many dogs have a prefix attached to their name, and not many dogs are like Mr. Pricklepants. Stately, dignified and the picture of a senior gentleman, Mr. Pricklepants is one unique individual. When you first meet Mr. Pricklepants, you might assume he is aloof or standoffish. With a few treats and an abundance of pets, he quickly turns into your BFF. Many assume he is a low-key and easygoing senior, which he is 97% of the time, but the other 3% is pure enthusiasm. Mr. Pricklepants enjoys nothing more than getting out and about in the yard where he can run to his heart's content.Â 

Mr. Pricklepants is a dog with a story to tell: he came to us from our rescue partner in West Virginia, where he had been a primarily outdoor dog before coming to their shelter. He was a favorite of the staff and volunteers who saw just how special this senior guy is when he opens up. Mr. Pricklepants is truly an ideal companion for a family that wants a dog for nice long walks around the neighborhood, but who would equally be as comfortable watching a movie or Sunday night football. Stop by the shelter today and ask about fostering or adopting this awesome senior guy!

Is This Dog Currently Available?... This dog is available at the Small Miracles rescue facility in Ellicott City.  To submit an application, please come meet this dog in person. How Old is this dog?...  We look at a dogs' teeth to estimate its age, and then the age is reevaluated by our veterinary staff when the dog is spayed/neutered.  If an age is not posted online, please feel free to inquire.

All we can tell you for sure is whether/or not a dog's crate is clean when we come to walk them in the AM.  All this means is that they are crate trained and waited to pee until we took them outside.

If a dog is at Small Miracles, it likes people and has a good temperament.  We always suggest you meet the dog to see if it is the right fit for your lifestyle.

Heartworm preventative costs $40-60 depending on the weight of the dog.  This means that a large dog will total $405.00 and an extra large dog will total $415.00.

Why can't I adopt a FREE dog?...  Our adoption fee covers many procedures which cost much more for us then the amount we ask for from you. We spay/neuter all pets, and we give them their first round of vaccines (canine distemper, bordatella, Rabies if age appropriate).  At a typical vet clinic this would cost you $500 at minimum for the surgery, and each vaccine is roughly $35 each.  Even if your adopted dog does not have all of its shots due to the mandatory waiting period between booster shots, we offer vaccinations at the low cost of $20/shot.  We test all dogs for heartworm disease and tickborn illnesses such as Lymes.  We never euthanize a heartworm positive dog, and treatment routinely costs us $3000/dog.  We collect a fecal sample from every rescued dog and run a microscopic parasite test.  Any parasites found will be treated with two rounds of the appropriate dewormer.  We treat all dogs for fleas and ticks with Advantage.  If a dog has significant dental disease or \"very dirty teeth\

name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home. 

If you are interested in adopting or fostering Winter, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Lilly
description:
Hi there! My name is Lilly.  I am 8 months old, weigh 28 pounds, and am full of happiness and fun. I came to Canine Humane Network all the way from West Virginia and I am hoping to find my fur-ever home here in Maryland! 

I am curious and love just about everything including children, kitties, other dogs, my Kong with peanut butter, chasing butterflies and squirrels...you get the picture - I am a happy-go-lucky girl! 

I donât even mind my crate and am house-trained.  I am very energetic, but I still like to be close to my foster parents, and can chill-out on the couch with them and my foster dog sisters. My foster mom is taking me on a lot of walks so I can  learn to walk with her like a grown-up dog. My favorite thing to do is run around in a fenced yard! 

WIll you please think about making me a part of your family fur-ever?  Ask about adopting me today!

Please note that puppies need to have human interaction every 3 hours. 
Adoption Fee is $350 with Spay/Neuter Contract. A separate $100 deposit will be collected but will be returned after we receive the spay/neuter certificate for your puppy at 6 months of age. 

Applications are required prior to meeting the puppy.  You can apply at: http://caninehumane.org/adoption-application/. If you have questions you can email chninquiries@caninehumane.org. Calling or emailing may delay your consideration without an application submitted.

name: Murry Murdoch da Tank!
description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.  

If you are interested in adopting or fostering this dog, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

description:
Lakota is a 2-year-old boy born July 2017 who came to us from a shelter where his previous owners dumped him. He was purchased as a puppy and lived most of his life outside. He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

Lakota would do best in a home with no young children. He did well when seeing other dogs on walks and we will continue to work with him and see how he does with a female companion. name: Apollo the White Knight
description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature. 

If you are interested in adopting Apollo, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.   

If you are interested in adopting Finn, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

Ginger is a beautiful female Goldendoodle, possibly a mix, who is two years old.  This gorgeous gal came to CARE as an owner surrender from Beckley, WV.  Her family is young and has a ton of responsibilities, and they just do not have the time to devote to the needs of a young dog.  Ginger is in need of an experienced owner who will invest some time in providing her with structure and training.

Ginger appears to be in good health.  She is spayed and microchipped and will be up to date on vaccines and blood testing before adoption.  Ginger has been around young children but plays to tough for most.  She is learning how to integrate with other dogs, and may be best as an only pet.

CARE Rescue is  foster-base rescue located in Richmond, VA.  We do not have a facility for you to come to meet animals at.  You must visit our weekly adoption stand (calendar on our website) to meet the adoptable dogs.  Out of area adoptions can only be facilitated when we are able to find a volunteer to do a home visit for us and when the potential adopter already has a veterinary reference.

name: Hobbes
description: COME MEET ADOPTABLE DOGS EVERY SATURDAY AND SUNDAY from 10AM - 4PM at the Homeward Trails Adoption Center- 11116 Fairfax Station Road, Fairfax Station VA 22039! In an effort to save more lives, HT is allowing expedited adoptions for certain animals if applicants bring required paperwork. You can bring your new family member home more quickly by bringing your current pets' vet records, a copy of your lease or landlord letter stating you are permitted to have pets, and photos of your home. Help us help you adopt more quickly! If you are interested in adopting this dog, please fill out our dog adoption questionnaire and e-mail it to adoptioncenter@homewardtrails.org Hobbes is a sweet, young hound mix originally from Fayette County, WV. He loves being with people and actively exploring outdoors. Like most hounds, he requires exercise and activities to keep him happy and content. Hobbes is housetrained and crate-trained, though he does not do well in there for long periods of time as he can get nervous and anxious. For shorter periods of time, he is fine. He plays well with other dogs and would be happy to share his home with another dog. He might be a bit too playful for little kids, but with proper introductions and training may be fine. Hobbes loves to cuddle and play with toys. He does well walking on leash and meeting other dogs. Come meet Hobbes this weekend! PLEASE VISIT THIS WEBSITE TO FIND THE ADOPTION QUESTIONNAIRE: http://www.homewardtrails.org/adopt-a-pet/adoption-forms/ Adoption Coordinator: Adoption Center Location: Adoption Center The adoption fee for this dog is $375. This fee INCLUDES spay/neuter and microchip. Every adopted Homeward Trails animal comes with 30 days of free pet health insurance. We are proud to partner with the following veterinarians who offer a free first exam for your animal, exclusively for HT adopters: Caring Hands Animal Hospital, Palisades Veterinary Clinic, Sunshine Animal Hospital and Clarendon Animal Care and all VCA Animal Hospitals. Additionally, any VCA hospital will cover illnesses up to $250 at no cost to any Homeward Trails adopter. We also provide a 30-minute phone consult with a professional dog trainer at Fur-Get Me Not within the first 30 days of adopting - just for HT adopters in the Arlington/Alexandria area. Start your new dog out on the right foot with this valuable, expert advice and guidance FREE! You can save animals like this one by becoming a foster! Fosters are like way stations between high kill shelters and forever homes. We need fosters so that we can save dogs before they are euthanized at the shelters. If you are interested in becoming a foster, please check out our information about fostering by visiting http://www.homewardtrails.org/foster-a-pet/dog-and-cat-foster-program/

name: Pudding
description:
These puppies were rescued from a WV high kill shelter.   These puppies are about 10 weeks old and 12#

TO ADOPT:

These pups are NOT in the shelter and you MUST submit an application to smpetfinder@gmail.com to get the process started.  Go to www.smallmiraclesrescue.org and click \"How to Adopt\".  There you will find the dog/puppy application available for download. The more information you provide, the faster the process is for all of us.  Once you are approved to adopt we will schedule an appointment to see the puppy in person and you will be allowed to take it home that day.  Due to the ease of our adoption process, please apply only if you are ready to adopt right now and committed to the level of care that having a puppy requires.  If you are not ready to adopt, we totally understand - just wait to apply until you are ready.  Many of our puppies are placed less than 72 hours after the application is submitted (ex: an application submitted on a Thurs could be approved and the puppy sent home as early as Saturday). 

Make sure to note in the email subject line which puppy you are interested in.  I will take back up applications for every puppy in the event an adoption falls through.

Adoption Fee Broken Down:

Before our puppies are available for adoption, they will always be spayed or neutered, vaccinated (distemper, bordatella, rabies if age appropriate), dewormed, and stool sample checked for parasites.  Adoption fee for our puppies is $325, an additional $30 for a microchip and registration and an additional small discounted amount for a 3 month supply of heartworm preventative, priced at $20.

name: Baldur
description:
Tyr, Heimdall and Baldur are baby puppies, the most perfectly cute and handsome little guys ever!!!   We don't know who their parents are, or what breeds they are mixed with.  They look like small Boxers though, so we think they are Boxer x small breed.  The pups were rescued from a shelter in WV.  They are 8-9 weeks old now and ready to be adopted!

Spay/neuter is required and will be required to be done when they are 6-8 months old. A $100 refund will be given with proof of spay/neuter, unless the owner chooses to donate the fee to the rescue.

description:
